data.summary: A SAMA circular to banks operating in the Kingdom clarifying three points in the updated Consumer Finance Regulations: when the borrower's right to terminate or withdraw from the finance agreement lapses (it ends within the stated day-count from contract signature once the customer has actually benefited from the financing, e.g. drawing cash, shares deposited to the customer's portfolio, or taking possession/use of the financed asset), the obligation to use SAMA's initial disclosure form for finance contracts, and the requirement to follow SAMA's published guide for calculating the annual percentage rate. It is an interpretive/clarifying instruction rather than a new rule, and binds banks as an operational compliance requirement.
lookup_terms: حق العميل في إنهاء الاتفاقية أو الانسحاب
Updated Consumer Finance Regulations Article 10 Article 11

data.summary: An annex/reporting template setting out the disclosure format for total remuneration paid to board of directors and board committee members, broken down by membership type (executive, non-executive, independent) and by component: fixed amounts, attendance allowances, in-kind benefits, profit share, granted shares, chairman/managing director/secretary remuneration, and other items, all in SAR thousands. It is a disclosure schedule supporting governance and remuneration transparency obligations for supervised entities' boards.

A 2014 SAMA circular to all banks issuing a revised package of guidance for the Amended Liquidity Coverage Ratio, following a comprehensive gap review of SAMA's Basel III regulations against BCBS standards. The package comprises general and specific guidance, the prudential return, FAQs and national discretions, and banks are also directed to benchmark liquidity practices against BCBS sound liquidity risk management principles. It binds all banks supervised by SAMA and supersedes/updates the earlier 2013 LCR guidance.

A 2013 SAMA circular to banks transmitting the Amended LCR guidance package (guidance documents, prudential returns, FAQs and national discretions) and setting the reporting mechanics: monthly LCR prudential returns from the June 2013 month-end within 30 days of each month-end, with an extended deadline for the first submission. It confirms that NSFR reporting continues unchanged under the earlier 2012 circular pending BCBS alignment. Binds all banks except foreign bank branches for the LCR return obligation.

A SAMA document (1436H) setting the criteria used to designate payment systems as systemically important in the Kingdom, defining such systems as those whose disruption could impair participants or cause systemic failure of the financial infrastructure. Criteria include handling interbank or customer payments that could threaten financial stability, being the principal system by daily volume and value, being used to settle for another systemically important financial infrastructure, and being a central payments infrastructure with customer confidence and no substitutes. On this basis SAMA designates SARIE (RTGS), SPAN (ATM/POS network) and SADAD (electronic bill presentment and payment) as systemically important; SAMA acts as owner, operator and sole regulator of these systems.

A SAMA circular to all financial institutions under its supervision reaffirming, pursuant to a Royal Order and an earlier SAMA circular, that the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) is the sole entity authorised to receive relief, humanitarian and charitable donations — whether from government or private sources — for delivery to beneficiaries abroad. Institutions must verify that such donations and cross-border transfers are channelled through KSrelief, review donation transactions made on foreign platforms using bank and credit cards, and continue awareness and monitoring measures when providing services.
lookup_terms: donations via foreign platforms card payments
Royal Order sole authorised entity donations

data.summary: SAMA circular directing all SAMA-supervised financial institutions to establish technical linkage with Elm in order to use the Ministry of Interior's "Digital Document" service, which allows an electronic copy of the digital ID to be taken and the identity, its validity date and an enquiry reference number to be verified (via QR reader or entry of the national ID/iqama number). It follows an earlier circular on accepting digital identity for existing customers and supplies the mechanism for transactions that require retaining an ID copy. Institutions must coordinate directly with Elm, notify SAMA of implementation difficulties, comply with applicable laws, and preserve the customer's freedom to choose between the physical or digital ID.

Short SAMA circular (issued by the Payment Systems and Companies Control Department) prohibiting all financial institutions from using social media or instant-messaging applications, directly or indirectly, to exchange any official data or documents. Such exchanges must instead take place through official, secure and approved channels, on grounds of data protection, customer confidence and operational risk. Effective from its date of issue and binding on all financial institutions.

SAMA circular announcing an update to the Requirements for Appointment to Leading Positions in SAMA-supervised financial institutions (second edition, previously issued by circular 17/1594), extending their scope to cover "activities supporting finance activity". The updated version is published on SAMA's website and applies from the circular's date. Distributed to banks, finance and real estate finance companies, finance-support companies, credit information companies, exchange businesses, and payment companies and systems.

The primary statute governing finance companies in the Kingdom: it defines core terms (Finance Company, Borrower, Consumer, Finance, License), restricts the law's application to companies licensed under it, and requires Sharia-compliant conduct. It sets out SAMA licensing of specified finance activities (real estate, production asset, SME, finance lease, credit card, consumer finance, microfinance and other SAMA-approved activities) and of entities engaged in activities supporting finance activity, plus prohibitions on non-finance business, deposit-taking, trading, uncollateralised finance and related-party/connected lending. It binds licensed finance companies, their boards, directors and external auditors, with detail left to the Implementing Regulations.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulations of the Finance Companies Control Law

data.summary: SAMA circular setting minimum standards where a financial institution offers or promotes products under a brand different from its original corporate identity and trade name, issued under the SAMA Law and framed as consumer protection, disclosure and transparency. Requirements include addressing brand/identity impersonation (cyber and fraud risk) in the risk management strategy and policy, engaging brand-protection service providers, updating usage and data-privacy policies, registering the new or updated trademark and notifying SAMA, running an awareness campaign, and displaying the trade name together with the brand in customer calls, first SMS contact, on websites and alongside any statement of SAMA supervision, including the licence number. Binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions from its date.

SAMA circular reaffirming that supervised financial institutions must apply the Law on the Use of Security Surveillance Cameras, its Ministry of Interior Implementing Regulation, and the associated security conditions and general technical specifications for installing surveillance camera systems. It notes that financial institutions are classified among high-sensitivity sites under the site-sensitivity classification, and also requires compliance with SAMA's Security and Safety Guide for the financial sector. Binding on all financial institutions supervised by SAMA.
lookup_terms: Security and Safety Guide for the financial sector

data.theme: SAMA's counter-fraud regime for supervised institutions: the mandatory governance, prevention, detection and response obligations that sit alongside (and interlock with) the cyber security and IT governance frameworks.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Counter-Fraud Framework and its fundamental requirements sit above the four domains (Governance, Prevent, Detect, Respond), each of which decomposes into named controls such as fraud risk assessment, multi-factor authentication, mule account detection and the fraud response plan.

Obligation chain: board-level fraud risk appetite drives the fraud risk assessment, which drives key risk indicators, intelligence monitoring and the maturity model used for SAMA supervisory assessment and notification duties.

Accountability structure is defined by role: Counter-Fraud Governance Committee, Head of Counter-Fraud and the Counter-Fraud Department, with whistle-blowing and supervisory notification as escalation routes.

Cross-regime linkage: authentication, system development, change security and IT project management controls are cited from the SAMA Cyber Security and IT Governance Frameworks, so fraud controls inherit those requirements; sector-specific application to finance companies comes via the Anti-Fraud Rules circular.

data.theme: Circular-level due diligence expectations where onboarding/KYC intersects with the distribution of investment products through electronic money institution channels.
how_members_connect: Both instruments are SAMA circulars imposing customer-facing verification duties rather than framework-level rules.
Shared concept: the depth of information required about a customer (notably income/source of funds) before a product or channel may be offered.
Cross-regime interaction: AML/CTF customer due diligence expectations are applied within a payments/EMI distribution setting, so the EMI's 'customer' and the fund's investor must be reconciled.
start_here: Customer Income Verification Due Diligence Circular
Investment Fund Distribution via EMI Channels Circular

data.theme: Consumer protection: SAMA's phased mandate for supervised entities to operate a complaint management system with defined intake, handling and reporting obligations.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone circular setting the first-phase implementation obligation and timeline.
Reads across to consumer protection principles and to conduct reporting duties owed to SAMA, though those instruments sit outside this cluster.
start_here: Complaint Management System Phase One Circular

data.theme: Prudential and financial reporting obligations: what supervised institutions must submit to SAMA, in what form and on what cycle.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a circular fixing periodic financial statement and prudential data submission duties.
Functions as the reporting limb of the wider governance and risk regime; accuracy and timeliness of submissions are the enforceable elements.
start_here: Financial Statements and Prudential Data Reporting Circular

data.theme: Access and accountability for the designated 'Main User' role on SAMA's eSAMA e-Services Portal, i.e. who within a supervised entity is authorised to transact with SAMA electronically and administer sub-users.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: the concept is a defined administrative role rather than a rule family, so its legal weight comes from cross-references in supervisory circulars requiring nomination of an authorised contact.
Links outward to entity governance (senior management sign-off) and to reporting/notification duties channelled through the portal.
start_here: Main User of eSAMA e-Services Portal

data.theme: The institutional governance, control and conduct architecture SAMA imposes on banks, finance and real estate refinance companies, and exchange centres — board and committee mandates, the three lines of defence (compliance, internal audit, risk), Shariah governance, remuneration, and code-of-conduct obligations.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: governance principles documents sit at the top, with sector-specific compliance and internal audit principles (banks vs finance/real estate refinance companies) elaborating the same core duties for different licensee populations.

Obligation chains run board → committees (audit, risk, nomination and remuneration, executive) → executive management → control functions (compliance unit/officer, internal audit unit, Shariah committee), each with defined independence, reporting-line and escalation duties.
Shared defined terms and the three lines of defence model tie compliance, internal audit and risk together, including the second-line/third-line relationship and quality assurance over audit work.

Cross-regime hooks: compliance principles pull in AML/CTF obligations, information confidentiality/classification, and conduct rules; remuneration rules (2023, superseding the 2010 compensation practices) attach malus/clawback to misconduct risk and require compliance reporting.
start_here: Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions

data.theme: Observance of the Founding Day public holiday (1447H) by SAMA-supervised institutions, affecting business days, settlement windows and regulatory deadline calculation.
how_members_connect: Isolated announcement-type node; its legal relevance is derivative — it modifies when duties falling on working days become due.
Connects conceptually to payment system operating calendars and to any regulation computing periods in business days.

data.theme: Enforceability of close-out netting and collateral (financial security) arrangements in KSA, including their treatment on counterparty default or insolvency and the resulting effect on exposure measurement.
how_members_connect: Standalone regulation node; legally it interacts with prudential capital/exposure rules that permit netted exposure recognition only where netting is legally enforceable.
Cross-references insolvency and contractual enforceability concepts, so it should be read alongside risk governance and credit exposure regimes rather than in isolation.
start_here: Close-Out Netting and Collateral Arrangements Regulation

data.theme: Consumer credit lifecycle for individuals: credit card issuance and operation, cost-of-credit disclosure (APR and related consumer finance controls), and the conduct limits that apply when the resulting debt is collected.
how_members_connect: The credit card rules operate as the primary conduct regime and cross-refer to the consumer finance controls circular for pricing/APR and term-clarification obligations (Articles 10 and 11).

Collection of card and consumer finance arrears is governed by the debt collection regulations, so the issuance rules import those constraints on contact, disclosure and treatment of individual customers.
Shared scope anchor: the natural-person 'individual customer' / consumer, which limits these obligations relative to corporate exposures.
Duplicate documents in the cluster are near-identical versions of the same instrument and should be reconciled by issuance date before citing.
start_here: Rules for Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards
Updated Debt Collection Regulations for Individual Customers

data.theme: Governance disclosure of board and board-committee remuneration — what must be reported, by whom, and on what periodic basis.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone reporting/disclosure requirement in the corporate governance regime with no internal cross-references captured here.
Its legal effect sits downstream of general governance and disclosure duties for supervised entities; read alongside the applicable governance framework rather than in isolation.
start_here: Report on Total Remunerations for the Board of Directors and Committees

data.theme: Prudential liquidity regime: the Liquidity Coverage Ratio standard and the associated supervisory reporting of LCR and NSFR positions.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the amended LCR regulations set the substantive ratio requirement; the circular operationalises it through amended prudential returns and extends reporting to NSFR.
Shared defined terms (high-quality liquid assets, net cash outflows, stable funding horizons) mean the circular cannot be read independently of the underlying regulation.
Scope is limited to banks subject to SAMA prudential supervision; effective dates in the circular govern which return format applies.
start_here: SAMA Revised Amended Liquidity Coverage Ratio Regulations
SAMA Circular: Amended LCR Prudential Returns and NSFR

data.theme: Oversight of payment systems designated as systemically important, together with operational and counterparty-risk expectations for participants — including SARIE operating hours and dealings with e-commerce payment technical support providers.
how_members_connect: The systemically important payment systems standards act as the parent framework; the SARIE operating-hours notice is an operational instruction issued under that oversight regime.
Guidance on e-commerce payment technical support companies links to the same framework through participant risk management and outsourcing/third-party dependency concerns in the payments chain.
Cross-regime interaction: entities in scope may also be licensed PSPs, so payment-services licensing and AML/CDD duties apply in parallel to these oversight standards.
The Ramadan/Eid hours notice is time-bound and does not alter the substantive standards.
start_here: Standards for Systemically Important Payment Systems in KSA
Dealing with E-Commerce Payment Technical Support Companies

data.theme: Channelling of humanitarian and charitable donations through a single state-authorized entity (KSrelief), as an AML/CTF and terrorist-financing control over the non-profit sector.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: the obligation stands alone as a directive-level control rather than part of a rule chain.

Legally it sits at the intersection of AML/CTF duties on financial institutions and NPO-sector abuse risk, restricting permissible counterparties/purposes for cross-border and domestic donation flows.

Consequence for a decision: collection or transfer of humanitarian donations outside the authorized channel should be treated as a prohibited activity and a red flag for reporting, not merely a policy preference.
start_here: KSrelief as Sole Authorized Entity for Humanitarian Donations

data.theme: Use of a mandated electronic link to the national digital document service (Elm) for verifying customer identity and official documents.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster; the requirement operates as an implementation directive attached to CDD/identification obligations rather than a standalone regime.
Cross-regime relevance: identity verification for AML/CTF customer due diligence, and reliability/accuracy of customer data under consumer protection and data-quality expectations.
Decision impact: reliance on the authoritative government source narrows scope for accepting alternative or self-declared documentary evidence.
start_here: Electronic Linkage with Elm for Digital Document Service

data.theme: Restriction on the channels used to exchange official and customer-related data, specifically prohibiting social media platforms.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: a confidentiality and information-handling prohibition directed at supervised entities and their staff.
Links conceptually to banking secrecy, customer data protection and operational/conduct risk governance obligations.
Decision impact: any exchange of official or customer data over social channels is a compliance breach regardless of consent or convenience.
start_here: Prohibition on Social Media for Exchanging Official Data

data.theme: Updated requirements governing appointment to senior leadership positions in SAMA-supervised entities (fit-and-proper style controls and supervisory clearance).
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster within the governance/risk regime, amending previously issued appointment criteria.
Obligation chain: entity nominates, criteria are assessed, supervisory non-objection conditions the validity of the appointment.
Decision impact: appointments made without meeting the updated criteria or clearance are exposed to challenge and supervisory action.
start_here: Update to Leadership Position Appointment Requirements

data.theme: Seasonal operational-readiness and business-hours expectations imposed by SAMA on currency exchange centres (and comparable outlets) around Ramadan, Eid and the Hajj season, where service continuity and cash availability for pilgrims and the public are supervisory concerns.
how_members_connect: Both are SAMA supervisory communications addressed to the same licensee population (exchange/money-changing sector) and operate as periodic instructions rather than standing regulation.
Shared obligation logic: adjust and publish working hours, and maintain adequate staffing/liquidity so branches remain serviceable during peak seasonal demand.

The Ramadan/Eid hours instruction dates the readiness expectation to a specific Hijri year, so the general readiness circular supplies the standing rationale and the annual notice supplies the applicable timing.
start_here: Currency Exchange Centers Readiness for Ramadan and Hajj

data.theme: Continuity of cash services during Ramadan — permitted or expected hours for ATM replenishment and cash-in-transit operations, sitting at the intersection of operational resilience and physical security/safe-transport requirements.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone SAMA instruction to banks and cash-services providers on timing of replenishment and transport activity.
Legally it functions as a temporary variance/clarification against normal cash-handling and security-of-transport expectations, not a change to underlying licensing obligations.
Read alongside seasonal working-hours instructions for other licensee types, which share the same continuity-of-service objective.
start_here: ATM Replenishment and Cash Transport Hours during Ramadan

data.theme: Application of the Commercial Register and Trade Names Laws to SAMA-supervised entities — i.e. the corporate-identity and registration prerequisites that sit upstream of, and are separate from, SAMA licensing.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: SAMA transmitting/enforcing another authority's statutory regime (Ministry of Commerce laws) onto its supervised population.

Creates a cross-regime compliance chain: valid commercial registration and lawful trade-name use are conditions of good standing that supervised entities must maintain and reflect in customer-facing naming and disclosure.
Relevant to KYB and onboarding analysis, since registration data and trade names are core identification evidence for corporate customers and merchants.
start_here: Applying Commercial Register and Trade Names Laws

data.theme: Bank capital adequacy under the Basel III framework as adopted in KSA, specifically the composition and calibration of regulatory capital and the macroprudential buffer layered on top of minimum requirements.
how_members_connect: Hierarchical: the Basel III capital standards set the definitional base (capital components, risk-weighted assets, minimum ratios) and the CCyB instrument is calibrated and enforced by reference to it.
Explicit citation link — the countercyclical buffer material draws its defined terms and calculation mechanics from the capital standards rather than restating them.

Shared consequence chain: shortfalls against the buffer trigger constraints on distributions and require supervisory engagement, so both must be read together to determine an institution's effective requirement.
Applies to the same scope of banks licensed under the Banking Control Law, distinguishing this regime from finance-company or PSP prudential rules.

data.theme: Licensing, ownership and conduct of SAMA-supervised finance companies — covering entry into finance/refinance and finance-support activities, debt-based crowdfunding, real estate finance and mortgage documentation, portfolio and debt transfers, and ongoing governance, disclosure and fraud-control duties.
how_members_connect: The Finance Companies Control Law is the statutory anchor: nearly every rule, guideline, circular and form in the cluster cites or is issued under it, forming a law → implementing rules → licensing guideline → circular hierarchy.

Licensing pathways share common gatekeeping instruments — the Fit and Proper assessment for controllers/senior officers and entity identification requirements — so the crowdfinance and finance/refinance guidelines converge on the same suitability and identification evidence.

Asset-side instruments interlock: portfolio purchases (including residential real estate finance) and inter-company consumer debt purchases depend on the mortgage documentation and real estate valuation obligations that establish enforceable security and valuation quality.

Ongoing supervisory obligations attach to licensed status rather than to a product line: pre-announcement notification of periodic financial statements, the mandatory compliance certificate, committee terms of reference and counter-fraud requirements apply across the licensee population.
start_here: Finance and Refinance Activities Licensing Guidelines
Rules for Engaging in Debt-Based Crowdfunding

data.theme: Two conduct/operational control requirements applied to supervised entities' customer-facing presence: how products may be marketed under a brand other than the licensee's own, and the physical security surveillance standards for premises.
how_members_connect: Both are supervisory conduct requirements addressed to the licensed entity at the point of customer interaction — one governing identity/disclosure of who is actually providing the product, the other governing the physical environment where that interaction occurs.
The link is thematic rather than a citation chain: neither instrument is the legal basis for the other, so each should be read against its own scope and addressee.

Brand-identity rules matter for consumer protection and accountability (the consumer must be able to identify the licensed provider); surveillance requirements sit in the operational risk and fraud/physical-security space.
start_here: Presenting Products under a Different Brand Identity

data.theme: The GCC-NET point-of-sale payment service — cross-border regional card acceptance and switching arrangements at POS involving Saudi payment infrastructure.
how_members_connect: Isolated node in the graph: no internal citation links, so its obligations must be read against the wider payments/PSP regime rather than inferred from neighbours.

Relevant cross-regime touchpoints to check separately include payment service provider licensing and operational requirements, merchant acceptance/acquiring duties, and consumer protection on disputed or cross-border transactions.

data.theme: Safeguarding of customer funds — the requirement that money held on behalf of clients be protected and held in custody separately from the firm's own assets, so it is insulated from the firm's insolvency and misuse.
how_members_connect: Standalone instrument with no internal cross-references captured; its meaning depends on which regime's defined 'funds' and 'customer/client' terms apply to the firm relying on it.

Practically it interacts with payments/PSP and finance-company regimes (segregation, permitted holding arrangements, reconciliation duties) and with AML/CTF where safeguarding accounts hold pooled customer money.
Scope should be confirmed before application: safeguarding obligations differ by licence type and are not a general deposit-taking permission.
start_here: Protection and Custody of Safeguarded Funds

data.theme: Issuance and operation of credit cards by banks and credit card issuers, covering disclosure, fees and charges, billing, cardholder consent and conduct obligations toward consumers.
how_members_connect: The FAQ is an interpretive companion to the substantive Rules and derives its answers from them, so the Rules govern where the two diverge.
Both share the same defined terms (issuer, cardholder, credit limit, statement cycle) and the same scope of licensed card issuers.
Hierarchy: binding Rules at the top, supervisory clarification (FAQ) below, informing consumer-protection expectations.
start_here: Credit Card Issuance and Operation Rules

data.theme: Prudential risk governance for banks, spanning the Shari'ah-compliant banking risk and governance frameworks, the standard risk taxonomy (credit, market, liquidity, operational, equity investment, Shari'ah non-compliance), stress testing, and internal control expectations.
how_members_connect: A shared risk taxonomy links the Shari'ah RMF, the Stress Testing Rules and the Operational Risk Guide: each attaches obligations to the same named risk categories.
Obligation chain into capital: identified risks (including Shari'ah non-compliance) must feed ICAAP and regulatory reporting, and stress testing results must inform capital and board decisions.
Governance layer is common: board and senior management roles, internal control guidelines and Company Law duties define who owns the framework and approves it.
Version hierarchy: the current Shari'ah RMF supersedes the earlier circular, and interacts with the Shari'ah Governance Framework and PSIA Rules for investment-account holder risk.
External standards (BCBS sound stress testing principles) are referenced as the benchmark SAMA rules localise.
start_here: Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking
Rules on Stress Testing for Banks

data.theme: Administrative determination of official holidays, banking working hours and the corresponding RTGS system operating schedule.
how_members_connect: Single standalone circular; its consequence is timing — settlement finality, value dates and deadline computation for other obligations.
start_here: Official Holidays and Working Hours / RTGS Circular

data.theme: Post-trade transparency and risk mitigation for OTC derivatives: who must report which transactions to an authorised trade repository, with what identifiers, and what bilateral risk-mitigation duties apply to non-cleared trades.
how_members_connect: The current requirements supersede the earlier OTC derivatives circular; the duplicate entry is the same instrument under a different identifier.
The instrument splits into two obligation streams — Section A (reporting) and Section B (risk mitigation) — each with its own scope and counterparty duties.
Reporting depends on mandated identifier standards (LEI, UTI, UPI) as definitional prerequisites, and on submission to a SAMA-authorised trade repository operator.
start_here: Trade Repository Reporting and Risk Mitigation Requirements for OTC Derivatives

data.theme: Governance and control expectations attaching to derivative trade confirmation and valuation — who owns the process, how trades are confirmed within required timeframes, and on what basis positions are valued.
how_members_connect: The governance member sets the accountability layer (board/senior management ownership, policies, internal control) that the confirmation and valuation requirements operate under.
Direct cross-reference: governance obligations are discharged by evidencing compliance with the confirmation/valuation duties, making the two a single obligation chain rather than parallel duties.
Shared scope: both apply to the same population of counterparties and covered derivative transactions, so a scope carve-out for one affects the other.

data.theme: Post-trade risk-mitigation duties for non-centrally-cleared derivatives: periodic portfolio reconciliation between counterparties and the procedures for identifying, escalating and resolving the discrepancies that reconciliation surfaces.
how_members_connect: Sequential obligation chain: reconciliation is the detection duty; dispute resolution is the remediation duty triggered by a reconciliation mismatch (terms or valuation).
Shared defined terms — portfolio, counterparty, valuation — mean a discrepancy identified under one member is the trigger condition of the other.
Both typically require agreed written procedures with the counterparty in advance, and escalation/notification thresholds, so drafting is done together.

data.theme: Portfolio compression as a risk-mitigation technique: the duty to periodically assess and, where appropriate, run compression exercises to reduce gross notional and outstanding contract counts in non-cleared derivative portfolios.
how_members_connect: Standalone node in this graph; its legal effect is a conditional duty (assess, and act if criteria such as portfolio size or number of outstanding trades are met), not an unconditional one.
Operates on the same portfolio construct used by reconciliation and dispute-resolution duties, so scope definitions should be read consistently across those risk-mitigation obligations.
Compression outcomes change the reportable population, linking it downstream to trade-reporting obligations.

data.theme: Identification and reporting data standards for derivative trade reporting — mandatory counterparty identification using the ISO 17442 LEI and the field-level data and reporting-obligation rules that govern what must be submitted.
how_members_connect: Definitional dependency: the counterparty data table and the reporting-obligation rules both incorporate the ISO 17442 LEI as the required identifier, so LEI eligibility/renewal status conditions reportability.
Hierarchy: the reporting obligation rules (who reports, when, on what basis) sit above the appendix data tables that specify the fields to be populated.
Cross-regime read-across: LEI-based entity identification interacts with KYC/KYB customer identification, though the LEI requirement is a reporting standard, not a substitute for CDD.

data.theme: Data-field architecture for derivatives/trade reporting to SAMA: what must be reported per trade, how each report is identified, and how subsequent changes to a live trade are represented.
how_members_connect: Common Data operates as the master reporting table; the trade identifier and action-type fields are elements it points to, so obligations attach through it.
The Unique Trade ID is the linking key that lets lifecycle events, collateral updates and corrections be matched to the original submission.
Action Type plus the lifecycle-event appendix together determine which report type must be filed on modification, termination, error or compression — an obligation chain, not a menu.
Evolutive collateral data is a companion table sharing key common fields, so collateral updates must stay reconcilable with trade-level data.

data.theme: Prescribed interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB) stress scenarios that supervised banks must apply when measuring and reporting rate sensitivity.
how_members_connect: The standardised shock set is the parent requirement; parallel, short-rate, long-rate and rotation shocks are its mandated sub-scenarios, so applying the standard means applying all of them.
Rotation (steepener/flattener) shocks are constructed from the short- and long-rate shocks, creating a definitional dependency.
The scenario calibration is imported from Basel Committee IRRBB standards, so SAMA expectations should be read against that international baseline while SAMA's text controls.

data.theme: Obligation on supervised entities to capture and use the Saudi National Address for customer correspondence and postal delivery, supporting identification and reliable customer communication.
how_members_connect: Single-node topic: the requirement stands alone in the graph, with no internal cross-references extracted.
Read it as an adjunct to customer identification/record-keeping and consumer-notification duties, since address data feeds both CDD records and service of notices.
Scope should be checked against the specific instrument that imposes it before extending it across regimes.
start_here: National Address Requirement for Postal Services

data.theme: Duty of residential real estate financiers to share borrower and facility data with the licensed credit bureau (SIMAH), sitting at the intersection of real estate finance rules and the credit information regime.
how_members_connect: Single-node topic with no extracted internal links; its legal force derives from credit information law/regulation and real estate finance rules read together.
Data sharing presupposes customer consent and accuracy/update duties under the credit information regime, so the obligation is conditional, not unrestricted.
Cross-regime flag: consumer protection and data confidentiality limits apply to what may be disclosed and for what purpose.
start_here: Residential Real Estate Finance Data Sharing with SIMAH

data.theme: Operational readiness and service-continuity expectations for money exchange businesses during peak-demand seasons (Ramadan and Hajj), when currency exchange and remittance volumes for pilgrims and expatriate workers spike. Sits at the intersection of prudential/operational supervision and consumer/customer service standards.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone SAMA circular addressed to licensed exchange centres/companies, operating as a periodic supervisory instruction rather than a standing rule.
Its obligations presuppose the underlying exchange-business licensing and AML/CTF framework (CDD and remittance controls continue to apply unchanged during peak periods).
Seasonal circulars of this type are time-bound directives: compliance teams should check whether the instruction is recurring or superseded by a later-year equivalent before relying on it.
start_here: Circular on Exchange Centers Readiness Ramadan/Hajj

data.theme: Macroprudential designation of domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs), which determines which institutions carry heightened capital, governance, recovery-planning and supervisory intensity requirements.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an annual designation list, i.e. an applicability instrument rather than a substantive obligation — it identifies who is in scope of D-SIB add-ons.
Legal effect flows outward: the list triggers requirements set elsewhere in the prudential/governance regime (capital surcharge, recovery planning, board and risk oversight expectations).
Designation is periodic; the 2025 list supersedes prior-year lists, so entity scope must be re-checked each cycle rather than assumed stable.
start_here: List of Domestic Systemically Important Banks 2025

data.theme: A protective carve-out from creditor enforcement: amounts paid to martyrs' beneficiaries are shielded from seizure/attachment on bank accounts, limiting what banks may freeze or set off against debts.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a targeted instruction to banks that constrains execution of seizure/garnishment orders over identified funds.
Interacts with the consumer protection and banking-account regimes (account operation, set-off and debt-collection practice), creating a duty to distinguish protected from attachable balances.

Practical consequence is at the level of enforcement handling rather than product design: the exemption is a defined-scope exception and does not generalise to other government payments unless separately provided.
start_here: Exemption of Martyrs' Cheque Amounts from Seizure

data.theme: Physical safety and premises-governance compliance for supervised entities, requiring appointment and proper functioning of a fire safety officer in line with the national fire safety regulation.
how_members_connect: Single-care cluster: a SAMA instruction directing supervised institutions to comply with an externally issued (civil defence / national) fire safety regulation.
Legal chain runs law/regulation → SAMA circular: SAMA does not create the substantive fire safety duty but makes adherence a supervisory expectation for licensees.
Sits within operational risk and internal-controls governance (business continuity, branch premises, staff and customer safety) rather than any conduct or AML regime.
start_here: Compliance with Fire Safety Officer Duties Regulation

data.theme: Administrative rules governing how supervised entities may host, sponsor or take part in events and exhibitions, including temporary pavilion presence — essentially conduct and prior-approval conditions on promotional/representational activity rather than prudential regulation.
how_members_connect: A common rule-set hierarchy: the hosting/sponsoring rules and the participation rules are companion instruments issued under the same supervisory mandate, with the later version cross-referring to the earlier.
Participation rules extend the general framework to a specific fact pattern (temporary pavilions), so the specific rules must be read as an overlay on, not a replacement for, the general rules.
Shared scope concepts (event, sponsorship, participation, approval/notification thresholds) determine which instrument governs a given activity.
Versioning matters: V2 participation rules supersede prior text, so the applicable obligation depends on the date of the event.
start_here: General Rules for Participation in Events (V2)
General Rules for Hosting and Sponsoring Events (V1)

data.theme: The targeted financial sanctions / TFS regime: obligations to screen against designated lists, act without delay on matches, freeze and unfreeze funds, escalate and report, and maintain records and staff competence, anchored in UN Security Council resolutions and their domestic implementation.
how_members_connect: A single core instrument (the TFS Rules) is the parent obligation source; the screening, list-management, alerts, freezing/unfreezing, record-keeping and training items are its operative components rather than independent regimes.

Obligation chain: list ingestion and maintenance feeds screening; screening output feeds alert handling and escalation; a confirmed match triggers freezing without delay and reporting, with record-keeping evidencing each step.
Upward citation to UN Security Council resolutions establishes the legal basis and the immediacy standard that domestic rules transpose.

Cross-regime interaction with AML/CTF: customer identification and CDD data are the input to screening, and TFS record-keeping and training duties sit alongside, but are distinct from, AML retention and training obligations.
A duplicate/near-identical rules node exists; treat one as authoritative and reconcile before citing.

data.theme: Consumer protection in pricing and charging: what fees, commissions and administrative charges financial institutions may impose on consumers, how they must be disclosed, and the fair-treatment principles that constrain consumer finance terms.
how_members_connect: The tariff guide is the operative pricing schedule; the administrative fees amendments modify caps and permitted charge categories, so the guide must be read as amended.
Consumer finance controls supply the substantive limits (e.g. charge and cost treatment in finance contracts) that the tariff guide prices, creating a rules-to-schedule relationship.
The customer protection principles are the umbrella standards (transparency, fairness, disclosure) against which any specific tariff item is tested.
Shared defined terms — consumer, service fee, administrative fee — determine whether a charge is permitted, capped, or prohibited.
A duplicate tariff guide node requires version control: identify the current effective edition before advising.

data.theme: Authorisation of finance companies: which financing activities require a licence, the entry conditions and application process, and the minimum capital thresholds that vary by activity, including the lighter regime for micro finance and micro consumer finance.
how_members_connect: Clear hierarchy: the Finance Companies Control Law's Executive Regulation is the parent instrument from which licensing conditions, capital thresholds and activity definitions derive.
Licensing requirements and minimum paid-up capital are interdependent — capital is an eligibility condition for the licence and is calibrated to the activities applied for.
Micro finance / micro consumer finance is a scoped-out activity class with its own capital and conduct treatment, so activity classification drives the applicable threshold.
Downstream relevance: licensed activity scope determines which consumer protection, BNPL and AML obligations attach to the entity.
start_here: Executive Regulation for Finance Companies Control Law

data.theme: Licensing and permissibility of debt collection as a finance support activity, and the conditions under which finance companies may outsource collection to third parties. Covers the shift from a standalone licensing requirement to reliance on the finance support activity regime.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Finance Companies Control Law's Implementing Regulation is the parent instrument from which the Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities and the collection circulars derive authority.

The Licensing Rules and their amendment share the same defined scope of 'finance support activities', with the amendment altering entry conditions; the cancelling circular removes a licensing prerequisite, so effective dates determine which text governs a given collection arrangement.

Outsourcing circular chains obligation back to the licensor: a finance company remains accountable for the conduct of the collection entity it engages, linking licensing status of 'Finance Debt Collection Entities' to the outsourcing permission.
Consumer-protection and conduct consequences flow through: who may contact a debtor depends on whether the collector is licensed, contracted, or acting for the finance company.
start_here: Implementing Regulation of Finance Companies Control Law
Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities
Circular Cancelling Debt Collection Licensing Requirement

data.theme: Affordability and creditworthiness limits on individual lending, including caps on financing amounts and restrictions on security instruments taken from consumers.
how_members_connect: The Responsible Lending Principles for Individuals is the anchor standard; both circulars operate as amendments or clarifications layered onto it.
Shared defined terms — 'individual', financing cap, debt burden ratio — mean a change in one circular re-scopes the base principles rather than creating a separate regime.
The BNPL cap circular creates a cross-regime touchpoint: BNPL 'Consumer' treatment must be reconciled with the individual-borrower affordability tests in the base principles.
The promissory note circular constrains a creditor's remedy, so it interacts with collection and enforcement practice downstream.
start_here: Circular Raising BNPL Individual Financing Cap

data.theme: The AML/CTF/PF statutory core and its preventive-measure obligations for financial institutions, DNFBPs and NPOs, including beneficial ownership identification, business-level risk assessment, and the governance and supervisory architecture supporting them.
how_members_connect: Law-to-guidance chain: the AML Law and the Combating Terrorism and Financing of Terrorism Law set the offences and preventive duties; the Preventive Measures provisions specify CDD, record-keeping and reporting; the ML/TF/PF Business Risk Assessment Guide operationalises the risk-based approach.

Institutional linkage: the Financial Intelligence unit receives STRs, Supervisory Authority Powers grant SAMA inspection and sanctioning authority, and confiscation provisions supply the asset-recovery consequence.

Beneficial ownership is the shared defined concept binding the Wathiq verification-service circulars and the NPO inquiry service to the CDD duty in the AML Law — verification source, not substitution for the obligation.
SAMA Law (M/36) is the enabling authority for the circulars; governance principles and the compliance circular connect AML accountability to board and senior management responsibility.
Note scope drift: pricing-disclosure rules and pre-investment notification sit here via the SAMA Law authority link, not via AML substance.

data.theme: Authorisation, oversight and supervision of payment systems, system operators and payment service providers in KSA, benchmarked against international financial market infrastructure standards.
how_members_connect: Statutory base: the Law of Payments and Payment Services (M/21) confers SAMA's designation, licensing and oversight powers; the Oversight and Supervisory Frameworks are the implementing instruments.
Both frameworks incorporate the CPMI-IOSCO PFMIs and the CPSS-IOSCO Disclosure Framework as the substantive benchmark, so PFMI principles become effective expectations for designated systems.
Oversight (systemic, system-level) and supervision (entity-level conduct and prudential) are distinct but overlapping regimes — the same operator may sit under both.
The PSP licensing guidelines translate the Law's authorisation requirement into application criteria, determining when an entity is a licensed PSP versus an operator of a designated system.
start_here: Law of Payments and Payment Services (M/21)
Oversight Framework for Payment Systems and Operators
Guidelines to Apply for Payment Service Providers License

data.theme: Licensing and conduct of finance companies, real estate finance and refinance entities, including BNPL, digital brokerage, outsourcing and advertising. Covers who may carry on financing activity, on what prudential and consumer terms, and how retail credit must be granted responsibly.
how_members_connect: Two primary laws (Finance Companies Control Law M/51 and Real Estate Finance Law M/50) sit at the top of the hierarchy; the rules, instructions and controls below are subordinate instruments issued under them.

Responsible Retail Financing Principles act as a cross-cutting conduct layer that the BNPL Rules expressly pull in, creating a chained obligation for affordability and disclosure on top of licensing requirements.
Outsourcing Rules for finance companies are referenced by both the BNPL Rules and the Real Estate Refinancing Rules, so delegated functions stay under the licensee's residual accountability.
Note the defined-term interaction: BNPL uses 'Consumer' while AML/CTF obligations attach to 'Customer' — scope and CDD triggers must be reconciled rather than assumed identical.
start_here: Rules for Regulating Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) Companies

data.theme: Operational currency-handling standards for banks and cash handlers: fitness sorting, authentication and recirculation criteria for the sixth issue of Saudi banknotes.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster; a standalone technical instruction with no internal cross-references in the graph.
Relevance is operational compliance (cash handling and currency integrity) rather than prudential or conduct regulation.
start_here: Technical Sorting Instructions for 6th Issue Saudi Banknotes

data.theme: Debt collection and repayment instruments used by financiers — the issuance and enforcement of promissory notes and the use of standing payment orders against borrower accounts.
how_members_connect: Both instruments govern how a financier secures and collects instalments, so they share the same consumer-protection concern about coercive or excessive collection mechanics.
Linked conceptually rather than by citation: each constrains a distinct collection tool, and a financier's practice must satisfy both where the two are used together.
Both operate downstream of finance company licensing and responsible lending obligations, and interact with consumer disclosure duties at contract formation.
start_here: Instructions for Financiers Dealing with Promissory Notes
Standing Payment Order for Financier Controls

data.theme: Consumer protection obligations to make financial products, branches and channels accessible to persons with disabilities.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster; a standalone conduct requirement directed at supervised financial institutions.
Sits within the consumer protection regime and overlays other channel and disclosure obligations rather than replacing them.
start_here: Services for Persons with Disabilities in Financial Institutions

data.theme: Licensing and conduct of payment services in KSA: who may provide payment, e-money, payment initiation and account information services, how protected funds must be safeguarded, and how payment systems and PSPs must treat consumers (advertising, complaints, conflicts of interest).
how_members_connect: Hierarchy runs from statute to instrument: the Saudi Central Bank Law and the Law of Payments and Payment Services confer SAMA's authority, and the Payment Services Regulation operationalises it for licensed entities.

Shared defined actors — Payment Service Provider, Electronic Money Company, Payment System Operator, Agent/E-Money Distributor — carry the obligations across the Regulation and the consumer-facing rules.
Prudential/infrastructure limb: designation of Systemically Important Payment Systems is anchored to the international Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures.

Conduct limb: Financial Consumer Protection Principles, advertising rules and complaints/disputes handling apply to PSPs alongside the Regulation, creating a payments/consumer-protection cross-regime overlay for the same customer relationship.
start_here: Law of Payments and Payment Services
Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules

data.theme: Sector-wide expectations for cyber threat intelligence: how supervised financial entities must produce, classify, share and act on strategic, operational and technical/tactical CTI, and how that intelligence feeds threat-led testing.
how_members_connect: The Financial Sector CTI Principles act as the parent instrument, with the Core, Strategic, Operational and Technical/Tactical principle sets as its subordinate layers.
CTI obligations cross-refer to the Cyber Security Framework (baseline controls) and to the Ethical Red Teaming (FEER) Framework, where intelligence drives scenario design.
Common technical vocabulary is imported from external standards — MITRE ATT&CK, Kill Chain, Traffic Light Protocol — which govern how findings are described and how sharing restrictions are applied.
Physical-security specifications (CCTV) sit adjacent as a conceptually related control expectation for the same regulated population.
start_here: Financial Sector Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles
Financial Entities Ethical Red Teaming Framework

data.theme: A mixed prudential/Shariah/financial-crime cluster: Basel-derived capital, large exposure, margin and liquidity requirements for banks, alongside Shariah governance for finance companies and Islamic banks, and the AML/CTF compliance and suspicious-transaction reporting chain.
how_members_connect: Prudential spine: Large Exposure Rules, margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives and the LCR/NSFR guidance all cite the Basel/BCBS-IOSCO source frameworks and share definitional building blocks (exposure value, connected counterparties, eligible collateral, HQLA tiers).

Shariah limb: Shariah Governance Instructions, the Shari'ah Committee and Profit Sharing Investment Account rules (Mudarabah, PER/IRR reserves) connect to prudential text through Shari'ah-compliant bank treatments in the liquidity framework.
AML/CTF limb: transaction monitoring feeds suspicious transaction reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit, with the AML/CTF Compliance Function as the accountable owner.
Senior Management and board-level committees (ALCO, Shari'ah Committee, compliance function) are the shared governance nodes tying the three limbs to one accountable body.
start_here: SAMA General Guidance Concerning Amended LCR
Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies

data.theme: Governance and control expectations for technology, cyber security and operational resilience in supervised entities — board/committee accountability, maturity-based assessment, IT and cyber risk management, third-party risk and business continuity.
how_members_connect: Two parallel SAMA frameworks (IT Governance and Cyber Security) share the same architecture: domains plus a maturity model against which entities are assessed and report to SAMA.
Accountability chain is defined by role and forum — Board/IT Steering Committee, CIO, Cyber Security Committee, CISO — with internal IT audit as independent assurance.
Both frameworks cross-refer to the Business Continuity Management Framework and its minimum requirements, linking control failure to resilience obligations.

External standards (NIST, PCI-DSS, SWIFT CSCF) are cited as baselines incorporated into SAMA's control expectations, and supervision is channelled through the General Department of Cyber Risk Control.
start_here: SAMA Information Technology Governance Framework v1.0

data.theme: Prudential liquidity and funding requirements for finance companies, especially deposit-taking finance companies, together with the governance and capital scaffolding that makes those requirements enforceable.
how_members_connect: The Deposit Taking Finance Companies Regulations sit at the top of the hierarchy and pull in capital, liquidity and governance requirements as licensing/ongoing conditions.

The liquidity risk management rules operationalise the headline liquidity requirement through named components: governance of liquidity risk, stress testing/scenario analysis and a contingency funding plan.
Stress testing and the contingency funding plan are legally paired - scenario outcomes are the trigger and calibration basis for the funding plan.
Corporate governance and risk management obligations allocate board/senior management accountability for the liquidity limits and appetite, linking prudential ratios to individual responsibility.

data.theme: Bank-level liquidity adequacy and funding-concentration supervision: the internal liquidity adequacy assessment process, Basel-style ratios, and related-party/large-exposure limits that constrain the funding and asset side.
how_members_connect: The Central Bank Law is the enabling authority cited by the subordinate rules (loans-to-deposits guidelines, related-parties rules), giving the law -> rules -> guidelines chain.
The ILAAP guidelines act as the integrating instrument, cross-referencing LCR/NSFR, liquidity stress-testing and the contingency funding plan as required inputs to the bank's own adequacy assessment.
HQLA is the shared defined term linking the ratio regime to the contingency funding plan's usable liquidity buffer.

Related-party and large-exposure rules connect prudentially: concentration limits shape the deposit/funding base measured by LDR and the ratios; IFSB standards are referenced for Islamic-window treatment.
start_here: SAMA Rules on Large Exposures of Banks

data.theme: Classification, provisioning and workout of credit exposures - how exposures are staged and defaulted, how expected credit losses are measured, and the mandatory treatment of problem assets, forbearance and restructuring.
how_members_connect: Two anchor instruments dominate: the credit risk classification and provisioning rules (staging, default definition, ECL) and the problem-loan management rules (early warning, watch list, workout, restructuring); each cites the other.
IFRS 9 is the shared accounting reference that gives content to staging, ECL and NPV testing, while SAMA rules impose supervisory floors and definitions on top of it.
The default and forbearance definitions are the pivot between regimes - they determine stage migration, NPL designation, cure and re-default outcomes.
BCBS 403 supplies the international prudential taxonomy for non-performing and forborne exposures that the SAMA problem-loan rules localise.

Workout mechanics (viability assessment, term sheet, restructuring agreement, KPIs, cure rate, collateral and LTV) form an obligation chain running from early warning detection to monitoring of the executed plan.
start_here: Rules Governing Credit Risk Exposure Classification and Provisioning
Rules on Management of Problem Loans

data.theme: Consumer finance conduct rules: cost-of-credit disclosure via APR, standardised contract terms, and the transfer/buyout of individual consumer debts between finance companies including clearance-letter timeframes.
how_members_connect: The debt-purchase (buyout) instructions and the clearance-letter timeframe instructions form a sequenced obligation chain - transfer of the debt triggers deadlines for issuing the clearance letter and moving the account.
APR is the shared defined term: the calculation rules fix the method, and the standard consumer finance contract requires its disclosure, so buyout pricing comparisons rest on the same measure.

The SAMA standard contract is the consumer-facing instrument carrying early repayment, default and late-payment notice terms, with the finance lease executive bond circular as a related enforcement mechanism.
Credit information company reporting links the conduct regime to the credit-information regime - status changes on buyout, clearance and default must be reflected in the consumer's record.
start_here: Rules Governing Calculation of Annual Percentage Rate (APR)
Instructions for Purchasing Individual Consumer Finance Debts Between Finance Companies

data.theme: Account-opening rules for government entities — the conditions under which banks may open and operate accounts for ministries, agencies and other public bodies, and the approvals that gate them.
how_members_connect: The account-opening rules are the governing instrument; the Ministry of Finance appears as the authorising/confirming party whose consent or instruction underpins a government account request.

SAMA approval and notification operates as a procedural condition layered on top of the substantive rules — the bank's ability to act depends on obtaining or filing with SAMA, not merely on customer documentation.

Cross-regime note: government-entity onboarding still sits within the AML/CTF customer due diligence regime (legal-person identification, authorised signatories, beneficial-ownership treatment), so these rules qualify rather than displace standard KYC obligations.
start_here: Rules for Opening Accounts for Government Entities (500)

data.theme: Periodic prudential and risk reporting by debt-based crowdfunding platforms to SAMA, covering portfolio exposure, arrears and operational risk on a quarterly cycle.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: the obligation is a standalone supervisory reporting duty imposed on licensed debt crowdfunding entities.
It functions as the ongoing-supervision limb of the crowdfunding licensing regime — breach is a licence-condition and enforcement matter, not merely an administrative lapse.
Reporting content typically interacts with governance/risk-management expectations, so the report is evidence of the board- and management-level controls required elsewhere.
start_here: SAMA Quarterly Risk Report Requirements for Debt Crowdfunding Entities

data.theme: Statutory reserve requirements applied to money exchange centres — a prudential capital/liquidity buffer condition attached to the exchange licence.
how_members_connect: Standalone prudential obligation directed at licensed exchange businesses rather than banks; scope is limited to the exchange regime.
Sits alongside, and is distinct from, the AML/CTF obligations that dominate the exchange sector — reserve compliance is a solvency/licence matter, not a financial-crime one.
Non-compliance bears on continued licensing and supervisory action by SAMA.
start_here: SAMA Statutory Reserve for Money Exchange Centers

data.theme: Consumer-protection controls on the use of external (outsourced) debt collection service providers when pursuing individual customers, including permitted contact practices and the creditor's retained responsibility.
how_members_connect: Standalone conduct instrument that constrains outsourcing: the finance provider or bank remains accountable for the third party's conduct toward the Consumer.
Cross-regime interaction with consumer protection principles (fair treatment, privacy of debt information, complaint handling) and with outsourcing/governance expectations on third-party oversight.
Relevant to BNPL and finance-company portfolios where the counterparty is a 'Consumer' with protective rights distinct from the AML notion of 'Customer'.
start_here: SAMA Collection Controls for Individual Customers via External Service Providers

data.theme: Asset-based finance regimes in KSA — finance leasing and real estate finance/refinance — including contract registration, enforceability of executive bonds, standardised contracts and responsible lending, with an attached AML/CTF customer due diligence layer applying to the licensed entities involved.
how_members_connect: Classic hierarchy: the Finance Lease Law and Real Estate Finance Law (royal decrees) are elaborated by their Implementing Regulations, then operationalised by SAMA rules and circulars (contracts register procedures, executive bond extracts, standard real estate financing contracts).

Registration chain: the Contracts Register is the pivot — registration rules create the record, and the executive bond extract rules convert a registered lease contract into an enforceable instrument, so both cite the Finance Lease Law.

Refinance/secondary-market branch: Rules Governing Real Estate Refinance Companies and the Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company sit downstream of the Real Estate Finance Law, with governance and risk management obligations and Capital Market Law cross-references where securitisation touches the secondary market.

AML/CTF overlay: the AML Law and Terrorist Crimes implementing regulations, CDD/KYC measures, FATF standards and the FIU attach to the same licensed financiers and to remittance/SARIE channels — a distinct regime whose 'Customer' concept must be reconciled with the lessee/borrower under the finance laws.
Consumer-protection overlay: Responsible Lending Principles and the deductible-ratio limits constrain individual real estate and lease financing regardless of the contractual form.
start_here: Implementing Regulation of the Finance Lease Law

data.theme: Controls on reproducing images of Saudi currency (banknotes and coins) for advertising, media or other non-monetary use, protecting currency integrity and reducing counterfeiting risk.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument community: the reproduction rules stand alone as SAMA's issuing-authority measure over the national currency.
Obligation runs to any party reproducing currency imagery, with SAMA prior-approval and format conditions as the operative constraint.
start_here: Rules for Reproduction of Currency in Saudi Arabia

data.theme: Consumer-facing disclosure standards for ATM transaction receipts — what information must be presented to the customer at the point of cash withdrawal or other ATM services.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument community: a SAMA initiative imposing minimum receipt content and availability duties on card issuers/ATM operators.
Sits in the consumer protection and payments regime; consequence is a service-quality obligation testable against banks' ATM channel practice.

data.theme: Operational AML/CTF onboarding and identification duties — KYC, CDD and beneficial ownership verification — as applied across banks, exchange houses, deposit-taking finance companies, POS/merchant acquiring and cross-border cash movement.
how_members_connect: KYC and CDD function as the shared defined-term hub; each sectoral instrument (DTFC Regulations, Exchange Houses Operations Manual, non-resident property owner account rules, POS sale rules) attaches its own scope to those same measures.
Beneficial owner verification links entity-level onboarding to external registry sources (GAA data services), creating a verification-source question rather than a new obligation.

Exchange-sector chain: the Exchange Houses Operations Manual is the base manual, updated by the Exchange Companies Procedures circular, and carries CDD, correspondent banking and FATF-aligned requirements.

Cross-border cash reporting (including King Fahd Causeway movements and cash transport) sits alongside CDD as a separate declaration/reporting duty on carriers and transporters, not on account onboarding.
Merchant-as-customer point: KYC before POS sale/operation extends customer identification obligations to acquiring relationships (KYB), distinct from the retail customer relationship.
start_here: Benefiting from GAA Services for Verifying Beneficial Owner Data

data.theme: Supervisory direction requiring finance companies to revise their credit granting policies, affecting affordability/creditworthiness assessment and internal credit approval standards under the finance companies regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a SAMA directive that operates as a binding instruction layered on the Finance Companies Control Law and its implementing regulations.
Obligation runs to licensed finance companies' boards/senior management, who must reflect the update in approved internal credit policy.
Interacts with responsible-lending and consumer protection duties (debt burden ratio, disclosure) and with credit information use in underwriting.
start_here: SAMA Directive to Update Credit Granting Policies of Finance Companies

data.theme: SAMA's promotion of financial awareness and education programmes aimed at SMEs, sitting at the softer end of the consumer/customer protection and market-conduct spectrum.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an encouragement-style communication rather than a hard obligation, so compliance consequence is expectation-setting and supervisory dialogue.
Links conceptually to financial literacy and fair-treatment duties owed to business customers in the banking and finance company conduct rules.
Relevant when assessing whether SME-facing disclosure and onboarding practices meet SAMA conduct expectations.
start_here: SAMA Encouragement of Financial Awareness Programs for SMEs

data.theme: Clarification that a real estate financier's obligations continue in the secondary market context, i.e. after refinancing or transfer of mortgage assets.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a SAMA confirmation interpreting existing real estate finance obligations rather than creating new ones.
Obligation chain: Real Estate Finance Law and implementing regulations to the originating financier, with duties surviving securitisation/assignment of the financing portfolio.
Cross-regime relevance to consumer protection (continuity of borrower rights and servicing standards) after asset transfer.
start_here: SAMA Confirmation of Real Estate Financier Obligations in Secondary Market

data.theme: The AML/CTF risk-based framework applicable to SAMA-supervised institutions: assessing ML/TF risk and calibrating controls for higher-risk channels such as correspondent banking and wire transfers.
how_members_connect: The SAMA AML/CTF Guide is the hub, operationalising the Law on Combating Terrorism Crimes and Financing and aligning supervised entities with FATF standards.
Risk-Based Approach and ML/TF Risk Assessment form the core definitional pair: the enterprise-wide assessment drives the intensity of CDD, monitoring and enhanced measures.
Correspondence Relationship and Wire Transfer are named higher-risk activity types where the Guide layers specific due diligence and originator/beneficiary information duties.
Hierarchy to note: statute (terrorism financing law and the AML Law it sits beside) to implementing regulation to SAMA guide, with FATF as persuasive international benchmark, not domestic law.
start_here: Law on Combating Terrorism Crimes and Financing

data.theme: Licensing and conduct framework for money exchange (currency exchange and remittance) businesses in the Kingdom, covering permitted activities, operational controls and supervisory expectations for exchange houses.
how_members_connect: Single standalone instrument in this cluster: the guide operates as SAMA's consolidated rulebook for the exchange sector rather than as a node in a citation chain.
Sits downstream of the primary banking/exchange licensing statute and interacts with AML/CTF and remittance obligations applicable to money service providers.
Relevance is scope-driven: it determines when an entity is treated as an exchange business rather than a bank or PSP, and which regime's customer due diligence duties apply.
start_here: Guide for Organizing Exchange Business Operations

data.theme: Core prudential and institutional supervision of licensed banks — the enabling statute plus derived requirements on branch presence, financial inclusion, capital adequacy (including Shari'ah-compliant products), senior appointments and currency handling.
how_members_connect: The Banking Control Law is the parent statute; the branch network regulation, circulars on leadership appointments and damaged currency, and the Shari'ah capital adequacy requirements all cite it as their legal basis (law → regulation → circular).
Branch network obligations are linked to financial inclusion policy objectives, making geographic coverage a supervisory outcome rather than a purely commercial choice.
Capital adequacy add-ons for Shari'ah-compliant banking sit as an overlay on the SAMA Basel Framework, so the two must be read together when computing requirements.
Fit-and-proper style appointment controls tie governance obligations back to the licensing power under the statute.

data.theme: Circular-level instruction concerning real estate registration and its treatment by supervised financial institutions, relevant to collateral, title verification and real estate finance documentation.
how_members_connect: Standalone circular: binding supervisory instruction issued under SAMA's general authority over supervised entities.
Cross-regime relevance to real estate finance and mortgage collateral requirements, and to customer/property documentation held for onboarding and enforcement.

data.theme: The bank account lifecycle regime: who may open an account, what evidence and due diligence is required by customer type, and how accounts are operated, frozen, made dormant, disclosed or enforced against. This is the principal intersection of consumer/account-opening rules with AML/CTF customer due diligence.
how_members_connect: The Rules for Bank Accounts is the hub instrument; the natural-person (200), juristic-person (300), foreign-investor (400) and operations (Chapter IV) parts are subordinate chapters that all reference back to it, with sub-rules (expatriates, Hajj/Umrah entities, NPOs, multilateral organisations, liquidation/restructuring, non-residents) nested beneath the juristic-person rules.

KYC and AML/CTF requirements are incorporated into the account-opening rules, so the account-type documentation lists function as the operational expression of CDD obligations — the 'account holder' under these rules must also be assessed as the 'customer' under the AML regime.

Statutory cross-references define eligibility and restrictions: the Companies Law and Foreign Investment Law govern juristic-person capacity and foreign investor scope; the Bankruptcy Law drives the liquidation/restructuring account category; the Law of Terrorism Crimes and Financing underpins freezing and non-dealing duties.

Supervisory/administrative bodies act as documentary gatekeepers — licences and registrations issued by the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah, HRSD, the General Authority for Awqaf and the MOI ten-digit number are conditions precedent to opening specified account types.

Freezing, dormancy/unclaimed balances, disclosure and enforcement obligations form a downstream chain applying once the account is live, with the electronic record system as the shared evidentiary layer.
start_here: Rules for Opening Accounts for Juristic Persons (300)

data.theme: Identification and differentiated prudential treatment of institutions whose failure would threaten financial stability, split between the global designation regime (G-SIBs) and SAMA's domestic designation (D-SIBs).
how_members_connect: All three labels share a single underlying concept — systemic importance — with SIFI as the umbrella term and G-SIB/D-SIB as the two designation tracks.
The linkage is definitional and hierarchical: Basel-derived global criteria feed the domestic assessment methodology SAMA applies to locally licensed banks.

Designation is the trigger condition for add-on obligations (higher loss absorbency, enhanced supervision, recovery/resolution planning), so the terms operate as scope gates rather than free-standing duties.
Cross-regime relevance: designation status also conditions governance, risk and capital expectations applied to the same entity.

data.theme: Measurement of exposure value for trading book positions under the capital framework, including the look-through treatment of positions held through funds and structured vehicles.
how_members_connect: Direct cross-reference: the trading book exposure-value rules point to the CIU/structures provisions for how to value indirect exposures.
Shared calculation chain — exposure value feeds capital requirement, so the fund treatment is a carve-out/specification within the general method.
Both are technical definitional provisions in the prudential (capital/large exposures) regime rather than conduct rules.
start_here: Exposure Value for Trading Book Positions

data.theme: The instant payments infrastructure operated within the SARIE environment — rules governing participation, clearing and settlement of real-time transfers.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the system operates as a defined payment infrastructure to which participation, operational and settlement obligations attach.
Cross-regime relevance: payments/PSP licensing, consumer protection for transfer errors, and AML/CTF transaction monitoring all reference activity conducted through it.

data.theme: Consumer protection governance inside financial institutions: the mandatory establishment, structure and staffing of a customer care function covering complaints, quality analysis and financial awareness.
how_members_connect: The establishment controls act as the parent obligation and cross-refer to each mandated sub-unit, creating a structural hierarchy.
Complaint Handling, Quality and Performance Analysis, and Financial Awareness units are the prescribed components — each carries its own functional mandate under the same instrument.
Professional certification requirements attach to staff of the complaint-handling function, linking fitness/competence duties to the consumer protection regime.
Consequence chain: failure to constitute the units or certify staff is a supervisory breach independent of any individual complaint outcome.

data.theme: Recognition of government-issued digital identity and digital attestation channels (Absher, Tawakkalna) as acceptable proof of identity, family status and contract certification by supervised finance entities. Sits at the intersection of customer identification/KYC evidence rules and consumer-facing contracting formalities.
how_members_connect: All three items address what counts as an acceptable identification or certification instrument, extending the traditional national ID/paper-document baseline to state digital platforms.
