The family record and digital identity circulars are directly cross-referenced, the former building on the identity-acceptance position for a specific document type.

Digital certification of finance company products relies on the same acceptance premise: if the digital identity is valid for verification, it can underpin electronic execution and attestation of product documentation.
Practical consequence spans regimes: CDD/identification evidence under AML/CTF, and documentation/disclosure duties toward the Consumer in finance company dealings.
start_here: Acceptance of Digital Identity from Absher and Tawakkalna
Acceptance of Family Record from Absher and Tawakkalna

data.theme: Treatment of a VAT rate increase as it flows through cooperative insurance premiums attached to lease finance products, and who bears the incremental cost.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an isolated tax-pass-through instruction affecting pricing and cost allocation in lease contracts.
Connects conceptually to consumer protection and contract-amendment principles, since repricing an existing lease-linked insurance charge touches disclosed cost terms.
start_here: VAT Increase on Cooperative Insurance for Leases

data.theme: Obligation on finance companies to keep public-facing channels (websites and social media) current and accurate, as an extension of disclosure and transparency duties toward consumers.
how_members_connect: Standalone conduct-of-business requirement; the legal hook is accurate disclosure of products, terms and licensing status to the public.
Interacts with consumer protection principles on misleading information and with licensing-status representation rules.
start_here: Updating Finance Company Websites and Social Media

data.theme: Requirements applicable to POS acquiring and payment services routed through the GCC-NET regional switch, covering participation, service handling and cardholder-facing conditions.
how_members_connect: Standalone payments-regime instrument; obligations attach to banks/PSPs operating POS acceptance rather than to consumers directly.
Links outward to the wider payment services and merchant acceptance framework, including merchant onboarding as a customer relationship for AML/KYB purposes.

data.theme: Baseline duty of supervised entities to observe SAMA circulars as binding supervisory instruments alongside laws, rules and regulations.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: the obligation is generic rather than regime-specific, so it attaches to whichever rulebook the circular amends or interprets.
Sits at the bottom of the instrument hierarchy (law -> implementing regulation -> rules -> circular), meaning circular content can tighten or supersede earlier guidance without a rule amendment.
Practical consequence: compliance mapping must track circular issuance dates and supersession, not only the consolidated rulebook.

data.theme: Protection of personal data held by financial institutions, and the interaction between KSA data protection duties and sector obligations such as CDD record-keeping, credit information sharing and outsourcing.
how_members_connect: Isolated node whose legal force derives from the national personal data protection regime as applied to SAMA-supervised entities.
Cross-regime tension point: AML/CTF retention and reporting duties, and credit information disclosure, operate as lawful bases or carve-outs against data subject rights.
Relevant wherever customer data is processed by third parties (reliance on third-party CDD, outsourcing, payment service providers).

data.theme: Adoption of and amendments to international accounting standards by supervised entities, and SAMA's supervisory expectations on financial reporting treatment.
how_members_connect: Standalone node: obligations flow from SAMA's endorsement of the standards rather than from a bespoke SAMA rulebook article.
Links outward to prudential and governance regimes through provisioning, capital and disclosure consequences.
Changes are typically communicated by circular, so effective dates and transition provisions determine the applicable reporting period.

data.theme: Minimum control requirements for remote (non-face-to-face) customer registration, identity verification and authentication in digital channels — the operational layer where e-KYC/CDD duties, payments and lending onboarding, and fraud controls meet.
how_members_connect: The Minimum Verification Controls document acts as the parent instrument: it references the onboarding controls, MFA, biometric verification and the lending-application special controls as constituent requirements.
Registration/onboarding controls in turn invoke OTP as an authentication factor, forming an obligation chain from customer registration to step-up authentication.
Hierarchy and supersession matter: the earlier e-wallet security controls are referenced but superseded, so the current baseline applies across channels rather than only to wallets.

Sector-specific overlays (lending applications) sit on top of the common baseline, so finance/BNPL providers must satisfy both the general and the special controls, alongside AML CDD identification duties.

data.theme: The core AML/CTF customer due diligence regime: identifying and verifying the Customer and Beneficial Owner, and calibrating the intensity of measures (simplified, standard, enhanced) to assessed ML/TF risk, including the PEP trigger.
how_members_connect: All members hang off the same defined term chain: Due Diligence Measures presupposes identification/verification of the Customer and the Beneficial Owner, so the Beneficial Owner definition governs the scope of every variant.
Enhanced and Simplified Due Diligence are risk-calibrated derogations from the baseline Due Diligence obligation, not free-standing regimes — they inherit its elements and vary only intensity/timing.
PEP status is a mandatory EDD trigger, linking status-based classification to the escalated obligation set (senior management approval, source of funds/wealth, ongoing monitoring).
Preventive Measures for FIs and DNFBPs is the umbrella obligation layer that imposes the CDD duties on the obliged-entity population, showing the law → implementing rules hierarchy.
start_here: Preventive Measures for FIs and DNFBPs

data.theme: The obligation on obliged entities to maintain an independent audit function that tests the adequacy and effectiveness of the AML/CTF compliance programme.
how_members_connect: Stands alone in the graph as one of the mandated internal control pillars, but is legally dependent on the preventive-measures programme it is required to test.
Its scope is defined by reference to the CDD, monitoring, reporting and training obligations it audits — findings feed governance and board-level accountability.

data.theme: The standing requirement to deliver ongoing AML/CTF training to staff (and, where relevant, agents and outsourced personnel) so that preventive obligations are actually executed.
how_members_connect: Isolated node whose content is derivative: training must cover the CDD, red-flag detection, suspicious transaction reporting and TFS duties imposed elsewhere.
Sits within the same internal-controls set as the compliance officer and independent audit obligations, and is a typical supervisory examination point.

data.theme: SAMA's Agent Banking Regulation: the conditions under which a bank may deliver banking services through third-party agents, covering agent eligibility, fit-and-proper vetting, agent-level due diligence, registration, and the permitted/prohibited activity perimeter.
how_members_connect: The Regulation is the parent instrument; the article-level nodes (Arts 9, 13, 14, 19, 20, 29) are its operative obligations and should be read as a single onboarding-to-oversight chain: eligibility → fit and proper → agent due diligence → registry notification → activity limits.

Two distinct diligence concepts intersect: Agent Due Diligence (bank assessing the agent, akin to KYB of a contracted party) versus Customer Due Diligence (AML/CTF obligations on the end customer performed at the agent channel) — the bank retains legal responsibility for the latter even when the agent executes it.
The Bank Board of Directors node anchors non-delegable governance accountability: outsourcing the activity does not outsource the obligation or supervisory liability.

Permissible and Prohibited Activities define the scope limit that constrains everything else, and cross-regime interaction with the AML/CTF preventive-measures regime arises wherever agents perform identification or transaction handling.

data.theme: Saudization/localization and job-restriction requirements applying to money exchange centers, including the prohibition on staff holding dual roles.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone supervisory instruction directed at licensed exchange businesses rather than part of a definitional chain.
Sits in the licensing/conduct-of-business regime for exchangers; consequence is staffing and role-segregation compliance, with implications for internal control and AML oversight duties.
start_here: No Dual Jobs at Exchange Centers / Localization

data.theme: SAMA's cyber resilience testing regime for supervised financial entities: intelligence-led ethical red teaming, the roles of the parties involved, and the mandated reporting and remediation outputs.
how_members_connect: The F.E.E.R. framework is the parent instrument; all team roles, methodologies and deliverables are defined terms drawn from it.

Role hierarchy: White Team commissions and controls the exercise, the Red Teaming Provider (with Threat Intelligence input) executes against the Cyber Kill Chain methodology, the Blue Team defends, and the Green Team supports.
Obligation chain in deliverables: the Red Team Evaluation Report and Blue Team Report feed the Remediation Plan, which is the entity's corrective-action commitment to the supervisor.
Scope boundary: red teaming is distinguished from ordinary Penetration Testing, so the two cannot be substituted for one another in demonstrating compliance.

data.theme: Conduct and contractual standards for real estate finance, covering standardised finance contract terms and the deadlines applicable to transferring real estate debt between financiers.
how_members_connect: Both are SAMA circulars issued under the real estate finance regime, sitting below the Real Estate Finance Law and its implementing regulation.
The debt-transfer timeframes circular cross-references the contracts circular, so the mandated contract terms and the refinancing/transfer deadlines must be read together.
Consumer protection effect: the pairing constrains financier discretion on documentation and on how quickly a customer can move financing.
start_here: Timeframes for Real Estate Debt Transfer Circular

data.theme: Standardised documentation and regulatory amendments for vehicle finance leasing, fixing mandatory lease contract content for finance companies dealing with lessees.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: amendments to the Finance Lease Implementing Regulation set the rule base, and the standard vehicle lease contract circular operationalises it as mandatory contract wording.
Shared defined terms (finance lease, lessor/lessee) mean the circular must be interpreted consistently with the amended regulation.
Consequence: deviations from the standard contract in vehicle leasing are a compliance exposure under the finance companies regime and consumer protection principles.
start_here: Amendments to Finance Lease Implementing Regulation

data.theme: Entry-level authorisation of banks in KSA: the substantive minimum criteria SAMA applies to licence a bank, plus the incremental conditions imposed on digital-only banking models.
how_members_connect: The general licensing guidelines set the baseline minimum criteria (ownership, capital, governance, fit-and-proper management, business plan) and anchor them to the Basel Core Principles as the supervisory benchmark.
The digital-only guidance is an overlay, not a substitute: it incorporates the general criteria by reference and adds conditions tied to the 'Digital-Only Bank' defined term.

Cross-regime linkage into technology risk: the digital-only overlay pulls the SAMA Cybersecurity Framework into the licensing assessment, so IT/cyber maturity becomes an authorisation gate, not only an ongoing supervisory expectation.
Hierarchy to keep straight: Basel principles (international benchmark) → SAMA licensing guidelines → digital-only supplement.
start_here: Licensing Guidelines and Minimum Criteria for Banks
Additional Licensing Guidelines for Digital-Only Banks

data.theme: Outsourcing and third-party risk governance for SAMA-supervised entities: when a delegated activity counts as material outsourcing, what board-approved policy and continuity controls attach, and how sector-specific rulebooks (finance companies, debt crowdfunding, foreign bank branches) inherit that regime.
how_members_connect: Shared defined terms drive scope: 'Material Functions' / 'Material Outsourcing' and 'Third-Party Service Provider' determine whether the heavier notification, due-diligence and contractual obligations are triggered.

Obligation chain: an approved Outsourcing Policy plus Business Continuity Management arrangements are conditions attached to permitted outsourcing, with responsibility for the outsourced function remaining with the licensee.

Parallel instruments for different populations — general Rules on Outsourcing, the finance-company version, and the foreign bank branch treatment — overlap in substance; identify which applies before citing an obligation.

Debt-based crowdfunding entities are linked in because their rulebook cross-refers to the finance-company outsourcing rules while carrying its own defined terms (Platform, Participant, Institutional Beneficiary) and prudential limits (Risk Management Framework, Credit Limits).
start_here: Rules on Outsourcing for Finance Companies

data.theme: Segregation and handling of funds in debt-based crowdfunding: use of pooled accounts to hold and manage financing value on behalf of participants and beneficiaries.
how_members_connect: The pooled-account instruction defines and operationalises the 'Financing Value Management Account' as the required vehicle for holding participant funds.
Core legal point is client-money segregation: platform funds must be kept distinct from participant financing value, with controls on permitted movements.
Connects outward to the debt-crowdfunding rulebook and to AML/CTF expectations, since pooled structures affect identification of the underlying beneficial holder of funds.
start_here: Pooled Accounts for Debt-Crowdfunding Financing Value Management

data.theme: Authorisation pathway for non-bank consumer credit providers — BNPL companies and consumer microfinance — covering application content, corporate and shareholder suitability, and the substantive rulebook the applicant commits to.
how_members_connect: Both licence routes share the fit-and-proper assessment instrument, applied to founders, controlling shareholders, board and senior management.
Hierarchy: the BNPL rulebook sets the substantive licensing conditions and ongoing obligations; the application guidelines and application pack are the procedural layer implementing them.

The microfinance and BNPL guidance are parallel finance-company licence tracks under the same finance-companies framework, so scope of activity (deferred payment vs. microfinance lending) determines which applies.
Downstream consequence: a licence obtained here brings the entity within consumer protection, AML/CTF and outsourcing obligations applicable to finance companies.
start_here: Guidelines for Applying for BNPL License
License Application Guidelines for Consumer Microfinance

data.theme: Conduct rules governing how exchange (money transfer) businesses receive and process inbound transfer instructions, including customer identification and record-keeping expectations at the receipt stage.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: the rules stand alone as the operative conduct standard for the receiving leg of a transfer.
Sits at the intersection of the money exchange/transfer regime and AML/CTF wire-transfer obligations (originator/beneficiary information and CDD on the receiving side).
Obligations attach to the licensed exchange entity, not the sending institution, so reliance on a correspondent's CDD must be assessed separately.
start_here: Rules for Receiving Money Transfers for Exchange

data.theme: Disclosure obligations requiring finance companies to publish financial statements, supporting supervisory transparency and market/consumer visibility of licensee financial condition.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster within the finance companies regime; the publication duty derives from the finance company licensing and supervision framework.
Interacts with governance and accounting/audit requirements — the content published is defined by the applicable accounting standards, while the publication trigger and timing are supervisory.

data.theme: Accessibility and safety obligations requiring supervised entities' premises and emergency procedures to accommodate persons with disabilities during evacuation.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster; the duty sits within consumer protection / fair treatment of customers with disabilities rather than prudential regulation.
Applies at branch and premises level, so the obligation runs to the licensed entity's operational and business-continuity arrangements.
start_here: Emergency Evacuation for Persons with Disabilities

data.theme: Supervisory reporting of interest/return rates on banks' assets and liabilities, and the reference standards used to classify and price those exposures.
how_members_connect: The reporting guidelines are the parent obligation; both other members are incorporated by reference as mandatory classification and pricing inputs.
ISIC4 fixes the economic-activity taxonomy used to segment reported balances, so counterparty classification errors propagate directly into reporting non-compliance.
SAIBOR is the referenced benchmark for rate reporting, linking this cluster to benchmark-integrity and pricing-transparency expectations.
Hierarchy is guideline-level instruction relying on external standards, not standalone rules — read the guidelines first to see the scope of incorporation.
start_here: Interest Rates on Assets and Liabilities Reporting Guidelines

data.theme: Minimum qualifying requirements and estimation mechanics for banks using the Internal Ratings-Based approach to credit risk capital: how rating systems must be built, how PD/LGD/EAD are estimated and validated, and how mitigants, collateral and purchased receivables feed the risk-weighted asset calculation.
how_members_connect: Anchored by the IRB minimum requirements node, which acts as the parent obligation set and cross-refers to rating system design, risk quantification, validation, disclosure and leasing recognition.

Shared defined terms drive the chain: the definitions of default and of loss condition PD, LGD and EAD estimation, which in turn feed the foundation vs advanced IRB treatments and the RWA computations for default and dilution risk.

Credit risk mitigation is a second obligation strand: guarantees, credit derivatives and eligible collateral (real estate, financial receivables, other physical, leasing) adjust either PD or LGD rather than the exposure class.

Supervisory fallbacks (supervisory LGD/EAD estimates, slotting for object finance) and transition arrangements sit as alternatives where a bank cannot meet own-estimate requirements — relevant to scope and approval decisions.

data.theme: Classification of banking book exposures into IRB asset classes — sovereign, bank, corporate, retail and equity — which determines the applicable risk weight function and capital treatment.
how_members_connect: The categorization node is the gateway obligation: every exposure must be assigned to a defined class before any risk weight function applies.
Each class node supplies the operative definition (sovereign, bank, corporate, retail), with sub-classes such as QRRE and the MSME firm-size adjustment refining the treatment within a class.

Equity and subordinated debt form a boundary problem: the equity definition, speculative unlisted equity and materiality thresholds for commercial holdings determine when an instrument leaves the corporate class.
Classification outcomes feed directly into the IRB risk weight functions and, downstream, into the parameter estimation requirements of the IRB minimum-requirements cluster.
start_here: Categorization of Exposures into Asset Classes

data.theme: Governance of the frequency and triggers for refreshing obligor and facility ratings so that internal ratings remain current.
how_members_connect: Stands alone in the graph but is functionally a rating system design obligation, supporting the use test and the integrity of PD estimates.
Timeliness of refresh is a precondition for relying on internal ratings in capital calculation and credit decisioning.

data.theme: Controls over human override of model-generated ratings, including the circumstances permitting an override and the documentation and monitoring expected.
how_members_connect: Isolated node but legally dependent on the rating system design and use-of-statistical-models requirements, which permit judgemental adjustment only under defined controls.
Override frequency and outcomes are an input to validation of internal estimates and to supervisory assessment of model reliance.

data.theme: Record-keeping and data retention obligations attached to risk measurement and rating systems — what data must be collected, maintained and made available to supervisors and validators over time.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: the data maintenance duty stands as a standalone compliance obligation rather than part of a cross-referenced chain.
Functionally dependent on upstream regimes (rating/model governance, capital calculation) because retained data is the evidentiary basis for demonstrating compliance.
Interacts with AML/CTF and credit information retention rules where the same records serve multiple regulatory purposes; retention periods should be reconciled to the longest applicable requirement.

data.theme: Supervisory expectation that institutions run stress testing to assess capital adequacy under adverse conditions, as a condition of using advanced/internal capital approaches.
how_members_connect: Standalone obligation node: the stress-testing duty is expressed as a self-contained supervisory requirement.
Legally downstream of capital adequacy rules — stress test outcomes feed the assessment of whether held capital remains sufficient.
Consequential link to governance: results are ordinarily an input to board and senior management oversight and to supervisory dialogue.

data.theme: Governance, control and assurance architecture around credit risk measurement: who owns oversight, who independently controls the rating/credit risk function, and who provides independent review.
how_members_connect: The credit risk control unit provision cross-refers to the corporate governance and oversight requirements, making independence of the control function an element of board-level accountability.
Internal and external audit provisions in turn reference the control unit, creating a three-layer assurance chain (board oversight → independent control function → independent audit review).
Shared subject matter: all three allocate roles and responsibilities over the same credit risk rating and measurement processes, so a gap in one layer undermines reliance on the others.
Hierarchically, these are supervisory requirements that condition permission to use internal approaches; failure is a governance breach, not merely a methodological one.

data.theme: Transitional treatment for equity exposures — time-limited phase-in arrangements that defer or modify the full capital treatment of equity holdings.
how_members_connect: Standalone transitional provision: it operates as a carve-out qualifying the general capital treatment of equity exposures.
Time-bound by nature — its effect depends on the transition window, so scope and expiry must be checked before relying on it.
Cross-regime consequence: relief here affects capital adequacy outcomes and therefore feeds stress testing and supervisory capital assessment.

data.theme: Prudential conditions on banks' investment activity — what banks may invest in, the internal governance that must sit behind investment decisions, and the ongoing risk oversight and prior-approval gates SAMA imposes.
how_members_connect: The Banks Investment Rules act as the parent instrument; the governance, risk-monitoring and approval members are its component obligation sets rather than free-standing instruments.
Obligation chain: board/committee governance duties feed the investment approval controls, which in turn trigger continuing measurement, limit-monitoring and reporting duties.

Approval requirements operate as scope gates — certain investment categories or thresholds cannot be entered without SAMA or internal senior authorisation, so the approval node conditions the other two.
Shared subject matter (the bank as licensed entity and its permitted investment exposures) keeps definitions consistent across all members.

data.theme: Licensing and conduct regime for money changers in KSA, spanning market entry, AML/CTF duties and customer-facing protections for a sector treated as higher-risk for financial crime.
how_members_connect: The Rules Regulating Money Changing Business is the governing instrument; licensing, AML/CTF and customer protection are its obligation streams.

Cross-regime interaction: AML/CTF duties here layer on the national AML Law and its Implementing Regulation, so the sector rules supplement rather than replace CDD, record-keeping and STR obligations.
Licensing conditions are continuing conditions — AML/CTF and consumer-protection breaches feed back into licence suspension or withdrawal.
The AML term 'Customer' and the consumer-protection addressee overlap but are not identical; walk-in exchange transactions raise occasional-customer and threshold questions.

data.theme: Basel III structural liquidity regime as adopted by SAMA: the Net Stable Funding Ratio, its funding-side and asset-side components, and the associated disclosure obligation.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy runs from the BCBS October 2014 NSFR standard to SAMA's adopting/guidance document, then to the operative ratio and its defined inputs.
ASF and RSF are the defined numerator and denominator of the NSFR; their factor assignments determine compliance with the ratio.
The NSFR disclosure template is the reporting limb — it consumes the same ASF/RSF categorisations, so definitional choices flow straight into published figures.
LCR is the short-horizon companion metric; several asset and funding classifications are defined by reference across the two ratios.

data.theme: Identification of domestic systemically important banks in Saudi Arabia and the additional capital burden imposed on them, adapting the Basel Committee's systemic-importance framework to the local market.
how_members_connect: SAMA's D-SIB framework is the operative instrument; it cites the BCBS G-SIB methodology as the source standard it localises.
The assessment methodology determines designation and bucketing, which is the legal trigger for the Higher Loss Absorbency surcharge.
HLA sits on top of minimum capital and buffer requirements, so designation has consequential effects across the wider capital adequacy regime.
Designation is periodic and status-based — a researcher must check both the methodology's indicators and the timing/phase-in provisions.

data.theme: Capital-adequacy rules for measuring counterparty credit risk exposure and the recognition of collateral and maturity effects in that measurement. It sits at the junction of the CCR framework, the IRB risk parameters and the market risk framework.
how_members_connect: Shared quantitative building block: exposure at default is the common measure the CCR framework, IRB parameters and add-on rules all feed into or draw from.
Credit risk mitigation chain: the simple approach for collateral and the maturity-mismatch treatment condition how much protection may be recognised against a CCR exposure.
Cross-framework boundary: IRB risk components and the market risk framework are cross-referenced to allocate trading-book versus banking-book treatment of the same counterparty positions.
Hierarchy: the CCR framework is the governing rule set; add-on and collateral provisions are subordinate computational specifications.
start_here: IRB Risk Components (PD, LGD, EAD, M)

data.theme: The standardised approach to counterparty credit risk (SA-CCR) as applied to OTC derivative and margined exposures, including how replacement cost, collateral and margin are recognised. Practically, it determines the exposure amount a bank must hold capital against for derivatives.
how_members_connect: Single governing method: SA-CCR is the parent rule and every other member either defines an input to it or illustrates its application.
Definitional chain: replacement cost depends on the net independent collateral amount and on the treatment of cash variation margin, so those definitions are load-bearing for the calculation.
Worked examples (sample portfolios, standard margin agreements) are interpretive aids subordinate to the operative SA-CCR provisions, not independent obligations.
Scope carve-outs: written credit derivatives and general derivative-exposure treatment set the perimeter of what SA-CCR captures.

data.theme: IRB credit risk parameter estimation, credit risk mitigation via guarantees and credit derivatives, and the corresponding Pillar 3 disclosure templates. It covers both how a bank computes IRB inputs and how it must publicly evidence them.
how_members_connect: Parameter definitions (PD, LGD, effective maturity) are the shared vocabulary used by the expected-loss/provisioning rules, the guarantee and collateral provisions and the disclosure templates.

Mitigation chain: recognition of guarantees, sovereign counter-guarantees and credit derivatives under IRB is expressly tied back to the standardised approach CRM eligibility and operational requirements.
F-IRB collateral rules operate as supervisory overrides of own-estimated LGD, linking the parameter layer to the mitigation layer.
Disclosure templates (CR6, CR9, CCR4) are downstream reporting obligations whose line items are defined by the upstream IRB parameter rules; CR9 backtesting evidences the PD estimates.

data.theme: The scope and architecture of the internal ratings-based approach in KSA: which exposures fall into which asset class, which IRB variant applies, and on what timetable a bank may adopt IRB. Asset-class classification is the gateway decision that drives all downstream risk weighting.
how_members_connect: Taxonomy hierarchy: the overview provision defines asset classes, which then branch into corporate, specialised lending sub-classes, retail and qualifying revolving retail definitions.
Approach selection: the foundation versus advanced distinction determines whether a bank supplies own estimates or uses supervisory values for a given asset class.
Fallback route: supervisory slotting, with its criteria tables, applies where a bank cannot estimate parameters for specialised lending.
Implementation layer: the SAMA Basel III guidance and the phased rollout provisions are the national adoption instruments conditioning use of the framework, and are cited by the substantive rules.
start_here: IRB Approach: Overview and Asset Class Definitions
Adoption and Phased Rollout of IRB

data.theme: The umbrella capital-adequacy regime SAMA applies to banks under Basel II/III: scope of application, minimum credit risk capital, and the specialist add-ons for counterparty credit risk and CVA. It sets which entities are consolidated and which calculation approach (standardised vs IRB) a bank may use.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Basel III Framework and SAMA's implementing circular (BCS290) sit above the topic-level chapters, which cite them as the source of the obligation to hold minimum capital.
The minimum credit risk chapter acts as the hub, cross-referencing the IRB approach, credit risk mitigation and securitization as alternative or modifying treatments of the same exposure.
CCR and CVA form an obligation chain off the credit risk base: derivative and SFT exposures are measured under CCR rules, then attract a separate CVA capital charge.
Purchased receivables under IRB link back into the securitization framework, showing where an exposure changes regime depending on structure.
start_here: Guidance Note on Scope of Application of Basel Framework
Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk

data.theme: Regulatory capital treatment of securitization and resecuritization exposures: when risk transfer is recognised, how exposures are ranked into calculation approaches, and the preferential STC regime. Also covers the external-rating infrastructure and conduit/SPE structures that the treatment depends on.
how_members_connect: Defined terms drive the whole cluster: traditional vs synthetic securitization, resecuritization, SPE, ABCP conduit and sponsor determine whether the securitization framework applies at all.

Gateway obligations chain into calculation: operational requirements for risk transference and due diligence must be met before a bank may use the hierarchy of approaches (SEC-IRBA, SEC-ERBA, SEC-IAA, SEC-SA).
Parameters are shared across approaches - KIRB, supervisory parameter p, attachment/detachment points, caps and dilution risk - so a change in one input flows through several treatments.
Eligibility of ECAIs and inferred-rating rules condition the ratings-based approaches; STC criteria (term and short-term ABCP) act as a qualifying overlay for reduced charges.
SAMA circulars (Basel III implementation; SRC residential mortgage portfolio purchases) localise the Basel text to KSA, including the KSA capital charge.
start_here: Operational Requirements for Recognition of Risk Transference

data.theme: Standardised-approach exposure classification and the permitted use of external credit ratings: which ECAI ratings may be relied on, and how corporate, retail, specialised lending and real estate exposures are bucketed for risk weighting.
how_members_connect: Ratings-usage rules (eligibility, mapping, multiple ratings, issue vs issuer, short vs long term) are the shared gateway conditions for every rated exposure class in the cluster.
Independent due diligence is an express obligation that overlays external ratings - a bank may not mechanically adopt an ECAI grade.
Exposure-class definitions nest: specialised lending subdivides into project, object, commodities, IPRE and HVCRE; real estate subdivides into regulatory residential/commercial, other and land ADC.
Modifiers apply across classes: loan-to-value, whole-loan vs loan-splitting, material dependence on cash flows, transactor status and the currency-mismatch multiplier all change the resulting weight.
Supervisory slotting and expected-loss treatment link this standardised classification back to IRB-style outcomes for specialised lending.
start_here: Use of External Ratings and ECAIs

data.theme: Recognition of credit risk mitigation under the standardised approach: when collateral, netting, guarantees and credit derivatives may reduce a capital requirement, and by how much.
how_members_connect: A single framework node governs the eligibility conditions, then branches into the three mitigation channels - collateralised transactions, on-balance-sheet netting, and guarantees/credit derivatives.
Collateral treatment forks into the simple and comprehensive approaches, both dependent on the shared definition of eligible financial collateral.
The comprehensive approach imports supervisory haircuts and master netting agreement rules for SFTs, so haircut recognition is the common quantitative link.
Cross-cutting adjustments - maturity mismatch treatment and the treatment of defaulted exposures - qualify the amount of recognisable protection.

data.theme: Scope boundary rules that determine whether an instrument or position sits in the trading book or the banking book, and therefore which capital regime (market risk vs credit/banking book treatment) applies. Also governs how risk may be moved between the two books.
how_members_connect: Shared defined terms: 'Trading Book', 'Banking Book' and 'Trading Desk' are the definitional anchors on which the boundary rule operates; assignment must be to a designated trading desk.
Obligation chain: designation/classification at inception, restrictions on reclassification, and supervisory notification/approval flow from the boundary provision to the two book definitions.
Internal risk transfer is the controlled exception to the boundary — it cross-references both books and sets conditions (e.g. recognition and hedging eligibility) for transferring risk between them.
Hierarchy: the boundary provision is the operative rule; the definitions are the interpretive layer it references.

data.theme: Standardised approach calibration for commodity market risk: the bucket structure for commodity risk factors and the prescribed correlation parameters used in aggregating sensitivities.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: a calibration table applied within the sensitivities-based method rather than a standalone obligation.
Legally dependent on the trading book scope and risk-class definitions elsewhere in the market risk framework; the parameters are mandatory inputs, not firm discretion.

data.theme: Standardised approach calibration for foreign exchange risk: bucket (currency pair) definitions and correlation parameters used to aggregate FX sensitivities into a capital charge.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster functioning as a prescribed parameter set within the sensitivities-based method.
Interacts with the trading book boundary and with banking book FX positions that are nonetheless subject to market risk capital; parameters are fixed by the regulator and not adjustable by the firm.
start_here: Foreign Exchange Risk Buckets and Correlations

data.theme: Criteria determining whether a risk factor qualifies as modellable under the internal models approach, and therefore whether it is capitalised through the expected shortfall model or via the stressed capital add-on for non-modellable risk factors.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster acting as a gatekeeping test that conditions eligibility for internal model treatment.

Operationally tied to trading desk designation and model approval provisions elsewhere in the market risk framework; failure of the test has a direct capital consequence rather than a mere reporting one.

data.theme: Capital treatment of a bank's equity exposures to investment funds, and the counterparty-credit-risk inputs those treatments depend on. It covers the tiered hierarchy of measurement approaches and the leverage adjustment applied to fund exposures.
how_members_connect: The equity-investments-in-funds rule is the parent obligation; it prescribes a descending hierarchy of the look-through, mandate-based and fall-back approaches according to the granularity of information available to the bank.

Both the look-through and mandate-based approaches require the fund's underlying derivative and off-balance-sheet positions to be risk-weighted, which pulls in the counterparty credit risk framework, SA-CCR and the credit derivatives rules as computational cross-references.

The leverage adjustment is a corrective step applied to the risk weight produced under the look-through and mandate-based approaches, so it is legally dependent on them rather than a stand-alone requirement.
Scope note: these are credit-risk capital rules for banking-book fund holdings; the market-risk look-through concept is a distinct provision.

data.theme: Capital consequences of transactions that have not settled on the contractual date, including failed trades and the distinction between delivery-versus-payment and free-delivery settlement.
how_members_connect: The unsettled-transactions rule is the operative capital requirement; the DvP definition sets the scope condition that determines which capital charge schedule applies.
Timing triggers (business days past the agreed settlement date) drive escalating capital treatment, so the two members form a single condition-to-consequence chain.
Small cluster: it functions as an annex-level detail to the wider credit and counterparty credit risk capital framework.
start_here: Capital Treatment of Unsettled Transactions and Failed Trades

data.theme: The standardised (and simplified standardised) measurement of minimum capital for market risk, spanning the sensitivities-based method, default risk capital and the residual risk add-on, plus the legacy interest rate, equity, FX, commodities and options methods.
how_members_connect: The minimum capital requirements for market risk sit at the top; the standardised approach is decomposed by mandatory sub-components — sensitivities-based method, default risk capital and residual risk add-on — which must be summed.

The sensitivities-based method fans out into defined risk classes (GIRR, CSR, equity, commodity, FX) and defined sensitivity measures (delta via PV01/CS01, vega, curvature), each with prescribed buckets and correlations.

Default risk capital chains through gross and net jump-to-default positions and the hedge benefit ratio, and cross-cites the credit risk capital rules for risk weights and the securitisation and correlation-trading definitions for scope.

The simplified standardised approach and the older maturity ladder, delta-plus and scenario methods are alternative or transitional regimes; eligibility to use them is a scope condition, not a free choice.
Boundary members (leverage ratio, credit conversion factors, CCR/CVA minimums) are cross-regime references pulling in adjacent capital frameworks.
start_here: Minimum Capital Requirements for Market Risk

data.theme: The internal models alternative for market risk capital: supervisory permission conditions, the expected shortfall measure, risk-factor modellability, and the ongoing backtesting and P&L attribution tests that determine continued use of models.
how_members_connect: The internal models approach is the permissioned regime; its general provisions set the SAMA approval condition and the desk-level qualification tests that must be passed on a continuing basis.

Capital is built as an aggregation of the modellable component (IMCC, derived from stressed expected shortfall with prescribed liquidity horizons and a reduced risk-factor set) plus the stress scenario charge for non-modellable factors plus the internal-model default risk charge.

The risk factor eligibility test and its bucketing method are the gateway determining whether a factor is modellable; failure moves the factor into the NMRF regime, so the two are linked by a direct legal consequence.

Backtesting exceptions (via hypothetical and actual P&L, and the green/amber/red zones) drive the multiplication factor and can force a desk back to the standardised approach; the PLA test uses the Spearman and Kolmogorov-Smirnov metrics comparing risk-theoretical to hypothetical P&L for the same purpose.

data.theme: Operational risk regulatory capital under SAMA's adoption of the Basel III post-crisis standardised approach, covering how the capital charge is built from business volume indicators and internal loss experience.
how_members_connect: Single calculation chain: Business Indicator feeds the Business Indicator Component, which is multiplied by the Internal Loss Multiplier (driven by the Loss Component) to give Operational Risk Capital.
Loss-data rules act as the evidential precondition for the ILM: identification/collection criteria and the loss event type taxonomy define which losses may enter the Loss Component.
Hierarchy runs from the Basel III post-crisis reforms as source standard, through SAMA's minimum capital requirements framework, down to the definitional and classification annexes.
Duplicate-titled members reflect the same obligation expressed in the framework document and its detailed methodology sections.
start_here: SAMA Minimum Capital Requirements for Operational Risk
Loss Data Identification and Collection Criteria

data.theme: Counterparty credit risk exposure measurement under internal models and the resulting CVA capital charge, including the choice between basic and standardised CVA approaches and eligibility of hedges.
how_members_connect: Exposure chain: IMM produces Effective EPE, scaled by the alpha factor, subject to stress testing, wrong-way risk and cross-product netting conditions before feeding capital calculations.

CVA framework branches into BA-CVA (reduced and full versions, with stand-alone CVA capital as the building block) and SA-CVA (delta/vega sensitivities, vega risk buckets, eligible hedges); use of one approach is conditioned on model approval and hedging.
Market risk RWA is the parent aggregation node that pulls in the CVA framework and its approaches.
Wrong-way risk (general and specific) operates as a qualifying condition on IMM exposure estimates rather than a standalone charge.

data.theme: The parameter set used to compute the potential future exposure add-on under SA-CCR for derivative exposures.
how_members_connect: The PFE add-on is the parent obligation; effective notional, supervisory delta, maturity factor and supervisory factor are its mandated inputs.
Effective notional is itself derived from supervisory delta and the maturity factor, creating a nested calculation dependency.
The margin period of risk is the conditioning variable for the maturity factor, linking margining arrangements to the capital outcome.

data.theme: Scope and aggregation rules under SA-CCR: how exposures are grouped into netting sets and hedging sets and how replacement cost is determined under margin agreements.
how_members_connect: SA-CCR is the governing methodology; netting set is its defining scope unit and determines the perimeter for offsetting.
Hedging sets sit inside netting sets as a finer risk-category grouping for add-on aggregation.
Margin agreement replacement cost examples are illustrative guidance applying the netting set definition to margined versus unmargined trades.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of asset encumbrance — the extent to which a bank's on-balance sheet assets are pledged or otherwise unavailable to unsecured creditors.
how_members_connect: Single standalone disclosure template within the SAMA Pillar 3 framework; its obligation is to present encumbered versus unencumbered assets consistently with the accounting balance sheet.
Conceptually feeds liquidity and resolution/creditor-hierarchy analysis, so it should be read alongside liquidity and balance-sheet reconciliation disclosures rather than in isolation.

data.theme: Pillar 3 remuneration transparency: qualitative governance of the remuneration policy plus quantitative disclosure of amounts awarded, special payments and deferred/retained pay for material risk takers.
how_members_connect: The qualitative table sets the policy, governance bodies and scope of covered staff; the three quantitative templates report figures against that same defined population.
All three templates cross-reference the policy table, so definitions of 'senior management' and 'material risk takers' flow one-way from the qualitative table into the numeric disclosures.
Together they operationalise the risk-alignment obligations of the remuneration/governance regime — deferral, malus and clawback become observable through the deferred remuneration template.

data.theme: Pillar 3 credit risk disclosure: the quality of exposures (defaulted vs non-defaulted, provisions), movements in defaulted stock, and the extent to which credit risk mitigation reduces exposure.
how_members_connect: The credit quality of assets template is the hub: the defaulted-stock reconciliation, the CRM overview and the supplementary qualitative tables all tie back to its exposure and provision figures.
Shared defined terms — 'default', 'past due', accounting provision categories and 'problem assets' (restructured/non-performing) — are set in the qualitative tables and applied in the templates.
The prudential treatment of problem assets table supplies the classification and write-off policy that explains the numbers reported in the quantitative templates.
Duplicate labelling of the CRM techniques overview indicates the same disclosure obligation surfacing in more than one place; treat as one requirement.
start_here: Template CR1 - Credit Quality of Assets
Table CRB-A - Prudential Treatment of Problem Assets

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure for banks using the supervisory slotting approach to specialised lending under the IRB framework, where exposures are assigned to regulatory categories with prescribed risk weights instead of own estimates.
how_members_connect: Standalone template applying only to IRB-permitted banks that lack sufficient estimates for specialised lending sub-classes (project, object, commodities finance, income-producing real estate).
Depends on the IRB approval and exposure-class definitions in the capital adequacy framework; scope is limited to those specific sub-asset classes.
Reads alongside the broader credit risk and IRB disclosure set to give a complete picture of risk-weighted assets.
start_here: Template CR10: IRB Specialised Lending Slotting

data.theme: Capital treatment of bank exposures arising from central clearing: trade exposures and default fund contributions to central counterparties, with preferential treatment conditional on the CCP meeting qualifying (QCCP) status.
how_members_connect: Definitional hierarchy: CCP is the base defined term, and QCCP is the qualifying sub-set whose status determines which capital treatment a clearing member may apply.

Obligation chain runs from the CCP exposure capital rules to the roles they bind (clearing member, and clients accessing clearing through it) and to the exposure types captured (trade exposures, default fund contributions).

Calculation cross-references: default fund capital depends on the CCP's hypothetical capital requirement (KCCP), which in turn feeds the per-clearing-member charge (KCMi) — a change in QCCP status cascades through all three.
Consequence for a decision: loss or absence of QCCP status re-characterises the same exposure into a materially harsher capital outcome, so counterparty status verification is the gating question.

data.theme: The non-risk-based leverage ratio: how the denominator (exposure measure) is built up across on-balance-sheet items, derivatives, securities financing transactions and off-balance-sheet commitments, deliberately limiting netting and collateral recognition.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the leverage ratio framework sets the ratio; the exposure measure is the operative denominator; the derivative, SFT and written credit derivative components are its defined sub-measures.
Derivative exposure builds on replacement cost plus an aggregate add-on, with cash variation margin recognition and written credit derivative treatment as the two main adjusting rules.

SFT treatment appears twice by design — once as the general exposure rule and once as the leverage-specific measure — and interacts with the minimum haircut floors regime, so the same transaction can be assessed under both lenses.
Practical consequence: techniques that reduce risk-weighted assets (collateral, netting) do not necessarily reduce the leverage exposure measure, so the binding constraint must be tested separately.

data.theme: Supervisory expectations for banks dealing with highly leveraged counterparties (hedge funds and similar), addressing counterparty credit risk that conventional current-exposure measures understate.
how_members_connect: The SAMA sound practices document is the parent instrument; exposure measurement, limit setting, collateral/contractual provisions and ongoing monitoring are its component obligation areas.
Definitional trigger: whether a counterparty falls within the HLI definition determines whether the enhanced due diligence, collateral and monitoring expectations apply.

Measurement chain: potential future exposure feeds exposure measurement, which in turn drives limit setting and is stress-tested; monitoring closes the loop by tracking positions against those limits.
Collateral and contractual provisions are treated as risk mitigants that must be documented and enforceable, not as a substitute for measurement or limits.
start_here: SAMA Sound Practices for Banks Interactions with HLIs

data.theme: The finalised Basel III package as adopted in KSA: revised standardised and internal-model approaches for credit, counterparty credit/CVA and operational risk, constrained by an aggregate output floor, plus the Pillar 3 disclosure regime that makes the outcomes comparable.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the post-crisis reforms framework is the parent; the credit risk, CCR/CVA (SCCR) and operational risk (SOPE) minimum requirements are the calculation modules beneath it.

The output floor is the binding cross-cutting constraint — it aggregates modelled RWA across all risk types against a standardised benchmark, so a change in any single module can alter the floor outcome.
Credit RWA depends on conversion of off-balance-sheet items via credit conversion factors, linking commitment and facility structuring directly to capital.
Pillar 3 sits downstream: its templates and guiding principles disclose the results of each Pillar 1 module, so disclosure scope follows the approaches actually applied.

data.theme: Narrative (qualitative) Pillar 3 disclosure on counterparty credit risk: how a bank explains its CCR risk management objectives, methodologies for assigning economic capital and credit limits, policies on collateral and wrong-way risk, and the effect of a ratings downgrade on collateral it must post.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the qualitative table is the narrative anchor that gives interpretive context to the quantitative CCR templates (exposure analysis, collateral, credit derivatives) sitting in adjacent clusters.

Obligation runs from the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements framework down to a fixed-format table; scope, frequency and format are set by the parent disclosure regulation rather than by the table itself.
Relies on CCR definitions and measurement approaches (e.g. counterparty credit risk, collateral, wrong-way risk) that are defined in the capital adequacy/credit risk rules, not restated here.
start_here: Table CCRA: Qualitative Disclosure related to CCR

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of counterparty credit risk exposures broken down by the measurement approach used, showing replacement cost, potential future exposure, EAD post-CRM and resulting RWA.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: this template is the primary quantitative counterpart to the CCR qualitative table, which must explain the approaches reported here.
Depends on approach definitions and EAD/CRM calculation rules in the capital adequacy framework; the template prescribes presentation, not methodology.
Feeds and must reconcile with the bank's overall RWA and capital adequacy disclosures.
start_here: Template CCR1: Analysis of CCR Exposures by Approach

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of the collateral used to mitigate counterparty credit risk, split between derivative transactions and securities financing transactions, and between segregated and unsegregated, received and posted.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: it operationalises the collateral and credit risk mitigation policies described narratively in the CCR qualitative table.
Cross-references the CRM recognition rules in the capital adequacy framework, which determine which collateral may reduce EAD reported in the exposure template.
Segregation categories connect to downgrade-trigger and margining disclosures required qualitatively.
start_here: Template CCR5: Composition of Collateral for CCR

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of credit derivative positions, distinguishing protection bought from protection sold and separating notionals from fair values, covering both hedging and intermediation activity.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: credit derivatives operate both as CCR-generating exposures and as credit risk mitigants, linking this template to the CCR exposure and collateral templates.
Governed by the same Pillar 3 disclosure framework setting format, frequency and scope of application.
Uses credit derivative and protection buyer/seller concepts defined in the capital adequacy and CRM rules; wrong-way risk commentary sits in the qualitative table.

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure obligations for securitisation activity — what a bank must narrate about its role (originator, sponsor, investor, servicer), objectives, risk-transfer intent and accounting/regulatory treatment of securitised exposures.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the qualitative securitisation table sits at the top of the securitisation disclosure chain and frames the quantitative templates that follow.

Relies on the securitisation definitions and the significant-risk-transfer / originator-sponsor concepts used in the capital adequacy framework; disclosure scope follows the prudential consolidation scope.
Hierarchy: Basel-aligned SAMA capital rules set the treatment; this table sets the narrative reporting duty on that treatment.

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 reporting of securitisation exposures held in the trading book, split by the bank's role and by whether exposures are on- or off-balance sheet.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the trading-book securitisation template is the quantitative counterpart to the securitisation qualitative narrative.
Depends on the banking-book / trading-book boundary determination, so it interacts with the market risk disclosure set as well as the securitisation framework.
Uses the same role taxonomy (originator, sponsor, investor) as the securitisation qualitative disclosure, ensuring narrative and figures are read together.
start_here: Template SEC2: Securitisation Exposures in Trading Book

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure for banks using the standardised approach to market risk — describing the risk strategy, structures and processes underlying standardised market risk capital charges.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: this table is the entry point of the standardised market risk disclosure chain and precedes the related quantitative market risk templates.
Presupposes the trading-book scope and the standardised approach eligibility rules in the market risk capital framework.
Parallel obligation to the internal models qualitative table: which one applies depends on the approach the bank is approved to use.
start_here: Table MRA: Market Risk Standardised Approach Qualitative

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure for banks permitted to use internal models for market risk — covering model scope, characteristics, validation, stress testing and supervisory approval conditions.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the IMA qualitative table is the counterpart obligation to the standardised approach table, triggered by SAMA model approval.
Cross-references the internal models approval and validation requirements in the market risk capital framework; the approval determines the disclosure perimeter.
Feeds the interpretation of the quantitative model-based market risk templates, which are unreadable without this narrative.

data.theme: Pillar 3 market risk disclosure for banks that compute market risk capital under the simplified standardised approach, setting out the quantitative reporting format for capital requirements by risk class.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the template stands alone as the disclosure vehicle for institutions permitted to use the simplified standardised approach rather than the full SA or internal models approach.
Depends on upstream market risk capital calculation rules for its defined risk categories; the template itself imposes only a disclosure obligation, not a measurement rule.
Scope is conditional — applicability turns on the bank's approved approach for market risk capital.
start_here: Template MR3: Market Risk Simplified Standardised Approach

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure of a bank's credit valuation adjustment risk management — governance, scope of the CVA framework, and the approach used for derivatives and securities financing exposures.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster serving as the general narrative disclosure that frames all approach-specific CVA disclosures.
Cross-references the CVA capital regime; the qualitative content must be consistent with the calculation approach the bank is authorised to apply.
Functions as the entry point in the CVA disclosure hierarchy, with approach-specific tables layered beneath it.
start_here: Table CVAA: General Qualitative Disclosure CVA

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure specific to banks applying the standardised approach for CVA risk, covering risk management, hedging strategy and governance under that approach.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster whose applicability is conditioned on the bank using SA-CVA rather than the basic approach.
Sits below the general CVA qualitative disclosure in the disclosure hierarchy and should be read together with it to avoid duplicative or inconsistent narrative.
Content is driven by the SA-CVA eligibility and hedging recognition conditions in the CVA capital rules.

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure of a bank's operational risk management framework, including governance, policies, risk appetite and the approach used to determine operational risk capital.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster acting as the narrative counterpart to quantitative operational risk capital reporting.
Draws its defined terms and scope from the operational risk capital regime and from broader governance and internal control requirements.
Disclosure obligation is enforceable at the reporting-entity level and must reflect the bank's actual approved framework, not a generic description.
start_here: Table ORA: Operational Risk Framework Qualitative

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of risk-weighted assets across credit, counterparty credit, securitisation, market risk and CVA, including the mandated comparison of internally modelled outcomes against standardised approach outcomes. It governs what a bank must publish about how RWA is calculated and how it moves period to period.
how_members_connect: All templates roll up into the overview of RWA, which acts as the anchor disclosure and fixes the risk-category taxonomy the detailed templates must reconcile to.

Credit risk templates (standardised exposure/CRM and asset-class-by-risk-weight, IRB by portfolio and PD, credit derivative effects, IRB flow statements) inherit their measurement rules and defined exposure classes from the minimum capital requirements for credit risk framework.

The modelled-vs-standardised comparison templates create a cross-cutting obligation chain: internal-model users must restate the same exposures on the standardised basis, linking IRB, IMM, IMA and SA-CVA disclosures to a common benchmark.

Flow-statement templates (IRB credit risk, counterparty credit risk under IMM, SA-CVA) share a common structure requiring explanation of RWA movements, so they are read together rather than in isolation.
start_here: SCRE - Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk
Template CMS1 - Comparison of Modelled and Standardised RWA at Risk Level

data.theme: Disclosure of the composition and quality of regulatory capital, buffers, leverage and the constraints that follow when buffer requirements are breached. Covers what counts as capital, on what terms, and what a bank may distribute.
how_members_connect: The Basel III capital reforms guidance is the parent instrument; the composition of capital template, the main features table for capital instruments and the distribution-constraint template all draw their eligibility criteria and deduction rules from it.
Key metrics operates as the summary disclosure that must be consistent with the detailed capital composition, countercyclical buffer, leverage ratio and distribution-constraint templates.
Distribution constraints link buffer shortfalls to an enforceable limit on dividends, buybacks and discretionary bonuses, and connect to creditor ranking disclosure where loss absorbency is relevant.
Leverage ratio templates form a pair: the reconciliation from accounting assets to leverage exposure supports the common disclosure figure, and prudent valuation adjustments feed capital composition.
start_here: SACAP - Guidance on Implementation of Capital Reforms Under Basel III

data.theme: Total loss-absorbing capacity disclosure for globally systemically important banks and their material subgroups, including the ranking of creditors at resolution and subgroup entity level. This is a resolvability regime distinct from going-concern capital adequacy.
how_members_connect: The FSB term sheet is the source standard: the TLAC key metrics, composition and creditor-ranking templates all derive their eligibility criteria, subordination requirements and scope from it.
The TLAC concept entry supplies the defined term that binds the composition and key-metrics templates together.
Creditor ranking is disclosed at two levels — resolution entity and material subgroup entity — which must be read as a pair to assess where losses fall in a resolution.
TLAC key metrics parallel the going-concern key metrics disclosure, so the two regimes must be reconciled for the same entity.
start_here: Template TLAC1 - TLAC Composition for G-SIBs

data.theme: Reconciliation between published financial statements and the regulatory scope of consolidation, and from the balance sheet to regulatory capital. It addresses the problem of explaining why accounting figures differ from prudential figures.
how_members_connect: The linkage templates form an obligation chain: differences between accounting and regulatory scope, then main sources of those differences, then a narrative explanation table — each successive item explains the preceding one.

The capital reconciliation template ties balance-sheet line items to the composition of regulatory capital, which in turn is governed by the Basel III capital reforms guidance and the main features table for capital instruments.
Key metrics summarises outputs from capital composition, countercyclical buffer geographical distribution and leverage ratio disclosures, and must be internally consistent with them.
Banking-book securitisation exposures are disclosed by reference to the regulatory scope of consolidation, tying that template into the accounting-versus-regulatory linkage set.
start_here: Template LI1: Differences Accounting vs Regulatory Scope
Template CC2 - Reconciliation of Regulatory Capital to Balance Sheet

data.theme: Pillar 3 public disclosure of operational risk under the standardised approach, covering the loss data, business indicator inputs and the resulting minimum capital requirement.
how_members_connect: The three templates form a single computational chain: historical loss data (OR1) and the business indicator with its subcomponents (OR2) are the inputs that feed the minimum required operational risk capital reported in OR3.

They share the defined terms of the standardised operational risk regime (business indicator, business indicator component, internal loss multiplier), so a bank's reporting choices in one template constrain the others.

All sit at the same hierarchical level as disclosure templates issued under the supervisory disclosure framework, meaning a gap or inconsistency in OR1/OR2 is directly auditable against the OR3 outcome.
start_here: Template OR3: Minimum Required Operational Risk Capital
Template OR2: Business Indicator and Subcomponents

data.theme: Qualitative disclosure of how a bank governs and manages interest rate risk in the banking book, including risk appetite, measurement assumptions and hedging strategy.
how_members_connect: Stands as the narrative counterpart to the IRRBB quantitative template: the modelling assumptions and governance disclosed here are what make the reported IRRBB figures interpretable.
Relies on the IRRBB defined terms (banking book scope, economic value of equity, net interest income) used consistently across the disclosure framework.
Sits within the governance/risk-management regime, so the disclosure obligation overlaps with internal board and ALCO oversight requirements.
start_here: Table IRRBBA: IRRBB Risk Management Objectives

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of interest rate risk in the banking book, reporting the impact of prescribed rate shock scenarios on economic value of equity and net interest income.
how_members_connect: Operates as the numerical output of the IRRBB regime whose assumptions and governance are described in the accompanying qualitative table.
Uses the supervisory shock scenarios and measurement definitions fixed by the IRRBB standard, limiting bank discretion in presentation.
Disclosure content is bounded by the banking book scope definition, which separates it from market risk (trading book) disclosures.
start_here: Template IRRBB1: Quantitative Information on IRRBB

data.theme: Disclosure of the indicators used to assess a bank's global systemic importance, feeding the identification and bucketing of G-SIBs and any resulting higher loss absorbency requirement.
how_members_connect: Applies to banks meeting the size/scope threshold that triggers the G-SIB assessment, so the obligation is conditional rather than universal.

Indicator categories (size, interconnectedness, substitutability, complexity, cross-jurisdictional activity) are defined terms whose values drive capital surcharge consequences elsewhere in the capital framework.
Sits at template level beneath the systemic-importance assessment methodology, which supplies the definitions and calculation basis.
start_here: Template GSIB1: Disclosure of G-SIB Indicators

data.theme: Qualitative disclosure of a bank's liquidity risk management framework, covering governance, funding strategy, stress testing and contingency funding planning. It frames the narrative context in which the quantitative liquidity ratios are to be read.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure table sitting within the liquidity disclosure family alongside the LCR and NSFR templates.
Operates as the explanatory counterpart to the numeric liquidity templates - supervisory expectation is that the narrative reconciles with reported ratio outcomes.
Sits downstream of SAMA's liquidity risk management and prudential rules, which supply the underlying obligations the table reports against.

data.theme: Standardised disclosure of the Liquidity Coverage Ratio - the short-term (30-day stress) liquidity metric based on high-quality liquid assets against net cash outflows.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a quantitative Pillar 3 template whose definitions (HQLA, outflow/inflow categories) derive from SAMA's liquidity rules implementing the Basel LCR standard.
Read together with the NSFR template and the liquidity risk management table to form the full liquidity disclosure set.
Disclosure duty is derivative: the template reports compliance with an underlying prudential minimum ratio requirement rather than creating it.

data.theme: Standardised disclosure of the Net Stable Funding Ratio - the structural, one-year measure of available versus required stable funding.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a quantitative Pillar 3 template whose weighting categories flow from SAMA's adoption of the Basel NSFR standard.
Pairs with the LCR template (short-term) to cover both horizons of the liquidity regime, with the qualitative table supplying management context.
Reporting obligation attaches to the same scope of consolidation used across the prudential disclosure framework.
start_here: Template LIQ2: Net Stable Funding Ratio

data.theme: Reconciliation between accounting carrying values in published financial statements and the exposure amounts used for regulatory capital purposes, explaining the differences by risk framework.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a Pillar 3 linkage template that bridges financial-statement scope of consolidation with the regulatory scope.
Cross-references the credit, counterparty credit, securitisation and market risk frameworks, since each column maps exposures to the applicable capital treatment.
Sits in the disclosure hierarchy below SAMA's capital adequacy rules - it evidences, rather than establishes, the exposure measurement obligations.

data.theme: Fee obligations attaching to registration/licensing steps under the Finance Companies regime, as set by SAMA circular rather than the primary regulation text.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a circular sits at the lowest tier of the hierarchy (Finance Companies Law -> Implementing Regulation -> circular) and operationalises a fee obligation.
Legal effect depends on the parent registration/licensing article it supplements; the circular should not be read as creating standalone registration criteria.
Relevant to finance companies and, by extension, BNPL entities registered under the same framework.
start_here: Registration Fees in Finance Companies Regulation Circular

data.theme: Capital adequacy treatment of residual balance-sheet exposures that do not fall in a named asset class, i.e. the fallback risk-weight bucket in the credit risk standardised approach.
how_members_connect: Isolated node functioning as the catch-all class once all specific standardised-approach exposure categories are exhausted.
Interacts with the credit risk mitigation and exposure-classification rules that determine when an item drops into this residual bucket.

data.theme: Credit risk mitigation under the capital framework: who may act as a protection provider, how guarantees and credit derivatives change the risk weight of an exposure, and how residual mismatches are penalised.
how_members_connect: Eligibility of the guarantor is a precondition to the substitution treatment — the risk-weight rule cross-references the permitted range of protection providers.
The haircut rule is a corrective overlay: recognition of protection is reduced where the protection is denominated in a different currency from the underlying exposure.

All three share the same defined terms (eligible protection provider, protected/unprotected portion) and sit within the same standardised-approach chapter, forming a single obligation chain: eligibility -> recognition -> adjustment.
start_here: Range of Eligible Guarantors and Protection Providers

data.theme: Conditions under which purchased receivables qualify for the dedicated capital treatment, including operational criteria and the distinction between default and dilution risk.
how_members_connect: Standalone node defining a qualifying exposure class; its criteria gate entry into a specific risk-weight methodology.
Connects conceptually to credit risk mitigation and residual-asset rules, since receivables failing the eligibility tests revert to general exposure treatment.

data.theme: Prudential credit risk classification for specialised lending exposures, specifically the supervisory slotting approach applied to commodities finance under the capital adequacy framework.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the slotting criteria operate as a standalone supervisory grid mapping commodities finance exposures to prescribed risk categories and associated risk weights.
Sits downstream of the capital adequacy/credit risk regime; it is an application rule rather than a source of independent conduct obligations.
Relevant to finance companies and banks that cannot rely on internal rating estimates for specialised lending and must default to supervisory categories.

data.theme: SAMA guidance on the documentary basis for property ownership within Economic Cities, affecting how supervised lenders treat such property as collateral or subject matter of financing.
how_members_connect: Isolated circular: it addresses recognition of a specific ownership document rather than cross-referencing a broader regulation.
Practical effect is on collateral eligibility, title verification and real estate finance underwriting decisions.
Read together with real estate finance and mortgage registration requirements outside this cluster.
start_here: SAMA Circular on Economic Cities Property Ownership Document

data.theme: Registration formalities for finance lease contracts, which condition enforceability and the lessor's protected position under the finance lease regime.
how_members_connect: Standalone circular imposing a procedural registration obligation on finance lessors.
Operates as an implementing instruction beneath the Finance Lease Law and its implementing regulation (law → regulation → circular chain).
Non-registration is a compliance and enforceability risk rather than merely an administrative lapse.
start_here: SAMA Circular on Registration of Finance Lease Contracts

data.theme: The credit information regime: licensing of credit bureaus, the content and use of credit records, and the data-quality and reporting duties of member entities feeding the system.
how_members_connect: The Executive Regulation is the hinge instrument, defining the credit record and setting the licensing conditions for credit information companies — both other members are referenced from it (law → executive regulation → circular).
The Qawaem circular is a downstream operational mandate that determines the source and standardisation of financial data entering credit records.
Shared defined terms (credit information, credit record, member, consumer/subject) govern consent, disclosure and correction rights across all members.
Cross-regime interaction: credit record use intersects with responsible lending/affordability duties and with data protection and consumer protection obligations.
start_here: Executive Regulation of the Credit Information Law

data.theme: Capital adequacy measurement for market risk: the reduced-complexity option that certain banks may apply instead of the full standardised approach.
how_members_connect: Single defined term operating as a scope/eligibility carve-out within the market risk capital regime.
Its meaning depends on cross-reference to the standardised approach it substitutes, so it cannot be read as a free-standing rule.
Use of the alternative is typically conditional on supervisory eligibility criteria and SAMA acceptance rather than firm election alone.

data.theme: Trading book boundary and governance: how a bank documents which positions and organisational units are treated as trading activity for prudential and market risk capital purposes.
how_members_connect: The policy statement is the governing document that defines and evidences trading book classification; the trading desk is the organisational unit whose activity that policy scopes.
