Obligation chain runs from board/senior management approval of the policy to desk-level mandates, limits and reporting.
Both terms feed the market risk capital regime, so classification decisions have direct capital-treatment consequences.

data.theme: Credit risk workout and forbearance: the recognised restructuring techniques a creditor may use with a distressed borrower, and their classification as short- or long-term measures.
how_members_connect: "Restructuring" is the umbrella defined term; each technique (forgiveness, splitting, debt-to-equity, debt-to-asset swaps) is an enumerated instance referenced from it.
The short-term/long-term split drives differing treatment, monitoring and documentation expectations for each measure.
Cross-regime consequence: restructuring decisions interact with provisioning/classification rules and, for retail exposures, with consumer protection and fair-treatment obligations.

data.theme: Workout negotiation planning: the analytical preparation a creditor is expected to perform before agreeing terms with a distressed counterparty.
how_members_connect: The negotiating strategy is the governing step; SWOT analysis is referenced as an input method supporting it.
Both sit upstream of formal restructuring measures, linking preparatory analysis to the eventual documented agreement.
Practical consequence: adequacy of this preparation is evidence of prudent credit governance rather than a stand-alone obligation.

data.theme: Coordinated multi-creditor handling of a distressed borrower: how banks jointly manage a restructuring process and agree to hold enforcement in abeyance while a workout is negotiated.
how_members_connect: The coordinator role is the procedural anchor — the standstill arrangement is the instrument that role is expected to convene and administer among participating creditors.
Linkage is operational-obligation based: appointment of a lead/coordinating bank triggers the standstill negotiation and information-sharing expectations across creditors.
Both terms sit inside the same credit-risk / problem-loan regime and should be read as defined terms of that framework, not as general commercial concepts.

data.theme: Operational and cyber resilience obligations for SAMA-supervised entities: maintaining continuity of critical services and withstanding, responding to and recovering from cyber and disruption events, including for newer licence categories such as aggregation entities and sandbox participants.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: the Business Continuity Management Framework and the Cyber Security Framework are the parent instruments; activity-specific instructions (e.g. for aggregation activity) incorporate them by cross-reference, so the same resilience obligations attach to newly regulated entity types.

Obligation chain within BCM: business impact analysis and risk assessment feed the business continuity plan and IT disaster recovery plan, which in turn must be exercised through periodic testing, all under a defined governance structure and crisis management arrangement.

Cyber side mirrors this through domains (leadership and governance, operations and technology, resilience), with the CISO as the accountable role and the resilience domain expressly tied back to business continuity.

External standards and glossaries (ISO 22301, NISTIR terminology) are cited as reference points for defined terms, while Vision 2030 and the sandbox materials supply the policy and scope context for applying the frameworks to innovative entrants.

data.theme: Controls over changes to IT estate — change and release management, patching and pre-deployment testing — as a component of the IT governance expectations applicable to supervised entities.
how_members_connect: Patch management is treated as a species of change: it must run through the change/release control and be validated by testing before deployment.
Testing is the common control condition linking the change and patch obligations; the governance glossary supplies the defined terms used across them.
Hierarchy is framework-to-control: the IT governance instrument sets the umbrella requirement, the individual control statements specify what must be done.

data.theme: Baseline control over the configuration of systems — establishing, approving and maintaining secure configuration standards as part of IT and cyber control expectations.
how_members_connect: Standalone node in this extract: it carries a single control obligation without internal cross-references in the graph.
Read alongside the change and patch control cluster, since configuration baselines are what change controls protect.
Its meaning depends on the parent IT governance / cyber framework definitions rather than on peer nodes.

data.theme: Quality assurance as a control-function obligation: the requirement that regulated entities test and validate the effectiveness of their compliance and operational controls rather than rely on design alone.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: QA appears as a standalone control expectation not yet linked to a parent framework in this graph.
Legally relevant as an assurance layer over other regimes (AML/CTF programme testing, governance and risk oversight), so its obligation content is normally borrowed from those instruments.
Practical consequence: absence of documented QA evidence is typically read as a control-effectiveness gap, not merely a documentation gap.

data.theme: The procedural route by which a supervised entity (or SAMA itself) seeks amendment of an existing framework's requirements, i.e. how binding rule text is changed rather than departed from.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster describing a process rather than a substantive obligation.
Pairs conceptually with the waiver process: update changes the rule for all addressees; waiver relaxes it for one addressee.
Relevance is hierarchical - it sits at the framework-maintenance level above individual articles, so it governs the currency of any requirement cited from that framework.

data.theme: The mechanism for an entity to request relief from a specific framework requirement, and the conditions under which SAMA-granted relief is valid and time-bound.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster covering an exemption/derogation pathway rather than a primary duty.
Directly complements the update process: both are framework-governance procedures, distinguished by general versus entity-specific effect.
Decision consequence: a granted waiver narrows scope of an otherwise enforceable obligation only to its stated terms and period; it does not displace parallel obligations under other regimes.

data.theme: SAMA's circular-level instrument communicating obligations arising under the Credit Information Law, covering the collection, sharing and use of consumer and commercial credit information.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster sitting at the circular tier of the hierarchy (law → implementing regulation → circular), so its content is derivative of and must be read with the Credit Information Law.

Cross-regime relevance: credit information duties intersect with consumer protection (consent, disclosure, dispute rights) and with finance/BNPL underwriting obligations that rely on credit bureau data.
Scope caution: circular obligations bind the addressed entity classes only; do not extend them to persons outside the law's definition of credit information providers or users.

data.theme: Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure templates for market risk (standardised and internal models approaches) and credit valuation adjustment risk, plus the RWA overview and modelled-versus-standardised comparison tables that sit above them. The regulatory problem-space is comparable, consistent public disclosure of capital requirements by risk type and calculation approach.
how_members_connect: All templates feed the same aggregate: OV1 is the RWA overview into which the market risk, CVA and counterparty credit risk lines are reported, so each detailed template references it as its reconciliation point.

The CVA templates are tiered by permitted calculation approach (reduced basic, full basic, standardised) with a separate flow statement for SA-CVA movements, mirroring the approach hierarchy in the underlying capital rules.

MR1 (standardised) and MR2 (internal models) are the paired disclosures for market risk, and both feed the CMS1 comparison of modelled versus standardised outcomes; CMS2 extends the same comparison logic to credit risk asset classes.

Disclosure obligations here are derivative: the templates do not create capital requirements but require publication of results computed under the capital adequacy framework, so scope depends on which approaches the bank is approved to use.
start_here: Template MR1 - Market Risk under Standardised Approach
Template CMS1 - Comparison of Modelled and Standardised RWA

data.theme: Disclosure of the gap between the accounting scope of consolidation and the regulatory scope of consolidation, and between carrying values and regulatory exposure amounts. Addresses the risk that published financial statements are read as if they matched prudential figures.
how_members_connect: LI1 maps financial statement categories to regulatory risk framework categories; LI2 then reconciles those carrying values to the exposure amounts actually used for capital purposes.
Table LIA is the qualitative counterpart: it requires narrative explanation of the differences that LI1 and LI2 present numerically, so it cross-references both.

The cluster relies on a shared distinction between the accounting consolidation perimeter and the prudential consolidation perimeter — the defined scope determines every downstream capital and disclosure figure.
start_here: Template LI1 - Accounting vs Regulatory Consolidation
Table LIA - Explanations of Accounting/Regulatory Differences

data.theme: Baseline qualitative disclosure on credit risk: the bank's business model as it translates into credit risk profile, the components of its credit risk management framework, and the relationship between credit risk management and the accounting treatment of impairment.
how_members_connect: Stands as the narrative gateway to the credit risk disclosure suite — the quantitative credit risk and asset quality templates are read against the qualitative framework described here.

Uses definitions (past due, impaired, restructured exposures) that govern how the quantitative credit risk tables must be populated, so inconsistency between narrative and figures is itself a disclosure defect.
Sits at the qualitative tier of the Pillar 3 hierarchy: an obligation to explain policy and governance rather than to compute a capital number.
start_here: Table CRA - General Qualitative Info about Credit Risk

data.theme: Qualitative disclosure of credit risk mitigation: the policies and processes for collateral valuation and management, main types of collateral and guarantors, and concentrations arising within mitigation techniques.
how_members_connect: Provides the narrative basis for the recognised CRM effects reported in the quantitative credit risk exposure templates, so eligibility conditions in the capital rules constrain what may be disclosed as mitigation.
Depends on defined terms for eligible collateral, netting and guarantees drawn from the credit risk mitigation provisions of the capital adequacy framework, not from the disclosure standard itself.
Complements the general credit risk qualitative disclosure: exposure policy first, then the techniques used to reduce that exposure.
start_here: Table CRC - Qualitative Credit Risk Mitigation

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of how a bank uses external credit assessment institutions (ECAI) ratings when applying the standardised approach to credit risk. It covers the qualitative narrative on which ratings are recognised, for which exposure classes, and how they are mapped to risk weights.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a qualitative disclosure table that sets the interpretive basis for the quantitative standardised-approach templates elsewhere in the framework.

Depends on the defined concepts of eligible ECAI, exposure class and risk-weight mapping used in SAMA's capital adequacy/credit risk rules; the table discloses application, it does not itself set the mapping.
Sits at the circular/framework-annex level beneath the credit risk capital regulation it implements.
start_here: Table CRD - Use of External Credit Ratings

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of standardised-approach credit risk: the effect of credit risk mitigation on exposure amounts and the resulting distribution of exposures across asset classes and risk-weight buckets.
how_members_connect: Both templates report the same underlying standardised-approach exposure population at different stages: pre/post-CRM amounts feed the risk-weight breakdown, so the figures must reconcile.
Shared defined terms (exposure class, on/off-balance-sheet exposure, CCF, eligible collateral and guarantees) drawn from the credit risk capital rules.
Direct cross-reference between the two templates creates a consistency obligation rather than two independent disclosures.
start_here: Template CR4 - Standardised Approach CRM Effects
Template CR5 - Exposures by Asset Classes and Risk Weights

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure for banks permitted to use internal ratings-based models for credit risk: model scope, structure, governance, validation and supervisory approval status.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster providing the narrative context required to interpret the quantitative IRB templates (exposure-by-PD and PD backtesting).
Relies on defined terms from the IRB regime (PD, LGD, EAD, rating system, model validation) and on the condition that SAMA has granted IRB permission.
Framework-annex level disclosure implementing the model-governance expectations in the capital adequacy rules.

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of IRB credit risk: exposures distributed by PD grade with associated risk parameters, and backtesting of estimated versus realised default rates.
how_members_connect: The backtesting template tests the same PD grades and obligor populations disclosed in the exposure template, so the two must use a consistent rating scale and segmentation.
Shared IRB defined terms (PD band, obligor grade, defaulted exposure, average PD) and the same supervisory approval precondition.
Explicit cross-reference between members makes the backtesting disclosure an accountability layer over the reported parameter estimates.
start_here: Template CR6 - IRB Credit Risk Exposures by PD Range
Template CR9 - IRB Backtesting of PD

data.theme: Pillar 3 credit-risk disclosure showing the effect of credit derivatives used as risk mitigants on risk-weighted assets calculated under the internal ratings-based approach. It addresses transparency over how recognised credit protection changes IRB capital outcomes.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone disclosure template within the SAMA-adopted Pillar 3 framework, sitting under the capital adequacy/Basel regime rather than conduct or AML rules.
Legally dependent on the IRB permission and the credit risk mitigation eligibility rules that determine when a credit derivative may reduce RWA at all.
Links upward through the disclosure hierarchy: Basel standard as adopted by SAMA circular, then the template as the prescribed reporting form.
start_here: Template CR7 - IRB Effect on RWA of Credit Derivatives

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of period-on-period movements in credit risk RWA computed under the IRB approach, explaining the drivers of change (asset size, asset quality, model updates, methodology, FX and other).
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a prescribed flow-statement template completing the IRB disclosure set alongside the exposure and mitigation templates.
Obligation arises from the bank's IRB approval and the general Pillar 3 disclosure duty; content is defined by fixed movement categories rather than free narrative.
Cross-reads with other IRB templates because closing balances must reconcile to the RWA figures disclosed elsewhere in the same set.
start_here: Template CR8 - RWA Flow Statements under IRB

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure for specialised lending (and equity) exposures where a bank cannot estimate own PD and must instead use the supervisory slotting criteria, mapping exposures to regulatory categories and their prescribed risk weights.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a disclosure template that operationalises the supervisory slotting fallback within the IRB regime.

Depends on the defined exposure sub-classes (project finance, object finance, commodities finance, income-producing real estate) and on supervisory risk-weight tables set in the underlying capital rules.
Sits in the same hierarchy as the other IRB templates: Basel text adopted by SAMA, then template as mandated form.
start_here: Template CR10 - IRB Specialised Lending Slotting

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on counterparty credit risk: the bank's objectives, methodologies and governance for managing CCR, including collateral and credit reserve policy, wrong-way risk, and the impact of a credit-rating downgrade on collateral it would have to post.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the narrative table that frames and contextualises the quantitative CCR templates in the same disclosure suite.
Ties the capital/disclosure regime to internal governance and risk-management obligations, since the narrative must describe actual policies rather than generic statements.
Relies on CCR definitions and exposure measurement methods set in the underlying capital adequacy rules adopted by SAMA.

data.theme: Pillar 3 counterparty credit risk disclosure: the core templates through which a bank presents its aggregate CCR exposure picture, the standardised measurement of that exposure, and its exposures to central counterparties.
how_members_connect: Shared regime and defined terms: all three are CCR disclosure templates sitting under the same Pillar 3 disclosure requirements, using a common exposure/EAD and risk-weighted assets vocabulary.

Obligation chain by aggregation: the overview template summarises CCR exposures by measurement approach, with the standardised-approach and CCP templates supplying the disaggregated components that must reconcile back to it.

Cross-references run both ways between the summary and the CCP template, so scope decisions (qualifying vs non-qualifying CCP, cleared vs bilateral) taken in one template determine what is reported in the other.

Hierarchy: these are template-level instruments implementing higher-level capital adequacy and disclosure rules, not free-standing obligations - read them against the parent framework for scope and applicability.
start_here: Template CCR1 - Analysis of CCR Exposures

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of counterparty credit risk exposures for banks using internal ratings-based approaches, broken down by probability-of-default band.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an IRB-specific CCR template whose applicability is conditional on SAMA approval to use internal ratings for the relevant portfolios.
Legally dependent on the CCR overview disclosure - it disaggregates the IRB portion of total CCR exposure and must be consistent with it.
Uses IRB defined terms (PD scale, EAD, average risk weight) imported from the capital adequacy framework rather than defined in the template itself.
start_here: Template CCR4 - IRB CCR Exposures by PD Scale

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of the collateral posted and received against derivative and securities-financing transactions, evidencing credit risk mitigation in the CCR framework.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a supporting template that substantiates the risk mitigation assumed in the CCR exposure calculations disclosed elsewhere.
Depends on eligible-collateral and segregation concepts defined in the credit risk mitigation rules of the capital framework.
Practical consequence: collateral recognised here should be traceable to the exposure reductions reflected in the CCR measurement templates.
start_here: Template CCR5 - Composition of Collateral for CCR

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of credit derivative positions - protection bought and sold - as a distinct component of counterparty credit risk exposure.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster covering a product-specific disclosure that feeds the broader CCR exposure and credit risk mitigation picture.
Relies on notional and protection-bought/sold distinctions defined in the capital adequacy framework; the template does not create independent definitions.
Cross-regime relevance: positions disclosed here may simultaneously be treated as credit risk mitigation for banking book exposures, so scope boundaries matter for consistency.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of a bank's capital treatment where it acts as investor in securitisation exposures, covering exposure amounts, risk-weight bands and resulting capital requirements. It sits within the securitisation framework rather than the ordinary credit-risk framework.
how_members_connect: Single-template cluster: the SEC4 template is the investor-side leg of the securitisation disclosure series, paired with the originator/sponsor templates and the qualitative securitisation narrative.

Depends on securitisation defined terms (originator, sponsor, investor, resecuritisation) and on the hierarchy of securitisation risk-weight approaches set in the capital adequacy rules that the template merely reports.
Obligation chain runs from the Basel-aligned capital framework adopted by SAMA down to the periodic disclosure requirement the template operationalises.

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure of a bank's overall market-risk management: strategy, governance, structure of the trading function, and the scope and nature of measurement and reporting systems.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster acting as the narrative anchor for the market-risk disclosure family; the quantitative market-risk templates are read against it.
Relies on the trading book / banking book boundary definitions and the approach-selection rules in the capital adequacy framework.
Links upward to general governance and risk-management disclosure obligations, and sideways to the model-specific qualitative table.
start_here: Table MRA - General Qualitative Market Risk

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure specific to banks permitted to use an internal models approach for market risk, covering model scope, supervisory approval, validation, stress testing and backtesting arrangements.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster that is conditional in scope: it binds only institutions with supervisory permission to use internal models.
Supplements the general qualitative market-risk table, adding model-governance detail on top of the baseline narrative.
Ties back to the approval and ongoing-use conditions in the capital adequacy framework, which determine whether the disclosure obligation is triggered at all.
start_here: Table MRB - Qualitative Disclosures for IMA

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of market-risk capital requirements computed under the simplified standardised approach, broken down by risk class (interest rate, equity, foreign exchange, commodity, options).
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster representing the disclosure output of one permitted calculation method; its use is conditional on eligibility for the simplified approach.
Mutually exclusive in practice with internal-models and full standardised-approach reporting for the same exposures, so the approach-eligibility rules govern which template applies.
Read together with the general qualitative market-risk narrative, which explains the approach choice the template reflects.
start_here: Template MR3 - Market Risk under SSA

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of movements in counterparty credit risk RWA where the bank uses the Internal Model Method, isolating period-on-period drivers of capital consumption rather than end-state balances.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the flow-statement template sits in the counterparty credit risk (CCR) family of disclosure templates and depends on prior supervisory approval to use IMM.

Legally downstream of the capital adequacy/CCR measurement rules — the template does not create the measurement obligation, it fixes the reporting format and periodicity for banks already within IMM scope.

Flow logic (opening balance, drivers of change, closing balance) links it analytically to other RWA flow disclosures, so consistency of the closing figure with headline RWA disclosure is the practical compliance point.
start_here: Template CCR7 - RWA Flow Statements under IMM

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of banking-book securitisation exposures, combining a narrative/qualitative account of securitisation activity with the quantitative exposure template.
how_members_connect: Explicit cross-reference: the quantitative banking-book template is read against the qualitative table, which supplies the policy, role (originator/sponsor/investor) and risk-transfer narrative that makes the numbers interpretable.
Shared defined terms — securitisation, resecuritisation, originator, sponsor, traditional vs synthetic — are set in the qualitative table and carried into the template's line items.
Both sit at the disclosure layer beneath the securitisation framework rules; scope (banking book only) is the key limiting condition, with trading-book exposures disclosed elsewhere.
start_here: Template SEC1 - Securitisation in Banking Book

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of securitisation exposures held in the trading book, the counterpart to banking-book securitisation disclosure.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster whose scope is defined by the banking-book/trading-book boundary; correct book allocation determines which template applies and prevents omission or double-counting.
Relies on the same securitisation defined terms and role classifications used in the qualitative securitisation disclosure, so it should be read alongside that narrative table.
Exposure amounts disclosed here feed the capital-requirement view presented in the originator/sponsor and investor capital templates.
start_here: Template SEC2 - Securitisation in Trading Book

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of securitisation exposures where the bank acts as originator or sponsor, together with the associated capital requirements.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster linked to the securitisation exposure templates: exposures reported there are mapped here into risk-weight bands and resulting capital charges.

Turns on the originator/sponsor definitions and on whether significant risk transfer conditions are met — a classification question that drives whether exposures remain in scope of the securitisation framework.
Sits at the bottom of the hierarchy (framework rules to disclosure template); the template prescribes presentation, not the underlying capital treatment.

data.theme: Pillar 3 narrative disclosure of a bank's credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk framework — the general qualitative explanation of how CVA risk arises from derivatives and securities financing exposures and how it is governed and managed.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the entry-level qualitative CVA disclosure table that all other CVA disclosures (standardised and basic approach) presuppose.
Sits in the disclosure layer of the capital hierarchy: minimum capital rules on CVA risk feed the disclosure obligation, not vice versa.
Uses CVA-specific defined terms (covered transactions, CVA risk capital requirement) shared with the counterparty credit risk regime.
start_here: Table CVAA - General Qualitative CVA Disclosure

data.theme: Narrative disclosure specific to banks using the standardised approach for CVA risk (SA-CVA), covering governance, risk management and the conditions of use of that approach.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster that is conditional on approach eligibility: the obligation only bites where the bank is approved for / applies SA-CVA.
Legally downstream of the general CVA qualitative disclosure — read together as general-then-specific within the same disclosure regime.
Shares defined terms and scope boundaries with the CVA capital requirement rules and counterparty credit risk framework.
start_here: Table CVAB - Qualitative Disclosures for SA-CVA

data.theme: Pillar 3 narrative disclosure of the bank's operational risk management framework — policies, governance, and the business lines and event types to which the framework applies.
how_members_connect: Single-member qualitative table that provides the interpretive context for the quantitative operational risk templates in the adjacent cluster.
Depends on operational risk defined terms (business indicator, loss event) established in the operational risk capital rules.
Disclosure-layer obligation: it reports on compliance with the substantive operational risk governance requirements rather than creating them.
start_here: Table ORA - General Qualitative Operational Risk

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of operational risk capital under the standardised approach: historical loss experience, the business indicator and its subcomponents, and the resulting minimum capital requirement.
how_members_connect: Computational obligation chain: loss history (OR1) and the business indicator components (OR2) are both inputs that feed the capital outcome disclosed in OR3.
Both input templates cross-reference the OR3 result, so inconsistency between them is itself a disclosure defect.
All three rely on the same defined terms (business indicator, business indicator component, internal loss multiplier) set by the operational risk capital rules.
Read alongside the qualitative operational risk table, which supplies the framework narrative for these figures.
start_here: Template OR3 - Minimum Required Operational Risk Capital
Template OR2 - Business Indicator and Subcomponents

data.theme: Pillar 3 liquidity disclosure of the Net Stable Funding Ratio, i.e. the requirement to publish the stable funding position over a one-year horizon in SAMA's prescribed format.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the NSFR disclosure template sits under the standardised liquidity disclosure regime, taking its defined inputs (available and required stable funding) from the underlying NSFR standard rather than defining them itself.
Obligation chain runs from the Basel-based liquidity standard adopted by SAMA to the periodic disclosure duty operationalised through this template.
start_here: Template LIQ2 - Net Stable Funding Ratio

data.theme: Pillar 3 credit risk disclosure showing the extent to which exposures are covered by eligible credit risk mitigation (collateral, guarantees, credit derivatives).
how_members_connect: Standalone template whose content depends on the CRM eligibility and recognition rules in the capital adequacy framework; the template imposes the disclosure obligation, not the eligibility test.
Cross-reads to the wider credit risk exposure and asset quality templates, since mitigated amounts must reconcile to disclosed gross exposures.

data.theme: Pillar 3 counterparty credit risk disclosure of collateral used in securities financing transactions and derivative exposures.
how_members_connect: Standalone template within the CCR disclosure series; its scope is set by the counterparty credit risk and collateral treatment rules, which supply the defined transaction types.
Links outward to the CRM and CCR exposure templates so that posted and received collateral is presented consistently across the disclosure set.

data.theme: Reconciliation between accounting (financial statement) scope of consolidation and the regulatory scope used for capital purposes, including how securitisation exposures are mapped into that regulatory perimeter.
how_members_connect: LI2 explains the sources of differences against the mapping set out in LI1, so LI1 is the anchor disclosure and LI2 the explanatory bridge.
SEC1 references LI1 because securitisation exposures must be reported by reference to the regulatory consolidation perimeter established there.
Shared defined terms - scope of regulatory consolidation, carrying values under accounting versus regulatory treatment - govern all three templates.
Together they form an obligation chain: define the perimeter, explain the deltas, then disclose specific exposure classes on that basis.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), covering both the qualitative description of a bank's IRRBB governance and measurement approach and the quantitative impact of prescribed interest rate shock scenarios on economic value of equity and net interest income.
how_members_connect: Both members are components of the same IRRBB disclosure requirement: the narrative table supplies the modelling assumptions, measurement basis and risk appetite that make the quantitative template interpretable.
The quantitative template explicitly refers back to the qualitative table, creating a paired obligation - a bank cannot satisfy one without the other.

Shared defined terms (banking book, economic value of equity, net interest income, supervisory shock scenarios) and a common reporting frequency and scope of application under the disclosure framework.
Sits in the governance/risk regime as a downstream implementation of the banking capital and risk management rules, not a standalone rule.
start_here: Table IRRBBA - IRRBB Risk Management Objectives
Template IRRBB1 - Quantitative Information on IRRBB

data.theme: Disclosure of the indicators used to assess systemic importance, feeding the identification and any higher loss-absorbency requirement for global systemically important banks.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone disclosure template whose content is driven by the systemic importance assessment methodology rather than by other disclosure tables.
Scope limit matters - the obligation only bites for banks meeting the size or designation threshold, so applicability must be confirmed before treating it as a live requirement.
Cross-references the capital adequacy regime, since indicator scores drive any additional capital buffer.
start_here: Template GSIB1 - Disclosure of G-SIB Indicators

data.theme: Qualitative disclosure of a bank's liquidity risk management framework - governance, funding strategy, stress testing and contingency funding arrangements.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster providing the narrative counterpart to the quantitative liquidity ratio templates; it explains the assumptions behind reported liquidity metrics.
Anchored in the liquidity risk management rules and the defined terms used across the liquidity regime (liquidity risk, funding concentration, stress scenarios).
Operates as a governance obligation on the board and senior management, distinct from the numerical reporting obligation.

data.theme: Quantitative disclosure of the Liquidity Coverage Ratio - high-quality liquid assets against net cash outflows over a 30-day stress horizon.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster implementing the LCR minimum standard through a prescribed disclosure format, with averaging and observation-period conventions that affect how compliance is assessed.
Depends on the liquidity regime's defined terms (HQLA levels, run-off and inflow rates, net cash outflows) set in the underlying liquidity rules.
Read together with the qualitative liquidity management table, which supplies the explanatory context for reported figures.

data.theme: A single standardised credit-risk disclosure template within the Pillar 3 / public disclosure framework, prescribing the fixed format and data fields a bank must publish for its credit risk exposures.
how_members_connect: Isolated node: the template is a form-level instrument that operationalises the broader credit risk disclosure requirements rather than creating standalone obligations.
Hierarchy point: template sits at the lowest tier (framework rules -> disclosure requirements -> prescribed template), so its content is only enforceable as read with the parent disclosure rules.
Read together with the disclosure frequency/timing rules, which fix when this template must be published.

data.theme: Timing dimension of the public disclosure regime: how often and by when supervised banks must publish Pillar 3 information, and how disclosure cadence tracks reporting periods.
how_members_connect: Isolated node that functions as a cross-cutting timing obligation applying to the full set of disclosure templates, including credit risk templates.
Compliance consequence: frequency/timing determines the deadline against which any individual template's publication is assessed.

data.theme: Capital treatment of bank exposures to central counterparties (CCPs): calculating a CCP's hypothetical capital requirement and, from it, each clearing member's capital charge for its default fund contributions.
how_members_connect: Direct calculation chain: the clearing member's default fund capital requirement is derived from, and cross-references, the CCP's hypothetical capital requirement.
Shared defined terms and inputs (qualifying CCP status, default fund contributions, trade exposures) mean both must be applied as a single sequential methodology.
Both sit within the counterparty credit risk / capital adequacy regime, so misapplication flows straight into reported capital ratios.
start_here: Clearing Member Default Fund Capital Requirement (KCMi)

data.theme: Supervisory instruction requiring financial institutions to respond promptly to judicial and court-related requests, bridging the supervisory regime with judicial process obligations.
how_members_connect: Isolated circular-level instrument: it imposes a direct conduct obligation on supervised entities rather than amending an underlying regulation.

Cross-regime relevance: interacts with customer confidentiality, account freezing/attachment and data-disclosure duties, so it must be reconciled with bank secrecy and data protection limits before responding.

data.theme: Consumer protection channel requirements for receiving and answering customer complaints — mandating an accessible unified contact line and a standardised form of response to complainants.
how_members_connect: Both sit in the consumer-protection/complaint-handling regime and bind the same supervised entities' customer-facing complaint function.
Obligation chain: the toll-free number governs intake/accessibility; the response template governs the content and format of the outgoing reply, closing the same complaint lifecycle.
Shared defined concepts of 'complaint' and complainant communication, so the two instruments are read together when assessing complaint-handling adequacy.

data.theme: Currency handling and cash-processing standards: how banknotes are inspected, sorted and presented (banding) by institutions dealing in SAMA-issued currency.
how_members_connect: Both are operational currency-issuance instructions addressed to cash-handling institutions, forming a single quality-control obligation set.
Sequencing: inspection/fitness sorting determines outcome, banding card templates prescribe the mandated labelling of the processed bundles.
Templates are the prescribed form supporting the substantive inspection duty — non-use of the template is itself a compliance gap.

data.theme: Identification of counterparties and service providers by the National Unified Number, including its use for legal representatives and the replacement of superseded identifiers.
how_members_connect: Explicit cross-reference: the lawyers requirement relies on the unified-number replacement instructions for which identifier is authoritative.
Shared defined term (National Unified Number) that carries into identification/verification and record-keeping obligations across regimes.
Hierarchy of specificity: general replacement instruction (all entities) narrowed by a sector-specific requirement for engaged lawyers.

data.theme: Handling of requests and information demands issued by the Committee for the Settlement of Banking Disputes, and the supervised entity's duty to respond to that adjudicatory body.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument community: a standalone circular addressed directly to banks on Committee-originated requests.
Interfaces with confidentiality/banking-secrecy and customer-data rules, since disclosure to the Committee is a lawful-authority exception.
Read alongside complaint-handling and consumer-protection materials, which the Committee route sits downstream of.

data.theme: Authenticity and verification of bank-issued documents (e.g. certificates, statements, letters) when produced and validated electronically rather than on paper.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the instruction stands alone as the operative rule on how banks issue and subsequently verify their own documents electronically.
Legally it sits downstream of general banking supervision powers and interacts with e-transactions validity and consumer-facing service delivery obligations.
Relevant to reliance questions: a document's evidentiary weight for third parties (including in CDD/KYC file build-up) depends on the issuing bank's verification mechanism.
start_here: Electronic Issuance and Verification of Bank Documents

data.theme: Application of the Kingdom's Personal Data Protection Law to SAMA-supervised entities, and how data-protection duties overlay financial-sector confidentiality, credit information and customer-record obligations.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster acting as the sector-level compliance hook for a general (non-SAMA) statute, so the linkage is law-to-supervisory-instruction rather than internal cross-reference.

Interacts across regimes: banking secrecy, credit information sharing, AML record-keeping and consumer protection all involve processing of personal data and must be read consistently with PDPL lawful-basis and retention rules.

Practical consequence: data-subject rights and cross-border transfer limits do not override statutory AML/CTF record retention or supervisory reporting duties, so conflicts must be resolved by identifying the governing legal obligation.

data.theme: Governance expectations for the internal audit function in locally incorporated banks: independence, mandate, board/audit-committee reporting lines and assurance coverage.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster forming part of the governance/risk pillar; it presupposes the board and audit-committee structures set by banking governance requirements.

Creates an obligation chain: internal audit provides third-line assurance over compliance functions in other regimes (AML/CTF, consumer protection, operational risk), so findings feed supervisory reporting.
Read alongside external audit and compliance-function requirements to allocate responsibility correctly when a control failure is identified.
start_here: Internal Audit Principles for Local Banks

data.theme: Regulatory treatment of remote/telework arrangements in financial institutions, covering both labour-market localisation conditions and the control and consumer-protection conditions for serving customers from outside branch premises.
how_members_connect: The two SAMA circulars expressly reference the Ministerial Decision on remote work localisation, making the labour instrument the upstream authority for Saudisation crediting of remote roles.

The initiative circular and the remote customer service circular are conceptually paired: one enables the arrangement, the other sets conduct, confidentiality and supervision conditions when the remote role is customer-facing.

Cross-regime interaction: remote handling of customer interactions engages banking secrecy, personal data protection and consumer protection duties, and does not relax CDD or record-keeping requirements.
Hierarchy to observe: ministerial decision (labour law) then SAMA circulars applying it to supervised entities.

data.theme: Treatment of subsidised development fund lending — how financiers must account for and consider government development fund loans when assessing or extending credit.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: a SAMA circular directing supervised financiers on how development fund loans are to be considered in credit decisions.
Sits downstream of the finance/credit regime (law → implementing regulation → circular) as a supervisory clarification rather than a standalone rule set.
Interacts with responsible-lending and affordability obligations under consumer finance and credit information regimes.

data.theme: Payment-fraud prevention and customer-facing controls in card and mada transactions: pre-authorisation abuse, identity verification against a trusted source, standardised transaction notifications, and fee treatment on claims.
how_members_connect: Shared subject population: payment service providers, card issuers and acquirers supervised under the payments/PSP regime.
Obligation chain from identity assurance at onboarding/transaction stage, through fraud-specific controls, to customer notification and dispute/claims handling.
Cross-regime linkage: identity verification via a trusted source touches AML/CTF customer identification standards, while notification and fee rules engage consumer protection duties.
All are circulars — supervisory instruments elaborating existing payment regulations rather than creating a new licensing regime.
start_here: Customer Identity Verification via Trusted Source

data.theme: Cost and product-term controls in real estate finance: amendments to mortgage product instructions and the fees chargeable for real estate valuation.
how_members_connect: Both address the pricing and disclosure side of mortgage origination for banks and real estate finance companies.
Valuation fee limits operate as a component of the total cost the borrower bears under the mortgage product terms, so the two instruments must be read together.
Consumer protection obligations (transparency of charges, no undisclosed cost pass-through) run through both.
Instrument hierarchy: circular-level amendments sitting under the real estate finance law and its implementing regulations.

data.theme: Mandated adoption of electronic payment acceptance across defined merchant sectors (grocery, retail, personal services), progressively extending POS/e-payment obligations to categories of merchants.
how_members_connect: Parallel sector-by-sector circulars applying the same underlying obligation to accept electronic payments, differing only in the merchant population covered.
Shared definitional dependence on merchant categories and on payment service providers' onboarding duties, which brings merchant-as-customer / KYB obligations into play.
Implementation-phase instruments under the national payments framework, coordinated with acquirers who must enable the covered merchants.
Sequential rollout gives a timing/scope reading: each circular sets the effective perimeter for its sector.

data.theme: Consumer-protection conduct obligations governing how financial institutions communicate with and serve the public — fair, non-misleading advertising and marketing, and equitable access to products and channels for persons with disabilities.
how_members_connect: Both sit in the consumer protection / market conduct regime rather than prudential or AML rules, and bind the institution's dealings with the 'Consumer' as a defined term.
Shared obligation logic: disclosure that is clear, accurate and comprehensible — advertising rules set what must not mislead, accessibility rules set for whom information and channels must be usable.
Both operate as ongoing conduct duties enforceable through SAMA supervisory action and complaint handling, not one-off approvals.
Typical hierarchy: consumer protection principles issued by SAMA, elaborated through instructions/circulars addressed to banks, finance companies and PSPs.

data.theme: Two distinct supervisory levers over finance companies and other supervised entities: SAMA's publication of enforcement penalties, and the authorisation/conditions for finance companies raising debt through special purpose vehicles.
how_members_connect: Linked by regime rather than subject matter — both are SAMA instruments applying to licensed finance companies as supervised entities.
Obligation chain: SPV debt issuance is a permission subject to conditions/notification; failure to observe those conditions feeds the enforcement and penalty-publication track.
Publication of penalties functions as a reputational sanction layered on top of the substantive licensing and funding rules.
Hierarchy: Finance Companies Control Law and its implementing regulation sit above both the issuance rules and the enforcement/publication instructions.
start_here: Finance Company Debt Issuance via SPV

data.theme: Licensing and operating conditions for money exchange businesses — physical premises standards, Saudization of staffing, and customer identification requirements at branches, including a narrow exception for airport locations serving travellers.
how_members_connect: All three attach to the same licensed activity (exchange business) and to the same defined entity, the exchange centre/branch.
Premises requirements are the baseline licensing condition; Saudization and ID rules are operating conditions layered on the licensed premises.

The airport traveller exception is a scope carve-out from the general customer identification duty — read it against the AML/CTF CDD baseline, since an exemption from routine ID at the branch does not displace AML obligations, thresholds or STR duties.
Hierarchy: exchange business rules issued under the Banking Control Law / SAMA supervisory authority, refined by circulars and inquiry responses.
start_here: Minimum Requirements for Exchange Center Premises

data.theme: SAMA instruction on subscription to SMS notification services, i.e. the institution's duty to enrol and alert customers about account and transaction activity through text messaging.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone circular with no internal cross-links captured in the graph.
Its legal weight comes from the consumer protection regime — customer notification supports transparency, unauthorised-transaction detection and dispute/complaint rights.
Read alongside advertising/disclosure and payments rules, as notification duties interact with consent, data confidentiality and fee-disclosure obligations.

data.theme: A single, unlinked SAMA circular node identified only by its reference number, with no substantive content or cross-references captured in the graph. Its regulatory problem-space cannot be characterised from the available context.
how_members_connect: Isolated member: no internal edges, so no shared definitions or obligation chains are evidenced in the knowledge base.
As a circular, it sits at the instruction level of the hierarchy and would normally implement or clarify a parent law, rule or regulation — that parent is not recorded here.
Any compliance conclusion drawn from this node requires the underlying circular text and its issuance date/addressees to be retrieved before use.

data.theme: Physical cash handling and transport risk: SAMA's supervisory expectations on the hazards of moving or carrying large cash amounts and on adherence to the applicable cash transport requirements. Sits at the interface of operational/security risk and AML/CTF cash-based exposure.
how_members_connect: Both members are circular-level instructions on the same subject matter — cash in transit — and one expressly references the other, forming a single directive thread.
The awareness circular functions as risk communication supporting the compliance circular's enforceable adherence obligation on regulated entities.
Practical linkage to cash-intensive activity monitoring under the AML/CTF regime, though the definitional anchors sit in the AML law and rules rather than in these circulars.
start_here: Circular on Compliance with Cash Transport Regulations
Circular on Awareness of Risks of Carrying Large Cash Amounts

data.theme: Supervisory requirements addressed to money exchange companies and exchange centres, covering workforce Saudization, external audit standards and the submission of financial statements to SAMA. A licensee-specific compliance and reporting cluster within the money-changing sector.
how_members_connect: Common addressee class — licensed exchange companies/centres — which defines the scope limit of all three circulars.
Two of the three form a reporting/assurance chain: external auditor accounting standards govern the quality of the financial statements that must be filed with SAMA.
The Saudization circular is conceptually adjacent rather than dependent — a separate obligation head (labour/nationalisation) imposed on the same licensees.
All sit at circular level and operate under the money exchange licensing and supervision framework; the enabling law/rules are not represented in this cluster.
start_here: Circular on Financial Statements from Exchange Centers
Circular on External Auditor Accounting Standards for Exchange Companies

data.theme: Whistleblowing and protected internal reporting within SAMA-supervised financial institutions: establishing channels for raising concerns about violations or misconduct and protecting those who report. A governance and conduct-control obligation rather than a prudential one.
how_members_connect: Standalone policy-level instrument with no internal edges; it is the parent obligation for institution-level whistleblowing arrangements rather than a member of an obligation chain in this cluster.

Cross-regime relevance: interacts with governance/internal-control frameworks, AML/CTF suspicious-activity escalation, and consumer protection complaint handling — but those linkages are not captured here and should not be assumed as textual cross-references.
Applies to institutions within SAMA's supervisory perimeter; the precise addressee scope and any confidentiality/non-retaliation protections must be read from the policy text itself.
start_here: Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions

data.theme: Scope-setting for how SME status is defined in KSA and when SAMA-supervised entities may apply a lighter or optional compliance treatment to dealings with SMEs.
how_members_connect: All three instruments turn on a single defined term - the SME classification adopted by the General Authority for SMEs (Monshaat) resolution - which the SAMA circulars import rather than restate.

Hierarchy runs from the underlying SME definition resolution to SAMA's defining circular, then to the operative circular that attaches optional compliance consequences to entities meeting that definition.
The linkage is cross-referential: the optional-compliance circular is unusable without the definitional circular, since eligibility (headcount/revenue thresholds) determines who benefits.
Practical consequence: misclassifying a counterparty as an SME misapplies the relief; SME status is a scope filter, not a waiver of AML/CTF or consumer-protection duties that apply on other grounds.
start_here: Circular Defining Small and Medium Enterprises
Circular on Optional Compliance for SME Dealings

data.theme: Prudential and conduct limits on real estate finance - maximum financing ratios, eligibility of land financing, mortgage registration accuracy, and non-discrimination in financing terms and insurance cover.
how_members_connect: The Real Estate Finance Law and its Implementing Regulation are the parent instruments; each circular either amends a numeric limit under them or clarifies application of a specific article.

The financing-limit and land-financing circulars form an obligation chain: the maximum LTV/financing cap is set by circular, then a further circular fixes whether land-only financing falls within the Article 12 regime.

Mortgage registration and equal-treatment circulars address conduct duties on the same contracts - registering security for the actual contracted amount and not differentiating financing or insurance terms between comparable customers.

Cross-regime note: the equal-treatment and registration duties overlap with consumer-protection principles and with insurance conduct rules, so a single real estate finance product can attract obligations from more than one SAMA regime.
start_here: Real Estate Finance Law and Regulation
Circular on Increasing Maximum Real Estate Financing Limit
Circular on Land Financing Subject to Article 12

data.theme: Standing and representation - whether a supervised entity's in-house legal department staff may act as its legal representatives in proceedings and dealings, and the conditions attached.
how_members_connect: Standalone SAMA circular with no internal cross-links in this cluster; it operates as a governance/authority rule for the entity's legal function.
Its consequence is procedural: it determines who can validly bind or represent the institution, which matters for enforcement correspondence, litigation and regulatory responses.
start_here: Circular on Legal Department Staff as Legal Representatives

data.theme: Treatment of investment funds that participate indirectly in financing activity - whether such participation falls inside the licensed finance activity perimeter and the conditions SAMA attaches.
how_members_connect: Isolated circular in this graph; it functions as a perimeter/scope clarification for finance companies and their funding structures.

Decision relevance: it bears on whether an indirect funding arrangement triggers finance-company licensing and related conduct obligations, and on the boundary with capital-markets supervision of funds.
start_here: Circular on Investment Funds Indirect Participation in Financing

data.theme: Confidentiality and controlled disclosure of supervisory information: supervised entities must obtain SAMA's prior no-objection before sharing data, correspondence or findings originating from the supervisory relationship with any third party.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster; the obligation is a standalone prior-consent gate rather than part of a chained rulebook.

Legally it sits in the governance/supervisory-relationship regime and conditions any outward disclosure (auditors, consultants, group entities, foreign regulators) that other regimes might otherwise assume is permitted.
Interacts with outsourcing, group reporting and data-sharing arrangements: a permission to share data under another framework does not displace the SAMA no-objection requirement.
start_here: Circular on No-Objection Before Sharing Supervisory Data

data.theme: Protection of SAMA's identity and the avoidance of implied regulatory endorsement: supervised entities are barred from using the SAMA logo (and, by extension, any suggestion of SAMA sponsorship) in their materials.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster; a prohibition addressed to all supervised entities rather than a regime-specific rule.
Doctrinally adjacent to consumer-protection and advertising/disclosure obligations, since the harm addressed is misleading consumers about official backing.
Licensing status may be stated as a fact where required, but that is distinct from logo use, which remains prohibited.
start_here: Circular on Prohibition of SAMA Logo Use

data.theme: Evidential integrity of consumer finance documentation: lenders must ensure the borrower signs the contract pages, so that informed consent covers the whole agreement and not only a signature block.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster; a documentation-execution requirement layered on top of finance/consumer-credit contracting rules.
Connects legally to disclosure and pre-contractual transparency duties: page-level signature is the evidence that terms were presented to the Consumer/Borrower.
Relevant to dispute handling and enforceability, since defective execution undermines the creditor's evidentiary position.
start_here: Circular on Borrower Signature on Contract Pages

data.theme: Acceptability of electronically notarized limited liability company contracts (articles/memoranda) as valid documentary evidence in onboarding and credit files.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster; it settles an evidentiary question rather than creating a new customer-due-diligence standard.
Feeds directly into KYB/legal-person CDD: it identifies an acceptable form of constitutive document for verifying legal status, authorised signatories and ownership structure.
Does not relax verification duties; identification, beneficial-ownership and record-keeping obligations under the AML/CTF regime continue to apply to the electronically notarized document.
start_here: Circular on Accepting Electronically Notarized LLC Contracts

data.theme: Cost-of-credit transparency in consumer finance: how the Annual Percentage Rate must be computed, what fees and charges enter the calculation, and how the resulting figure is disclosed to the consumer.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy runs from the Regulations for Consumer Financing (substantive disclosure and pricing obligations) down to the dedicated APR calculation rules, with the circular acting as SAMA's interpretive gloss on the fees-and-charges article.

Shared defined term 'APR' anchors the cluster: the annex description and the calculator operationalise the same definition the regulations impose, so a divergence in inclusion of a fee changes the disclosed rate.
Obligation chain: identify chargeable items → include/exclude them per the fees clarification → compute per the APR rules → disclose in the contractual form referenced by the annex.
The calculator is a supervisory reference point rather than an independent source of obligation; its outputs are meaningful only against the rules and annex it implements.
start_here: Circular Clarifying Article 83 on Fees and Charges

data.theme: Enforcement route available to lessors/finance companies when recovering leased assets, channelled through competent authorities rather than self-help repossession.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: a standalone SAMA circular with no captured cross-references in this graph.
Legally it sits downstream of the finance lease regime and consumer-protection constraints on collection and enforcement conduct; those links are not modelled here and should be verified directly.
start_here: Circular on Repossession of Leased Assets via Competent Authorities

data.theme: Supervisory instruction to finance companies on holiday dates, relevant to timing of obligations such as instalment due dates, notice periods and business-day computation.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster with no internal edges captured.
Its practical effect is procedural: it conditions deadline calculation under other finance-company rules rather than creating a substantive obligation of its own.
start_here: Circular on Finance Company Holiday Dates

data.theme: An isolated SAMA circular identified only by its reference number; its regime and subject matter are not established by the surrounding graph.
how_members_connect: Singleton node with no cross-references, parent regulation or implementing guidance captured.
Scope, addressees and effective date must be read from the instrument itself before it is relied on; do not infer a regime from adjacent clusters.

data.theme: Timing and sequencing of the move to international accounting standards by SAMA-supervised entities, including the transition to the IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss framework. The regulatory problem is when reporting obligations change and what preparatory steps supervised firms must complete before the effective date.
how_members_connect: Both are SAMA circulars addressed to supervised institutions setting the effective/transition dates for adopting international accounting standards, so one sets the general timetable and the other the instrument-specific implementation path.
Shared obligation chain: identify the adoption date, prepare an implementation plan, and report readiness to SAMA — a supervisory reporting duty rather than a substantive prudential rule.
Cross-regime relevance: accounting classification and impairment feed into prudential capital and provisioning outcomes, so the timing decision has knock-on effects for regulatory reporting.
Hierarchy note: these are circulars operating beneath the applicable banking/finance-company supervisory framework; they supplement rather than replace the underlying standards.
start_here: Circular on Timing of Adopting International Accounting Standards

data.theme: Registration treatment of land subject to the white land fee regime, as it bears on financing and collateral taken over undeveloped land. The compliance issue is whether and how a financier may deal with, or rely on, such land where a fee liability or registration requirement attaches.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone SAMA circular directing supervised lenders on handling lands falling within the white land fee registration requirement.
Links outward to real estate finance and collateral-valuation obligations rather than to a sibling instrument inside this cluster.
Read together with title-documentation and real estate financing scope instruments before drawing conclusions about applicability.
start_here: Circular on Registration of White Land Fee Lands

data.theme: Acceptability of title and property deeds issued by licensed notaries for purposes of real estate finance and security documentation. The question is evidentiary sufficiency of the deed relied on when granting or securing financing.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a SAMA circular instructing supervised financiers on treatment of deeds originating from licensed notaries.
Functionally chained to real estate finance underwriting and collateral-perfection duties — the deed is the document on which the security position rests.
Interacts with customer/property due-diligence expectations; verification of the deed source is part of the lender's documentation obligation.
start_here: Circular on Deeds from Licensed Notaries

data.theme: Scope definition distinguishing commercial real estate financing from other real estate finance products. Definitional scope determines which prudential, reporting and consumer-protection rules apply to a given exposure.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a definitional SAMA circular whose main legal effect is to fix the boundary of a defined term.
Acts as a gateway instrument — classification under it drives applicability of real estate finance regulation, exposure limits and reporting lines.
Consumer-protection cross-cut: exposures classified as commercial typically fall outside consumer-facing real estate finance protections, so misclassification carries dual-regime risk.
start_here: Circular Defining Commercial Real Estate Financing

data.theme: Removal of the formal requirement to affix an official stamp on documents/instruments handled by supervised entities, i.e. a formality-reduction measure affecting how validity and authentication of banking documentation is evidenced.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: a SAMA circular acting as an amending instruction that overrides an earlier procedural formality rather than creating a new obligation regime.
Its legal effect is subtractive — it removes a documentary condition, so it must be read against the underlying rules/forms that previously assumed a stamped document.
Relevant to authentication and evidentiary practice in customer documentation and contract execution; no substantive change to identification or record-keeping duties.
start_here: Circular on Cancelling Official Stamp Requirement

data.theme: Operational controls that supervised institutions must apply when executing and processing banking-procedure transactions, addressing authorisation, verification and internal handling discipline.
how_members_connect: Standalone circular imposing process-level controls; sits below the governing banking regulation as an implementing/supervisory instruction.
Interacts with governance and internal-control expectations, and indirectly with AML/CTF transaction scrutiny where handling controls support detection of irregular activity.
Should be read alongside customer documentation and authentication requirements, since the controls determine who may act and on what evidence.
start_here: Circular on Controls for Handling Banking Procedures Transactions

data.theme: The consumer finance regime governing finance providers' dealings with individual borrowers: pre-contract disclosure, cost-of-credit transparency (APR), contractual terms, borrower treatment, and complaint/dispute handling.
how_members_connect: The Consumer Financing Regulations are the parent instrument; the APR annex, the borrower-dealing article and the dispute-resolution article are internal components that give effect to its disclosure and conduct obligations.
Shared defined terms (Consumer/Borrower, finance contract, cost of credit) bind the members: the APR methodology in the annex is the calculation basis for the disclosure duties in the main text.
The Finance Contract Summary Form is the prescribed disclosure vehicle referencing the Regulations — a form-level obligation chain from rule to standardised customer-facing document.

Cross-regime note: the consumer-protection concept of Borrower/Consumer is not co-extensive with the AML concept of Customer; CDD duties run in parallel and are not satisfied by consumer-disclosure compliance.

data.theme: A requirement for a financial certification/attestation statement to be provided in connection with specified financial documentation or reporting, addressing accountability for the accuracy of certified financial information.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: a discrete SAMA requirement operating as a documentary/attestation condition rather than a full regime.
Ties into governance and accountability chains — certification places responsibility on the attesting party for the accuracy of the underlying figures.
Read with related documentation and authentication instruments in this graph, since certification substitutes for or supplements other formalities.

data.theme: Conduct, confidentiality and disclosure obligations of banks toward customers, counterparties and authorities — covering what must be disclosed (licensing status, account terms), what must be kept confidential (bank–customer secrecy), and the lawful gateways for sharing account and payment data.
how_members_connect: Shared axis of banking secrecy: the confidentiality/disclosure rules set the default duty, and the disclosure-to-authorities and instant-payments data-sharing items function as carve-outs or permitted purposes.

Standardised current account agreement templates operationalise disclosure duties at the contract level, referencing licence disclosure and payment-system data-sharing terms as customer-facing consent/notice.
The code of conduct sits above as the institutional governance layer and pulls in AML/CFT obligations, which themselves override secrecy for reporting and CDD purposes.
Cross-regime tension to flag: consumer-protection/contract disclosure vs AML/CTF reporting vs data confidentiality — the same customer data is governed by three different duty sets.
start_here: Bank Account Data Disclosure to Authorities

data.theme: SAMA's enforcement transparency regime: when and how penalties imposed on supervised banks are published, and how the underlying violations are categorised by subject matter.
how_members_connect: The publication instructions set the obligation/discretion to disclose enforcement outcomes; the classification guide supplies the taxonomy used to label each published violation.
Direct reference linkage — classification categories are the controlled vocabulary for the publication output.
Practical consequence: the classification determines reputational exposure and how a penalty is read across regimes (AML, consumer protection, governance).

data.theme: Treatment of Premium Residency holders as an accepted customer identification/eligibility status for financial services in KSA.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: a SAMA circular directing supervised entities to accept Premium Residency as a valid status.
Interacts with CDD/identification requirements under AML/CTF and with account-opening eligibility rules, even though those instruments sit in other clusters.
start_here: SAMA Circular 5783 - Acceptance of Premium Residency

data.theme: Licensing, conduct and prudential-supervisory framework for money exchange centers, plus SAMA's ongoing supervisory reporting and control-testing expectations for that sector.
how_members_connect: Clear hierarchy: the Rules Regulating Money Exchange Business is the base instrument, with each circular amending, clarifying or adding obligations under it.
Reporting chain — supervisory data forms are the obligation, the RMS portal is the prescribed submission channel, creating a filing duty with defined periodicity.
Independent periodic testing links the sector to AML/CTF control-assurance expectations (independent audit of the AML/CFT programme).
Permitting POS services at exchange centers expands permitted activity scope and therefore extends payments-regime obligations onto exchange licensees.
start_here: SAMA Circular 5840 - Supervisory Data Forms for Exchange Centers (RMS)
SAMA Circular 5860 - Independent Periodic Testing for Exchange Centers

data.theme: Participation arrangements for government debt issuance — the primary dealer role for Saudi government securities and the supervisory expectations SAMA places on institutions acting in that capacity.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone SAMA circular addressed to institutions engaged in the government securities market.
Sits in the markets/capital-raising regime rather than AML or consumer protection; linkage to other clusters would run through licensing and governance obligations of the participating institution.
No internal cross-references captured in the graph, so obligations must be read on the face of the circular itself.
start_here: SAMA Circular 5858 - Primary Dealer Government Securities

data.theme: Sector-wide social responsibility expectations — a SAMA directive marking a designated social responsibility observance and the associated participation expectations for supervised entities.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an isolated SAMA circular with no captured cross-references.

Conduct/corporate-citizenship in character rather than a prudential or AML obligation; enforceability is weaker than rule-based instruments and should be characterised as a supervisory expectation unless the text states otherwise.
Relevant to governance and reputational-conduct workstreams rather than to any licensing or customer-facing regime.

data.theme: Embedding cyber security requirements into the project lifecycle — the expectation that supervised entities address security risk at initiation, design and change stages of projects rather than after deployment.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster within the governance and operational/cyber risk regime.
Reads as a control-domain requirement that presupposes a broader cyber security framework and board/senior-management accountability for risk ownership.
Conceptually adjacent to the cyber security awareness material; both are components of the same overarching cyber risk regime even though no edge is recorded.

data.theme: Cyber security awareness obligations — expectations that supervised entities build and maintain staff and, where relevant, customer awareness of cyber threats as part of their cyber risk control environment.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster in the governance/operational-risk regime with no captured internal cross-references.
Functions as a human-factor control domain that complements technical and lifecycle controls such as project-stage security requirements.
Interacts indirectly with consumer protection where awareness activity is customer-facing (fraud and scam prevention messaging).

data.theme: Independent periodic review of the effectiveness of the cyber security function, strategy and controls, as required under SAMA's cyber security governance expectations for supervised member organisations.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: the review obligation stands as a discrete control domain within the cyber security governance regime rather than sharing definitions with adjacent clusters.
Legally it sits downstream of the board/senior-management accountability chain — the review is the assurance mechanism that evidences the governance obligation has been discharged.
Cross-regime relevance: findings feed the institution's risk governance and internal control reporting to SAMA, and overlap with operational-risk and outsourcing oversight duties.

data.theme: Audit of cyber security controls — the assurance obligation requiring internal (and where applicable external) audit coverage of the cyber security domain.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: audit coverage is an enforceable, standalone control requirement within the cyber security framework's governance layer.
Obligation chain: audit findings must be tracked to remediation, linking this node to the institution's compliance and risk-reporting duties toward SAMA.
Distinct from periodic review — audit is the three-lines-of-defence assurance function, so scope, independence and reporting lines are the key legal questions.

data.theme: Identity and access management as a mandated control domain — governing user identification, authentication, authorisation, privileged access and periodic entitlement recertification.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster covering a defined technical control domain whose obligations attach to the member organisation, not to a service provider by default.
Interacts with customer-facing regimes: authentication expectations here sit alongside payments/PSP customer authentication and consumer-protection duties on unauthorised transactions.
Access controls are the evidentiary basis for accountability in incident investigation and audit, tying this node back to the audit and review obligations.

data.theme: Application security requirements — secure development, testing and maintenance obligations for in-house and acquired applications used in regulated financial activity.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: a discrete control domain in the cyber security framework, expressed as requirements on the member organisation across the application lifecycle.
Where applications are vendor-supplied or hosted, the obligation persists with the regulated entity and interacts with outsourcing and third-party risk rules.
Compliance evidence is typically surfaced through the audit and review obligations, creating a practical dependency on those assurance clusters.

data.theme: Workforce cyber security awareness and training as a standing control obligation — ensuring staff (and, where relevant, third parties) are competent to discharge cyber security duties.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: the training requirement stands as a discrete control obligation rather than part of an internal chain.
