data.summary: Sets out the core reporting duty under SAMA's OTC derivatives trade repository framework: reporting banks must report directly to the SAMA-authorised TR Operator (no agents or outsourcing), enter into a reporting service agreement containing a counterparty-consent clause, complete systems linkage and user testing, and populate all template fields. Reporting is compulsory on first execution of a reportable transaction and on subsequent business events, subject to the T+1 deadline and a limited exemption where a trade is cancelled or fully terminated within T+1 (not applicable to cancellations for central clearing). Reporting banks must also retain records evidencing compliance.
lookup_terms: reporting bank duty to report TR

data.summary: A SAMA circular (Arabic, dated 1446H) directing digital brokerage companies licensed by SAMA to submit quarterly and annual audited financial statements with the auditor's report, plus quarterly and annual prudential data on SAMA's prescribed templates, each within fixed business-day deadlines after the relevant quarter-end or year-end. Templates must be filed electronically in the required format together with a signed Data Certification form executed by the Chief Accountant, CFO and CEO or Managing Director, and the annual prudential templates must be reviewed and certified by the company's external auditor. It binds only SAMA-licensed digital brokerage companies and applies from the stated commencement quarter.

A SAMA-issued frequently asked questions document accompanying the Credit Card Issuance and Operation Rules, circulated to banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom for publication through customer channels. It explains, in guidance form, issuer duties on card issuance only upon a documented customer request, acceptance/rejection notification, re-issued and supplementary cards, the minimum age condition, and the treatment of annual fees, international purchase transaction fees, cash withdrawal/transfer/wallet top-up charges, grace period and late payment charges. It is expressly indicative only: it does not replace the Rules, and the Rules and other applicable laws and instructions prevail in any conflict.

The Credit Card Issuance and Operation Rules, notified by SAMA circular (1446H), governing how credit cards may be issued, re-issued and operated and how fees, costs and term cost may be charged. As reflected in the accompanying FAQ, they require a documented customer request before issuance, notification of acceptance or rejection with reasons and an objection route, conditions for re-issued and supplementary cards, a minimum age condition, activation before annual fees accrue, a minimum grace period, and prohibitions on increasing agreed term cost due to late payment or default. They bind banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom as card issuers; this node's context is drawn from the FAQ, so the operative article text must be read in the Rules themselves.
lookup_terms: Credit Card Issuance and Operation Rules

data.summary: SAMA's Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking, issued under the SAMA Law and the Banking Control Law, setting supervisory expectations for identifying, measuring, mitigating, monitoring and reporting risks specific to Shari'ah compliant activities (credit, market, operational, liquidity, equity investment, and Shari'ah non-compliance risk). It allocates board/delegated committee and senior management responsibilities, requires an independent risk management function and CRO access to the Risk Management Committee, and addresses product structuring, contract documentation, MIS and profit sharing investment accounts. It applies to all domestic banks licensed by SAMA that conduct Shari'ah compliant banking activities, extending to majority-owned banking subsidiaries and branches, and supplements SAMA's general risk management requirements.
lookup_terms: Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking

data.summary: The Shari'ah Governance Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking issued by SAMA in February 2020, referenced as the companion instrument that must be read together with the Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking and any subsequent updates. It is the governance-side source for the Shari'ah Committee's role in approving Shari'ah rules and principles applied to a bank's products and activities, which the risk framework then treats as a compliance and operational risk obligation. It binds SAMA-licensed banks conducting Shari'ah compliant banking activities; the full text is not contained in this node's context.

The earlier Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking issued by SAMA circular No. 43038156 dated 27-04-1443H (02-12-2021G). It has been updated and superseded by the current Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking, so it is relevant mainly for historical or transitional analysis of obligations applicable before the new framework took effect. It bound the same population of SAMA-licensed domestic banks conducting Shari'ah compliant banking activities.

Field-level reporting specification (Table 3, evolutive/common data) for collateral attributes of OTC derivative contracts reported to a trade repository under SAMA's OTC derivatives reporting and risk mitigation requirements (version 4.0, September 2025). It sets the permitted values and formats for collateralisation status, portfolio-basis flag and portfolio code, initial and variation margin posted/received, excess collateral, and the associated ISO currency codes. It binds reporting counterparties subject to the SAMA trade repository reporting obligation.

SAMA's recalibrated standardised interest rate shock scenarios for interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB): six prescribed shocks (parallel up/down, steepener, flattener, short rates up/down) for EVE and two for NII, applied per currency where the bank has material positions. It contains the currency-specific absolute shock sizes in basis points (parallel, short, long), the parameterisation formulas, and a zero floor on post-shock rates that SAMA may revise. It binds banks measuring and reporting IRRBB.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book

data.summary: Defines the parallel shock scenario within SAMA's standardised IRRBB shock set: a constant upward or downward shift applied across all time buckets using the currency-specific parallel shock size in Table 1 (e.g. SAR 275 bp, USD 200 bp). It is one of the six EVE scenarios and is subject to the zero floor on post-shock rates. Applies to banks measuring IRRBB per material currency.

Defines the short rate shock scenario in SAMA's standardised IRRBB framework: a shock largest at the shortest tenor midpoint that decays exponentially towards zero at the longest tenor via a shaping scalar with decay parameter x = 4 (unless SAMA determines otherwise). Includes a worked example converting a 100 bp short shock to 41.7 bp at a 3.5-year tenor midpoint. Applies to banks calculating IRRBB per material currency.

Defines the long rate shock in SAMA's standardised IRRBB framework: greatest at the longest tenor midpoint, derived as one minus the short-rate shaping scalar, and used only as an input to the rotational (steepener/flattener) scenarios rather than as a standalone prescribed scenario. Relevant to banks computing the six EVE shock scenarios per material currency.

Defines the two rotational IRRBB scenarios — steepener (short rates down, long rates up) and flattener (short rates up, long rates down) — as weighted combinations of the absolute short and long rate shocks at each tenor midpoint, with worked examples at a 3.5-year midpoint. Post-shock rates are floored at zero. Binds banks applying SAMA's standardised IRRBB shock scenarios per material currency.

This is the parent node for SAMA's Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules (First Issue, 1446H/2025), issued by the Deputy Governor for Market Conduct and circulated to all SAMA-supervised financial institutions. It sets the minimum mandatory obligations for implementing TFS arising from UN Security Council resolutions on counter-terrorism/terrorist financing and on preventing the proliferation and financing of weapons of mass destruction, and it supersedes the earlier SAMA circulars on those UNSCR implementation mechanisms. It binds financial institutions subject to SAMA regulation and supervision, requires the Rules to be presented to the board (or equivalent for non-joint-stock entities), and covers definitions, governance, screening, list management, alerts, freezing/unfreezing, record keeping, training and closing provisions.
lookup_terms: UN Security Council resolutions implementation mechanism

data.summary: Chapter Three of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, covering screening procedures and controls that SAMA-supervised financial institutions must apply against sanctions lists. It is the operative source for when and against whom screening must be performed under the TFS regime (as distinct from general AML/CTF customer due diligence). Binding on all financial institutions within SAMA's regulatory and supervisory perimeter.

Chapter Four of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, on management of sanctions lists — the lists issued under the UNSCR implementation mechanisms for counter-terrorism/TF and for preventing WMD proliferation and its financing. It governs how financial institutions must obtain, update and maintain those lists as the reference data for their TFS obligations. Binding on all SAMA-supervised financial institutions.

Chapter Five of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, addressing how screening alerts must be handled, reviewed and escalated within the financial institution, including reporting matches to SAMA. It links the screening function to the freezing obligation and to SAMA's designated notification channel for immediate reporting of matches. Binding on all SAMA-supervised financial institutions.

Chapter Six of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, setting out freezing and unfreezing procedures for funds and other assets of designated persons and entities, including the prohibition on making funds or assets available directly or indirectly. It is the core enforceable action step of the TFS regime and defines the scope of "funds/assets" broadly (including virtual assets and any derived income). Binding on all SAMA-supervised financial institutions.

Record-keeping node drawing on Chapter Seven of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules together with a second SAMA instrument, covering the obligation to retain records evidencing screening, alerts, freezing actions and related TFS decisions. Useful for retention-period and evidential-availability questions, and for comparing TFS record retention with AML/CTF record-keeping duties. Binding on SAMA-supervised financial institutions.

This node captures the Basel Committee-derived standardised interest rate shock scenarios that SAMA applies to interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), including the recalibrated currency-specific shock sizes (parallel, short and long) set out in the shock table. It requires banks to run six prescribed scenarios for economic value of equity and two for net interest income, per currency in which the bank holds material positions. It binds banks supervised by SAMA for IRRBB measurement and reporting purposes.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book

data.summary: A SAMA circular (Arabic) reiterating that supervised financial institutions must supply the National Address when submitting requests to postal/courier providers for delivery of documents linked to customers' financial products and services. It follows a Transport General Authority decision obliging postal service providers to refuse shipments not addressed with the National Address from 1 January 2026, and reaffirms earlier SAMA instructions that the National Address registered with Saudi Post (SPL) is the primary reference for customer addresses. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA.

A SAMA circular (Arabic) directing all financing entities to share individuals' residential real estate finance data with the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH), in line with forthcoming SAMA guidance and templates. It is grounded in the SAMA Law, Credit Information Law, Banking Control Law and Finance Companies Control Law, and is aimed at credit-risk transparency and credit assessment; compliance with the Personal Data Protection Law and other regulators' instructions is expressly preserved. It binds banks, real estate finance companies and credit information companies, effective from its date.

First issue (Jumada II 1447 / Nov 2025) of SAMA's General Rules for Hosting and Sponsoring Events, setting minimum requirements for financial institutions that host or sponsor conferences, forums, seminars and similar events inside or outside the Kingdom. It covers definitions, a board-approved events policy, documentation and annual reporting to the board, professional-conduct duties of representatives (confidentiality, avoiding political or sensitive topics, no unauthorised commitments), and due diligence on event content, participants, sponsors and speakers. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA; it does not apply to temporary offices opened for marketing or product display, which fall under separate SAMA instructions. Superseded by the second issue.
lookup_terms: General Rules for Hosting and Sponsoring Events

data.summary: Second issue (Safar 1448 / July 2026) of SAMA's General Rules for Participation in Events, updating and replacing the first issue circulated in 1447. It broadens scope to any form of participation in any event for any purpose — hosting in whole or part, sponsoring, or presence through a temporary pavilion, in or outside the Kingdom, directly or via a third party — and retains requirements for a board-approved policy, documentation and annual board reporting, conduct obligations for representatives, and risk assessment/due diligence on content, participants, sponsors and speakers. It binds all financial institutions licensed and supervised by SAMA.
lookup_terms: General Rules for Participation in Events

data.summary: Defined-term node from the second issue of the events rules: a "temporary pavilion" is a space occupied at an event for the purpose of introducing and marketing the financial institution. Presence through such a pavilion is expressly brought within the definition of participation in an event, but is exempted from the requirement to obtain SAMA's no-objection. The exemption applies to financial institutions licensed by SAMA, which remain subject to the policy, documentation, conduct and due diligence requirements of the rules.

This node points to the training and awareness chapter (Chapter Eight) of SAMA's Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules (First Edition, 1447H/2025), which set minimum obligations for implementing TFS relating to terrorism financing and proliferation financing of weapons of mass destruction. The Rules are mandatory on all financial institutions regulated and supervised by SAMA and replace the earlier SAMA circulars on UNSC implementation mechanisms. The training/awareness component sits alongside chapters on governance, screening, list management, alert handling and escalation, freezing/unfreezing, and record keeping.

This node covers the general/closing provisions of SAMA's Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules requiring financial institutions to monitor the official Saudi channels for UNSC-derived sanctions lists and implementation mechanisms — the Permanent Committee for Combating Terrorism and its Financing (State Security) and the MOFA Permanent Committee on Chapter VII UNSC resolutions. It confirms the Rules are a minimum standard that does not displace other SAMA instructions or applicable laws, and that they take effect upon publication on SAMA's website. Binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions.
lookup_terms: Permanent Committee for Combating Terrorism and its Financing

data.summary: A duplicate instance of SAMA's Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules (First Edition, 1447H/2025), issued under cover of a circular from the Deputy Governor for Market Conduct. The Rules set the minimum obligations for applying targeted financial sanctions on terrorism financing and WMD proliferation financing — including asset freezing, prohibition on making funds or other assets available directly or indirectly to designated persons, screening controls, list management, alerts and escalation, and record keeping — and supersede the listed prior circulars. Mandatory for all financial institutions supervised by SAMA, which must present the Rules to the board (or equivalent) and allocate responsibilities across the board, senior management and relevant units.

The Financial Institutions Services Tariff Guide (First Edition, Rajab 1447H / 2025), issued by SAMA under the Central Bank Law, sets binding limits and criteria for fees charged for services and products, including a schedule of tariffs for basic services to individual customers and criteria for setting product/service fees. It defines terms such as Financial Institution, Customer, documented channels, identification certificate, debt-confirmation document, account statement and clearance letter. It binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions and overrides any conflicting provisions, effective 90 days after publication.

This node covers the amended regulatory texts on administrative fees issued with the Tariff Guide circular: Article 9 of the Consumer Finance Regulations, Rule 1 of the specific conduct rules in the Principles and Rules for Financial Institution Customer Protection, and Article 11.1 of the standard individual consumer finance contract. The amendments require financiers/banks and finance companies to follow SAMA's administrative-fee instructions, bar deduction of administrative fees before contract signing (with a real-estate valuation exception after preliminary mortgage approval), and cap total costs and administrative fees at the lower of SAR 5,000 or 1% of the finance amount, excluding taxes.
lookup_terms: Principles and Rules for Financial Institution Customer Protection

data.summary: This node addresses the Consumer Finance Regulations (Rules) as amended by the Tariff Guide circular, specifically the article obliging finance providers to comply with SAMA's instructions on administrative fees when granting finance. It is the anchor for how fee caps and fee-timing restrictions interact with consumer finance contracts and customer protection conduct rules. It binds banks and finance companies supervised by SAMA that grant consumer finance to individuals.

SAMA's Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law (as amended by Governor's decision, Rajab 1447/December 2025), issued with a covering circular that also repeals the Microfinance Activity Rules and the Micro Consumer Finance Companies Rules and gives finance companies a rectification period. It sets the core definitions (financing activities, finance contract, instalment, term cost, total cost of financing, financing amount, APR, board, senior management, exposure, large exposure, controlling interest) and the licensing, prudential, governance and conduct framework for finance companies, including dedicated licence categories for micro consumer finance, BNPL (deferred payment), debt-based crowdfunding and microfinance companies. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom, SAMA-licensed digital brokerage firms and licensed debt collection entities.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law
اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مراقبة شركات التمويل

data.summary: Duplicate/parallel version of the amended Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law with the same covering circular repealing the microfinance and micro consumer finance rules. Contains the definitions chapter and general provisions establishing SAMA's regulation and supervision of the finance sector, and the licence-specific activity definitions (micro consumer finance, deferred payment/BNPL, debt-based crowdfunding, microfinance). Binds licensed finance companies and related SAMA-licensed entities in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: Finance Companies Control Law implementing regulation

data.summary: SAMA's Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities (amended version, Rajab 1447/December 2025), issued under the SAMA Law and the Finance Companies Control Law and its implementing regulation. They define finance support activities (activities supporting or complementary to financing, expressly including digital brokerage for finance entities but excluding debt collection for finance entities), and set licence application requirements, minimum capital (SAR 2 million for digital brokerage), fit-and-proper/management conditions, conduct of activity, and supervision and compliance provisions. They bind any person seeking or holding a SAMA licence to carry on a finance support activity, notably digital brokerage platforms.
lookup_terms: Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities
قواعد الترخيص للنشاطات المساندة لنشاط التمويل

data.summary: Amendment version of the Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities, circulated to SAMA-licensed digital brokerage firms under a Governor's decision approving the amendments. Same substantive content: definition and scope of finance support activities, licensing conditions and documents, capital thresholds, management eligibility, conduct-of-activity, supervisory and final provisions. Binds licensed and applicant finance support entities, in particular digital brokerage platforms connecting customers to finance entities.

SAMA circular prohibiting finance entities from requesting promissory notes or any commercial paper from individual customers when offering credit card financing products, referencing the existing instructions on finance entities' dealings with promissory notes and the responsible retail finance principles. Requires internal policies, procedures and controls to be updated, effective 1 February 2026, and a remediation plan submitted to SAMA's Consumer Protection Supervision Department covering return or cancellation of previously obtained instruments, with execution capped at a set period. Binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular on outsourcing debt collection for banks and finance companies, which cancels the earlier circulars that had restricted such outsourcing to SAMA-licensed debt collection entities and set transitional deadlines. Going forward, collection may be outsourced to entities meeting the requirements set out in the applicable laws, regulations and instructions after obtaining SAMA's no-objection letter, without a standing requirement that the counterparty be SAMA-licensed, and without prejudice to the outsourcing rules and other relevant instructions. Binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom and SAMA-licensed debt collection entities.

SAMA circular (Arabic) transmitting the first edition of the Financial Institutions Services Tariff Guide and notifying amendments to three fee-related provisions: the administrative-fee article of the updated Consumer Finance Regulations, the relevant special conduct rule in the Principles and Rules for Financial Institution Customer Protection, and the costs/fees clause of the Standard Consumer Finance Contract for Individuals. It governs what fees supervised financial institutions may charge for services and products, defines core terms (Financial Institution, Customer, documented channels, identification certificate, debt/liability-clearance documents, account statement) and caps total administrative fees on financing. It binds all entities under SAMA supervision, effective within the stated grace period from publication, and supersedes conflicting provisions.
lookup_terms: Principles and Rules for Financial Institution Customer Protection

data.summary: Duplicate publication of the SAMA circular and first-edition Financial Institutions Services Tariff Guide, together with the amended texts on administrative fees in the Consumer Finance Regulations, the customer protection conduct rules, and the standard individual consumer finance contract. Content covers definitions, tariffs for basic retail services, criteria for setting service and product fees, and the cap on administrative fees when granting finance. Binding on all financial institutions supervised by SAMA when charging customers.
lookup_terms: free of charge basic services individuals
administrative fee 5,000 SAR / 1% of finance amount

data.summary: Amended Executive Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law issued by SAMA, together with the covering circular that repeals the Microfinance Activity Rules and the Micro Consumer Finance Companies Rules and gives finance companies a rectification period. The extract covers Part One definitions (financing laws, finance contract, instalment, term cost, total cost of financing, finance amount, APR, board and senior management, exposure, large exposure, controlling interest) and SAMA's supervisory mandate over the finance sector. It binds licensed finance companies, SAMA-licensed digital intermediation companies and debt collection entities acting for financiers.
lookup_terms: Executive Regulation Finance Companies Control Law
اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مراقبة شركات التمويل

data.summary: Licensing dimension of the amended Executive Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law: which financing activities require a SAMA licence and how activity-specific licences (micro consumer finance, deferred payment/BNPL, debt-based crowdfunding, microfinance) are defined and delimited to a single activity. The supplied extract contains only the covering circular and the definitions chapter, so specific licensing conditions, applications and approvals must be read in the full regulation. Binds companies seeking or holding a finance licence in the Kingdom.

Capital-adequacy dimension of the amended Executive Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law, covering minimum paid-up capital by financing activity and related prudential limits such as large exposure measured against paid-up capital and reserves. The provided extract shows only the circular and definitions, so the numeric capital thresholds must be verified in the full regulation text. Applies to all finance companies licensed by SAMA, including those adjusting status after the repeal of the microfinance and micro consumer finance rules.
lookup_terms: large exposure 10% of capital and reserves

data.summary: Node on microfinance and micro consumer finance activities under the amended Executive Regulation: the standalone Microfinance Activity Rules and the Micro Consumer Finance Companies Rules were repealed and these activities are now regulated within the Executive Regulation itself, with the applicable controls set out in its Article Nine. Definitions distinguish a microfinance company, a micro consumer finance company and a deferred payment (BNPL) company, each licensed for that single activity. Existing licensees were given a transition period to rectify their position.
lookup_terms: micro consumer finance التمويل الاستهلاكي المصغر
deferred payment BNPL activity no term cost

data.summary: A SAMA circular that raises the ceiling in paragraph (1) of Article 22 of the Rules for Regulating Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) Companies on total outstanding financing per individual consumer, from five thousand to ten thousand Saudi riyals, exercising the Central Bank's express power in that article to vary the amount. It confirms that all other provisions and requirements — notably the debt burden ratios under the Responsible Lending Principles for Individuals — continue to apply. It is addressed to banks, finance companies and BNPL companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA circular announcing the decision to abolish the licensing requirement for carrying out the activity of collecting debts owed to finance entities, following approved amendments to the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law and to the Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities. Entities that previously obtained a SAMA licence or initial approval for this activity must comply with the relevant legal requirements to update the activity recorded in their commercial registration. It is directed to banks, finance companies and SAMA-licensed debt collection entities.
lookup_terms: Finance Companies Control Law implementing regulation

data.summary: A SAMA circular extending mandatory application of the Key Principles of Governance for financial institutions supervised by SAMA to all finance companies and payment service providers. It prescribes a compliance pathway: a current-state governance gap assessment, a board/managers-approved roadmap, submission of both to SAMA's compliance mailbox within the stated deadline, and full compliance within one year of the circular or by the end of the sitting board's term, whichever is earlier, with SAMA retaining discretion to extend on justified grounds.
lookup_terms: board of directors term compliance deadline

data.summary: SAMA's Guide on assessing business risks related to money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, issued under the SAMA Law, the AML Law and the Law on Combating Terrorism Crimes and its Financing. It sets the minimum factors a financial institution must consider when conducting its enterprise-wide business risk assessment, with chapters on definitions, governance and institutional responsibility, the stages of the assessment, and final provisions, and defines terms such as business risk, risk-based approach, inherent risk, mitigating measures, residual risk, risk appetite, customer/geographic/delivery-channel and emerging risks. It applies to all financial institutions supervised by SAMA and is expressly non-exhaustive and not a single mandated methodology, without limiting other AML/CTF/CPF obligations.

A duplicate publication of SAMA's Guide on assessing business risks related to money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, with the same covering circular and content. It sets the minimum factors and controls for a financial institution's business-wide risk assessment, defines the core risk terminology (business risk, risk-based approach, inherent and residual risk, risk appetite, customer, geographic, delivery-channel and emerging risks), and covers governance responsibility and the assessment stages. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA's supervision from the date of publication on SAMA's website and does not displace other AML/CTF/CPF obligations.

An extract from SAMA's oversight framework for payment systems and their operators, stating that SAMA is the competent authority for regulating, supervising and overseeing payment systems and operators in the Kingdom under the Payment Systems Law and its implementing regulation. Oversight is described as monitoring and assessing existing and planned systems against safety and efficiency objectives and requiring changes where needed, with standards set by reference to the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI). It is relevant to operators of payment systems and participants subject to SAMA oversight.

This node sits under a SAMA circular prohibiting banks and finance companies from taking promissory notes or any commercial paper from individual (retail) customers when providing credit card finance products, issued without prejudice to existing obligations including the Responsible Lending Principles for Individuals. Financiers must update internal policies, procedures and controls, comply from 1 February 2026, submit a remediation plan to SAMA's Consumer Protection Supervision Department within the stated period, and return or cancel previously obtained non-compliant notes within the execution deadline. It binds all banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

This node covers SAMA's directive extending the Key Governance Principles for Financial Institutions Supervised by SAMA to all finance companies and payment service providers. Firms must perform a gap assessment of current governance arrangements, adopt a board/managers-approved roadmap, send the assessment and plan to SAMA's stated compliance address within the set period, and achieve full compliance within one year of the circular or by the end of the sitting board's term, whichever is earlier, with SAMA able to extend on justified grounds.
lookup_terms: board of directors term compliance roadmap

data.summary: This node is SAMA's supervisory (oversight) framework for payment systems and their operators, grounded in the Payments and Payment Services Law and its Implementing Regulation. It sets out SAMA as the competent authority for regulating, supervising and overseeing payment systems, defines oversight objectives of safety and efficiency, and applies international standards (PFMIs) through ongoing monitoring, self-assessment, supervisory assessment and change requirements. It binds licensed/designated payment system operators, including systemically important and unclassified systems.

Reference node for the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI), the BIS standard-setting body that, with IOSCO, issued the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures and the related disclosure framework. In the SAMA payment systems oversight framework it is the source of the standards SAMA applies when setting controls, assessing risk and requiring operator self-assessment and public disclosure. It is a definitional/standard-source node rather than a directly binding obligation.
lookup_terms: Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures
لجنة المدفوعات والبنى التحتية للأسواق المالية

data.summary: Reference node for IOSCO, the International Organization of Securities Commissions, co-issuer with CPMI of the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (April 2012, as amended) and the FMI Disclosure Framework. Within SAMA's payment systems oversight framework these joint standards form part of the regulatory framework operators must observe, including the disclosure framework treated as binding on payment systems and other financial market infrastructures.

Defined-term node for the CPSS-IOSCO (CPMI-IOSCO) Disclosure Framework for Financial Market Infrastructures, the document setting standard public disclosure requirements for FMIs including payment systems. Under SAMA's oversight framework, a systemically important payment system operator must publicly disclose its PFMI self-assessment summary in line with this framework after obtaining SAMA's no-objection letter, and the framework is listed among the requirements binding payment systems and other FMIs.
lookup_terms: إطار الإفصاح للبنى التحتية للأسواق المالية

data.summary: SAMA guidance setting out the procedural and documentary requirements for applying for a payment service provider licence under the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services. It explains the two-stage process (in-principle approval, then final licensing) and the four licence categories: micro and major electronic money institutions (e-wallet) and micro and major payment institutions. It binds prospective applicants seeking to provide payment services in the Kingdom and is to be read alongside the Implementing Regulation and other SAMA rules.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services

data.summary: SAMA circular requiring supervised financial institutions to establish technical linkage with the Ministry of Commerce's Wathiq service to verify beneficial owner identity data disclosed by companies. Institutions must observe the applicable conditions, notify the Ministry via the platform where a company has not disclosed a beneficial owner or where discrepancies emerge from their due diligence, and notify SAMA of implementation difficulties. It applies to all financial institutions under SAMA supervision, without prejudice to STR obligations and personal data protection requirements.
lookup_terms: Beneficial Owner Rules Ministry of Commerce

data.summary: SAMA circular exempting from judicial seizure the cheque amounts payable to families of martyrs, following arrangements with the Ministry of Justice and building on the Enforcement Law's list of non-seizable assets and SAMA's updated exempt-amounts list. It sets the exempt proportion available to the customer and conditions release on presentation of a notary-issued declaration in the attached form. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular reaffirming that all supervised financial institutions must comply with the Ministry of Interior / Civil Defense regulation on the duties of the fire safety, prevention and protection officer. It highlights appointing a qualified safety officer, maintaining and periodically inspecting fire safety systems, preparing and testing evacuation and emergency plans, and documenting and retaining related records. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision.

SAMA circular directing finance entities carrying out vehicle finance leasing to verify economic total loss determinations for individually leased vehicles by relying on reports from valuation firms licensed by the Saudi Authority for Accredited Valuers, in applying the Finance Lease Law provision on destruction of the leased asset. It also requires the lessor, on notice of damage, to exercise due care with all parties so the lessee can continue benefiting from the vehicle before it is treated as an economic total loss. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: comprehensive insurance controls for leased vehicles

data.summary: SAMA circular requiring non-bank financial institutions to notify SAMA at least five business days before conducting an investment round, submitting the timetable, purpose, size, effect on ownership structure and financial position, the type and structure of the instrument, and any other supporting or requested documents. Notification does not displace other obligations, including obtaining SAMA's prior no-objection where required. It binds finance companies, payment service companies, exchange houses and SAMA-licensed finance support entities.

SAMA rules issued under the Real Estate Finance Law setting the licensing, prudential and governance framework for real estate refinancing companies (joint-stock companies licensed to refinance real estate financiers and trade rights arising from real estate finance contracts). Chapters cover capital adequacy and liquidity, governance, permitted activities, internal organisation, outsourcing, risk management, compliance, internal audit, SAMA supervision and the secondary market. Binds SAMA-licensed real estate refinancing companies, with services normally directed at real estate financiers (banks and finance companies licensed for real estate finance); dealing with non-financiers or issuing securities requires a SAMA no-objection letter.

SAMA rules issued under the Finance Companies Control Law regulating Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) companies: licensing procedure and conditions, internal organisation, conduct-of-activity rules, supervision and compliance. The defined BNPL activity is financing a Customer's purchase of goods or services from Stores at no term cost to the Customer; the activity may not be carried on without a SAMA licence. The covering circular exempts BNPL companies and other finance companies conducting the activity from the DBR/affordability ratios in the Responsible Lending Principles for aggregate financing up to SAR 5,000/threshold stated, without affecting other obligations, including Article 19 of these Rules.

SAMA controls (first issue, 2023) setting the minimum standards and procedures financial institutions must follow when advertising any product or service, issued under the Saudi Central Bank Law's consumer-protection and rule-making powers. Defines Advertisement, Medium, Customer, Consumer and Products and Services, and requires due care over advertising content alongside sector laws and other content-regulation authorities. Applies to all financial institutions supervised by SAMA whenever they advertise.

SAMA rules (2018) governing outsourcing by finance companies, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation. They define outsourcing and service provider, distinguish material from non-material functions (including any arrangement involving sharing, transferring, processing or storing beneficiary data), and require a board-approved annually updated outsourcing policy, risk assessment at contracting and renewal, due diligence on the provider's licences and qualifications, data confidentiality and retrieval/destruction safeguards, record keeping, and monitoring. Responsibility remains with the finance company, and SAMA and the external auditor retain access to the provider's information and premises.

The Finance Companies Control Law (Royal Decree M/51) is the primary statute for licensing and supervising finance companies in Saudi Arabia and the legal basis on which SAMA issues subordinate rules such as the BNPL Rules. It confers on SAMA the power to license, regulate and supervise finance activity and to issue implementing rules and instructions. Binds all finance companies, including BNPL companies and other entities conducting finance activities in the Kingdom.

The Law of Payments and Payment Services (Royal Decree M/21) makes SAMA the competent authority for regulating, supervising and overseeing payment systems and their operators in the Kingdom, together with its Implementing Regulation. Oversight covers existing and planned systems, assessment against safety and efficiency objectives, and standards aligned with the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures. Binds payment system operators and participants subject to SAMA oversight.
lookup_terms: Law of Payments and Payment Services

data.summary: SAMA circular, issued under the supervisory-instruction power in the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business, directing exchange centres located in Makkah, Madinah, King Abdulaziz International Airport and the Hajj City in Jeddah to raise their operational readiness ahead of the Ramadan and Hajj seasons. An annex sets minimum service standards, including adequate Saudi riyal cash and denominations, extended days and hours over the seasons and Eids, queue and crowd management, staff identification and shift schedules, visible exchange-rate boards linked to live rates, customer-rights signage, availability of card/electronic payment acceptance, functioning CCTV and storage, sufficient security personnel, modern counting/counterfeit-detection machines with prescribed handling of counterfeits, bilingual mapping of the branch location, and notification back to SAMA. It binds only the licensed exchange centres in those pilgrimage-related locations.

SAMA circular publishing the annual list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), designated by reference to the earlier SAMA circular setting out the D-SIB identification methodology and associated capital requirements, based on year-end data. It names four banks (Saudi National Bank, Al Rajhi Bank, Riyad Bank and Saudi Awwal Bank) as D-SIBs for the stated year. It binds the designated banks, which become subject to the D-SIB capital surcharge and related supervisory expectations.

Node covering the Anti-Money Laundering Law regime as applied by SAMA, together with associated SAMA instruments — notably the guide on assessing business risks related to money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing. The guide sets the minimum factors, criteria and controls a financial institution must consider when performing its enterprise-wide business risk assessment (inherent risk, customer/product/delivery-channel/geographic and emerging risks, mitigating controls, residual risk and risk appetite), without imposing a single mandatory methodology and without limiting obligations under the AML Law, the Law of Combating Terrorism Crimes and its Financing, and related regulations. It binds all financial institutions licensed, regulated and supervised by SAMA.

Node on the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMIs) issued by CPMI-IOSCO as adopted in SAMA's oversight framework for payment systems. It explains SAMA's principles-based oversight activities — ongoing monitoring, operator self-assessment against the PFMIs, and independent supervisory assessment — and the scope covering the national payment system, systems operated in or across the borders of the Kingdom, systemically important payment systems (SIPS) and non-classified systems. Under the Implementing Regulation, SIPS operators must self-assess at least annually or on material operational change or SAMA request, and must publicly disclose the self-assessment summary in line with the CPMI-IOSCO disclosure framework only after a SAMA no-objection letter; non-classified operators self-assess on the periodicity set in their licence or by SAMA. It binds payment system operators.

Concept node for the Payment Systems and Services Law and its Implementing Regulation, which make SAMA the competent authority for the regulation, supervision and oversight of payment systems and their operators in the Kingdom. The Law underpins SAMA's oversight mandate to monitor and assess existing and planned systems against safety and efficiency objectives, to set controls and standards aligned with the CPMI-IOSCO PFMIs, and to require changes where needed. It binds payment system operators and, through the Regulation, licensed payment service providers.
lookup_terms: safety and efficiency of payment systems

data.summary: SAMA circular on the outsourcing of debt collection by banks and finance companies to finance-entity debt collection firms, issued under the SAMA Law, the Finance Companies Control Law and the Banking Control Law. It cancels the earlier circulars that had restricted such outsourcing to debt collection entities licensed by SAMA and that had set transition periods for entities holding initial approval; going forward, outsourcing may be to firms meeting the requirements set in the applicable laws, regulations and instructions, after obtaining SAMA's no-objection letter to contract with a debt collection provider, without a requirement that the provider be SAMA-licensed. Compliance with the outsourcing rules and other related instructions remains mandatory. It binds banks, finance companies and licensed finance-entity debt collection firms operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: licensing rules for finance support activities

data.summary: A SAMA circular easing the terms on which real estate financiers may sell residential real estate finance portfolios to the Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company (SRC): sale is permitted after at least one month from the financing grant date or one month from receipt of the first instalment from the beneficiary, whichever is earlier, with a shortened recourse period on the originating financier. It also exempts portfolios sold to SRC from the prior SAMA no-objection requirement under the rules on disposal of finance assets, subject to continued compliance with statutory periods for the disposed contracts and notification to SAMA within five business days of the final sale contract. Binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom and SRC.
lookup_terms: residential real estate finance portfolio sale
disposal of finance assets or rights arising therefrom

data.summary: SAMA's technical sorting instructions for the sixth issue of Saudi banknotes, setting uniform fitness criteria, counting/sorting controls, counterfeit and material-defect handling, quality levels, density measurement, sensor and quality-control requirements, and follow-up obligations. It applies to "financial institutions" as defined for these purposes — banks, cash centres and exchange centres supervised by SAMA — with staged effective dates by denomination and a requirement to coordinate with SAMA to obtain specimen notes for machine programming.

A SAMA circular directing supervised financial institutions to use the National Center for Non-Profit Sector Development's electronic service for inquiring about beneficial owner information of associations and non-profit foundations, as part of satisfying customer due diligence obligations. Where a beneficial owner is undisclosed by the association/foundation, or where discrepancies appear in the beneficial owner data, the institution must apply its CDD measures and consider suspicious transaction reporting, consistent with the AML Law, the CTF Law and their implementing regulations, and without breaching the Personal Data Protection Law and SAMA instructions; the Center is also to be notified.
lookup_terms: National Center for Non-Profit Sector Development NCNP

data.summary: Updated SAMA rules requiring disclosure of prices of financing and savings products, replacing the earlier circulars on the same subject. They define and standardise APR, AER, credit card purchase rate, finance amount, maturity, monthly instalment, minimum payment, property market value, LTV, early repayment charges and deposit amount, and prescribe disclosure table formats for individuals and for micro and small enterprises. They bind all SAMA-licensed banks and finance companies, with a short implementation deadline and a confirmation report to SAMA.
lookup_terms: micro and small enterprises disclosure tables

data.summary: SAMA's Responsible Retail Financing Principles (issued 1439H/2018), setting affordability, disclosure and conduct expectations for financing granted to natural-person customers. They define financier, customer, finance amount, term cost (fixed and variable), total amount payable, monthly credit obligations, gross salary and gross monthly income, and are read alongside the Banking Control Law, Finance Companies Control Law, Real Estate Finance and Finance Lease Laws, consumer finance controls, collection controls and the customer protection principles. They bind banks and finance companies licensed to carry out financing activities.
lookup_terms: debt burden ratio / monthly credit obligations
total amount payable by the customer

data.summary: Instructions issued under the Finance Companies Control Law approving and governing the practice of digital brokerage activity — intermediation between customers and financiers via an electronic platform — by entities licensed by SAMA under the rules for licensing finance support activities. They set minimum technical and organisational requirements, customer identification and verification of submitted information and documents from reliable independent sources, record-keeping, conflict-of-interest management, disclosure obligations, and mandatory contract terms between the licensed entity and both the customer and the financier. They bind SAMA-licensed finance support entities, and are relevant to banks and finance companies acting as financiers.

Node anchored on the Real Estate Finance Law (Royal Decree M/50) as the statutory basis SAMA invokes when issuing subordinate rules for the real estate finance sector; the attached source is SAMA's circular and Rules for Regulating Real Estate Refinance Companies, approved by Governor decision and applicable to SAMA-licensed refinance companies. It defines the core terms of the sector (real estate financier, real estate finance contract, beneficiary, primary and secondary market, refinancing activity) and covers capital adequacy and liquidity, governance, permitted activities, internal organisation, outsourcing, risk management, compliance, internal audit, SAMA supervision and secondary-market dealings. It binds licensed real estate refinance companies, and is addressed for information to banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

Node anchored on the Saudi Central Bank Law (Royal Decree M/36) as the source of SAMA's supervisory mandate; the attached source is SAMA's circular issuing the updated Oversight Framework for Payment Systems and their Operators, which replaces the earlier framework for payment and financial settlement systems. It is issued under the Law of Payments and Payment Services (M/16) and its Implementing Regulation, and sets the framework's scope, classification of systemically important versus non-classified payment systems, supervisory methodology (self-assessment and supervisory assessment), supervisory activities, operator obligations and the applicable PFMIs. It binds payment systems and licensed payment system operators (PSOs) in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: PFMIs / مبادئ البنى التحتية للأسواق المالية

data.summary: SAMA's Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions (third edition), issued under the Saudi Central Bank Law and replacing the earlier governance principles for banks. It sets definitions (financial institution, board, executive management, executive/non-executive/independent member, relatives, major shareholders, related parties) and seven principles covering board qualifications, composition and appointment, board and executive management responsibilities, board committees, shareholder rights, and disclosure and transparency, with an annex on money exchange sector governance. It binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions other than insurance and reinsurance companies — including banks, finance and real estate refinance companies, exchange houses, payment and fintech companies, and credit bureaus — as mandatory from the stated effective date.

Principle 1 of SAMA's Key Principles of Governance, addressing the qualifications required of board members of SAMA-supervised financial institutions. It works together with the framework's definitions of executive, non-executive and independent members, including the listed independence-disqualifying factors (ownership thresholds, kinship, recent employment, remuneration and credit-exposure limits, tenure of more than nine years). It binds the financial institution and its nominating/appointing bodies when selecting and assessing board and committee members.

Principle 3 of SAMA's Key Principles of Governance, setting out the responsibilities of the board of directors of a SAMA-supervised financial institution — the body ultimately accountable for strategy, oversight of executive management, risk and control arrangements. It should be read with the framework's definitions and with Principles 2 (composition and appointment), 4 (executive management) and 5 (board committees). It binds the board collectively and its individual members in institutions within scope (all SAMA-supervised entities except insurance and reinsurance).

Principle 4 of SAMA's Key Principles of Governance, addressing the responsibilities of executive (senior) management — the persons charged with running the financial institution's day-to-day business and proposing and implementing strategic decisions. It delineates management's duties relative to the board's oversight role under Principle 3. It binds senior executives of SAMA-supervised financial institutions other than insurers and reinsurers.

Concept node for the board-level Audit Committee as required under SAMA governance instruments, principally the Key Principles of Governance for Financial Institutions subject to SAMA supervision (third edition) and related sector governance rules. It covers the committee's composition, independence conditions for members, and its mandate over internal and external audit, financial reporting integrity and internal control oversight. It binds boards of SAMA-supervised financial institutions (banks, finance and real estate refinance companies, exchange businesses, payment and fintech companies, credit information companies), with insurance/reinsurance excluded from the governance principles' definition of financial institution.
lookup_terms: Key Principles of Governance for Financial Institutions

data.summary: Concept node for the board Risk Committee under SAMA's Key Principles of Governance for Financial Institutions and related governance instructions. It concerns the committee's formation from the board, its role in advising on risk appetite and strategy and in overseeing the risk management function independently of executive management. It applies to boards of SAMA-supervised financial institutions within the scope of the governance principles (banks, finance companies, exchange, payments/fintech, credit information companies; insurers excluded).

Concept node for the Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) established by the board under SAMA governance and compensation instructions. It governs board and executive nominations, assessment of member independence against the disqualifying criteria in the governance principles, succession, and the design and review of remuneration policy. It binds boards of SAMA-supervised financial institutions falling within the scope of the governance principles.

SAMA instructions setting minimum requirements for how financiers deal with promissory notes, issued under the Central Bank Law and the Finance Companies Control Law and effective from the date stated in the covering circular. They require a board-approved policy covering steps before and during court enforcement of a promissory note, documentation (financing contract, matured note, proof of default and of contact with the customer), designated responsible departments and approval authority, and compliance obligations where enforcement is outsourced to a third party. They bind banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom and operate without prejudice to related SAMA instructions on collection, standard contracts, outsourcing and blank promissory notes.
lookup_terms: تعليمات تعامل جهات التمويل مع السند لأمر

data.summary: SAMA instructions on services provided to persons with disabilities by financial institutions, aimed at financial inclusion, equal access and removal of physical and behavioural barriers so customers can manage their finances independently and privately. Requirements include establishing a dedicated administrative unit, accessible built environment across premises and branches, accessible self-service and electronic channels, fairness and transparency in dealings, and financial education for this group. They apply to all financial institutions supervised by SAMA, including banks, finance companies, insurers/reinsurers, credit information companies, exchange businesses and payment companies.

SAMA principles on conduct and work ethics in financial institutions, setting the minimum standards of professional behaviour, integrity, transparency, objectivity and loyalty expected of institution personnel. Topics include stakeholder dealings, AML/CTF and suspicious transactions, anti-bribery and corruption, gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, confidentiality and disclosure, misuse of inside information and market manipulation, whistleblowing on actual or potential violations, remuneration and incentives, and consequences of non-compliance. They bind all personnel — board and committee members, executives, employees, contractors, consultants and third-party staff — of SAMA-supervised banks, finance and leasing registration companies, insurers/reinsurers and credit information companies, with the board required to adopt a conforming policy.

Domain 1 of SAMA's Financial Sector Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles, setting the baseline expectations for planning, collecting, processing, analysing and disseminating threat intelligence around the intelligence lifecycle. It covers foundational principles such as defined CTI roles and responsibilities, a dedicated and resourced threat intelligence team, internal and external communication channels, intelligence sharing, delivery of actionable intelligence and continuous improvement. It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA, including those that outsource their CTI capability.

The Strategic CTI layer of SAMA's Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles, addressing the specialised practice of identifying the objectives, motivations and intent of threat actors and mapping the financial sector's cyber threat landscape. It expects Member Organizations to identify relevant threat actors, trends and vulnerable assets, and to route this intelligence to executive management (e.g. the CISO) for strategic and resilience decisions. Applies to all SAMA Member Organizations, including where the CTI function is outsourced.

The Operational CTI layer of SAMA's Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles, focused on understanding the nature, intent and timing of specific attacks and the behaviour of threat actors on a network. It expects Member Organizations to define and taxonomize attack phases using recognised frameworks and to identify tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs) of relevant actors, tools and malware. Binds SAMA Member Organizations, including those outsourcing CTI.

The Technical and Tactical CTI layer of SAMA's Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles, covering identification and handling of technical components and indicators of cyber attacks. It sits alongside the Core, Strategic and Operational domains within the same instrument and feeds detection and mitigation activity, with outputs classified under the Traffic Light Protocol per SAMA's Cybersecurity Communication Protocols. Applies to SAMA Member Organizations, including those with outsourced CTI capability.

Concept node for SAMA's Cyber Security Framework as referenced within the Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles, including the glossary definitions (cybersecurity, cyber risk, asset, incident, threat actor, CTI, indicator of compromise) that align the CTI principles with the broader framework. It provides the definitional and governance backdrop against which CTI obligations are read. Relevant to SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

Concept node for the MITRE ATT&CK/kill-chain style frameworks referenced in the Operational CTI domain of SAMA's Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles as an example of an industry-standard taxonomy for attack phases and TTPs. It is cited illustratively rather than mandated by name, supporting the requirement that Member Organizations use a structured approach to analysing threat actor behaviour.

This node covers the anti-financial-crime strand of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Business Ethics for financial institutions, which sits under the heading on combating financial and administrative corruption and addresses money laundering, terrorist financing, suspicious transactions, and bribery/corruption as staff conduct duties. It is an ethics/governance instrument rather than the operative AML/CTF rulebook, so it frames expected employee behaviour and board-approved conduct policy rather than CDD or reporting mechanics. It binds all personnel of SAMA-supervised financial institutions (banks and foreign bank branches, insurance/reinsurance and free-zone insurance firms, finance and finance-lease registration companies, credit bureaus), including directors, executives, contract staff, consultants and third-party workers.
lookup_terms: principles of conduct and work ethics
code of conduct policy board approval

data.summary: This node is the confidentiality and information-disclosure strand of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Business Ethics for financial institutions, covering the duty to preserve confidentiality, the mechanisms for disclosing information, and the related prohibition on using or leaking inside information to manipulate the market. It operates as a minimum conduct standard that each institution's board-approved ethics policy must reflect. It binds all personnel of SAMA-supervised financial institutions, including directors, executives, employees, consultants and staff engaged through third parties.

This node covers the conflict-of-interest strand of SAMA's conduct and business-ethics framework for financial institutions, including related themes of dealing with stakeholders, gifts and hospitality, remuneration and incentives, and reporting actual or potential breaches. It sets minimum behavioural rules that the institution's board must implement through its own conduct policy, with consequences for non-compliance. It binds directors, board committee members, executives, employees (permanent and contract), consultants and third-party personnel of SAMA-supervised financial institutions.

Second edition (Nov 2021) of SAMA's Standing Payment Order in Favour of the Financing Entity rules, replacing the earlier real-estate-only version; it now covers all financing products and extends the beneficiary scope to government financiers including National Development Fund banks and funds. It defines the service, the Customer (a natural person holding a financing product) and reliable communication channels, and sets minimum obligations on banks (verifying stable monthly income, customer acknowledgement, notification of order terms, execution and non-execution notices, no-objection/clearance before amendment or cancellation, and respect for protected/non-deductible amounts and seizure instructions) and on the beneficiary financing entity (consent to amend on rescheduling, and issuing clearance letters within set working-day deadlines). It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom, without prejudice to responsible lending principles and collection rules.

SAMA's CCTV/security surveillance technical specifications (v1.0, July 2019) for financial-sector facilities, setting operational deployment requirements for CCTV rooms and cameras, access restriction and logging, daily system checks, vendor/technician attendance controls, incident reporting for overwritten or missing footage, and cooperation with law enforcement through bank procedures. It also fixes retention rules: a 90-day minimum for head office, branches, cash centres and ATMs, one year for footage relating to a customer claim or complaint, and five years where a claim or complaint is rejected, plus surveillance-objective standards (identification, recognition, detection) for camera coverage. It binds banks and financial organisations operating the covered facilities in the Kingdom.

SAMA's Financial Sector Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles, structured by domain: core CTI principles built on the intelligence lifecycle (roles and responsibilities, dedicated CTI team, collection, processing, analysis, dissemination and continuous improvement) and strategic CTI (identifying the organisation's cyber threat landscape, threat actors, motivations, attribution and sector trends for executive management such as the CISO). It is expressed as expectations on Member Organizations to build and operate their own CTI capability as part of sector cyber resilience in KSA. It binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations in the financial sector.

Defined-term node for "Executive Management" (also rendered as senior management) as used across SAMA instruments for finance companies and real estate refinance companies: the persons entrusted with running the company's day-to-day business and with proposing and implementing strategic decisions. The term fixes who bears management-level accountability distinct from the Board and the Audit Committee, notably in supporting and not impeding the internal audit function. It binds SAMA-licensed entities through the obligations that attach to this layer in the underlying instruments.

Concept node covering the first/second/third line structure underlying SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for finance companies and real estate refinance companies: business units that own and take risk within limits, control and oversight units, and the independent internal audit department. It matters mainly for the required relationship and demarcation between internal audit and the first and second line units, so that assurance stays independent of risk-taking and control functions. Binds SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.

Node on the Internal Audit Policy required under SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for finance companies and real estate refinance companies: a formal document prepared by the head of internal audit and approved by the Board, whose mandatory contents are set out in the seventh principle. It establishes the internal audit function's mandate, independence, objectivity and conflict-of-interest safeguards. Binds SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies and their Boards.

Node on the Internal Audit Plan required under SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for finance companies and real estate refinance companies (eighth principle), sitting alongside requirements on audit reporting, working policies and procedures, external quality assessment and record retention. It governs how the audit department scopes and schedules its assurance work and reports outcomes to the Board and Audit Committee. Binds SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.

SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies (issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation, effective 1 May 2023), setting a minimum standard for Shariah governance and compliance. It allocates roles to the Board, senior management and the Shariah Committee, and covers Shariah supervision, committee operating controls, member independence criteria and confidentiality. Mandatory for finance companies licensed for real estate finance, productive assets finance, SME finance, finance lease, credit card finance and consumer finance; indicative for other licensed finance activities unless SAMA requires otherwise.

Defined-term node for "Senior Management" as used in SAMA finance-company instruments, including the Shariah Governance Instructions where the Board and senior management must have a reasonable understanding of Shariah principles and their application in Islamic finance. The term identifies the layer accountable for implementing governance, compliance and control requirements below Board level, and overlaps with "Executive Management" in related SAMA texts. It binds SAMA-licensed finance companies.

A SAMA circular adopting the Financial Entities Ethical Red Teaming Framework, a supervisory framework for intelligence-led simulation of real-world cyber attack scenarios against supervised financial institutions. It establishes that SAMA will run periodic red-team exercises on institutions' live systems and expects institutions to conduct their own independent, periodic resilience testing consistent with the Cyber Security Framework. It is addressed to banks operating in the Kingdom, Saudi Payments and licensed payment companies, and insurance/reinsurance companies, with the framework itself distributed to compliance departments.

Concept node for the "Compliance Unit" as a defined term: the compliance function or department within a supervised institution, which under the Compliance Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies reports directly to the Audit Committee. The node covers the unit's required key attributes (independence, resourcing, permanent standing) and its duties to identify, assess and monitor compliance risk with laws and SAMA instructions. It binds licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies, alongside parallel compliance requirements for other SAMA-supervised institutions.

Concept node for the "Compliance Officer" as defined in the Compliance Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies: the head or manager of the Compliance Unit, distinct from Unit Staff. The node covers the officer's appointment, independence, reporting line and responsibilities for the compliance programme and for escalating compliance-risk matters. It is relevant to finance companies and real estate refinance companies licensed by SAMA, and interacts with leadership-appointment (fit and proper) requirements.

Concept node for the Audit Committee's role in the compliance regime for finance and real estate refinance companies: it is the body to which the Compliance Unit reports directly and which oversees the effectiveness and independence of the compliance function. Its duties sit alongside separate Board and Executive Management duties toward compliance set out in the same principles. It binds the boards and audit committees of SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.

Concept node for the Internal Audit Function as defined in SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies: an independent, objective assurance and consulting activity assessing the quality, adequacy and effectiveness of the internal control system and of governance, risk management and control processes. The node covers the department's independence and objectivity, conflicts of interest, audit charter, policy, plan, reporting, external quality assessment and its relationship with first- and second-line units. It binds licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies through their boards and audit committees.

Cross-instrument concept node for the Board of Directors of a SAMA-supervised institution, aggregating the board's duties as they appear across governance, internal audit, compliance and related principles. It captures the board's ultimate responsibility for approving strategy, policies, charters and control frameworks, for appointing and empowering control functions, and for overseeing risk management and the internal control environment. It binds boards of finance companies, real estate refinance companies and other institutions supervised by SAMA under the referenced instruments.

This node covers the Shariah compliance dimension of SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies (issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation, effective 2023). It anchors the statutory requirement that licensed finance companies conduct financing business in a manner not conflicting with Shariah rulings as determined by their own Shariah committee, and sets out preliminary provisions, definitions (Committee, Committee members, independent member, Shariah supervision), and the roles of the board, senior management and the Shariah committee. It binds finance companies licensed for real estate finance, productive-assets finance, SME finance, finance lease, credit card finance and consumer finance; for other licensed financing activities it is guidance only, unless other rules make a provision mandatory or SAMA imposes it.

This node addresses the Shariah oversight/monitoring function within SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies, where "Shariah supervision" is defined as monitoring and verifying the extent to which the company's business complies with Islamic Shariah rulings and principles. It sits alongside chapters on board and senior management responsibilities, rules governing the Shariah committee's work, and independence and confidentiality of information. It applies to finance companies licensed for the listed financing activities, with guidance status for other licensed financing activities.

This node is SAMA's Information Technology Governance Framework, which sets principles and control requirements across IT governance domains and subdomains (IT governance and leadership, IT risk management, IT operations management, system change management). It is structured as numbered control requirements per subdomain, is assessed through periodic self-assessment questionnaires reviewed and audited by SAMA against a six-level maturity model, and allows compensating controls with a formal waiver request. It binds Member Organizations regulated by SAMA.

This node covers the IT Steering Committee under SAMA's IT Governance Framework: the board is ultimately responsible for IT governance and may delegate to senior management or the ITSC, which defines IT governance and sets IT strategy. It specifies mandating by the board, chairmanship by a senior manager, required representation (senior managers from relevant departments, the CIO, internal audit as observer), and a board-approved charter covering objectives, roles, quorum, at least quarterly meetings and minute retention. It binds Member Organizations and allocates accountability between board and ITSC for the IT strategy, IT policy and governance practices.

This node concerns the Chief Information Officer role under SAMA's IT Governance Framework, requiring appointment of a full-time senior manager for the IT function at senior management level, with conditions including Saudi nationality, sufficient qualification and a written no-objection, and CIO representation on the IT Steering Committee. Related glossary definitions (e.g., Chief Operating Officer, enterprise architect, database administrator) sit in the framework's glossary appendix. It binds Member Organizations regulated by SAMA.

This node is the Information Technology Governance Maturity Model used to measure how well Member Organizations implement SAMA's IT Governance Framework, distinguishing six levels (0 non-existent through 5), where levels 3 to 5 require meeting all criteria of the preceding levels. It is applied through periodic self-assessment questionnaires completed by Member Organizations and reviewed and audited by SAMA to determine compliance and maturity. It supports the framework's objectives of a common approach to IT risk and an appropriate maturity level of IT controls across SAMA-regulated entities.

This is SAMA's Rules on Liquidity Risk Management for finance companies, setting out the governance, strategy, measurement, stress testing and contingency funding requirements for managing liquidity risk. It allocates ultimate responsibility to the Board (risk tolerance, organisational structure, annual approval of strategy, policies, CFP and stress testing framework) and operational responsibility to senior management, with recommended ALCO oversight and periodic reporting to the Board and SAMA. It binds licensed finance companies supervised by SAMA, not banks.

Concept node on the asset and liability committee (ALCO) within the finance company liquidity risk framework. SAMA recommends (rather than mandates) that finance companies form an ALCO of senior management including the CEO plus risk, treasury, financial control and key business functions to oversee liquidity risk, with the Board defining its mandate; committee members must ensure the framework measures exposure and produces timely reports to senior management, the Board and SAMA. Relevant to finance companies designing liquidity governance structures.

Defined-term node for liquidity risk tolerance: the maximum level of liquidity risk a finance company is willing to accept in both normal and stressed conditions, aligned with its business strategy. The Board must establish it, and it must be reviewed at least annually and supported by quantitative measures such as liquid asset holdings, maturity mismatches, funding concentration and contingent liquidity obligations. Binds finance companies through the Board's liquidity governance duties.
