Node on the standardised approach as the required methodology for calculating operational risk capital (and, by contrast, the standardised approach used for credit risk RWA reporting in the same framework). It anchors the BI/BIC/ILM calculation chain that replaces earlier and internal-model based approaches. Applies to SAMA-licensed banks for regulatory capital computation and Pillar 3 disclosure.

Defines the Business Indicator (BI), the financial-statement-based proxy for a bank's operational risk exposure, built from the interest, lease and dividend component, the services component and the financial component, averaged over three years. It is the input to the Business Indicator Component and must be disclosed with its subcomponents (Template OR2), including any SAMA-approved exclusion of divested activities. Binds all SAMA-supervised banks.

Defines the Business Indicator Component (BIC), obtained by applying the prescribed marginal coefficients/buckets to the Business Indicator, and forming the base of the operational risk capital requirement before the Internal Loss Multiplier is applied. It is the benchmark against which the Loss Component is compared to set the ILM above or below one, and is the sole basis of the charge for banks lacking sufficient loss data. Applies to SAMA-licensed banks.

Defines the Internal Loss Multiplier (ILM), the scaling factor reflecting a bank's own operational loss experience, equal to one when the Loss Component equals the Business Indicator Component and moving above or below one as losses are high or low relative to BIC. Sets the loss-data quality conditions (ten years, with a five-year transitional minimum subject to SAMA approval) and requires banks with insufficient data to use BIC alone or seek SAMA's direction. Binds SAMA-supervised banks and drives Pillar 3 loss disclosures.

Defines the Loss Component (LC) as fifteen times the average annual operational risk losses over the preceding ten years, the internal-loss input to the Internal Loss Multiplier. Related provisions set loss event thresholds (SAR 44,600 and SAR 446,000) for capturing, excluding and disclosing net losses and recoveries. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks calculating operational risk capital and making related disclosures.

This node covers the commodity risk component of the simplified standardised approach (SSA) for market risk capital, including how commodities positions and commodity option risks feed the Pillar 3 market risk disclosure template for banks using the SSA. It sits within SAMA's Basel-aligned capital framework and identifies which capital requirement blocks (outright products versus option risks under the simplified, delta-plus and scenario methods) apply to commodities. It binds SAMA-licensed banks that determine market risk capital requirements under the simplified standardised approach rather than the sensitivities-based standardised or internal models approaches.

This node explains the delta-plus method, one of the three permitted treatments of options under the simplified standardised approach for market risk: delta-weighted option positions are folded into the general market risk calculation, with separate add-ons for gamma and vega risk and specific risk determined via delta-equivalents. It sits alongside the simplified (carve-out) approach and the scenario approach and references the use of an approved exchange model or the bank's own option pricing model under SAMA oversight. It applies to SAMA-licensed banks that write options and calculate market risk capital under the simplified standardised approach.

This node covers the scenario approach for options under the simplified standardised approach for market risk, where general market risk capital is set by the worst-loss cell of a scenario grid combining changes in the underlying and its volatility, with specific risk calculated separately from delta-equivalent positions. It is presented as an alternative to the simplified carve-out treatment and the delta-plus method. It binds SAMA-licensed banks using the simplified standardised approach for options portfolios, subject to supervisory expectations on the models used.

This node is the umbrella treatment of options in the market risk framework: the simplified carve-out treatment (with a capital requirement table for long cash/long put, long call and similar positions), the delta-plus method, and the scenario approach, plus the identification of option-like instruments bearing residual risks (gap, correlation and behavioural risk) for the residual risk add-on. It sets out which method a bank may use depending on whether it buys or writes options and its level of trading activity. It applies to SAMA-licensed banks holding option positions in the trading book.
lookup_terms: long call long put capital requirement

data.summary: This node is labelled for the backtesting traffic-light classification (green, amber/yellow and red zones) used to assess internal model exception counts and drive capital multiplier or model-use consequences. Note that the supplied context material actually shows Pillar 3 credit risk mitigation disclosure content (Template CR3, secured versus unsecured carrying amounts), so the node's underlying source coverage should be verified before relying on it for backtesting rules. Any backtesting classification obligations would bind SAMA-licensed banks with approved internal models for market risk.

This node covers risk factor modellability under the internal models approach for market risk: the risk factor eligibility test (RFET), the qualitative principles a risk factor must satisfy on data quality and accuracy, and the consequence that failing factors are excluded from the expected shortfall model and capitalised as non-modellable risk factors (NMRF). It also records SAMA's discretion over evidence banks must produce (for example regression diagnostics for multi-factor beta models and price recovery testing) and the narrow, systemic-stress circumstance in which a failed factor might still be treated as modellable without reducing capital. It binds SAMA-licensed banks seeking or holding approval to use internal models for market risk capital.

Concept node for the potential future exposure (PFE) add-on component used in measuring counterparty credit exposure of derivative transactions, sitting alongside replacement cost in the exposure calculation and feeding the leverage ratio exposure measure (reported with the prescribed alpha factor) as well as capital requirements. It is defined and applied within SAMA's minimum capital requirement and leverage ratio/disclosure rules for banks. Binds banks subject to SAMA's prudential capital, leverage and Pillar 3 disclosure framework.

Concept node for the net independent collateral amount (NICA), the collateral term used in counterparty credit risk exposure measurement for derivatives to reflect independent collateral held or posted that is not variation margin. It is referenced within SAMA's minimum capital requirements and related prudential disclosure templates; the surrounding text in the sources also covers regulatory capital deductions and credit risk mitigation reporting. Binds banks calculating and disclosing counterparty credit exposures under SAMA's prudential framework.

Concept node for the effective notional of a derivative trade, computed from the adjusted notional multiplied by the maturity factor and the supervisory delta, then aggregated at entity, maturity-bucket, hedging-set and asset-class level to derive add-ons. The source sets it out through worked examples for credit, interest rate and margined netting sets. Relevant to banks computing counterparty credit risk exposure amounts under SAMA's minimum capital requirements.

Concept node for the supervisory delta adjustment, a trade-level parameter applied to adjusted notional amounts to reflect the direction (long/short in the primary risk factor) and non-linearity of a derivative; set at +1/-1 for non-option, non-CDO-tranche instruments and by prescribed formulas for options and CDO tranches using supervisory volatility. Applied in computing effective notionals for counterparty credit risk add-ons under SAMA's minimum capital requirements, and reflected in leverage ratio reporting adjustments. Binds banks in scope of SAMA's prudential capital and leverage framework.

Concept node for the maturity factor, the time-scaling parameter applied together with adjusted notional and supervisory delta to derive a trade's effective notional, with distinct treatments for margined and unmargined netting sets (unmargined trades with remaining maturity over one year receiving a factor of one). The cited source material also situates maturity-related bucketing in the market risk modellability/risk factor eligibility context. Relevant to banks calculating counterparty credit and market risk capital requirements under SAMA rules.

Concept node for the hedging set, the grouping of derivative trades within a netting set that determines the extent of offsetting permitted when calculating asset-class add-ons: separate sets per currency for interest rate, per currency pair for FX, single sets for credit and equity, and four commodity categories, with special sets for basis and volatility transactions. Supervisory factors are applied at hedging-set level to convert effective notionals into add-ons. Binds banks computing counterparty credit risk exposure amounts under SAMA's minimum capital requirements.

Defined-term node for the netting set, the unit of aggregation used in SAMA's counterparty credit risk framework (SA-CCR) for computing replacement cost, potential future exposure add-ons and the treatment of collateral. It governs how trades under legally enforceable netting arrangements are grouped, how one margin agreement covering several netting sets is handled, and how collateral taken outside a netting set is recognised. It binds SAMA-licensed banks calculating regulatory capital for counterparty credit risk.

Defined-term node for the supervisory factor, the regulator-prescribed volatility parameter applied per trade and hedging set in the standardised approach to counterparty credit risk add-on calculations (e.g. 4% for FX). It sits alongside adjusted notional, maturity factor and supervisory delta as the fixed inputs banks may not calibrate themselves. Applies to banks computing CCR exposure at default under SAMA's capital rules.

Node for Effective Expected Positive Exposure, the internal-model measure of counterparty exposure used to derive exposure at default for CCR capital purposes. The surrounding material in the source also covers credit risk mitigation disclosure templates and prudential treatment of problem assets, so the document reaches beyond the definition itself. Relevant to banks using internal model methods and to their Pillar 3 disclosure teams.

Defined-term node for the margin period of risk, the assumed close-out horizon used to calculate exposure on margined netting sets, together with the supervisory floors and the exceptions that lengthen them (large netting sets, illiquid collateral or hard-to-replace OTC derivatives, and a history of prolonged margin call disputes). It sets mandatory minimum assumptions banks cannot shorten. Binds banks calculating CCR capital on collateralised derivative and SFT exposures.

Defined-term node covering central counterparty, qualifying CCP (QCCP), clearing member and client, and the capital treatment of exposures arising through central clearing. It also sets Pillar 2 expectations that a bank hold capital above the minimum where CCP dealings are riskier, QCCP status is unclear, or shortcomings in the CCP have been identified, plus monitoring and board-level reporting duties. Binds banks that clear directly or indirectly through CCPs.

Node setting the requirement for a comprehensive stress testing programme, both for counterparty credit risk (complete trade capture, at least monthly single-factor exposure stress tests, at least quarterly multifactor and joint exposure/creditworthiness stress tests) and for banks using the internal models approach for market risk (desk-level and bank-wide scenarios). It also requires routine reporting of results to senior management and periodic reporting to the board. Binds banks using these approaches under SAMA capital rules.

Node covering SAMA's validation expectations for internal models used in counterparty credit risk (IMM/EPE models) and, in the market risk context, for risk-factor modellability under the expected shortfall framework. It sets out that banks must backtest exposure models across horizons matching trade maturities, benchmark pricing models independently, reassess parameter-update frequency, and correct discrepancies between realised and forecast exposures, with SAMA able to impose additional capital or deem data unsuitable pending remediation. Binds SAMA-licensed banks that have or seek approval to use internal models for regulatory capital.

Node on the alpha multiplier applied to Effective EPE when computing regulatory EAD under the internal models method, including SAMA's power to permit a more conservative alternative measure in place of alpha times Effective EPE with prior approval. Related context covers the evidence banks may be asked to provide on risk factor modellability (regression diagnostics, price recovery from risk factors). Binds banks using IMM for counterparty credit exposure.

Node addressing general and specific wrong-way risk in counterparty credit risk management: banks must identify exposures where risk factors are positively correlated with counterparty creditworthiness, design stress tests and scenario analysis accordingly, and monitor and report wrong-way risk by product, region and industry to senior management and the board or its delegated committee. It links wrong-way risk identification to the stress-testing and risk-appetite framework. Binds SAMA-supervised banks with derivative, SFT and other counterparty exposures.

Node isolating the concept of specific wrong-way risk — where future exposure to a particular counterparty is highly correlated with that counterparty's deterioration — as distinguished from general wrong-way risk driven by macro risk factors. It sits within the counterparty credit risk stress-testing, monitoring and senior-management reporting expectations. Binds banks calculating counterparty credit exposures under SAMA's capital framework.

Node on the Effective Expected Positive Exposure model used under the internal models method to measure counterparty credit exposure, and the validation, backtesting and performance-assessment duties attaching to it. Covers SAMA's ability to require correction of model or data deficiencies, to require additional capital while issues persist, and to approve more conservative alternatives to alpha times Effective EPE. Binds banks holding or applying for IMM approval.

Node setting out the Cross-Product Netting Rules permitting netting across SFTs, or across SFTs and OTC derivatives, for regulatory capital computation under the internal models method. It imposes legal criteria: a written bilateral cross-product netting arrangement creating a single legal obligation for a Cross-Product Net Amount on default or insolvency, supported by reasoned legal opinions on enforceability under the law of every relevant jurisdiction (counterparty's charter/branch, governing law of transactions, and law governing the netting contract), plus internal verification procedures before including a transaction in a netting set. Binds banks with IMM approval seeking netting recognition.

This node covers the capital treatment of bank exposures arising from centrally cleared transactions — trade exposures, initial margin (segregated and non-segregated) and prefunded/unfunded default fund contributions — together with the related Pillar 3 disclosure of exposures at default and risk-weighted assets split between qualifying and non-qualifying CCPs. It sits within SAMA's counterparty credit risk and capital adequacy framework transposing Basel standards. It binds SAMA-supervised banks that clear as clearing members or as clients.

Defines the qualifying central counterparty (QCCP) status that determines whether a bank's cleared exposures attract preferential capital treatment or the punitive non-QCCP treatment. The concept operates across the counterparty credit risk rules and the Pillar 3 disclosure templates, which require exposures to be reported separately for qualifying and non-qualifying CCPs. Relevant to all SAMA-supervised banks with cleared derivatives or securities financing transactions.

Sets out the capital treatment applicable to a bank acting as a clearing member, including capitalising client exposures as bilateral trades (with a reduced margin period of risk for cleared client transactions), recognition of client collateral passed to the CCP, and the conditions under which a bank that is a client of a clearing member may use the clearing member treatment. It also underpins the default fund exposure calculations attributed to each clearing member. It binds banks that clear for clients or access CCPs indirectly.

Covers the capital requirement for a bank's prefunded and unfunded contributions to a CCP's default fund, including the formula allocating the CCP's hypothetical capital requirement across clearing members and the 2%/8% floor, plus the disclosure of such contributions in the CCP exposures template. It also imposes information-sharing and calculation-frequency expectations on CCPs, banks and supervisors so that each clearing member and SAMA can verify the figures. Binds banks that are clearing members of qualifying or non-qualifying CCPs.

Concept node for KCCP, the hypothetical capital requirement of a central counterparty computed from the CCP's exposures to its clearing members, which is the input to allocating default fund capital charges among members. It is calculated at least quarterly (more often on material change, e.g. new cleared products) by the CCP, bank or supervisor, with results shared so members and SAMA can verify. Relevant to banks that are clearing members and to their reliance on CCP-supplied data.
lookup_terms: hypothetical capital requirement of a CCP

data.summary: Concept node for KCMi, the capital requirement attributed to an individual clearing member bank for its default fund contribution, derived from KCCP scaled by the member's share of prefunded contributions and subject to a floor. It determines the risk-weighted asset amount a member bank must carry for CCP default fund exposure and feeds the related Pillar 3 disclosure. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks acting as clearing members.

Chapter-level rules setting minimum haircut floors for certain non-centrally cleared securities financing transactions (SFTs) with specified counterparties, including the in-scope transaction list, the floor percentages by collateral type and residual maturity, and the portfolio-level formula. It also defines the carve-outs: SFTs with central banks, qualifying cash-collateralized securities lending, and collateral upgrade trades where the received securities cannot be re-used. Binds SAMA-licensed banks calculating counterparty credit risk capital; it does not apply where a jurisdiction prohibits transacting below the floors.
lookup_terms: shadow banking securities lending and repos

data.summary: Defines the Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) risk framework: what regulatory CVA is (counterparty-level adjustment to default risk-free prices of derivatives and SFTs), how it differs from accounting CVA, the scope of covered transactions in both banking and trading book, and conversion of CVA capital requirements into RWA via the 12.5 multiplier. Applies to all banks with covered derivative and fair-valued SFT exposures, with SAMA determining materiality of SFT CVA exposures.

Covers the basic approach to CVA capital (BA-CVA) as the default methodology banks must apply unless SAMA approves use of SA-CVA. Relevant to identifying which CVA calculation approach a bank may use, the supervisory approval gate, and the related Pillar 3 reporting of standardised versus modelled RWA components.

Covers the standardized approach for CVA risk capital (SA-CVA), which banks may use only with prior SAMA approval; absent approval the BA-CVA applies. Useful for questions on the approval condition, scope of covered derivatives and fair-valued SFTs, and how SA-CVA output feeds RWA and Pillar 3 disclosure rows.

Describes the reduced version of the basic approach for CVA risk, in which hedges are not recognised, and the associated mandatory Pillar 3 template (CVA1) disclosing the systematic and idiosyncratic CVA components and total RWA. Binds banks whose CVA RWA is measured in whole or part under the reduced BA-CVA, including a semiannual disclosure and narrative obligation on hedge types used.

Covers the full version of the basic approach for CVA, which recognises eligible CVA hedges, together with the treatment of eligible and ineligible, external and internal CVA hedges across the CVA portfolio and trading book, and the option to cap the IRB maturity adjustment factor at 1 for netting sets contributing to CVA capital. Applies to banks electing the hedge-recognising BA-CVA rather than the reduced version.

Concept node covering off-balance sheet items as they enter regulatory credit risk measurement and Pillar 3 disclosure, notably in the CR1 credit quality of assets template where gross carrying values must include guarantees given (maximum callable amount) and irrevocable loan commitments, gross of credit conversion factors and credit risk mitigation, with revocable commitments excluded. It also feeds the reconciliation of accounting to regulatory consolidation categories in the disclosure templates. Binds all banks subject to SAMA's disclosure and capital adequacy framework.
lookup_terms: Template CR1 credit quality of assets

data.summary: Concept node setting the conditions under which cash variation margin exchanged on derivative transactions may be treated as a form of pre-settlement payment and used to reduce the replacement cost component of the leverage ratio exposure measure. Conditions include non-segregation and free use of cash received, at least daily mark-to-market and margin exchange, eligible currency, full mark-to-market amount subject to thresholds/minimum transfer amounts, and coverage by a single legally enforceable master netting agreement. Applies to banks calculating the leverage ratio exposure measure, including clearing members offering client clearing.

Node covering the leverage ratio as a non-risk-based capital standard within SAMA's prudential and disclosure framework, including its role in key prudential metrics reporting (KM1) and as a trigger for capital distribution constraints alongside risk-based buffers. It governs how banks measure and disclose Tier 1 capital against the leverage ratio exposure measure. Mandatory for all banks in scope of SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Concept node on credit conversion factors used to convert off-balance sheet commitments and undertakings into credit exposure equivalents for risk-weighted asset purposes, including the 10% CCF for unconditionally cancellable commitments and the rule to apply the lower of two applicable CCFs where an undertaking to provide a commitment exists. SAMA may impose higher CCFs where a bank's practical ability to cancel is constrained. Relevant to banks applying the standardised approach to credit risk and to related counterparty credit risk and credit derivative treatments.

SAMA rules implementing the Basel III output floor, under which RWAs derived from internal models cannot fall below a set percentage of RWAs calculated under standardised approaches, issued under the Central Bank Law and Banking Control Law. Effective 1 January 2023 with transitional phase-in, and requiring quarterly reporting of regulatory capital and RWA on SAMA's template within 30 days of quarter-end. Applies to all domestic banks on consolidated and standalone bases; foreign bank branches in KSA are excluded and follow home-regulator capital rules.

Concept node for the output floor itself: the minimum level, expressed as a percentage of standardised-approach RWAs, below which a bank's internal-model-derived RWAs and resulting Pillar 1 capital requirement cannot fall. It affects how minimum capital requirements and 'pre-floor' metrics are computed and disclosed in prudential templates. Relevant to domestic banks using internal ratings-based or other internal model approaches.

Prudential guidance on how margined netting sets are treated when a bank uses an internal model (IMM) to estimate expected exposure and EAD for counterparty credit risk. It sets out what the model must capture — unilateral vs bilateral margin agreements, margin call frequency, thresholds, minimum transfer amounts and collateral valuation — and imposes supervisory floors on the margin period of risk (five/ten business days, rising to twenty for large netting sets and for illiquid collateral or disputed trades). Binds SAMA-supervised banks that hold model approval; it sits alongside the standardised credit risk approach and RWA disclosure definitions.

The leverage ratio component of SAMA's Basel-aligned capital framework and its associated Pillar 3 disclosure requirements, including the key metrics template (KM1) and the capital distribution constraints template (CDC). It defines the ratio as a non-risk-based backstop reported alongside risk-based capital and liquidity metrics, and identifies the leverage ratio buffer as a trigger for restrictions on capital distributions. Mandatory for all SAMA-supervised banks at consolidated group level, with quarterly (KM1) and annual (CDC) reporting frequencies.

Defines the denominator of the leverage ratio — the total exposure measure — and how it is built up from on-balance sheet assets, derivative replacement cost and potential future exposure add-ons, securities financing transactions and off-balance sheet items, with regulatory deductions reported as negative amounts. Includes the LR1 reconciliation template linking published financial statement assets to the leverage ratio exposure measure and the treatment of client-cleared trades, fiduciary assets and any temporary central bank reserve exemption. Binds all SAMA-supervised banks; disclosure is quarterly and on the regulatory scope of consolidation.

Covers the prudential treatment and disclosure of derivative exposures within the credit risk framework, including how collateral, financial guarantees and credit derivatives are recognised as credit risk mitigation (template CR3 and its worked allocation examples) and how problem assets are disclosed (table CRB-A, referencing SAMA's Rules on Management of Problem Assets, January 2020). Sets out definitions of unsecured versus secured carrying amounts and the ordering rules when an exposure benefits from multiple mitigants. Mandatory for all SAMA-supervised banks regardless of whether the standardised or IRB approach is used.

Addresses securities financing transaction (repo-style) exposures within the credit risk and disclosure framework, including their recognition under credit risk mitigation techniques (table CR3, covering collateral, financial guarantees and credit derivatives) and the accompanying problem-asset disclosures in table CRB-A. Specifies carrying-value reporting, the split between loans and debt securities, and narrative explanation of material period-on-period changes. Mandatory for all SAMA-supervised banks, semiannually for CR3 and annually for CRB-A.

Defines written credit derivatives broadly as any arrangement under which a bank effectively provides credit protection — not only credit default and total return swaps but also sold options — and sets the conditions for reducing the effective notional amount, including negative fair value adjustments and offsetting against purchased protection. Offsetting requires the same or more conservative material terms (subordination, optionality, credit events, reference obligation), identical legal-entity reference names, and equivalent economic coverage where pools of names are involved. Binds SAMA-supervised banks calculating derivative exposures for the leverage ratio exposure measure.

Concept node for the stand-alone CVA capital charge (SCVAc), the counterparty-level CVA capital component computed under the basic approach (BA-CVA) before recognition of hedges, within SAMA's minimum capital requirements for counterparty credit risk and CVA risk. It feeds the aggregate CVA capital requirement that in turn affects total capital ratios, buffer stacking and the disclosure templates (including capital composition and capital distribution constraint disclosures) referenced in the linked Pillar 3 framework. Binds SAMA-licensed banks calculating regulatory capital on a consolidated and solo basis.

Defines which CVA hedging instruments qualify as eligible hedges for CVA capital purposes and how eligible versus ineligible, and external versus internal, hedges are allocated between the CVA portfolio and the trading book. Eligible external hedges are removed from market risk capital and recognised in the CVA calculation; ineligible hedges are capitalised as trading book instruments, and internal hedges are recognised only where the trading desk offsets its position externally in specified cases. Applies to banks calculating CVA capital under BA-CVA or SA-CVA; hedge recognition is unavailable to banks using the below-threshold alternative treatment.

Sets out how delta and vega sensitivities of aggregate CVA and of eligible CVA hedging instruments to each risk factor are computed as inputs to the standardised approach CVA capital requirement. It requires vega sensitivities to be calculated in all cases (including where the portfolio holds no options), specifies volatility shifts for both path-generation and option pricing, permits smaller shifts and computational techniques consistent with internal risk management, and addresses index hedges. Binds banks that have obtained SAMA approval to use the SA-CVA.

Concept node for potential future exposure, the forward-looking add-on component of counterparty credit risk exposure at default under the standardised approach (SA-CCR), combined with replacement cost and scaled by a multiplier recognising excess collateral or negative mark-to-market. It is the driver of EAD used in credit risk RWA and in the counterparty credit risk Pillar 3 templates. Applies to banks with derivative and securities financing exposures in both banking and trading books.

Explains the aggregate add-on component of the PFE calculation for each netting set under SA-CCR, built up from asset-class-level add-ons and multiplied by the collateral/negative-MTM multiplier to produce PFE. It sits alongside the replacement cost formula (threshold, minimum transfer amount and net independent collateral amount, floored at zero) in determining counterparty credit risk exposure. Binds banks computing counterparty credit risk capital under the standardised approach.

Worked sample-portfolio illustrations showing how SA-CCR inputs and outputs (and related credit risk mitigation disclosures) are calculated and presented for representative netting sets and collateral arrangements. Useful as interpretive support for applying the exposure methodology and for completing the counterparty credit risk disclosure templates rather than as a stand-alone obligation. Relevant to banks computing and disclosing counterparty credit risk exposures under SAMA's capital and Pillar 3 frameworks.

A concept node covering how risk-weighted assets and Pillar 1 capital requirements for credit risk are determined and reported in SAMA's Basel-aligned disclosure templates (overview of RWA and capital requirement rows). It sets out the split between the standardised approach and the internal ratings-based approaches (F-IRB, A-IRB and supervisory slotting), the treatment of credit risk mitigation using the simple or comprehensive approach with supervisory haircuts, and the phase-in for equity exposures where IRB use is being withdrawn. It also fixes the perimeter by excluding counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity positions, settlement risk, securitisation exposures and amounts below deduction thresholds, which are reported elsewhere. It binds banks subject to SAMA's capital adequacy and Pillar 3 disclosure framework.

A concept node on risk-weighted assets and Pillar 1 capital requirements for market risk within SAMA's Basel-aligned RWA overview and disclosure instructions. The available context frames it alongside the other RWA components (credit risk, counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity positions, settlement risk, securitisation and operational risk) and the general rule that the capital requirement is normally 8% of RWA, subject to any applicable floor or scaling adjustment. It binds banks preparing regulatory capital calculations and Pillar 3 disclosures for SAMA.

A concept node on risk-weighted assets and Pillar 1 capital requirements for operational risk as reported in SAMA's Basel-aligned RWA overview template. The surrounding instructions position operational risk as one line of the total RWA build-up alongside credit risk, counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity, settlement and securitisation exposures, with capital normally computed as 8% of RWA subject to floors or jurisdictional scaling. It binds banks subject to SAMA capital adequacy and disclosure requirements.

Reference node for SCRE, the Basel-derived credit risk standard as adopted in SAMA's rulebook, cited throughout the disclosure instructions as the source of RWA and capital requirements for credit exposures. It is the anchor for the standardised approach provisions, the F-IRB and A-IRB provisions, the supervisory slotting approach, the equity exposure IRB phase-in and the treatment of failed trades and non-DvP transactions. It binds banks calculating and disclosing credit risk capital under SAMA's framework.

Reference node for SCCR, the Basel-derived counterparty credit risk and credit valuation adjustment standard as adopted by SAMA, cited in the disclosure instructions as the basis for the CCR and CVA rows of the RWA overview. It separates counterparty credit risk capital charges from general credit risk and identifies the CVA capital requirement as a distinct component. It binds banks computing and disclosing capital for derivative, securities financing and other counterparty exposures.

Reference node for SOPE, the Basel-derived operational risk capital standard as adopted by SAMA, providing the basis for operational risk RWA and Pillar 1 capital requirements reported in the disclosure templates. It is referenced within the same capital adequacy and Pillar 3 disclosure framework that governs capital composition, deductions and capital distribution constraints. It binds banks subject to SAMA's capital adequacy regime.

Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring a G-SIB resolution entity to set out, on a legal entity basis, the ranking of creditors within its liabilities structure, splitting total capital and liabilities into excluded liabilities, TLAC-eligible amounts and residual maturity bands. It mirrors Template TLAC2 but omits the resolution-entity-as-creditor dimension, so only one column per creditor hierarchy layer is used. Binds banks designated as G-SIBs under SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework, with semiannual nominal-value reporting and jurisdiction-specific narrative on credit hierarchies.

Pillar 3 template requiring banks to disclose the capital ratio thresholds at which capital distribution constraints are triggered, covering CET1 needed for minimum ratios, buffer requirements (conservation, G-SIB surcharge, countercyclical), Pillar 2 add-ons, TLAC interaction and the leverage ratio buffer. Disclosure is annual and fixed-format, with narrative explanation where constraints have actually been imposed and a link to SAMA's published buffer/stacking-hierarchy rules. Mandatory for all banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

Narrative Pillar 3 table accompanying Templates LI1 and LI2, in which banks explain the drivers of differences between accounting carrying values and regulatory exposure amounts, including scope-of-consolidation effects, valuation differences, netting rules, provisions and prudential filters. It provides the qualitative context that makes the quantitative LI templates interpretable. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework.

Pillar 3 template reconciling financial statement carrying values (on the regulatory scope of consolidation) to the exposure amounts used for regulatory capital purposes, isolating drivers other than consolidation scope: off-balance sheet amounts, valuation differences, Basel netting rules, provisions and prudential filters. Columns split items by credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitisation and market risk frameworks; format is flexible and rows adaptable, with Table LIA as the accompanying narrative. Mandatory for all banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, reported annually.

Pillar 3 template breaking down a bank's prudent valuation adjustments for fair-valued assets by risk category (equity, interest rates, FX, credit, commodities) and by trading/banking book, following the Basel prudent valuation guidance and SAMA's circular on assessing banks' financial instrument fair value practices. Fixed format with mandatory narrative on significant changes, "other adjustments" and instruments generating the largest PVAs. Mandatory annually for all banks that record PVAs.

Pillar 3 template requiring disclosure of encumbered versus unencumbered on-balance sheet assets at period-end carrying amounts, using a template-specific definition of "encumbered assets" (restricted from liquidation, sale, transfer or assignment by legal, regulatory, contractual or other limitations) that differs from the LCR definition by excluding the monetisation aspect. Reported semiannually on the regulatory scope of consolidation including securitisation exposures, with narrative on material changes. Mandatory for all banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

SACAP is SAMA's guidance document implementing Basel III capital reforms in Saudi Arabia, and it is the source referenced for the composition of regulatory capital — CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 — including eligibility criteria, regulatory adjustments and deductions. It underpins the line-by-line definitions used in Pillar 3 capital composition templates (goodwill and intangibles, deferred tax assets, cash flow hedge reserve, provision shortfall, own-share and reciprocal holdings, threshold deductions for investments in financial entities, and Tier 2/TLAC holdings). It binds banks licensed and supervised by SAMA when calculating and reporting regulatory capital.

This is SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, setting the guiding principles for market disclosure (clarity, comprehensiveness, meaningfulness, consistency over time and comparability across banks) together with rules on governance and assurance of disclosed data, use of signposting to other documents, and the frequency, timing and publication of the Pillar 3 report. It requires a board-approved disclosure policy and publication concurrent with the corresponding financial report. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Basel III framework.

This node covers SAMA's adoption of the Basel III post-crisis final reforms and the associated glossary of SAMA-issued standards (credit risk, counterparty credit risk and CVA, market risk, operational risk, leverage ratio, LCR and NSFR), which are the cross-referenced sources for Pillar 3 templates such as key metrics (KM1). It defines the standard-by-standard architecture of the Saudi prudential framework and the metrics banks must disclose quarterly. It applies to SAMA-licensed banks.

This node concerns the FSB Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Term Sheet as referenced in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, governing which regulatory capital and non-capital instruments qualify as external TLAC at resolution group level, subordination requirements and exemptions, caps on non-subordinated instruments, funding-vehicle and ex ante commitment eligibility, and deductions of holdings between resolution groups. It also frames the RWA and leverage exposure bases and buffer interaction for TLAC ratios. It is relevant to G-SIBs and their resolution groups (SPE and MPE approaches) rather than to domestic-only banks.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's adopted Basel disclosure framework requiring banks to compare risk-weighted assets produced by SAMA-approved internal models against RWA that would result from the corresponding standardised approaches, broken down at risk-category level. It specifies which exposures belong in which row (credit risk excluding counterparty credit risk, CVA and banking-book securitisations; equity phase-in treatment; settlement/failed trades) and how minimum capital requirements are derived. It binds banks subject to SAMA's capital adequacy and disclosure requirements that use modelled approaches.
lookup_terms: comparison of modelled and standardised RWA

data.summary: Template KM2 is the fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure of key TLAC metrics at resolution group level, covering available TLAC, RWA and leverage exposure at that level, TLAC ratios, fully loaded ECL variants and the subordination exemption indicator, with quarterly reporting and four prior quarter-ends plus narrative commentary. It is mandatory only for resolution groups of G-SIBs and must be reproduced per resolution group under the MPE approach.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring banks to compare, for credit risk specifically, RWA calculated under SAMA-approved modelled (IRB/supervisory slotting) approaches with RWA under the standardised approach, at portfolio/asset-class granularity. The instructions define the reference standardised approach (including credit risk mitigation via simple or comprehensive approach with supervisory haircuts) and the equity exposure IRB phase-in, and set out row scope exclusions for counterparty credit risk and banking-book securitisations. Applies to banks permitted by SAMA to use IRB approaches for credit risk.
lookup_terms: credit risk modelled vs standardised RWA

data.summary: This node relates to the Pillar 3 risk management overview disclosure and the accompanying definitions/instructions for allocating RWA and minimum capital requirements across risk types and approaches — credit risk (standardised, F-IRB, A-IRB, supervisory slotting), counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity positions, settlement risk and securitisation — including the phase-in for equity exposures under IRB and the treatment of modelled approaches requiring SAMA approval. It binds SAMA-supervised banks preparing Pillar 3 reports and shapes how they narrate their risk management approach.

A Pillar 3 disclosure table requiring banks to publish the main features of each regulatory capital instrument they issue (and, where relevant, TLAC-eligible instruments), supporting market assessment of capital quality and loss absorbency. The surrounding instructions also cover related capital disclosures, including capital distribution constraint triggers and the CET1 regulatory adjustments and deductions cross-referenced to SAMA's capital adequacy rules. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
lookup_terms: main features of regulatory capital instruments
capital instrument terms and conditions disclosure

data.summary: A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring banks to reconcile the regulatory capital components disclosed under the composition-of-capital template to the balance sheet in their published financial statements, expanding balance-sheet lines that feed regulatory capital elements and deductions. It relies on the regulatory scope of consolidation and the CET1 adjustment items (goodwill, intangibles, DTAs, cash flow hedge reserve, provision shortfall, own credit risk, holdings in financial entities) cross-referenced to SAMA capital adequacy provisions. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework.
lookup_terms: reconciliation of regulatory capital to balance sheet

data.summary: A Pillar 3 disclosure template setting out the composition of total loss-absorbing capacity at resolution group level, including regulatory capital and other TLAC-eligible instruments, deductions, adjusted RWA and leverage exposure measure, resulting TLAC ratios and buffer requirements. Instructions distinguish single point of entry from multiple point of entry structures and require separate reporting per resolution group. It is mandatory only for G-SIBs and their resolution groups, so it has no application to non-G-SIB Saudi banks.
lookup_terms: single point of entry / multiple point of entry

data.summary: A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring, on a legal entity basis, disclosure of creditor ranking in the liabilities structure of each material subgroup entity that has issued internal TLAC to a G-SIB resolution entity, including excluded liabilities, TLAC-eligible amounts and residual maturity buckets. The accompanying material also covers the parallel template for resolution entities themselves, which omits the resolution-entity-as-creditor information. Mandatory for G-SIBs only, reported semiannually per resolution group.
lookup_terms: creditor ranking at legal entity level

data.summary: Table REMA is the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table on a bank's remuneration policy and the key features of its remuneration system, covering the oversight body, external advisers, scope across business lines and foreign subsidiaries/branches, identification of senior management and material risk-takers, independence of risk and compliance staff pay, and how current and future risks are reflected in remuneration. It is mandatory for all banks, annual, with flexible format, and sits alongside quantitative templates REM1–REM3. Binding on banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

Template REM1 is the Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure of fixed and variable remuneration awarded during the financial year, broken down for senior management and other material risk-takers as defined in Table REMA. It is part of the remuneration disclosure set (REMA, REM1–REM3) and is published annually, as soon as possible after the annual report if not simultaneous. Applies to banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

Template REM2 is the mandatory annual Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure of special payments — guaranteed bonuses, sign-on awards and severance payments — showing number of employees and total amounts for senior management and other material risk-takers, using the employee categories defined in Table REMA. Format is flexible and banks may add narrative on significant movements. Binds all banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

Template REM3 is the Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure of a bank's total outstanding deferred and retained remuneration, completing the remuneration disclosure set with Table REMA and Templates REM1–REM2. Disclosure is annual, aligned with (or promptly after) the annual report. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

Template CR1 is the mandatory semiannual Pillar 3 disclosure giving a comprehensive picture of the credit quality of a bank's on- and off-balance sheet assets: gross carrying values of defaulted and non-defaulted loans, debt securities and off-balance sheet exposures, allowances/impairments, and the split of ECL provisions between specific and general categories for SA and IRB exposures. Columns on ECL provisions apply only to banks using an ECL accounting model, and banks must state their definition of default in narrative. Excludes securitisation and counterparty credit risk positions, which are disclosed elsewhere.

Template CR2 is the mandatory semiannual Pillar 3 flow statement of the stock of defaulted loans and debt securities, reconciling opening to closing balances through new defaults, returns to non-defaulted status, write-offs and other changes. Defaulted exposures are reported net of write-offs and gross of allowances; for standardised approach banks, default aligns with exposures past due more than 90 days. Banks must explain significant movements and state whether off-balance sheet items are included.
lookup_terms: changes in stock of defaulted loans

data.summary: Pillar 3 disclosure template CR4 within SAMA's Basel-aligned public disclosure framework, covering standardised approach credit risk exposures before and after credit conversion factors and credit risk mitigation, broken down by asset class with associated RWA and RWA density. It sets out the fixed format, definitions and instructions banks must follow, including the treatment of on- and off-balance sheet exposures and the simple versus comprehensive CRM approaches. It binds SAMA-licensed banks that compute credit risk RWA under the standardised approach, at the regulatory scope of consolidation.

Pillar 3 disclosure template CR5 requiring banks to present standardised approach credit exposures (post-CCF and post-CRM) allocated across asset classes and regulatory risk weight buckets. It provides the instructions and definitions for the risk-weight grid used to show the distribution and average riskiness of standardised portfolios. Applies to SAMA-licensed banks using the standardised approach for credit risk RWA.
lookup_terms: exposures by asset class and risk weight

data.summary: Pillar 3 disclosure template CR6 setting out the portfolio-by-portfolio, PD-band presentation of IRB credit risk exposures, including EAD post-CRM, average PD, number of obligors, average LGD, average maturity, RWA and expected loss. Instructions specify separate template sets where a bank uses both F-IRB and A-IRB, coverage of key group-wide models, and narrative commentary on material changes. Mandatory for SAMA-licensed banks with approval to use the foundation or advanced IRB approaches.
lookup_terms: IRB exposures by portfolio and PD scale

data.summary: Pillar 3 disclosure template CR8 requiring a quarterly flow statement explaining period-on-period movements in credit risk RWA computed under IRB approaches, attributing changes to drivers such as asset size, asset quality, model updates, methodology and policy, acquisitions and disposals, and foreign exchange. It is a fixed-format reconciliation supported by narrative commentary. Binds SAMA-licensed banks using IRB approaches for credit risk.

Node covering Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity: the composition, deductions, RWA and leverage exposure bases, ratios and buffer interaction disclosed for a resolution group under the TLAC regime. Instructions distinguish single-point-of-entry and multiple-point-of-entry G-SIB structures and explain how TLAC figures relate to, but do not necessarily aggregate with, regulatory capital reported under Template CC1. Relevant to G-SIB resolution entities and their groups within scope of SAMA's disclosure and resolution-related requirements.

Pillar 3 disclosure template CR9 requiring annual backtesting of probability of default estimates against realised obligor default rates, per regulatory portfolio and PD range, using at least a five-year average annual default rate. It applies to any SAMA-approved model or model combination used to generate PD for IRB capital calculations, with commentary on model scope and RWA coverage. Mandatory for SAMA-licensed banks using F-IRB and/or A-IRB, with separate template sets where both approaches are used.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework (Dec 2022, v2.1) covering IRB specialised lending exposures risk-weighted under the supervisory slotting approach. It sits in the credit risk section alongside other IRB templates (e.g. CR7 on the RWA effect of credit derivatives as CRM, CR9 on PD backtesting) and is relevant only where SAMA has approved the bank's use of IRB/slotting. It binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to Pillar 3 disclosure at the regulatory consolidation level.

Table CCRA is the qualitative disclosure requirement opening the counterparty credit risk (CCR) section of SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, which covers all banking book and trading book exposures attracting a CCR charge, including exposures to central counterparties. It frames the accompanying quantitative templates CCR1 and CCR3–CCR8. It applies to SAMA-supervised banks making Pillar 3 disclosures.

Template CCR1 requires banks to disclose counterparty credit risk exposures analysed by the approach used to determine exposure at default and RWA, distinguishing modelled approaches used with SAMA approval from standardised approaches. It is part of the CCR disclosure set (CCRA, CCR1, CCR3–CCR8) in SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework and binds SAMA-supervised banks.
lookup_terms: analysis of CCR exposures by approach

data.summary: Template CCR3 requires disclosure of counterparty credit risk exposures treated under the standardised approach for credit risk, broken down by regulatory portfolio and risk weight band. It forms part of the CCR disclosure section of SAMA's Pillar 3 framework and applies to SAMA-supervised banks using the standardised approach for the relevant exposures.

Template CCR4 requires disclosure of the parameters (PD scale, EAD post-CRM, average PD, obligor numbers, average maturity, RWA) used to calculate counterparty credit risk capital requirements where an IRB approach is applied, excluding CVA charges and CCP-cleared exposures. Separate templates are required for F-IRB and A-IRB portfolios, with narrative on model scope and RWA coverage. Mandatory semiannually for SAMA-approved IRB banks.
lookup_terms: IRB CCR exposures by PD scale

data.summary: Template CCR5 requires a breakdown by collateral type of collateral posted and received to support or mitigate counterparty credit risk on derivatives and securities financing transactions, including CCP-cleared trades, distinguishing segregated from unsegregated collateral. Both legs of a transaction are reported at fair value. Mandatory for all SAMA-supervised banks subject to Pillar 3, semiannually.

A fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, used to report market risk capital requirements computed under the simplified standardised approach. It sits alongside the other market risk and RWA overview templates (e.g. OV1) and ties into how standardised versus modelled RWA are presented. It binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to the Pillar 3 market risk disclosure regime.

Table CVAA is the general qualitative disclosure table for credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, covering a bank's CVA risk management, covered transactions and hedging. It is one element of the CVA disclosure set (CVAA, CVA1–CVA4, CVAB) and applies only where the CCR/CVA materiality threshold in SAMA's revised risk-based capital charge for counterparty credit risk is met. It binds SAMA-supervised banks with covered derivative and SFT exposures in banking and trading book.

Template CVA1 is a mandatory, fixed-format semiannual Pillar 3 template reporting the components of RWA under the reduced basic approach (BA-CVA) for CVA risk, split between systematic and idiosyncratic aggregations. Its total links to the CVA line in the RWA overview template (OV1) where the bank uses only the reduced BA-CVA, and banks must add narrative on hedges even where those hedges are not recognised. It binds SAMA-supervised banks measuring any part of CVA RWA under the reduced BA-CVA.

Template CVA2 is the Pillar 3 template for reporting CVA risk RWA computed under the full basic approach (BA-CVA), i.e. where eligible CVA hedges are recognised. It forms part of the CVA disclosure set that applies once the counterparty credit risk/CVA materiality threshold is satisfied, with BA-CVA being the default method absent SAMA approval to use SA-CVA. It binds SAMA-supervised banks using the full BA-CVA for part or all of their CVA risk.

Table CVAB sets the qualitative disclosure requirements for banks that have received SAMA approval to use the standardised approach for CVA (SA-CVA), covering how the approach is applied within the CVA portfolio. It complements the quantitative SA-CVA templates (CVA3 and CVA4) and applies only where the CCR/CVA materiality threshold is met. It binds SAMA-supervised banks approved for SA-CVA; banks without approval must use BA-CVA.

Template CVA3 is the Pillar 3 quantitative template reporting RWA and capital requirements for CVA risk calculated under the standardised approach (SA-CVA). It sits with Table CVAB and Template CVA4 (SA-CVA RWA flow statement) and feeds the CVA line of the RWA overview disclosures. It binds SAMA-supervised banks that have obtained SAMA approval to apply SA-CVA to some or all of their CVA risk exposures.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Basel-aligned disclosure rules covering credit derivatives exposures used for counterparty credit risk reporting, capturing protection bought and sold by product type. It sits in the counterparty credit risk (CCR) template series alongside CCR1–CCR8 and specifies purpose, scope, content, frequency and format for the disclosure. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework; note the surrounding text also carries credit risk mitigation templates (CR1, CR3) with definitions of unsecured/secured carrying amounts.

A Pillar 3 template presenting the flow statement of risk-weighted assets for counterparty credit risk exposures calculated under the Internal Model Method (IMM), explaining movements in RWA over the reporting period by driver. The accompanying text sets out how RWA and minimum capital requirements (normally RWA × 8%) are allocated across credit risk, CCR, CVA, equity, settlement and securitisation rows, and how standardised versus IRB/slotting approaches are distinguished. It applies to banks with SAMA approval to use internal models for CCR.

A mandatory fixed-format Pillar 3 template disclosing a bank's exposures to central counterparties, split between qualifying (QCCP) and non-qualifying CCPs, and broken down by trade exposures, segregated and non-segregated initial margin, and pre-funded and unfunded default fund contributions, reported as EAD post-CRM and RWA. Disclosure is semiannual with a narrative explaining significant period-on-period changes. It binds all banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 framework; the surrounding text also includes Table CRB-A on prudential treatment of problem assets (non-performing and forborne exposure definitions).

Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table requiring banks to describe their securitisation strategy, risk management objectives, roles (originator, sponsor, investor), risk transfer and retained risks, and related special purpose and affiliated entities, distinguishing banking book from trading book positions. Its scope covers all securitisation exposures, including those failing risk transfer recognition, with a flexible annual format. Mandatory for all banks with securitisation exposures under SAMA's disclosure framework.
lookup_terms: banking book vs trading book securitisation

data.summary: Pillar 3 template disclosing all securitisation exposures in the banking book, broken down by the bank's role (originator, sponsor, investor) and by underlying exposure type, irrespective of whether the securitisation framework capital treatment applies. It captures a comprehensive view of securitisation activity, including positions that do not meet risk transfer recognition criteria (which are excluded from SEC3/SEC4). It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Pillar 3 template disclosing securitisation exposures held in the trading book, broken down by the bank's role and underlying exposure type; capital charges for trading book securitisation positions are dealt with under the market risk disclosures rather than the securitisation framework templates SEC3/SEC4. Together with SEC1 it gives a complete picture of securitisation activity without double-counting capital requirements. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework.

Pillar 3 disclosure template SEC3 within SAMA's public disclosure requirements framework, covering banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as originator or sponsor and the exposures are subject to capital charges under the securitisation framework. It sits alongside Table SECA and templates SEC1/SEC2 (which capture all securitisation activity, including positions failing risk transfer recognition) and excludes trading book securitisation positions. It binds banks reporting under SAMA's Pillar 3 regime.

Pillar 3 disclosure template SEC4 covering banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as investor, limited to positions treated under the securitisation framework and subject to its capital charges. It is the investor-side counterpart to SEC3 and excludes trading book securitisation positions, which are disclosed elsewhere. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Table MRA sets the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure requirements for market risk, requiring banks to explain their market risk strategy, governance, measurement and reporting arrangements as context for the quantitative market risk templates. It orients readers to how market risk positions are identified and managed rather than prescribing capital calculations. Binding on banks reporting under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

Template MR1 is the quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of market risk capital requirements calculated under the standardised approach, broken down by risk class (e.g. interest rate, equity, FX, commodity, credit spread) and by sensitivities-based, default risk and residual risk components. It complements the internal models templates and the RWA overview table. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Table MRB sets the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure requirements for banks with SAMA approval to use the internal models approach (IMA) for market risk, covering model scope, trading desk eligibility, validation, backtesting and P&L attribution arrangements. It provides the narrative context for the IMA quantitative templates. Binds only banks permitted to use the IMA.

Template MR2 is the quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of market risk capital requirements under the internal models approach, presented per risk type and component — including unconstrained and constrained expected shortfall, non-modellable risk factors, the default risk capital requirement, any amber-zone trading desk surcharge, and standardised capital for desks ineligible for the IMA. It applies to banks with SAMA approval to use internal models for market risk.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk RWA disclosure, including flow statements for RWA under the standardised approach to CVA (SA-CVA) and the components of the reduced basic approach (BA-CVA) with their aggregation of systematic and idiosyncratic CVA risk. It is mandatory for banks whose CVA risk RWA are measured under the relevant approach, with semiannual frequency, fixed format, and an accompanying narrative on hedging. It binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to the capital and disclosure framework and links to the OV1 overview of RWA.

Table ORA is the mandatory qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on a bank's operational risk management framework, requiring description of policies and guidelines, the structure of the operational risk management and control function, the measurement system feeding the operational risk capital charge, reporting to executive management and the board, and risk mitigation/transfer (including insurance and outsourcing policy). It applies to all banks, annually, in flexible format. Useful when assessing operational risk governance disclosure obligations rather than capital computation.
lookup_terms: operational risk management and control function

data.summary: Template OR1 is the Pillar 3 disclosure of aggregate operational loss experience over the past ten years, net of recoveries and of excluded losses, at loss event thresholds of SAR 44,600 and SAR 446,000, together with whether losses feed the internal loss multiplier (ILM). It is mandatory for banks in the second or third business indicator bucket and for first-bucket banks with SAMA approval to use internal loss data, disclosed annually in fixed format with narrative on new loss exclusions. Retrospective-disclosure relief does not apply, so all prior periods must be shown unless SAMA has permitted fewer years transitionally.

Template OR2 requires annual fixed-format disclosure of the business indicator (BI) and its subcomponents — the interest, lease and dividend component, the services component and the financial component — plus the resulting business indicator component (BIC), over three reporting years. It is mandatory for all banks, with narrative explaining material changes and, where SAMA has approved exclusion of divested activities, the gross BI and the reduction attributable to those exclusions. Relevant to how the standardised operational risk capital requirement inputs are made public.

Template OR3 covers disclosure of the minimum required operational risk capital, sitting within the Pillar 3 suite alongside the overview of RWA and minimum capital requirements (normally RWA × 8%, subject to floors or jurisdictional adjustments) and capital distribution constraint disclosures. The accompanying material explains how RWA and capital requirements are allocated across credit risk approaches, counterparty credit risk, CVA and equity positions. It binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to the Pillar 3 framework.

This node covers the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure of risk management objectives and governance, including interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB) objectives and the general Table OVA description of the bank's risk strategy, governance structure, risk culture channels, measurement systems and risk reporting to the board and senior management. The surrounding context also addresses independence of the risk control unit, backtesting/PLA and independent model validation for internal models. Mandatory for all banks, annually, in flexible format.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book

data.summary: Node for the Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure template on interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB1), sitting alongside the qualitative Table IRRBBA within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. It requires banks to disclose measured changes in economic value of equity (ΔEVE) and net interest income (ΔNII) under the prescribed Basel supervisory interest rate shock scenarios, computed using the bank's own internal measurement system (IMS) as referenced in SAMA's IRRBB circular. Binds banks within the Basel IRRBB scope of application; disclosure frequency is annual, with supporting qualitative explanation of modelling assumptions.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book

data.summary: Node for Pillar 3 Template GSIB1, the annual disclosure of the indicators feeding the Basel Committee methodology for assessing global systemic importance. It covers at least the 12 assessment indicators and is mandatory only for banks classified as G-SIBs, with a leverage ratio exposure measure above EUR 200 billion, or included in the assessment sample by supervisory judgment; SAMA states it need not be completed unless SAMA identifies the bank as a G-SIB. Sits in the macroprudential supervisory measures chapter together with Template CCyB1.

Node for Pillar 3 Template CCyB1, which discloses the geographical distribution of private sector credit exposures used to calculate a bank's institution-specific countercyclical capital buffer. It defines what must be reported per jurisdiction (buffer rate in force, exposure values, RWA) and how the bank-specific weighted-average buffer rate and resulting buffer amount are derived, excluding pre-announced rates not yet applicable. The surrounding context also covers Template CDC on capital distribution constraints, which references buffer stacking.

Node for Pillar 3 Template LR1, the fixed-format quarterly reconciliation between total assets in published financial statements and the leverage ratio exposure measure. It specifies the adjustment rows (regulatory vs accounting consolidation, securitisation risk transference, temporary central bank reserve exemption, fiduciary assets, regular-way purchases and sales, cash pooling) and sign conventions, and requires banks to state the calculation basis (quarter-end, daily or monthly averaging). Mandatory for all banks, which must also explain material differences.

Node for Pillar 3 Template LR2, the common disclosure of the leverage ratio and its components. Within the source framework it sits among the fixed-format prudential templates alongside Template KM1 (key prudential metrics, quarterly) and Template CDC (capital distribution constraints, annual), which likewise reference the leverage ratio and any leverage ratio buffer requirement. Mandatory for banks subject to the leverage ratio standard.

Node for Table LIQA, the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure of a bank's liquidity risk management framework, governance and funding strategy. It is one of the flexible-format narrative disclosures in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, parallel in structure to Table OVA (overall risk management approach), which requires description of risk governance, risk culture, measurement systems and reporting to the board and senior management. Binds banks subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements; note the retrieved context also carries adjacent material on internal model validation and risk control units.

A fixed Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements covering the Liquidity Coverage Ratio, i.e. the breakdown of high-quality liquid assets and weighted/unweighted cash inflows and outflows underlying the reported LCR. It sets what liquidity data banks must publish, at what frequency and in what fixed format, together with narrative commentary on drivers of change. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime and feeds the LCR figures also summarised in Template KM1.

A fixed Pillar 3 disclosure template covering the Net Stable Funding Ratio, requiring banks to publish available and required stable funding components by residual maturity and the resulting NSFR. It specifies the reporting content, frequency and fixed format, with accompanying narrative on material changes. It applies to banks within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure scope and links to the NSFR line in Template KM1.

The Pillar 3 overview template presenting total risk-weighted assets and minimum capital requirements broken down by risk type (credit, counterparty credit, CVA, securitisation, market, operational, equity investments in funds, settlement risk and threshold deductions). Its instructions define which approaches (standardised, F-IRB, A-IRB, supervisory slotting, internal models approved by SAMA) map to each row. Mandatory for banks; OV1 is the denominator reference for the risk-based capital ratios disclosed elsewhere.

A Pillar 3 template requiring banks using foundation or advanced IRB approaches to disclose credit risk exposures by regulatory portfolio and PD scale, with parameters such as EAD post-CRM, average PD, LGD, maturity, RWA and expected loss. Separate template sets are required where F-IRB and A-IRB are both used, and narrative must explain model scope and coverage. Binds only banks with SAMA approval to use IRB approaches for credit risk.
lookup_terms: IRB credit risk exposures by portfolio and PD scale

data.summary: The consolidated-level key metrics template giving a five-quarter time series of a bank's available capital, RWA (including pre-floor figures), risk-based and leverage ratios, LCR and NSFR, plus fully loaded expected credit loss variants where ECL transitional arrangements are applied. Instructions fix the treatment of pre-floor and fully loaded figures and set cross-references linking KM1 cells to CC1 and OV1. Mandatory quarterly for all banks in SAMA's Pillar 3 scope; the related TLAC template KM2 applies only if SAMA specifies.

A Pillar 3 template comparing RWA produced by internally modelled approaches that SAMA has approved against RWA that would result from applying the full standardised approach, split by credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitisation, market risk, operational risk and residual RWA. Its instructions define the standardised benchmark for each risk row and how totals are aggregated. Relevant to banks permitted to use modelled approaches, supporting comparability and the output floor.
lookup_terms: comparison of modelled and standardised RWA

data.summary: A sub-node of SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk framework defining the corporate exposure class under the standardized approach, including its residual scope (incorporated entities, partnerships, trusts, funds, insurers and other financial corporates not captured as banks) and its exclusion of individuals. It splits corporates into general corporate exposures and specialized lending, and confirms that securities firms and other financial institutions are risk-weighted as corporates. It binds banks licensed and supervised by SAMA when calculating credit risk RWAs, and also carries the due diligence overlay requiring ratings-based risk weights to be adjusted upward, never downward.
lookup_terms: exposures to securities firms and other financial institutions
Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk

data.summary: Defines how micro, small and medium enterprise exposures are classified for credit risk RWA purposes: MSMEs meeting the "regulatory retail" criteria fall in the retail exposure class, while those failing the criteria are treated as corporate MSME exposures. It also sets out the retail class structure (regulatory retail non-transactor, regulatory retail transactor, other retail) and the product criterion, excluding real estate/mortgage, derivatives and securities. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks using the standardized approach.

Sets out the specialized lending (SL) subcategory of corporate exposures, defined by reliance on the income of a financed asset or project rather than the borrower's broader capacity to repay. Under the standardized approach it distinguishes project finance, object finance and commodities finance, and requires use of issue-specific external ratings only (issuer ratings are not permitted); the IRB chapters add income-producing real estate and HVCRE and a supervisory slotting approach. Binds SAMA-supervised banks in classifying and risk-weighting such exposures.
lookup_terms: project finance object finance commodities finance

data.summary: Defines project finance as a specialized lending sub-class where repayment and security derive primarily from a single project's revenues, typically through an SPV, and sets its capital treatment where no issue-specific external rating exists: 130% pre-operational, 100% operational, and 80% for high-quality operational exposures. It specifies the operational phase test (positive net cash flow covering remaining obligations and declining long-term debt) and the cumulative conditions for "high quality" status. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks calculating credit risk RWAs.

Defines object finance as specialized lending to fund acquisition of physical equipment (ships, aircraft, satellites, railcars, fleets) where repayment depends on cash flows from the financed and pledged asset. Where no issue-specific external rating is available, object finance exposures are risk-weighted at 100% under the standardized approach. Binds SAMA-supervised banks classifying and risk-weighting asset-based lending.

Defines commodities finance as short-term specialized lending against reserves, inventories or receivables of exchange-traded commodities, repaid from sale proceeds where the borrower has no independent repayment capacity. Unrated commodities finance exposures attract a 100% risk weight under the standardized approach; issue-specific external ratings, not issuer ratings, govern where available. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks.

Node within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering Template CC1, the fixed-format disclosure setting out the composition of a bank's regulatory capital (CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2, together with the associated regulatory adjustments and deductions cross-referenced to the SAMA capital rules). It sits alongside CC2 (reconciliation to the accounting balance sheet) and the capital distribution constraints disclosure, and banks must be able to trace CC1 figures back to their published balance sheet. It binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to the Pillar 3 framework, with certain rows relevant only to G-SIBs or TLAC-related holdings.

Node covering Template CR3 in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, the overview disclosure of the extent to which credit exposures are covered by credit risk mitigation techniques (collateral, guarantees and credit derivatives). It forms part of the credit risk disclosure set, which also includes qualitative Table CRC on CRM techniques and the credit quality templates CR1/CR2, and excludes securitization and counterparty credit risk positions disclosed elsewhere. It binds banks subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
lookup_terms: secured by collateral guarantees credit derivatives

data.summary: Node covering Template CR7, the Pillar 3 disclosure showing the effect of credit derivatives used as a credit risk mitigation technique on IRB risk-weighted assets, comparing hypothetical pre-credit-derivative RWA with actual RWA by IRB exposure class. Disclosure is semiannual, fixed format, and must be accompanied by narrative explaining the RWA impact. It is mandatory only for banks that SAMA has permitted to use the foundation or advanced IRB approaches for some or all exposures.

Node covering Template LI1 in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, which maps the carrying values in a bank's published financial statements to the carrying values under the regulatory scope of consolidation and allocates them across the credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitization and market risk frameworks (or items not subject to capital requirements). It is the starting point for the linkage exercise continued in LI2 and explained qualitatively in Table LIA. It binds all banks subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
lookup_terms: accounting versus regulatory scope of consolidation

data.summary: Node covering Template LI2, the Pillar 3 disclosure explaining the main sources of difference between financial statement carrying values (on the regulatory consolidation scope, per LI1) and the exposure amounts used for regulatory capital purposes — including off-balance sheet amounts, valuation differences, netting rules, provisions and prudential filters. It is annual, flexible in format, and supported by narrative in Table LIA. It is mandatory for all banks subject to the Pillar 3 framework.
