It is mandatory for banks using A-IRB and/or F-IRB, with separate portfolio breakdowns where both approaches are used, and requires narrative on model scope and the share of RWA covered. Disclosure is annual and in flexible format.

Pillar 3 template CR10 covers IRB disclosures for specialised lending (and equity) exposures treated under the supervisory slotting approach, sitting alongside CR7 (effect of credit derivatives as CRM on IRB RWA) and CR9 (PD backtesting) in the same framework section. It applies to banks using IRB approaches under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. Open it for the slotting category breakdown, remaining maturity bands and applicable risk weights.

Table CCRA is the qualitative disclosure requirement on counterparty credit risk in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, opening the CCR section that covers all banking-book and trading-book exposures attracting a CCR charge, including exposures to central counterparties. It sits ahead of the quantitative CCR1 to CCR8 templates and is aimed at explaining risk management objectives, collateral and wrong-way risk policies. It binds banks subject to SAMA Pillar 3 disclosure.

Template CCR1 requires banks to disclose an analysis of counterparty credit risk exposures broken down by the calculation approach used (e.g. SA-CCR, internal models method), showing exposure at default and associated RWA. It forms part of the CCR disclosure set (CCRA and CCR1 to CCR8) applying to banking-book and trading-book exposures subject to a CCR charge. Mandatory for banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

Template CCR3 requires disclosure of counterparty credit risk exposures calculated under the standardised approach for credit risk, broken down by regulatory portfolio and risk weight band. It complements CCR1 (exposures by approach) and CCR4 (IRB portfolios by PD scale) within the Pillar 3 CCR section covering banking-book and trading-book CCR charges. Binding on banks reporting under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework that use standardised credit risk treatment for CCR exposures.

Disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering all securitisation exposures held in the banking book, including those that fail the risk transfer recognition criteria and are therefore not treated under the securitisation capital framework. It sits alongside Table SECA and template SEC2 to give a comprehensive picture of a bank's securitisation activity by role (originator, sponsor, investor), separate from the capital-charge templates SEC3 and SEC4. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime.

Pillar 3 disclosure template for securitisation exposures held in the trading book, reported by the bank's role (originator, sponsor, investor). Like SEC1 it captures all such exposures regardless of whether they qualify for the securitisation capital framework; related trading book capital charges are disclosed under the market risk section rather than in SEC3/SEC4. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Pillar 3 template disclosing banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as originator or sponsor, together with the associated capital requirements and risk-weighted assets under the securitisation framework. It is limited to exposures actually treated under that framework (i.e. meeting risk transfer recognition), avoiding double counting with SEC1/SEC2. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime.

Pillar 3 template disclosing banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as investor, with the corresponding risk-weighted assets and capital requirements under the securitisation framework. It mirrors SEC3 on the investor side and is confined to exposures treated under the securitisation framework. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table requiring banks to describe their market risk management objectives and policies, including trading strategies, trading vs banking book designation policies, stale positions, internal risk transfers, and the market risk governance structure. Mandatory and annual, in flexible format, for all banks subject to the market risk framework.

Pillar 3 template disclosing market risk capital requirements calculated under the standardised approach, broken down by risk class components. It covers trading book and banking book positions subject to market risk capital requirements, excluding counterparty credit risk charges on the same exposures, which are disclosed in the counterparty credit risk section. Binds banks subject to SAMA's market risk and Pillar 3 frameworks.

Pillar 3 disclosure template CCR4 within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, setting out the semiannual, fixed-format disclosure of counterparty credit risk exposures broken down by regulatory portfolio and PD band, including EAD post-CRM, average PD, obligor numbers, average LGD/maturity and RWA. It binds banks that use foundation or advanced IRB approaches to compute RWA for CCR exposures, requiring separate templates where both F-IRB and A-IRB are used, and excludes CVA charges and CCP-cleared exposures. Rows for portfolio breakdown are set by SAMA, and a narrative on model scope, RWA coverage and period-on-period changes is expected.

Pillar 3 template CCR5 requires banks to disclose the composition of collateral posted and received in support of counterparty credit risk exposures arising from derivatives and securities financing transactions, including CCP-cleared trades. Reporting is by collateral type (cash by currency, sovereign and agency debt, corporate bonds, equities, other) and by segregated versus unsegregated status, at fair/carrying value. It is mandatory for all banks, semiannual, with fixed columns but flexible rows and an explanatory narrative.

Node for Pillar 3 template CCR6 on credit derivatives exposures within SAMA's Pillar 3 framework; the surrounding context supplied here covers related credit risk templates (CR1 credit quality of assets and CR3 credit risk mitigation illustrations) showing how exposures secured by collateral, financial guarantees and credit derivatives are allocated. Together these are mandatory disclosure templates for banks, defining gross carrying values, defaulted exposures, ECL provisions and the treatment of multi-secured exposures. Binds all banks subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure regime.
lookup_terms: Template CR1 credit quality of assets

data.summary: Covers Pillar 3 template CCR7, the RWA flow statement for counterparty credit risk exposures whose exposure value is determined under the internal models method, with rows isolating IMM model updates and methodology/policy changes. The accompanying interpretive Q&A clarifies that CCR7 splits by EAD methodology rather than risk-weighting methodology, so IRB model changes affecting IMM positions should be captured through additional inserted rows. Applies to banks with SAMA approval to use IMM; the row breakdown is flexible to show all significant RWA drivers.

Pillar 3 template CCR8 requires a comprehensive, fixed-format semiannual disclosure of a bank's exposures to central counterparties, split between qualifying and non-qualifying CCPs and by trade type (OTC derivatives, exchange-traded derivatives, SFTs, approved cross-product netting sets), plus segregated and non-segregated initial margin and pre-funded/unfunded default fund contributions, with EAD post-CRM and RWA. Mandatory for all banks, supported by a narrative on material changes. Adjacent context also references Table CRB-A on prudential treatment of problem assets and SAMA's Rules on Management of Problem Loans.

Section 21 of the Pillar 3 framework scopes securitisation disclosures and introduces Table SECA, the annual qualitative disclosure of a bank's securitisation strategy, objectives, risk management policies and activity features, distinguishing banking book from trading book positions and requiring lists of sponsored SPEs and affiliated entities involved in the bank's securitisations. Table SECA is mandatory for all banks holding securitisation exposures; templates SEC1/SEC2 capture all securitisation exposures while SEC3/SEC4 are limited to exposures treated under the securitisation framework, including originator risk-transfer recognition criteria.

Pillar 3 disclosure table MRB within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, setting the qualitative narrative banks must publish when they use the internal models approach (IMA) for market risk. It sits among the framework's other qualitative tables (e.g. credit-quality and problem-asset tables and the remuneration table REMA), each of which specifies purpose, scope, content, frequency and format. It binds banks in scope of the Pillar 3 regime, specifically those with SAMA approval to use internal models for market risk.

Pillar 3 template MR2 in SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, requiring banks using the internal models approach to disclose market risk capital components by risk type — including unconstrained and constrained expected shortfall, non-modellable risk factor charges, default risk capital, the amber-zone P&L attribution surcharge and standardised charges for IMA-ineligible desks. Row definitions cross-reference the Basel market risk standard (SMAR) and link to the overall RWA template OV1. Mandatory for banks with approved internal market risk models.

Pillar 3 template MR3 in SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, showing the components of the market risk capital requirement under the simplified standardised approach (SSA): interest rate, equity, commodity and FX outright products plus option risk under the simplified, delta-plus and scenario methods, and securitisation. Fixed format, semiannual, with row definitions keyed to SMAR14. Mandatory for banks that use the SSA to determine market risk capital requirements.

Table CVAA is the general qualitative disclosure requirement on credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, and heads the CVA disclosure set that also includes CVA1/CVA2 (basic approach) and CVAB/CVA3/CVA4 (standardised approach). The whole CVA section applies only where the materiality threshold in SAMA's revised risk-based capital charge for counterparty credit risk is met. Binds banks subject to the Pillar 3 regime that exceed that threshold.

Pillar 3 template CVA1 requires disclosure of the RWA components computed under the reduced basic approach for CVA risk — the aggregated systematic and idiosyncratic components and the total (K-reduced scaled by 12.5) — with fixed format and semiannual frequency, plus a narrative on hedge types used even where not recognised. Mandatory for banks with part or all of their CVA RWA under the reduced BA-CVA, covering only the relevant netting sets, and it links to the overall RWA template OV1.

Pillar 3 template CVA2 covers disclosure of RWA under the full basic approach for CVA risk (the hedge-recognising variant of BA-CVA), sitting alongside CVA1 in the CVA section of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. Like the rest of that section, it applies only where the counterparty credit risk materiality threshold is met, and it binds banks measuring CVA RWA under the full BA-CVA.

Table CVAB is a qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure item within the credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk section of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, applying where the CVA materiality threshold in SAMA's revised counterparty credit risk capital rules is met. It requires banks to describe their CVA risk management framework, senior management involvement, and governance arrangements (documentation, independent control and review, independence of data sourcing from business lines). It binds all SAMA-supervised banks that use the standardised approach (SA-CVA) to compute CVA risk RWA, on an annual, flexible-format basis.

Template CVA3 is the Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure template for CVA risk risk-weighted assets calculated under the standardised approach (SA-CVA), listed in section 23 of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework alongside Table CVAB and Template CVA4. It applies to banks meeting the CVA materiality threshold in SAMA's revised counterparty credit risk framework and using SA-CVA for part or all of their CVA exposures. Note that the retrieved context for this node contains generic RWA/approach definitions from other templates; open the source for the actual CVA3 rows and instructions.

Template CVA4 is the Pillar 3 RWA flow statement for CVA risk exposures measured under the standardised approach (SA-CVA), showing period-on-period movements in CVA RWA and their drivers. It sits in section 23 of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework and applies to banks that exceed the CVA materiality threshold and use SA-CVA. The retrieved context mixes in definitions from other templates (BA-CVA / general RWA overview), so the underlying document should be consulted for CVA4's own rows and frequency.

Table ORA is the general qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on a bank's operational risk management framework under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. Banks must describe their operational risk policies and guidelines, the structure of the operational risk management and control function, the measurement system used for the capital charge, reporting to executive management and the board, and mitigation/transfer arrangements including insurance and outsourcing policy. It is mandatory for all SAMA-supervised banks, annually, in flexible format.

Template OR1 requires annual Pillar 3 disclosure of aggregate operational risk losses over the past ten years (by accounting date of the loss), including losses net of recoveries, excluded losses, loss counts, and whether internal loss data feed the internal loss multiplier (ILM), using loss event thresholds of SAR 44,600 and SAR 446,000. It applies to banks in the second or third business indicator bucket and to first-bucket banks with SAMA approval to use internal loss data in their operational risk capital requirement. Banks must add narrative explaining new loss exclusions and other material information on losses and recoveries.

Template OR2 requires annual Pillar 3 disclosure of the Business Indicator (BI) and its subcomponents — the interest, lease and dividend component, services component and financial component — plus the resulting Business Indicator Component (BIC) used in the operational risk capital calculation, over three reporting periods. It is mandatory for all SAMA-supervised banks, with narrative on significant changes and additional narrative where SAMA has approved exclusion of divested activities from the BI.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering the minimum required operational risk capital, sitting alongside related capital-adequacy templates (e.g. overview of risk-weighted assets and capital distribution constraints) that translate Pillar 1 requirements into RWA and capital-charge line items. It specifies the scope, content, frequency and format (fixed or flexible) of the public disclosure rather than the underlying capital calculation itself. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Basel-aligned Pillar 3 regime at the consolidated level.

Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table requiring banks to describe their objectives, policies, governance and measurement approach for interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), including definition of IRRBB, mitigation and hedging strategies, calculation periodicity, shock and stress scenarios, and any divergence between internal measurement system assumptions and those prescribed for the quantitative template. Disclosure is annual and in flexible format. Mandatory for all banks within the IRRBB scope of application under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, read with SAMA's IRRBB circular.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book
IRRBB risk management objectives and policies

data.summary: Quantitative Pillar 3 template requiring banks to disclose measured changes in economic value of equity (∆EVE) and net interest income (∆NII) under the prescribed supervisory interest rate shock scenarios, using the bank's own internal measurement system. It is paired with the qualitative Table IRRBBA and is disclosed annually. It applies to banks falling within the IRRBB scope of application under SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework.

Pillar 3 template requiring disclosure of the twelve indicators feeding the Basel methodology for assessing global systemic importance, with an annual reference date, prior-exercise web link and optional narrative on estimates, structural changes and bucket allocation. Scope is limited: it applies to banks classified as G-SIBs, those exceeding the EUR 200 billion leverage exposure threshold, or those included in the assessment sample; in the SAMA context it is not required unless SAMA identifies the bank as a G-SIB.

Pillar 3 template disclosing the geographical distribution of private sector credit exposures used to compute the bank-specific countercyclical capital buffer rate, including the geographical allocation methodology and any departures from an ultimate-risk basis. Disclosed semiannually in flexible format. Mandatory only for banks with exposures to jurisdictions where the countercyclical buffer rate is above zero.

Pillar 3 leverage ratio template reconciling total accounting assets in published financial statements to the leverage ratio exposure measure, identifying consolidation and other adjustments. It sits within the Pillar 3 suite alongside key prudential metrics and asset encumbrance disclosures. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework and the leverage ratio standard.
lookup_terms: accounting assets vs leverage ratio exposure measure

data.summary: A fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's disclosure requirements framework, setting out the common disclosure of a bank's leverage ratio, its components (Tier 1 capital, total exposure measure) and the resulting ratio. It sits alongside the key metrics and capital-distribution-constraint disclosures that also report leverage figures. Mandatory for banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime, on the frequency and format prescribed for the template.

A qualitative/quantitative Pillar 3 table requiring banks to describe their liquidity risk management framework and liquidity position, including liquidity risk governance and risk tolerance, funding strategy and diversification, risk mitigation techniques, stress testing use and contingency funding plans, plus bank-specific metrics, concentration limits and entity/branch-level liquidity exposures. The table is mandatory for all banks, disclosed annually in a flexible format tailored to the bank's business model and liquidity risk profile.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template for the Liquidity Coverage Ratio, presenting unweighted and weighted values of high-quality liquid assets and net cash outflows and the resulting LCR. It complements the key metrics template, which also carries headline liquidity standard figures. Mandatory for banks within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure scope, using the prescribed fixed format and reporting frequency.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template for the Net Stable Funding Ratio, reporting available stable funding and required stable funding components and the resulting NSFR. It is the disclosure counterpart to the NSFR standard and feeds the liquidity metrics shown in the key metrics template. Mandatory for banks in SAMA's Pillar 3 scope, in the prescribed fixed format and frequency.

The NSFR common disclosure template with its line-by-line completion instructions, mapping asset and liability categories to available stable funding and required stable funding factors (e.g. performing loans, residential mortgages, non-HQLA securities, commodities, initial margin, derivative assets and liabilities, off-balance sheet items). Rows are compulsory for all banks, figures are quarter-end observations, and shading conventions and subtotal relationships are prescribed. Binds banks completing NSFR disclosures under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

A Pillar 3 template giving an overview of credit risk mitigation techniques, showing exposures unsecured versus secured by collateral, financial guarantees and credit derivatives. It sits in the credit risk disclosure block (with Table CRC on qualitative CRM disclosure) covering items subject to credit risk RWA, excluding securitisation and counterparty credit risk positions which are disclosed elsewhere. Mandatory for banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

This node concerns Template SEC1 within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements, covering the disclosure of carrying values for securitisation exposures and whether those figures reconcile to Template LI1. It also sits alongside the general rules distinguishing fixed-format from flexible-format templates and the use of signposting to other published documents. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework when preparing securitisation and counterparty credit risk disclosures.

This node sets out how often and when banks must publish Pillar 3 disclosures — quarterly, semi-annual or annual depending on the template — and requires the Pillar 3 report to be published at the same time as the corresponding financial report. It sits within the broader disclosure principles (clarity, meaningfulness, consistency, comparability), board-approved disclosure policy and assurance requirements, and the conditions for signposting information held in other documents. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

This node covers the minimum capital requirements for counterparty credit risk (CCR) and credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk, including the definition of CVA risk, the scope of covered transactions (derivatives and fair-valued SFTs), the CVA portfolio concept, and the choice between the basic (BA-CVA) and standardised (SA-CVA) approaches, with SA-CVA requiring SAMA approval. It also addresses eligible and ineligible internal and external CVA hedges and their interaction with market risk capital. It binds banks calculating regulatory capital under SAMA's Basel-based framework.

This node sets out the Standardised Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR), its scope over OTC derivatives, exchange-traded derivatives and long settlement transactions, and its mandatory use by banks without IMM approval. It also covers how CCR exposure (EAD) feeds into standardised or IRB credit risk RWA, exemptions where the CCR charge is zero (certain purchased credit protection and sold banking-book CDS), and the reference to minimum haircut floors for in-scope SFTs. It binds banks calculating CCR capital under SAMA's framework.
lookup_terms: sold credit default swap banking book

data.summary: This node is the definitional glossary for counterparty credit risk exposure measures, including current exposure/replacement cost, peak exposure, expected exposure, effective expected exposure, expected positive exposure (EPE) and effective EPE, plus credit valuation adjustment and one-sided CVA, and risk-neutral versus actual distributions. It also notes the CVA materiality threshold expressed by aggregate notional of non-centrally cleared derivatives. These defined terms govern how banks measure and calibrate CCR exposures under SAMA's capital framework.

This node prescribes how a clearing member bank capitalises its default fund contributions to a qualifying CCP, through the risk-sensitive capital requirement KCMi calculated in two steps: the CCP's hypothetical capital requirement (KCCP) and then the member-level allocation with a floor. It also allocates responsibility for producing and sharing the underlying data and sets a minimum quarterly calculation frequency for KCCP, subject to SAMA requiring more frequent calculation. It binds banks that are clearing members of CCPs and, in practice, the CCPs and supervisors supplying the inputs.

Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's public disclosure framework requiring a breakdown of collateral posted and received in support of counterparty credit risk exposures from derivatives and securities financing transactions, including CCP-cleared trades. It is mandatory for all banks, reported semiannually, with a flexible row structure (columns fixed) and an accompanying narrative explaining material period-on-period changes. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements at the level of what must be publicly disclosed, not how exposures are calculated.
lookup_terms: composition of collateral for CCR exposure
fair value of collateral received and posted

data.summary: Node for the market risk internal models approach (IMA) capital requirements disclosure template in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework; the captured context is largely adjacent material (Template CDC on capital distribution constraints and Tier 2/TLAC deduction line explanations) rather than the MR2 instructions themselves. Useful mainly as an entry point into the market risk and capital-composition disclosure templates. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Pillar 3 template requiring a flow statement of RWA movements for counterparty credit risk exposures measured under the internal models method (IMM), broken down by driver (including model updates and methodology/policy changes specific to IMM). Interpretive guidance in the context clarifies that CCR7 splits by EAD methodology rather than risk-weighting methodology, and that IRB model changes affecting IMM-valued exposures should be captured in added rows. Binds banks disclosing under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework that have approval to use IMM.

Pillar 3 template linking financial statement carrying values to regulatory scopes of consolidation and mapping balance sheet items to the credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitisation and market risk frameworks. The retrieved context includes the companion LI2 purpose statement and interpretive Q&A on LI1 (treatment of 1,250% risk-weighted exposures and which liabilities fall in the residual column). Mandatory for all banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
lookup_terms: linkages between financial statements and regulatory exposures

data.summary: Pillar 3 template disclosing the main sources of difference between financial statement carrying values (under the regulatory scope of consolidation) and the exposure amounts used for regulatory capital purposes, covering off-balance sheet amounts, valuation differences, netting differences, provisions and prudential filters. Annual, flexible format with rows adapted to the bank's most meaningful drivers, supported by narrative Table LIA. Interpretive Q&A distinguishes balance sheet netting from incremental Basel netting. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
lookup_terms: differences between regulatory exposure amounts and carrying values

data.summary: Node for one of the credit risk disclosure templates in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework; the retrieved context does not contain the CR9 instructions themselves but general framework rules on fixed versus flexible template formats, permitted row/column changes, signposting to other documents, and interpretive Q&A on other templates. Open it mainly for the cross-cutting presentation and signposting rules that apply to all banks disclosing under this framework.

A node within SAMA's counterparty credit risk capital rules covering how margin agreements affect exposure measurement, including the replacement cost and potential future exposure components of SA-CCR (EAD = alpha × (RC + PFE)) and the internal model method treatment of margined netting sets. It sets out what an EPE model must capture (unilateral vs bilateral margin, call frequency, margin period of risk, thresholds, minimum transfer amounts) and the supervisory floors on the margin period of risk, including higher floors for large or illiquid-collateral netting sets. It binds banks calculating regulatory capital for counterparty credit risk on derivatives and repo-style transactions.

Part of SAMA's leverage ratio framework dealing with how derivative exposures enter the leverage ratio exposure measure, including replacement cost plus add-on treatment, recognition (or non-recognition) of purchased credit protection such as total return swaps, and the option to exclude offset portions of written credit derivatives from the PFE netting set to avoid double counting. It also frames the boundary with securities financing transactions. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Basel III leverage ratio requirements.

Covers the inclusion of securities financing transactions — repos, reverse repos, securities lending/borrowing and margin lending — in the leverage ratio exposure measure, together with the general rules on on-balance sheet exposures, fiduciary asset exclusions, securitisation exposures and central bank (SAMA) reserves. It flags structures SAMA regards as leverage-ratio-minimising, such as agency-model transacting and collateral swaps. It binds banks computing the SAMA leverage ratio.

Defines written credit derivatives broadly for leverage ratio purposes (any instrument or option under which the bank effectively provides credit protection) and sets the conditions under which purchased credit protection may offset the effective notional amount of sold protection. Conditions include identical reference names (same legal entity), same or more conservative material terms, seniority/pari passu ranking, strike price limits, and full-pool coverage where protection is bought on a pool. It binds banks calculating the leverage ratio exposure measure for sold credit protection.

Addresses off-balance sheet items in the leverage ratio (conversion of commitments and similar exposures via credit conversion factors), the settlement-date accounting treatment that routes exposures into the off-balance sheet rules, and the treatment of cash pooling arrangements where individual customer balances are or are not transferred daily into a single account balance. It also lists structures SAMA views as leverage-ratio-minimising. It binds banks computing the SAMA leverage ratio exposure measure.

Sets the cumulative conditions under which cash variation margin may be treated as a form of pre-settlement payment for leverage ratio purposes — non-segregation and free use of cash received, at least daily mark-to-market exchange, currency specified in the contract/MNA/CSA, full extinguishing amount, and coverage by a single legally enforceable master netting agreement. Where met, cash variation margin received reduces the replacement cost component (not PFE) and margin provided may be deducted from the exposure measure; it also introduces the clearing member/CCP client clearing treatment. It binds banks calculating the leverage ratio for derivative exposures.

Defines the hypothetical capital requirement of a central counterparty (KCCP) — a supervisory construct computed on a consistent basis solely to determine how clearing member banks capitalize their default fund contributions to a qualifying CCP (QCCP), not the CCP's own capital requirement. It sits in the first step of the two-step risk-sensitive calculation of a clearing member bank's capital requirement (KCMi), and is accompanied by definitions of QCCP, clearing member and client, including CCP-to-CCP links. It binds locally licensed banks acting as clearing members, with SAMA retaining discretion where a CCP's jurisdiction does not apply the CPMI-IOSCO Principles and on the treatment of inter-CCP margin and default fund contributions.

Sets out the reduced version of the basic approach to CVA risk capital (Kreduced), which gives no recognition to counterparty credit spread hedges and is intended for banks that do not hedge CVA. Capital is the discounted aggregation across in-scope counterparties of stand-alone CVA capital, using a supervisory correlation parameter to combine systematic and idiosyncratic CVA risk components. It applies to banks calculating CVA capital under BA-CVA, and the same quantity also feeds the full BA-CVA calculation as a floor on hedging benefit.

Covers the full version of the basic approach to CVA risk capital (Kfull), which recognizes eligible counterparty credit spread hedges and is aimed at banks that actively hedge CVA; the reduced BA-CVA result is embedded in it as a conservative limit on hedging recognition. The surrounding provisions govern treatment of eligible and ineligible external hedges, internal CVA hedges between the CVA desk and trading desks, and interaction with market risk capital and IRB maturity adjustment. It binds banks using BA-CVA for covered derivative and SFT transactions.

Defines regulatory CVA and CVA risk and delimits the scope of the CVA capital charge: it excludes the bank's own default, imposes constraints on the accounting-based calculation, and covers derivatives (other than those with a qualified CCP or otherwise exempt) plus fair-valued SFTs where CVA loss exposure is material. Capital is computed for a stand-alone CVA portfolio comprising covered transactions and eligible hedges. All banks with covered transactions in either the banking or trading book are bound; BA-CVA is the default approach and SA-CVA requires prior SAMA approval, with materiality assessments for SFTs to be justified to SAMA.

Governs the vega risk component of the standardized approach to CVA capital (SA-CVA), computed as the simple sum of independently calculated vega requirements across five risk classes (interest rate, FX, reference credit spread, equity, commodity), with no vega charge for counterparty credit spread risk. It requires vega sensitivities to be calculated in all cases regardless of whether the portfolio contains options, applying volatility shifts to both path-generation and option-pricing volatilities, and addresses index hedge sensitivities and the SA-CVA multiplier that SAMA may raise for model risk. It binds banks approved by SAMA to use SA-CVA.

Explains the aggregate add-on component of potential future exposure under SA-CCR: add-ons are computed per asset class within a netting set and summed with no diversification benefit across the five asset classes, then scaled by a multiplier that recognizes excess collateral or negative mark-to-market, subject to a floor. It also covers the related replacement cost formulation using threshold, minimum transfer amount and net independent collateral amount, and the allocation of derivatives to asset classes by primary risk driver. It binds banks measuring counterparty credit risk exposure under SA-CCR.

A SAMA circular directing all supervised entities to respond promptly to judicial authorities, answer their requests within the prescribed statutory time limits, and receive and execute court judgments and decisions without delay. It follows an earlier circular on enforcing judicial rulings and warns that delay or procrastination may trigger supervisory/statutory action against both institutions and individual employees. It binds banks, finance companies, money exchangers and credit information companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: enforcement of judicial decisions by supervised entities
finance companies money exchangers credit bureaus circular
penalties for delay in responding to courts

data.summary: Rules (first issue) attached to a SAMA circular governing the electronic issuance of bank documents and the electronic verification of their authenticity. They require banks to process all customer document requests through technical systems, issue documents electronically in Arabic (and English on request), include issuance dates and confidentiality/authenticity markings, provide a verification means on every document, and comply with the Personal Data Protection Law, the Electronic Transactions Law and SAMA's information security and business continuity frameworks; a minimum list of documents (bank certificate, debt confirmation, account statement, clearance letter, IBAN certificate) must be available. Binding on banks licensed under the Banking Control Law, effective from the date stated in the circular.
lookup_terms: bank certificate account statement clearance letter

data.summary: A SAMA circular reminding supervised financial institutions of their obligations under the Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19) and the data governance policies, controls and rules issued by SDAIA. It requires institutions to review and align internal policies and procedures with those instruments within the statutory compliance period, perform a regulatory gap analysis, and submit a remediation timeline to the board for approval, with communications routed to a designated SAMA compliance mailbox. Effective immediately for entities under SAMA supervision.

The first issue of SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for local banks, issued under the SAMA Law and the Banking Control Law, structured in three chapters: definitions and scope; the roles of the board, audit committee and executive management toward internal audit; and detailed requirements for the internal audit unit as third line of defence (independence, audit policy, organisation, risk-based audit plan, quality assurance, reporting, subsidiaries). Binding on locally licensed commercial banks from the stated effective date.

Instrument-level node for SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for local banks operating in the Kingdom (first issue), issued under SAMA's supervisory powers. It sets governance expectations for internal audit: board, audit committee and executive management duties; independence, objectivity and professional ethics of the unit; audit policy, structure, reporting lines, SAMA non-objection to appointing or changing the head of the unit; risk assessment methodology, risk-based plan, quality assurance, periodic reporting and record keeping; and audit coverage of subsidiaries. Binds locally licensed banks.

Sub-node covering Principle 5 of SAMA's Internal Audit Principles: the requirement for a documented internal audit policy (audit charter) for the unit, sitting alongside principles on the unit's key attributes, organisation, working procedures and scope of work. It defines what must be set out regarding the unit's mandate, authority, independence and operating framework within the bank's governance structure. Applies to locally licensed banks and their boards/audit committees.
lookup_terms: audit committee approval of audit policy

data.summary: This node covers the Internal Audit Unit as defined and regulated under SAMA's first-issue Principles of Internal Audit for local banks operating in the Kingdom, issued under the Saudi Central Bank Law and the Banking Control Law. It sets out the Unit's definition as an independent, objective assurance and consulting function on the adequacy and effectiveness of internal control, together with its independence and objectivity, professional competence and due care, ethics, internal audit policy, organisational structure and reporting lines, and head-of-unit requirements including SAMA no-objection for appointment and replacement. It binds locally licensed banks, their Boards, Audit Committees and senior management, with the Principles effective from the date stated in the covering circular.

This node addresses the risk-based internal audit plan requirement within SAMA's Principles of Internal Audit for local banks, including the underlying risk assessment methodology, the inventory of auditable units and entities, and the audit cycle. It governs how the Internal Audit Unit prioritises and schedules coverage and how the plan is approved and reported to the Audit Committee. It binds locally licensed banks and their internal audit functions.
lookup_terms: خطة المراجعة الداخلية القائمة على المخاطر

data.summary: This node covers the quality assurance and improvement programme required of the Internal Audit Unit under SAMA's Principles of Internal Audit for local banks, alongside related requirements on audit information technology, periodic reporting to the Audit Committee, and retention of records, documents and reports. It governs how banks evaluate and evidence the quality and effectiveness of their internal audit activity. It binds locally licensed banks, their internal audit units and Audit Committees.

This node concerns the Internal Audit Unit's relationship with second line of defence functions (such as risk management and compliance) and with external auditors, and separately the internal audit of the bank's subsidiaries' activities, as set out in SAMA's Principles of Internal Audit for local banks. It governs coordination, non-duplication and the boundary between assurance provided by the third line and control functions in the second line, confirming internal audit supplements rather than substitutes management oversight. It binds locally licensed banks and their group entities.

This is a SAMA circular reaffirming compliance with the requirements for remote working in customer service roles, supplementing an earlier SAMA circular that required remote customer-service staff to be registered in the financial institution's official records and with GOSI, and their contracts documented on the portal designated by the competent authority. It transmits and requires adherence to the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development decision restricting remote customer-service work to Saudi nationals. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA and applies from its date of issue.

This node is the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development ministerial decision (with its procedural guide) localising remote customer-service occupations to Saudi nationals, covering both direct and indirect contracting, including outsourced service arrangements forming the entity's main activity. It applies to all occupations and roles delivering customer service remotely by phone, email, chat, social media or direct interaction, with penalties under the standing violations and penalties schedule and application irrespective of the entity's Nitaqat band; enforcement looks at actual work performed, not only job titles. As transmitted by SAMA, it binds SAMA-supervised financial institutions alongside other private-sector entities.
lookup_terms: توطين مهن خدمة العملاء عن بعد

data.summary: Defined-term node within SAMA's Compliance Principles for banks and commercial banks operating in the Kingdom (issued under the SAMA Charter and the Banking Control Law, replacing the earlier compliance manual). It designates the Compliance Policy as the document approved by the local bank's board — or by the branch manager for foreign bank branches — setting out overall compliance responsibilities, the compliance unit's powers, and the bank's methodology for managing non-compliance risk, with mandatory content elements cross-referenced to Principle 1. It binds all licensed local banks and foreign bank branches in KSA.

Defined-term node identifying the Head of Compliance under SAMA's Compliance Principles: the chief executive of the compliance unit in local banks, and, in foreign bank branches, the first-management-level officer reporting directly to the branch head. The role covers coordinating identification of non-compliance risk, advising senior management on managing it, and supervising compliance officers and compliance staff (the latter two are separately defined, with "compliance officer" meaning a delegate embedded in another business unit). Relevant to appointment, reporting-line and accountability questions for banks in KSA.

Node covering the board of directors' responsibilities toward compliance under SAMA's Compliance Principles, one of the document's headline sections alongside senior management duties. The Board (for a foreign bank branch, the branch's most senior officer assumes board-level duties) approves the compliance policy and oversees management of non-compliance risk. Binds boards of local banks and the equivalent officer in foreign bank branches licensed under the Banking Control Law.

Node covering senior management's compliance responsibilities under SAMA's Compliance Principles. "Senior Management" is defined as the executive leadership of a local bank (CEO, managing director, general manager) and the senior executives who run the bank's business and propose and implement strategic decisions, and the branch head for foreign bank branches. It is the layer that must implement the board-approved compliance policy and act on the compliance function's advice and reporting.

Defined-term node for non-compliance risk (compliance risk) in SAMA's Compliance Principles: exposure to legal or administrative sanctions, financial loss, or reputational damage arising from failure to observe laws, regulations and instructions, financial-crime/AML requirements, or codes of conduct and sound professional practice. It frames the mandate of the compliance function and the scope of the compliance policy, and applies to all banks and foreign bank branches licensed in KSA.

Node on the independence of the compliance function and compliance unit under SAMA's Compliance Principles. The compliance function is defined as an independent function at the first management level below senior management that identifies, assesses, advises on, monitors and reports non-compliance risk; the compliance unit is a dedicated business unit (group, sector or department in local banks; department, division or section reporting to the most senior officer in foreign bank branches) whose head and staff perform compliance duties only. Relevant to conflict-of-interest, dual-hatting and outsourcing questions, including the document's principle on outsourcing compliance unit tasks.

A SAMA circular reaffirming that all supervised financial institutions must maintain customer communication channels and replace the existing unified customer-service number (920) with the unified toll-free number (800) for all customer segments. It supplements an earlier SAMA circular on making contact channels available. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision.

A SAMA circular transmitting the fourth edition of the instructions on the design of banding/strapping cards used for bundling sixth-issue banknote denominations, adding a card template for the new SAR 200 note and superseding the third edition. It prescribes mandatory card content (bank name and logo, two officers' names and signatures, note count and denomination, issue series) and exact colour specifications per denomination. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom and cash centres, with compliance required within three months.

A SAMA urgent circular requiring supervised financial institutions to condition dealings with lawyers on the lawyer holding the national unified entity number beginning with (7) issued through the legal entity register, following a request from the Ministry of Justice / Saudi Bar Association and Council of Ministers decision. It builds on SAMA's earlier instructions replacing commercial registration and licence numbers with the unified national number for non-government entities. It binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions and credit information companies.

A SAMA circular reinforcing prior security instructions by directing banks and money exchange centres to strengthen banknote examination procedures, exercise utmost care in verifying the authenticity of circulating currency, immediately report any suspected banknote to the security authorities and notify SAMA. It binds banks and exchange (money changer) centres operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA circular requiring banks and finance companies to respond to document and information requests from the General Secretariat of the Banking and Finance Disputes and Violations Committees for case preparation, within the deadlines set out in an annexed schedule (generally three, seven, ten or fifteen business days by document type). Where a deadline cannot be met, the institution must reply immediately explaining why and state a supply date not exceeding 60 days from the request. SAMA states it will take regulatory action for non-compliance; it binds all banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA circular confirming that banks and finance companies must take into account loans granted to individual customers by the development funds and development banks affiliated with the National Development Fund when assessing affordability, relying on reports from licensed credit information companies. Deductions by those development lenders must be included in the customer's monthly debt-burden ratio, applying the Responsible Lending Principles requirement to count government-provided loans within monthly obligations. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A node within SAMA's Compliance Principles circular for banks and commercial banks operating in the Kingdom, which replaced the earlier regulatory compliance manual and sets out board and senior management responsibilities, the definition and independence of the compliance function, compliance policy, compliance risk, and the compliance unit's staffing and outsourcing arrangements. The relevant point here is how compliance sits alongside internal audit as a separate, independent control function whose work is subject to audit review rather than performed by it. It binds locally incorporated banks and licensed branches of foreign banks (with the branch's senior officer standing in for the board), and was issued for guidance before becoming mandatory.

A SAMA circular amending paragraph 3 of the mandatory instructions applicable when offering residential real estate finance products to individuals, so that the finance offer may be delivered to the customer electronically as well as on paper, and replacing the earlier instructions. It sets minimum conduct requirements: affordability assessment before any offer, documented plain-language explanation of terms and risks, a written offer valid for at least fifteen working days including the finance contract, disclosure form and (for variable-rate products) a credit risk acknowledgment, and an independent qualified credit advisor consultation documented before contracting. It binds banks and real estate finance companies supervised by SAMA.

A SAMA circular transmitting instructions (originally issued by email in April 2020) requiring readiness to supply electronic payment acceptance to the grocery and foodstuff retail sector, in support of the national anti-commercial-concealment programme and reduced cash use. It requires readiness to open merchant bank accounts and e-wallets, to receive and process requests for SAMA-authorised acceptance means (POS terminals and QR codes) across all channels, to apply the merchant category code 5411, and to brief staff internally. It binds banks and payment service providers operating in the Kingdom.

A short SAMA circular reaffirming existing advertising and marketing instructions after SAMA observed non-compliant promotional material from supervised institutions. It restates that promotional advertising of products and services must be clear and must not contain wording that directly or indirectly misleads customers, requires institutions to review all existing promotional advertising for conformity, and warns that enforcement action will be taken against violators. It binds banks, finance companies and payment companies operating in the Kingdom, effective from its date.

A SAMA circular mandating use of a unified template for responding to complaints received through the SAMA Cares ("Sama Tahtam") system, issued after SAMA observed quality deficiencies in responses. It prescribes response formats by category — requesting missing documents, informing the customer of the outcome and corrective action taken with supporting documents, and responding to complaints escalated to SAMA with reference to the specific instruction, contract or terms relied on — and requires institutions to strengthen their customer care function and maintain and periodically measure a service-level agreement for timely complaint handling. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA.

SAMA instructions on services provided to persons with disabilities by financial institutions, aimed at fairness, financial inclusion and removal of physical and behavioural barriers so that customers with disabilities can manage their financial affairs independently and privately. It defines "person with disability", "disability", "financial institution" and "accessibility", and imposes requirements including establishing a dedicated administrative unit, accessible premises and branches, accessible self-service and electronic channels, transparency and fairness in dealings, and financial education and awareness. It binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions — banks and foreign bank branches, insurance and reinsurance firms, finance companies, finance lease registration companies, credit information companies, payment companies and exchange businesses — with a three-month implementation period and a compliance plan due within one month.

SAMA circular addressing fraudulent use of the POS preauthorization transaction and the subsequent capture/purchase advice on cards issued under international payment schemes. It requires acquirers hosting POS payments to apply the relevant international scheme rules and conditions, to enable preauthorization only for eligible merchant sectors, to monitor and investigate suspicious and high-risk transactions relative to customer segment and amount, and to align fraud monitoring and detection arrangements with those standards, alongside full adherence to SAMA's counter-fraud manual. It binds banks and payment/fintech companies providing acquiring services, effective from its date.

SAMA circular strengthening KYC and identity-proofing by requiring financial institutions to confirm that the mobile number registered on a customer's account or membership belongs to the same person, by matching the account holder's ID with the ID of the mobile subscriber through the national trusted verification service. Institutions must assess and quantify existing non-matching accounts, report results and a remediation plan to SAMA, adopt the verified mobile number in new account/membership opening (in-person and remote), and comply within 45 days, with enforcement action for non-compliance. Applies to banks, finance companies, payment service providers and category (A) exchange centres.

SAMA circular implementing the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development's remote work initiative in the financial sector. It requires financial institutions to record remote customer-service staff in official registers and either enrol them in social insurance or document their remote-work contracts on the ministry's designated portal, including where the worker is engaged directly or supplied through an intermediary, contractor or outsourced provider. Binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions from the circular's date.

SAMA circular standardising the content of transaction notification messages sent to customers, extending earlier instructions on mada card notifications to all financial transactions on accounts, memberships and e-wallets. Attached tables set out the minimum data elements per transaction type (card purchases domestic/international, ATM withdrawals, deposits, cheques, domestic and international transfers, online purchases, bill payments, financing disbursement and instalments, fees, refunds/reversals, mobile app and wallet transactions) and a unified Arabic/English terminology list. Institutions must send notifications for all financial transactions within 15 days and file an implementation plan within two weeks; binds banks, payment service providers and category (A) exchange companies.

SAMA circular and accompanying instructions on replacing commercial registration and licence numbers with the National Information Center unified number beginning with 7 as the digital identifier for non-governmental entities. It extends the migration deadline, consolidates and supersedes all earlier replacement circulars, and sets requirements to add and link a unified-number field alongside the retained CR field in systems, to inventory affected customers, business partners and members, and to manage migration impacts on high-risk areas including credit, holds/blocking, dormancy, local and UN lists, KYC and beneficial ownership verification, with periodic reporting to SAMA. Binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions and credit information companies.

Issued under the SAMA Law and the Banking Control Law, these Compliance Principles replace the earlier compliance manual for banks and set the framework for managing compliance risk. They define the compliance function, compliance policy, compliance unit, head of compliance, compliance officers and compliance risk, and allocate responsibilities to the board and senior management, including policy approval, reporting, cross-border/foreign operations issues and outsourcing of compliance tasks. They bind local commercial banks and licensed branches of foreign banks (where the branch head assumes board-level duties), guidance-only until end 2015 and mandatory thereafter.

SAMA circular (1441) directing banks and payment service providers to be ready to receive and process requests from retail-sector merchants for electronic payment acceptance, following the mandatory roll-out agreed with the Anti-Commercial Concealment Program, Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Ministry of Commerce. It requires readiness to open merchant accounts and e-wallets, to install SAMA-authorised payment means (mada POS devices, e-wallets) through all channels, to apply accurate Merchant Category Codes, and to brief branches and customer-service staff. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom, PSPs and Saudi Payments.

SAMA circular on real estate valuation fees in individual (retail) real estate finance contracts. It prohibits financiers from charging the valuation fee to the customer before initial credit approval is granted, and requires them, before contracting steps begin, to inform the customer and obtain a written acknowledgement that the fee is non-refundable where the financing is not completed for reasons attributable to the customer. It binds banks and real estate finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

Short SAMA circular (1441) supplementing the earlier Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions circular. It confirms that money exchange companies and establishments operating in the Kingdom fall within the definition of "financial institutions" for purposes of those principles, and must therefore apply them to staff conduct, integrity, transparency and objectivity. It binds licensed exchange companies and establishments.
lookup_terms: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics

data.summary: SAMA circular (1443) imposing a refund deadline and penalty fees on mada-related customer claims. Banks must correctly refund customers for erroneous or incomplete transactions across ATM, POS and e-commerce services within two business days, and banks failing to do so incur a per-claim settlement fee under a set schedule. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom, PSPs and Saudi Payments, and is grounded in SAMA's authority over payment and settlement systems.

SAMA circular extending the electronic payment acceptance mandate to personal-services activities, requiring banks and payment service providers to be ready to receive merchant account and e-wallet opening requests and requests for SAMA-authorised payment means (POS devices or QR codes) through branches, website and unified call centre. It also requires use of the Merchant Category Codes designated for this sector and internal briefing of staff. It binds banks, PSPs operating in the Kingdom and Saudi Payments.

SAMA instructions on publication of penalties, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation. Finance and refinance companies must disclose, in their annual board of directors' reports under a "SAMA enforcement decisions" heading, violations for the current and preceding financial year, showing the violation subject, number of enforcement decisions (monetary and non-monetary) and total fines in SAR, using categories for supervisory instructions, consumer protection and AML/CTF due diligence. SAMA will reconcile disclosures against its records, publish violations on its website, and act against non-compliance; effective from the FY2021 board report.
lookup_terms: board of directors annual report disclosure
Finance Companies Control Law Implementing Regulation Article 72/73

data.summary: A SAMA circular to finance companies, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and the finance customer protection principles, requiring that natural-person customers sign every page of the contracts and agreements to which they are a party. Applying the same requirement to legal persons is optional, but finance companies bear the risk arising from not obtaining page-by-page signatures from corporate customers. Effective from its date and binding on all finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: borrower signature on all contract pages
principles for protecting finance company customers

data.summary: A SAMA circular instructing finance companies to accept electronically notarised articles of association of limited liability companies that carry only the Ministry of Commerce and Investment seal and no notary public stamp, following a Ministry of Commerce telegram permitting electronic notarisation for LLCs owned by Saudi partners (non-minors), a Saudi individual, or a registered resident. Companies must verify the incorporation contract data through the existing verification service used by banks and financial institutions or via the Ministry's 'Aamaly' page. Binding on finance companies operating in the Kingdom from its date.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Commerce and Investment seal

data.summary: A SAMA circular making compliance with specified articles of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law optional for finance companies when dealing with small, medium and large enterprises. The definitions of SMEs and large enterprises are those in the referenced SAMA circular adopting the Small and Medium Enterprises General Authority board decision. It effectively narrows certain conduct/disclosure obligations to non-enterprise (retail) dealings.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law

data.summary: A SAMA circular to banks and finance companies requiring equal, non-discriminatory access for all segments of society to financing products and to insurance coverage under finance lease contracts, based on the fair-treatment principles in the banking and finance customer protection principles. It links to SAMA's earlier circular to insurers prohibiting refusal of compulsory or comprehensive motor cover based on the age of the actual user of a leased vehicle, and bars financiers from refusing customers on that ground.
lookup_terms: actual user of leased vehicle age
principles for protecting finance company customers

data.summary: A SAMA circular informing finance companies that, following a Minister of Justice decision adding a provision to the Implementing Regulation of the Code of Law Practice, legal department employees of a private legal person are treated as its legal representative once licensed by the General Department of Advocacy and holding a power of attorney from the authorised signatory. Such employees may litigate for the finance company before competent judicial bodies in up to three cases at a time, subject to listed application documents and conditions.
lookup_terms: legal representative of private legal person
Code of Law Practice implementing regulation
litigation on behalf of finance company

data.summary: A SAMA circular, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and coordinated with the Capital Market Authority, clarifying the activities finance companies may undertake with CMA-licensed persons to diversify liquidity sources. It permits selling finance portfolios to investment funds, entering loan participation agreements with investment funds for co-financing, and allowing funds to invest amounts with finance companies provided the credit-granting decision remains with the finance company.
lookup_terms: investment funds indirect participation in finance sector
credit decision retained by finance company

data.summary: A SAMA circular (dated 30/04/1440H) reminding banks operating in the Kingdom to reactivate earlier circulars on cash-handling awareness and to educate customers about the security and crime risks of carrying large cash amounts. It directs banks to promote electronic channels as an alternative and to point customers to licensed cash-and-valuables transport companies as a safe option. It binds banks operating in Saudi Arabia; it is an awareness/customer-communication obligation rather than a prudential or AML reporting rule, though it sits alongside cash-crime concerns.

A SAMA circular (06/04/1440H) issued under Article 15(c) of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business (Ministerial Decision 1350) requiring that all jobs in money exchange businesses be restricted to Saudi nationals, with appropriate training. Exchange houses and exchange companies had to submit a Saudization plan within two weeks and complete full Saudization within one year, with enforcement action against non-compliant firms. It binds money exchange institutions and companies operating in the Kingdom (category A/B).
lookup_terms: Rules Governing Money Exchange Business Article 15

data.summary: A bilingual FAQ explaining the purpose, benefits and application logic of SAMA's Regulatory Sandbox, which permits testing of new business models, products and services in a live environment under pre-defined limits (client numbers, transaction volume and value). It clarifies that the Sandbox is reserved for propositions with no existing regulatory framework or licensing path, and that exemptions are assessed case-by-case under the published Regulatory Sandbox Framework. It is guidance for prospective applicants (fintechs and other innovators), not a binding rule instrument.

SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions (v1.0, August 2019) sets the minimum framework each financial institution must adopt for receiving and handling violation reports, covering the reporting unit, reportable cases, whistle blower and institution obligations, protection from retaliation, confidentiality, report processing and KPIs. It requires secure reporting channels, objective and progressive handling with corrective action plans, an internal approval/oversight policy, and an automated register of report data. It binds SAMA-supervised financial institutions and shapes duties toward employees and stakeholders who report suspected violations.

A SAMA circular to finance companies requiring them to obtain SAMA's no-objection before providing governmental or non-governmental entities with the periodic supervisory data submitted to SAMA or with unpublished statistical data. It is grounded in SAMA's supervisory role over the finance sector and its interest in data accuracy and controlled disclosure. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA circular prohibiting supervised entities from using SAMA's logo on their printed materials or publications without prior approval, to prevent reputational harm, commercial exploitation of the logo, or misleading customers. Entities must ensure their branches comply, and SAMA may take action against violators under the relevant laws. It binds banks, insurance and reinsurance companies, finance companies, credit bureaus, insurance-related professions firms, and money exchange institutions/companies.
lookup_terms: use of central bank logo on publications

data.summary: SAMA circular exercising the discretion in Article 12 of the Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Finance Law to reset the maximum loan-to-value ratio, raising the cap for Saudi citizens acquiring a first home to 90% while retaining 70% for banks and 85% for real estate finance companies on second and subsequent homes for all beneficiaries. It also reiterates expectations on risk management policy, credit concentration monitoring and affordability/repayment-capacity verification before granting any financing. Binds SAMA-licensed banks and real estate finance companies, effective from its date.
lookup_terms: Real Estate Finance Law Implementing Regulation Article 12

data.summary: Rules standardising the calculation and disclosure of the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) for retail lending, mandating use of SAMA's Excel-based APR Calculator and a net present value formula. They apply to APR shown in advertising, offers, contracts, periodic statements and any other disclosure, and require providers to update policies, maintain internal controls over calculator integrity, and align customer-facing website calculators. Bind all finance providers engaged in retail lending, read together with the Finance Companies Control Law, consumer microfinance and consumer financing regulations.

Short SAMA circular to all money exchange businesses operating in the Kingdom, grounded in Article 18 of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business, which requires each exchanger to appoint a SAMA-accepted licensed external auditor for annual audit. It directs the addressees to obtain and report to SAMA the accounting standards their external auditor applies when auditing the financial statements. Binds licensed exchange companies and establishments.
lookup_terms: Rules Governing Money Exchange Business Article 18

data.summary: SAMA circular reminding all exchange companies and establishments to comply with existing instructions on the movement and transport of cash and with the security safety manual, following observed non-compliance. It warns that transporting cash outside the regulated channels, or receiving cash so transported from other exchangers, exposes the party to statutory penalties under the Banking Control Law. Binds licensed money exchange businesses in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: transport of money and precious metals law

data.summary: SAMA circular confirming that, under Article 25(2) of the Finance Lease Law, repossession of movable leased assets from the lessee—where the contract grants the lessor that right—may only be carried out through the competent authorities, pending Ministry of Justice licensing of specialised repossession companies. It aligns with Ministry of Interior instructions barring self-help vehicle repossession and warns that finance company staff who repossess without recourse to the competent authorities face legal action. Binds banks and finance companies licensed to conduct finance leasing.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Justice licensed enforcement companies

data.summary: SAMA circular fixing official holiday dates for finance companies under Article 21 of the Finance Companies Control Law and Article 2 of its Implementing Regulation: four days for Eid al-Fitr starting after 29 Ramadan (Umm al-Qura calendar), four days for Eid al-Adha starting on the Day of Arafah, and National Day (23 September), with substitution rules when it falls on a Saturday or Friday. SAMA will circulate any changes to Eid dates. Binds all finance companies operating in the Kingdom and their branches.

A SAMA circular from the General Directorate of Supervision of Finance Companies reminding banks and finance companies to register lands subject to the White Land Fees Law within the prescribed period so that beneficial owners do not incur financial penalties. It is issued under SAMA's charter, the Banking Control Law and the Finance Companies Control Law, and refers to the White Land Fees Law and its Implementing Regulation. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA Banking Policies Department circular informing supervised entities that deeds and instruments issued by notaries licensed by the Ministry of Justice — within their competence (e.g. powers of attorney and their revocation, company contracts and amendments) — must be accepted and treated as enforceable instruments under the Enforcement Law. It notes that the validity of a notary's licence can be verified through the Ministry of Justice notaries portal. It binds banks, insurance and reinsurance companies, finance companies, credit information companies and money exchangers.

A SAMA circular issuing a unified definition of "commercial real estate financing": credit extended to a natural or legal person to purchase, develop or build real estate, qualifying as commercial where any one of four criteria is met (corporate beneficiary; five or more residential units; predominantly non-residential use; or income-producing property). Addressees must align policies, procedures and regulatory reporting with the definition from Q3 2017. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA Banking Policies Department circular adopting the SME definition approved by the board of the General Authority for Small and Medium Enterprises (Monsha'at), setting micro, small, medium and large enterprise thresholds by annual revenue with full-time employee headcount as the fallback criterion where revenue data is unavailable (e.g. new entities). It binds banks, finance companies and the credit information companies (SIMAH and Bayan).

A SAMA circular prohibiting licensed finance companies from requiring establishments and companies to affix an official stamp on documents and papers submitted in financing transactions, following Ministry of Commerce and Investment decisions and a Royal Order on improving investment-environment competitiveness. The prohibition applies without prejudice to Know Your Customer requirements, and is effective from the circular's date. It binds licensed finance companies.

A SAMA circular requiring all licensed finance companies to begin immediate preparation for implementing IFRS 9 (Financial Instruments) — covering classification and measurement, impairment on a forward-looking expected-loss basis, and hedge accounting — replacing IAS 39, effective for periods on or after 1 January 2018 with early adoption permitted. Companies must submit quarterly progress reports to SAMA starting from end of Q1 2017 and acknowledge receipt within one week. It is grounded in Article 71 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law and binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular interpreting the cap on fees, commissions and administrative service costs in Article 83 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law and Article 9 of the Consumer Finance Regulations (the lower of 1% of the finance amount or SAR 5,000). It clarifies that the cap covers every amount the borrower must pay other than the finance amount and the term cost, including unavoidable charges such as application study, real-estate valuation, property inspection and registration fees; the financier alone must deal with and pay third parties (valuers, registration bodies) and may not delegate that payment to the borrower, and all such charges must be reflected in the APR calculation. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom, effective from the circular date.

Urgent SAMA circular confirming that land financing granted to individuals falls within Article 12 of the Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Finance Law. It responds to recurring queries on scope and applies to all real estate financiers — banks and finance companies — operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: Article 12 Real Estate Finance Implementing Regulation

data.summary: A SAMA circular whose source text is largely illegible in the available scan (OCR-corrupted Arabic), so its subject matter and obligations cannot be reliably determined from the extract. Contextual markers suggest a supervisory circular issued to banks and/or finance companies referencing an article of an implementing regulation. The underlying PDF must be consulted directly before relying on it.

SAMA circular setting the start dates for finance companies to apply International Accounting Standards in preparing their accounts and financial statements under Article 71 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law. Applicants licensed as joint stock companies begin from the start of 2015 with quarterly IAS-based statements from Q1 2015; applicants licensed as limited liability companies begin from the date of the ministerial decision converting them into a joint stock company, filing quarterly statements from the first quarter of their first financial year as a JSC or Q1 2015, whichever is later, in line with Article 72. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular requiring banks and finance companies to document real estate mortgages according to the true nature of the contract and to stop procedures that transfer ownership of the property instead of registering a mortgage over it. It also requires rectification of properties currently registered in the name of the bank or finance company within a set period, customer awareness of that process, and reporting to SAMA of cases where notaries refuse to register a mortgage in the financier's favour. Effective from its date and binding on banks and finance companies in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: transfer of property title instead of mortgage
rectification of properties in bank's name

data.summary: SAMA circular to money exchange centers setting reporting obligations under the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business (Articles 15(c), 17 and 19): quarterly financial position within 15 days of the following quarter plus externally reviewed quarterly statements within 30 days, an audited annual balance sheet within one month and audited annual financial statements within two months of financial year end. It also caps external auditor tenure at five years, requires an annual external auditor assessment of internal control systems reported separately within two months, and specifies submission channels. Binding on exchange centers from financial year 2014, with enforcement action against non-compliant centers.

SAMA circular (Money Exchange Centers Supervision Division) issuing the minimum requirements that must be met in the premises of exchange centers, adopted under paragraph (c) of Article 15 of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business, with a one-year window to bring existing premises into compliance.
