It sets conditions on permitted location (main commercial street, mall, airport/border crossing) and SAMA prior no-objection before leasing, minimum floor areas and entrance setbacks (with a special threshold for the Central Haram Area), 3D engineering design by an approved office consistent with the financial sector security and safety guide, fit-out and customer-facing features (dedicated women's service window, accessibility, complaint and satisfaction mechanism, signage matching the commercial register and licence, insurance against fire and theft, national address), and technical requirements including an automated accounting/control system capable of applying AML requirements and screening against international prohibition lists in Arabic and English, off-site secure data backup with no external party access, and counterfeit-detection equipment. It binds licensed money exchangers and exchange institutions of categories (A) and (B).
lookup_terms: الحد الأدنى لمتطلبات مقار مراكز الصرافة
Article 15 Rules Governing Money Exchange Business
branch minimum area / Central Haram Area
sanctions list screening in exchange systems
data backup and system requirements for exchange centers

data.summary: Short SAMA circular answering exchange centers' queries on whether the child of a Saudi mother counts toward Saudization ratios, supplementing the earlier circular restricting all jobs in the exchange center sector to Saudis and requiring training/qualification of Saudi staff within one year. It confirms that categories treated as Saudis under decisions of the Ministry of Labour and Social Development are counted in Saudization percentages, must be disclosed in data submitted to SAMA, and that exchange centers must keep verifying and complying with whatever the Ministry issues on the point. It binds exchange centers of categories (A) and (B) operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: child of Saudi mother / أبن أبنة المواطنة
Ministry of Labour and Social Development
nationalization of jobs in money exchange sector
disclosure of staffing data to SAMA

data.summary: SAMA circular on subscription to SMS services, issued following a communication from the Minister of Communications and Information Technology on regulating SMS subscriptions under class (B) licence terms. It requires all financial institutions operating in the Kingdom to contract only with SMS service providers licensed by the Communications and Information Technology Commission, with licence status verifiable via the CITC website, effective from its date. It binds banks, finance companies, insurance sector companies, payment companies and exchange centers (A and B).

SAMA circular granting a narrow identification exception for customers of exchange center branches located in airports who are travelling outside the Kingdom: the national ID need not be presented, and a passport plus boarding pass matched against the customer's name suffices to execute transactions. It supplements the customer acceptance and identity verification policies in SAMA's manual on organising the work procedures of money exchange shops (February 2010) and rests on an approval conveyed by the Minister of Interior. It binds exchange centers of categories (A) and (B) and is effective from its date.
lookup_terms: دليل تنظيم إجراءات عمل محلات الصرافة

data.summary: SAMA circular (reference 48007/67, dated 1440/08/02) whose scanned text is heavily OCR-degraded and only partly legible. The legible fragments indicate it is issued by reference to the sector control laws (banking control, cooperative insurance companies control, real estate finance and finance companies control laws and their royal decrees) and concerns the provision/exchange of documents, information and data with SAMA and channels for communicating with supervised financial institutions. The distribution list covers banks, finance companies, insurance-sector companies and other licensed entities; the operative wording cannot be relied on from this extract and the source document should be opened for the actual requirement.
lookup_terms: Banking Control Law / Finance Companies Control Law reference
circular to banks finance and insurance companies

data.summary: SAMA circular on the issuance of debt instruments by finance companies through special purpose entities, grounded in Article 14 of the Finance Companies Control Law (permitting issuance of securities and sukuk under the Capital Market Law) and Article 66 of its Implementing Regulation (requiring a SAMA no-objection letter before issuing securities), and reflecting coordination with the Capital Market Authority. It confirms that finance companies may apply to the CMA to establish a special purpose entity under the CMA's SPV rules, must notify SAMA of that step, and must obtain SAMA's prior no-objection before issuing any debt instrument through the SPV. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: special purpose entity SPV finance company

data.summary: A concept node anchoring Vision 2030 as the policy driver cited in SAMA's Regulatory Sandbox Framework, alongside the Fintech Strategy approved by Council of Ministers decision No. 574 (25 May 2022). It is context rather than an obligation: it explains why SAMA operates a live testing environment for innovative financial products/services with real consumers under defined periods and controls, and frames the four sandbox exit outcomes (new framework, amended framework, amended rules/instructions, or confirmation that no SAMA approval is needed). It binds no one directly, but shapes how Innovators and licensed entities plan licensing pathways after testing.

The core scope and contracting provisions of SAMA's Consumer Financing Regulations, defining Consumer Financing (deferred debt or deferred repayment under a Financing Contract), the Amount of Financing basis (Gross Salary or monthly pension at application), and the form requirements for Financing Contracts and Guarantee Agreements. It excludes lease financing, real estate financing and margin lending. It binds Creditors dealing with Borrowers, including rules on Authenticated Communication for new financing and limit increases, documenting the purpose of financing, and the 20% repayment threshold before refinancing.

Annex 1 to the Consumer Financing Regulations setting the mandatory method for computing the Annual Percentage Rate: the discount rate equating the present value of all Borrower payments (Total Amount Payable) with the present value of financing amounts made available. It fixes calculation conventions — a 12 equal-month year, inclusion of all unavoidable costs and fees but exclusion of default/non-compliance charges, assumed contract validity and performance, fixed treatment of unquantifiable variable charges, and expression to at least two decimal/basis points. It binds Creditors whenever APR must be calculated or disclosed.
lookup_terms: Total Amount Payable by the Borrower

data.summary: Article 23 (Section Seven) of the Consumer Financing Regulations governing account statement errors and disputes: it defines what counts as an account statement error (failure to credit payments, accounting errors, improper fees) and sets the Creditor's investigation duty within 60 calendar days and no later than 90 calendar days from receipt of the Borrower's notice. Pending satisfactory resolution, the Borrower need not pay the disputed portion (including Term Cost) and the Creditor may not collect it, nor make or threaten adverse credit reporting or delinquency reporting on that basis. Confirmed errors must be corrected and refunded with notice by Guaranteed Communication means.

Article 22 (Section Six) of the Consumer Financing Regulations on ongoing conduct toward Borrowers: at least quarterly account statements (written or electronic, as pre-agreed) disclosing statement period dates, opening/closing balances, draw-downs, Term Cost charged, and fees and charges. It also requires at least 60 calendar days' advance notice via Guaranteed Communication before changing charges or payment methods, with the Borrower obliged to keep contact details current (failure releasing the Creditor from Article 22.5 liabilities). Related context includes affordability limits (33.33% of Gross Salary; 25% of pension), mandatory Licensed Credit Bureau checks with prior Borrower consent, and credit information registration and updating.

A SAMA Currency Department circular setting the agreed operating mechanism with Customs for the entry and exit of Saudi and foreign currency through the King Fahd Causeway customs point. It covers automated financial disclosure declaration forms, sealing and container/seal-number reconciliation, deposit and counting at SAMA's Dammam branch, escalation of discrepancies (declared versus delivered amounts, currency integrity, delays) and handling of counterfeit notes, plus armouring and armed-escort conditions for GCC cash-in-transit vehicles. It binds all banks and money exchange companies operating in the Kingdom, with SAMA's Dammam branch and supervisory functions as distribution recipients.

SAMA circular (Arabic) setting binding controls for how banks and money exchange companies handle "banking procedures transactions" received from SAMA on behalf of legally authorised government bodies — e.g. account attachment/seizure, lifting of attachment, disclosure of account information and documents under the Enforcement Law, AML Law, criminal and litigation procedure laws, and state revenue/VAT/zakat rules. It fixes maximum completion periods by category (judicial, civil/general, security), requires an immediate reply where no relationship exists, and requires dedicated, empowered and independent units with sufficient staff, technology, business-continuity plans and strict confidentiality, with a narrow exception for the customer or his authorised agent enquiring about execution affecting his own balance. Binds banks and exchange companies operating in the Kingdom, which bear responsibility toward the authorised bodies, SAMA and the customer, with enforcement action for non-compliance.

SAMA's Regulations for Consumer Financing, setting the conduct framework for granting Consumer Financing to a Borrower (a natural person financing outside trade or profession), covering financing contracts and guarantee agreements, obligations and accountability, advertising, disclosure rules, dealing with Borrowers, and dispute resolution. It requires a Borrower request via Authenticated Communication before new financing or any limit increase (each increase needing a new Financing Contract), documentation of the financing purpose, a refinancing eligibility threshold of at least 20% repayment of the original Amount of Financing, and full disclosure on refinancing. Applies to all kinds of Consumer Financing by Creditors supervised by SAMA; lease, real estate financing and margin lending are outside scope.

Annex 1 to the Regulations for Consumer Financing, describing the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) and its calculation convention: the discount rate equating the present value of all payments due from the Borrower (the Total Amount Payable) with the present value of the Amount of Financing made available. It sets the calculation assumptions — a 12 equal-month year, inclusion of all unavoidable costs and fees but exclusion of default/breach charges, continuation of the contract for the agreed term, and freezing of unquantifiable variable charges at initial level — and requires expression in percentage points to at least two decimal/basis points with rounding. Binds Creditors granting Consumer Financing whenever an APR must be calculated or disclosed.

SAMA Rules requiring finance providers engaged in retail lending to use SAMA's issued Excel-based APR Calculator and the prescribed net present value formula when determining APR. Finance providers must align policies and procedures, maintain internal controls and audit over the calculator, reconcile any automated tool against SAMA's Excel version, and keep customer-facing website calculators updated. The prescribed APR applies to advertising and promotional material, the offer stage, the financing contract, periodic statements and any other APR disclosure; the Rules are read with the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation, consumer microfinance rules, interest-rate disclosure rules and the Regulations for Consumer Financing.

SAMA circular under the Real Estate Finance Law and its Implementing Regulation adjusting the maximum loan-to-value cap in Article 12 of the Implementing Regulation, raising the ceiling for citizens acquiring a first home to 90%, while banks remain at 70% and real estate finance companies at 85% for a second or subsequent home for all beneficiaries. It also reiterates the requirement to review risk management policy, monitor and measure credit concentrations, and verify the beneficiary's repayment capacity — taking existing financial and credit obligations into account — before granting any financing. Binds SAMA-licensed banks and real estate finance companies, effective from its date.

SAMA circular adopting the SME definition approved by the board of the General Authority for Small and Medium Enterprises (Monsha'at), classifying enterprises as micro, small, medium or large by annual revenue bands with full-time employee headcount used only where revenue data is unavailable (e.g. a newly established entity). It is a definitional/classification instrument rather than a conduct rule, but drives SME-related reporting, lending classification and related supervisory treatment. Addressed to banks, finance companies operating in the Kingdom, and the credit information companies (SIMAH and Bayan).

SAMA circular (Deputy Governor for Supervision, 1440H/August 2019) issuing the Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics for Financial Institutions, with a three-month implementation window. It sets a minimum baseline of behavioural standards — professional conduct, dealings with stakeholders, gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, whistleblowing, remuneration and consequences of non-compliance — which the board must translate into an institution-specific code. It binds all 'financial institution personnel' as defined (board and committee members, executives, permanent and contract staff, consultants and third-party-supplied staff) across banks and foreign bank branches, finance and finance-lease registration companies, insurers/reinsurers and free insurance-profession firms, and credit bureaus supervised by SAMA.
lookup_terms: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics
conflict of interest gifts and hospitality

data.summary: The anti-financial-crime component of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics: a conduct-level duty on financial institution personnel to combat financial and administrative corruption, covering money laundering, terrorist financing and suspicious transactions alongside bribery and corruption. It expresses ethical/behavioural obligations for staff rather than the operational AML/CTF control framework, which sits in the AML Law, its Implementing Regulation and SAMA's AML/CTF Rules. Binds all personnel of SAMA-supervised financial institutions, with managers responsible for awareness and acknowledgement.

The confidentiality and disclosure strand of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics, covering safeguarding of information, disclosure mechanisms, misuse or leakage of internal (inside) information for market manipulation, and reporting of actual or potential violations. It frames staff-level secrecy and information-handling duties that overlay statutory banking secrecy and customer data obligations. Applies to all personnel of SAMA-supervised financial institutions, including contractors and third-party staff.

SAMA's Manual for Organizing the Business Procedures of Exchange Houses (First Edition, February 2015), supplementing the Rules Governing Money Changing Business and existing SAMA and AML/CTF instructions. It covers licensing categories (Category A permitted to issue/accept remittances, Category B limited to currency exchange and traveller's cheques), customer classification (membership customers vs. walk-in/transient customers), customer acceptance policies, KYC and CDD, remittance and bank cheque operations, cross-border transport of cash and negotiable instruments, correspondent banking, security systems, and staffing and training. Binds licensed exchange houses operating in the Kingdom; it also restates the prohibitions on deposit-taking and on non-banks conducting banking business.
lookup_terms: money changer Category A Category B

data.summary: The KYC/CDD component of the Exchange Houses Operations Manual: identifying and verifying customers and beneficial owners from reliable independent sources, risk-rating customer types, keeping identification data updated, monitoring changes, and making identification records available to the AML/CTF compliance officer. It sets transaction-tier requirements for currency exchange (ID copy, system registration and receipt content at defined SAR thresholds, passport/visa/entry-stamp checks for visitors, pilgrims and Umrah performers, GCC nationals treated as citizens), requires high-value individual exchange to be done only through a membership relationship consistent with the customer's income and occupation, and requires enhanced due diligence for corporate customers. Binds licensed exchange houses and their staff.

The section of the Exchange Houses Operations Manual addressing correspondent banking relationships used by exchange houses to route inbound and outbound domestic and international remittances. It sits within the manual's framework for remittance and bank cheque business and its AML/CTF requirements, and is relevant to due diligence on and oversight of counterparty institutions. Binds licensed exchange houses, in practice Category A houses permitted to issue and accept remittances.

A SAMA circular addressed to banks, finance companies (including real estate finance) and insurance companies in their capacity as clients of real estate valuation services. It requires them to deal only with valuers holding full membership of the Saudi Authority for Accredited Valuers, to govern the valuation process by separating financing/underwriting staff and decisions from valuer selection and report receipt, and prohibits any conduct that influences or coerces the valuer or valuation firm (fee withholding, blacklisting threats, inducements, supplying target or expected values, dictating valuation methods, imposing inadequate timeframes, linking fees to work volume, or excessive bank guarantee demands). It also requires supplying sufficient information on the asset, setting acceptance criteria for financeable properties, and bearing related costs.

A SAMA circular (Arabic, poorly digitised) on the submission of periodic financial statements to SAMA, requiring supervised entities to file annual and interim/quarterly financial data within stated deadlines and in the prescribed spreadsheet format. It mandates that submissions be accompanied by a signed Certification Statement attesting to the accuracy of the reported financial statements, executed by the Chief Accountant, Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Executive Officer or Managing Director. Open the source to confirm exact scope, filing deadlines and signatory requirements, as the OCR text is fragmentary.

A SAMA circular to banks and Class (A) money exchangers reinforcing Saudization obligations and setting requirements for contracting with recruitment/outsourcing service providers. It requires localisation across all job grades including senior and leadership roles, restricts branch, remittance-centre and cash-centre positions to Saudis (with a narrow non-Saudi customer-assistance exception carrying no systems access or account-opening authority), and confines cash handling, funds transfer, information security and AML/CTF roles to Saudi nationals. It also bans direct or indirect dealings with marketers of foreign banks' services in the Kingdom, and assigns HR to build localisation and training plans with Compliance overseeing implementation and quarterly progress reporting.

SAMA's License Disclosure Instructions, requiring all SAMA-supervised financial institutions to state their licensing status and SAMA supervision in correspondence, printed material, brochures, email, websites, mobile apps, directories, media advertising, press releases, direct customer contact and social media. It defines Financial Institution (banks and foreign bank branches, insurers and reinsurers, free professions companies, finance companies, credit bureaus, exchange houses and cash centres, payments and payment system companies), Advertising, Footers, Correspondence and Customers, and prescribes minimum disclosure content (legal name matching the licence, entity type, capital, CR number, address, licence number and SAMA supervision), with a reduced disclosure for advertisements and an exemption for commercial paper transactions.

A SAMA circular requiring banks operating in the Kingdom to publish in their annual reports the violations for which SAMA issued penal decisions, under a heading for SAMA penal decisions, covering the current and prior financial year. Disclosure must follow the prescribed table format showing the violation topic, the number of penal decisions and the total fines in Saudi riyals, using only the topic categories in the attached classification guide; SAMA will republish this information on its website.

The annex to SAMA's banking penalty publication circular: a mapping table translating the specific violation cited in a penal decision into one of the permitted public disclosure categories. Categories are limited to breach of SAMA supervisory instructions, consumer protection instructions, due diligence instructions, ATM/POS service-level instructions, and AML/CTF due diligence instructions; underlying decision topics range across banking procedures, account disclosure and seizure, liquidity, SAIBOR, interest rates, branch and ATM matters, outsourcing, products and services, clearing, e-service levels, internal policies, security, Saudization programmes, payment system operating rules, dispute/chargeback handling, and account opening rules.

A concept node anchored in SAMA's guide for regulating the operations of exchange houses (money changers), where FATF is defined as the intergovernmental standard-setter for AML/CTF and proliferation-financing measures, and its public statements on high-risk/non-cooperative jurisdictions are pointed to as a reference source. The surrounding material sets out exchange-house obligations on enhanced due diligence, screening membership-relationship customer names against asset-freeze lists (including UN Security Council designations and other national/bloc lists), transaction monitoring for activity without clear economic or lawful purpose, and reporting suspicions to the FIU or police. It binds licensed Category (A) and Category (B) exchange houses; the appendix also lists reference links to the Saudi AML Law and Bylaws, FATF, Basel and UN sources.
lookup_terms: Category A and Category B money changer

data.summary: A SAMA circular from the Deputy Governor for Supervision updating the standard-form current account opening agreement for individuals and legal persons, previously issued under an earlier circular, and attaching the revised template (parties, customer identification and profile data, and general terms and conditions). It adds a new clause under the rights and obligations section and reminds banks that only the versions published on SAMA's website are authoritative, since they are updated immediately. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom, which must implement the change within the timeframe set in the referenced circular.
lookup_terms: terms and conditions – rights and obligations of the parties

data.summary: The substantive amendment carried by the same circular: to enable activation of and subscription to additional services under the instant payments system, banks may share specified account information — customer name, account number, mobile number, ID/CR/unified number, and email — with Saudi Payments as national system operator, on a need basis and in strict confidence. The clause is inserted into the standard current account agreement so that customer consent/disclosure is contractually grounded. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: instant payments system / نظام المدفوعات الفورية

data.summary: A 1437H SAMA circular transmitting the recommendations of a joint security committee (Public Security, Ministry of Finance, SAMA) on the transport of cash, precious metals and valuable documents. It requires banks to strengthen oversight of contracted cash-transport companies inside cash centres and apply penalties for breaches, separates cash-transport duties from ATM-replenishment duties, sets crew and armed-escort composition, mandates dual-controlled sealing of ATM cassettes under CCTV, encourages high-specification tracking/ink-degradation containers, allows use of SIMAH credit records in screening job applicants, and requires banks to report their monitoring procedures to SAMA. It binds banks and licensed cash-transport companies.
lookup_terms: ATM replenishment / تغذية أجهزة الصرف الآلي

data.summary: A SAMA circular issuing the standard "Finance Contract Summary" form, grounded in Article 79 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law and Article 5(1) of the updated Consumer Finance Regulations. The form must appear at the front of every finance contract subject to those instruments and discloses beneficiary details, total cost of finance, term cost, administrative and real-estate valuation fees, instalment count and amounts, first/last due dates, total amount payable, and cross-references to key contractual clauses (including early repayment, collateral shortfall handling and termination), with a notice that the summary does not replace reading the contract. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: finance contract summary / ملخص عقد التمويل
Consumer Finance Regulations / ضوابط التمويل الاستهلاكي
Finance Companies Control Law implementing regulation Article 79

data.summary: A SAMA Banking Supervision circular relying on the Rules Governing Money Changing Business (Minister of Finance decision) — the duty to supply SAMA with any requested data, SAMA's power to issue supervisory instructions, and the record-keeping/financial-reporting duty — to impose a monthly return on cross-border cash movements into and out of the Kingdom through land, air and sea border crossings, using the attached form. It binds licensed money changers of Category (A) and Category (B).
lookup_terms: cross-border cash movement / حركة الأموال النقدية
money changing business rules / قواعد مزاولة أعمال الصرافة
Category A and B money changers

data.summary: A SAMA circular (with attached instructions) setting the mechanism banks and licensed money-exchange businesses must follow when governmental or non-governmental bodies request customer documents, information, data or disclosure of banking relationships and accounts. It splits cases into those where direct disclosure is prohibited without SAMA's no-objection — criminal matters routed via the Public Prosecution, civil/enforcement matters via the competent judicial authorities, and other agencies' statutory powers, all channelled through SAMA — and a defined set of exceptions where direct disclosure is permitted. It binds banks and licensed exchangers in the Kingdom, which must decline non-conforming direct requests in writing citing this circular.

A SAMA circular issued with the Ministry of Justice to standardise procedural requirements for documenting and registering real estate mortgages before notaries public, and mandating use of the attached registration and incident-recording forms. Conditions include attendance of mortgagor and lender representatives with valid powers of attorney, a licensed bank/finance company as mortgagee holding a valid real estate finance licence, ownership and eligibility of the mortgaged property, Shariah committee product approval, and completion of transfer and mortgage in a single procedure. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom, which must also report notary refusals to SAMA using the prescribed form.

A SAMA circular updating operating procedures for money exchange establishments and companies, issued under the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business. It requires minimum CCTV footage retention (one year), provision of account statements to verified members on request, retention of all customer transaction records for at least ten years with retrievable electronic archiving, recording of residential or national address at relationship establishment, a prohibition on deleting any transaction or membership record, and business continuity/disaster recovery plans tested periodically. It binds all licensed exchange establishments and companies, with compliance required within four months and enforcement action for non-compliance.

SAMA guidelines explaining how to apply for a licence to practise finance or refinance activities under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulations. They set out application instructions (no modification of the form, submission by founders or an authorised representative, soft-copy filing with originals on request), the documents required (draft articles of association, organisational structure, fit and proper forms for founders, 5%+ owners of corporate founders and board/committee candidates, feasibility study and business plan, an irrevocable bank guarantee equal to 20% of minimum capital, and draft third-party/related-party contracts), and the consequences of false or omitted material information. They bind applicants — founders or shareholders seeking incorporation approval and a licence.

Part of SAMA's finance/refinance licensing procedures describing the steps after application completion: written notice of completeness, initial approval or reasoned rejection within 60 business days (initial approval is not a licence), referral to the Ministry of Commerce for incorporation, and post-incorporation evidence of commercial registration, full capital payment and operational readiness. It specifically requires the company to prove it has obtained a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) from the Saudi Operating Unit accredited by GLEIF, followed by an on-site SAMA visit and issuance of the licence upon meeting requirements and fees.
lookup_terms: commercial register and capital payment proof

data.summary: A SAMA circular concerning acceptance of the Saudi Premium Residency (both limited-duration and permanent categories) issued via the Premium Residency Center, relevant to identification and eligibility of holders in dealings with supervised financial institutions. The extractable text of this item is essentially a Premium Residency Center graphic and web reference, so the operative wording must be read in the underlying document. Open the source before relying on it for identification or onboarding decisions.

A component of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework's risk management cycle, covering how a Member Organization determines the likelihood and impact of identified cyber security risks so they can be prioritised against risk appetite. It sits between risk identification and risk response, and its output feeds control selection and maturity assessment against the Framework's six-level maturity model. It binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations (banks, insurers, financing and other regulated entities) subject to the Framework.

Sets out how a Member Organization must treat assessed cyber security risks: documenting treatment options (accept, avoid, transfer/share, mitigate through controls) and the approvals required for each. Risk acceptance requires business-owner sign-off within predefined risk-appetite limits, reporting to the cyber security committee, and must not conflict with SAMA regulations; mitigation requires evaluation, costing and selection of controls with documented residual-risk sign-off. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations under the Cyber Security Framework.

The closing stage of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework risk management cycle: ongoing monitoring of cyber security risk treatment and review of control effectiveness, with periodic review and audit of compliance with the controls. It requires the cyber security risk management process to be defined, approved, implemented and aligned with the Member Organization's enterprise risk management process, protecting confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets. Applies to Member Organizations supervised by SAMA.
lookup_terms: cyber security risk monitoring and review

data.summary: Requires a Member Organization to establish a process to identify, communicate and comply with the cyber security implications of applicable regulations, run periodically and whenever new regulatory requirements take effect. The process must involve representatives from key business areas and result in updates to cyber security policy, standards and procedures. It is the Framework's hook for translating external regulatory change into internal cyber security documentation.

Obliges Member Organizations to comply with mandatory (inter)national industry standards for cyber security, specifically naming PCI-DSS, the EMV technical standard and the SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework (March 2017 version). It is the point where card-payment and interbank-messaging security standards become supervisory expectations under the SAMA Framework, relevant to payment-processing entities in particular.

Requires the cyber security status of a Member Organization's information assets to be subject to periodic cyber security review, with particular attention to critical information assets and customer/internet-facing services. The objective is to confirm controls are securely designed and implemented and that their effectiveness is monitored; results inform maturity-level assessment under the Framework.

A SAMA circular transmitting binding controls and procedures for compensating Saudi banknotes stained by security ink (from intelligent banknote neutralisation systems) as a result of technical or human error. It prohibits circulation of ink-stained notes, requires them to be presented to a SAMA branch with the prescribed compensation request and declaration forms, requires counting/sorting/ATM and self-service equipment to reject such notes, requires cash-staff training, bars their inclusion in bank deposits at SAMA branches (with a penalty per note under Article 23 of the Banking Control Law), and places operating costs and liability on the requesting bank, including for failures by its cash-in-transit contractor. It binds banks, exchange institutions and companies, and licensed cash-transport companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA circular addressed to exchange centres setting out the supervisory data returns to be filed to the Central Bank through its regulatory reporting portal, including monthly returns, total sales and purchases, currency export and import, and bank sales/purchase forms. It fixes the use of SAMA-provided templates, submission and validation steps, return due dates, and the resubmission route for corrections. Relevant to regulatory reporting obligations of licensed money exchange businesses.

A SAMA circular amending Appendix 1 of the second edition of the Requirements for Appointments to Leading Positions in SAMA-supervised financial institutions, adding a further senior role to the list of positions requiring SAMA's prior written no-objection. The appendix covers board members and committee chairs/members plus senior management roles (CEO, finance, risk, internal audit, compliance, AML/CTF, financial crime, fraud, credit, operations, legal, governance/board secretary, information/cyber security, IT, HR, retail and corporate banking, ALM/SAIBOR submitter, financial enforcement) and any executive reporting directly to the CEO. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom and applies to appointments made from the circular's date.

SAMA operational guidelines (March 2019) for banks acting as Primary Dealers (Bank-PDs) in the Saudi government securities market. They set eligibility conditions (capital adequacy under ICAAP, treasury/trading capability, risk management and hedging capacity, infrastructure, and SAMA no-objection), obligations in primary auctions, underwriting, market-making and secondary trading, the requirement to form a Primary Dealers' Committee with a code of conduct, board-approved investment policy content, application of held-for-trading classification and valuation rules, liquidity-ratio treatment, and separate books, audit trails and reporting including notification of breaches of the Debt Management Office undertaking. Binds banks authorised to undertake PD business.
lookup_terms: Primary Dealers Committee code of conduct

data.summary: A SAMA circular requiring exchange centres to comply with two provisions of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business: an independent periodic test, at least annually, of the centre's operations and automated systems and its adherence to internal policies and procedures, to be completed by end of July each calendar year; and an external auditor assessment of internal control systems whose report must at minimum record any observations on the centre's compliance with the Rules. Acknowledgement of receipt is required within a week, and SAMA reserves supervisory action against non-compliant centres. Binds exchange centres operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: internal control systems report external auditor
Rules Governing Money Exchange Business Article 14

data.summary: A SAMA circular directing all real estate finance companies to accept the ownership document issued by the Economic Cities Authority for property or land inside economic cities as an official, certified title document equivalent to a title deed used outside economic cities. It relies on the Finance Companies Control Law and the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Lease Law, read with the Economic Cities Authority statute provisions on issuing and registering ownership documents. Binds real estate finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

Concept node for SAMA's Returns Management System (RMS), the supervisory reporting portal through which SAMA-supervised entities submit prescribed prudential/supervisory return forms and through which SAMA supervisors review, accept or return them. The underlying material is a user guidance manual (account creation, submission, resubmission after supervisory observations) together with a circular applying the system to money exchange centres, which must file monthly, quarterly and annual supervisory returns within stated deadlines after period end. Relevance is operational-regulatory: it evidences the enforceable channel and timing for regulatory data submission rather than substantive conduct rules.

Section of SAMA's Cyber Security Framework requiring Member Organizations to embed cyber security into project management methodology and project governance. It expects cyber security objectives in project objectives, involvement of the cyber security function across all project phases, an initial risk assessment, registration and tracking of cyber security risks, allocated responsibilities, and an independent internal or external review. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations and is assessed against the framework's six-level maturity model.

Section of SAMA's Cyber Security Framework requiring a defined, approved cyber security awareness programme covering staff, third parties and customers of the Member Organization, aimed at building a risk-aware culture. It links to the cyber security policy requirement that relevant stakeholders be made aware of expected behaviour, and sits within the framework's governance domain. Applies to SAMA-supervised Member Organizations and is measured under the maturity model.

Node covering cyber security training expectations under SAMA's Cyber Security Framework, closely tied to the awareness programme and to the framework's roles-and-responsibilities requirements (board accountability, defined general and specific cyber security responsibilities). It supports the expectation that staff and stakeholders are equipped to apply cyber security controls consistently. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations; performance is assessed via the maturity model.

Section 3.2 of SAMA's Cyber Security Framework on cyber security risk management and compliance, requiring a defined, approved and implemented risk management process covering identification, analysis, response, and monitoring/review of cyber risks. The process must protect confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets and be aligned with the organization's enterprise risk management process, with periodic review and audit of control compliance. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

Node on the risk identification and treatment stage of SAMA's Cyber Security Framework risk management cycle, including documenting treatment options (accept, avoid, transfer/share, mitigate) against the organization's risk appetite. Risk acceptance requires business-owner sign-off, reporting to the cyber security committee, and must not conflict with SAMA regulations; mitigation requires control selection with cost, feasibility and compliance assessment. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

SAMA circular inviting all SAMA-supervised financial institutions to support the Kingdom's national Social Responsibility Day (established by Council of Ministers decision, observed in March each year) through developmental initiatives or awareness campaigns, and to report their contribution back to SAMA. It is an exhortative/administrative communication rather than a prudential or conduct obligation, though it carries a reporting expectation and references a guidance manual for use of the campaign logo. Addressed to the full population of institutions under SAMA supervision.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

data.summary: SAMA circular directing all money exchange centres in the Kingdom to make point-of-sale (POS) acceptance available and activated for customers, following SAMA's development of a unified pricing model for POS transactions carried out with mada cards at exchange centres. It relies on Article 14(b) of the Rules Regulating Money Exchange Business as the supervisory power to issue such instructions, and expressly warns that non-compliance will trigger statutory penalties. Binds licensed exchange establishments and companies operating in Saudi Arabia.
lookup_terms: point of sale POS exchange centres
Rules Regulating Money Exchange Business Article 14(b)

data.summary: SAMA guidance setting out how founders apply for a licence to practise finance support activities under the Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities, including the unmodifiable application form, submission channel, and the documents that must accompany the application (commercial register, shareholder list, organisational structure, Fit and Proper forms for founders, 5%+ owners of corporate founders and board candidates, feasibility study and three-year business plan, draft third-party/related-party agreements, and an irrevocable bank guarantee equal to 20% of minimum capital). It stresses that submitting false or incomplete material information is itself a breach of the Rules and can lead to rejection or cancellation of the application. Binds applicants/founders of prospective finance support companies, not yet licensed entities.
lookup_terms: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities

data.summary: SAMA circular updating the mandatory standard-form contracts for retail real estate finance — the Murabaha real estate finance contract and the Ijara real estate finance contract for individuals — supplementing the earlier circular requiring use of those standard forms. It requires all real estate financiers to adopt the attached updated forms by the stated deadline and prohibits concluding contracts that depart from, or amending, those forms thereafter; the annexed contract covers lease periods, variable rental payment calculation, late payment, early repayment/early ownership, title transfer, default and termination, withdrawal rights, and a borrower-facing contract summary sheet. Binds banks and real estate finance companies operating in the Kingdom in their dealings with individual consumers.

Concept node from SAMA's cyber security framework defining the information security function and the Chief Information Security Officer role: a function independent of IT, headed by the CISO, reporting directly to the CEO/managing director (or general manager of a control function), responsible for security policies, roles and goals, risk management frameworks, identifying emerging issues and shifts in risk appetite, and supporting management in designing controls. It sits alongside the required content of the cyber security policy and the allocation of cyber security roles and responsibilities, with ultimate accountability resting with the Board of Directors (including budget and approvals). Binds Member Organisations subject to the framework.
lookup_terms: Board of Directors cyber security accountability

data.summary: Concept node for the Rules Regulating Money Exchange Business (issued by Minister of Finance decision), the licensing and supervisory regime for exchange centres in the Kingdom; Article 14(b) empowers SAMA to issue any instructions needed to apply supervisory requirements to exchange business, and Article 31 obliges centres to provide SAMA with any data or reports it requests within the time it sets. The linked circular exercises those powers by updating the monthly, quarterly and annual supervisory return templates and requiring electronic submission through SAMA's Returns Management System within specified deadlines (sales/purchases, currencies, largest customers, counterfeit currency, staff data, financial-statement comparison, annual regulatory data). Binds exchange establishments and companies operating in Saudi Arabia, with statutory action for non-compliance.

A sub-domain of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework dealing with periodic independent review and audit of compliance with cyber security controls, read against the Framework's six-level maturity model (levels 3 and above require cumulative satisfaction of lower levels). It sits alongside the requirements for a board-endorsed cyber security policy and defined roles, with the Board holding ultimate accountability including budget and approvals. It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA and is assessed by SAMA through the maturity model.
lookup_terms: internal audit of cyber security controls

data.summary: Covers the SAMA Cyber Security Framework's identity and access management requirement: access to information assets must be restricted on need-to-have and need-to-know grounds, with an approved IAM policy whose compliance is monitored and whose control effectiveness is periodically evaluated. It addresses the joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle for internal staff, external staff and third parties, and formal approval of access requests. It binds Member Organizations and links into the Framework's wider cyber security risk management and compliance cycle.

A control area within the SAMA Cyber Security Framework addressing security of applications, framed by the Framework's maturity model and by the requirement for an approved cyber security policy covering asset classification, ownership, risk assessment, awareness, regulatory/contractual compliance and breach reporting. Board-level responsibility and defined cyber security roles apply. It binds Member Organizations subject to SAMA supervision.

Sets out the SAMA Cyber Security Framework's change management control: a defined, approved and implemented change process with monitored compliance and periodically evaluated control effectiveness. It requires impact assessment and classification of changes, security testing (including penetration testing and code review of internally and externally developed applications), business-owner and cyber security function approval before the Change Advisory Board, CAB approval, post-implementation review, segregation of development/test/production environments and duties, and emergency change and roll-back procedures. It binds Member Organizations and feeds the Framework's cyber risk management cycle.

Requires Member Organizations to define, approve and implement cyber security standards for infrastructure components, monitor compliance with those standards, and measure and periodically evaluate their effectiveness. It follows directly from the change management controls and sits within the Framework's policy, roles and maturity-model architecture, with the Board ultimately accountable. Applies to entities supervised by SAMA.

A control area of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework on cyber security event management — the logging, monitoring, analysis and escalation of security events — assessed against the Framework's six-level maturity model. It connects to the policy requirement that cyber security breaches and suspected weaknesses be reported and that cyber security be reflected in business continuity management, with defined roles and ultimate Board responsibility. It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA.

A control domain of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework dealing with how Member Organizations detect, respond to, escalate and report cyber security incidents, including reporting of breaches and suspected weaknesses to SAMA and internal stakeholders. It sits within the Framework's overall structure of governance, policy, defined roles and the six-level cyber security maturity model against which compliance is assessed. It binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations (banks, insurers, finance companies and similar entities), with ultimate accountability resting with the Board.

Covers the threat intelligence and threat management process that a Member Organization must define, approve, implement and periodically evaluate, drawing on internal telemetry and external sources including SAMA, government agencies and security vendors. It requires a documented analysis methodology, capture of threat attributes such as actors, motivation and modus operandi, actionable follow-up, and sharing of relevant intelligence with SAMA and other stakeholders. Applies to all SAMA-supervised Member Organizations and links into the enterprise-aligned cyber security risk management process.

Framework control (section 3.3.17) requiring Member Organizations to define, approve and implement a process for identifying and mitigating application and infrastructure vulnerabilities, with effectiveness measured and periodically evaluated. It is closely tied to threat intelligence inputs and to the wider cyber security risk identification, analysis, response and monitoring cycle, and is subject to periodic review and audit. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

Framework domain (section 3.4) requiring that the same level of cyber security protection applied inside a Member Organization is achieved at third parties it relies on, with third parties defined broadly to include information service providers, outsourcing and cloud providers, vendors, suppliers and government agencies. It sets how cyber security requirements with third parties are organised, implemented and monitored, and is the parent for contract/vendor management, outsourcing and cloud computing controls. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations; accountability remains with the Board.

Control 3.4.1 requiring Member Organizations to embed defined and approved cyber security requirements into contract and vendor management processes, monitor compliance, and periodically measure control effectiveness. It addresses when the cyber security function must be involved (e.g. due diligence), baseline security requirements applicable in all cases, and rights to conduct periodic reviews across the contract life-cycle. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations contracting with third parties.

Control 3.4.2 requiring cyber security requirements to be defined, implemented and monitored within the Member Organization's outsourcing policy and process, before, during and on exit from outsourcing arrangements. It expressly requires prior SAMA approval for material outsourcing, involvement of the cyber security function, and compliance with SAMA's outsourcing circular (Rules on Outsourcing) and related business continuity requirements. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations; note the adjacent cloud computing control applies to hybrid and public cloud but not private/internal cloud.

Node within the SAMA Cyber Security Framework covering outsourcing and cloud computing controls for Member Organizations (SAMA-supervised financial institutions). It sets the expectation of a defined, approved and monitored cloud policy and process for hybrid and public cloud only (private/internal cloud excluded), with prior SAMA approval before material outsourcing and before using cloud services or signing a cloud contract, plus contractual coverage of data location (in principle inside Saudi Arabia, otherwise explicit SAMA approval), no secondary use of data, security controls, logical data segregation, business continuity, audit/review/examination rights and exit arrangements. It binds the Member Organization, which remains accountable for controls executed by the service provider.

Concept node in the SAMA Cyber Security Framework tying the Security Operations Center to the framework's maturity model and governance layer: the SOC is the designated team required under cyber security event management, and its adequacy is assessed against maturity levels 0–5 (target levels require all preceding criteria to be met). Governance context includes the board's ultimate responsibility for cyber security, budget and policy approval, and defined cyber security roles. Binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA.

Glossary and control node covering SIEM (security information and event management) and related defined terms within the SAMA Cyber Security Framework, read together with the cyber security event management requirements. Those requirements oblige Member Organizations to define, approve and implement a security event management process and monitoring standard, staff a dedicated SOC with 24x7 monitoring in a restricted area, and detect and handle malicious code, anomalies and suspicious events; adjacent controls include SMS notification to customers for retail/personal financial transactions and for adding, modifying or activating beneficiaries.

Node covering the SAMA Cyber Security Framework's risk management and compliance section together with its risk-related glossary (risk register, risk tolerance, risk treatment, risk-aware culture, root-cause analysis). It requires Member Organizations to run a defined, approved and implemented cyber security risk management process — identification, analysis, response, monitoring and review — aligned with enterprise risk management and focused on confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets, with periodic review and audit of control compliance. Relevant to how SAMA supervises IT and cyber risk at supervised institutions.
lookup_terms: cyber security compliance review and audit

data.summary: SAMA Guidelines on Repurchase Agreements setting policy requirements for the Saudi repo market, issued under SAMA's Charter and the Banking Control Law and expressly binding on repo market participants. They apply to eligible counterparties (Section 9) and to SAR-denominated repo/reverse repo in eligible securities, without prohibiting existing foreign-currency repos governed by the GMRA, and must be read with other SAMA rules, the Capital Market Law and CMA rules, and the Bankruptcy Law. Includes defined terms (custodian, eligible security, held-in-custody, repo buyer/seller, Saudi Repo Market, SARIE, Tadawul).

Concept node for the standard Master Repurchase Agreement (MRA) for the Sale and Purchase of Securities (2020 version) approved by SAMA and appended to the repo guidelines. All repo market participants must document repo transactions in Saudi Arabia under this standard MRA, with any variations placed in Annexures, mutually agreed, and made clear in trade confirmations or equivalent agreed form; the GMRA remains referenced for certain cross-border/foreign-currency repos.

Definitional node from SAMA's Guidelines on Repurchase Agreement (Repo) setting out the core terms of the Saudi repo regime: repo and reverse repo, repo buyer (cash provider) and repo seller (securities provider), custodian, held-in-custody, eligible security, and market infrastructure references (SARIE, Tadawul, SOCPA, ICMA/GMRA). It also frames scope: the guidelines cover SAR-denominated outright sale/purchase of eligible securities with a repurchase or resale commitment, and bind all repo market participants (the eligible counterparties in Section 9), with the standard SAMA-approved Master Repurchase Agreement (2020) as the mandatory governing document under Saudi law.

Sets out who may transact repo in Saudi Arabia, subject to the overriding condition that at least one principal must be a SAMA-licensed bank. Eligible categories include SAMA-licensed financial institutions (banks, insurers, finance companies), CMA-approved capital market institutions, Saudi-incorporated corporates (subject to sophistication assessment), and non-domiciled corporates with maturity/tenor restrictions on the repo and its collateral. Also covers adjacent legal-risk duties: full transfer of ownership of eligible securities, adequate documentation for the repo type used, confidentiality of counterparty identity except for SAMA regulatory reporting, and general compliance with applicable law.
lookup_terms: at least one principal must be a licensed bank

data.summary: Concerns what qualifies as repo collateral and how it is valued on default. The guidelines' eligibility list includes bonds/sukuk listed on the Saudi Exchange and anything else SAMA specifies, with legal maturity at least matching the repo term and a prohibition on securities issued or guaranteed by the repo seller; the extracted context also reaches the MRA close-out machinery defining Deliverable/Receivable Securities, Net Value, Transaction Costs and Default Market Value. Binds repo market participants and, on the MRA terms, the non-defaulting party exercising close-out valuation discretion.
lookup_terms: sukuk and bonds listed in Saudi Exchange

data.summary: Imposes repo risk-management obligations on banks and all other repo market participants: documented policies and procedures covering governance, authorisation, risk management, internal controls and reporting, comprehensively addressing credit, counterparty, market, legal and operational risk. Also requires coordination across treasury, back office, risk, compliance and IT with adequate supporting infrastructure, counterparty and issuer exposure limits reviewed periodically, and compliance with SOCPA-endorsed accounting treatment for repos. Adjacent provisions cover collateral valuation, agreed price sources with a waterfall approach, haircuts/margin calls, substitution and events of default.

Governs custodial arrangements in repo transactions. Every repo market participant must fully understand the custody agreement's terms and its own rights and obligations before entering into a repo with a custodial arrangement, and a licensed bank holding eligible securities in custody for repo participants must maintain arrangements and processes to monitor and segregate those securities so they cannot be used more than once. Read with the definitions of Custodian and Held-in-Custody and the requirement that ownership fully transfers to the buyer notwithstanding custody.

The reporting and settlement section requires bank repo participants to report repo transactions to SAMA and addresses settlement of the repo legs. The extracted context largely draws on the MRA's supporting terms — party representations and warranties (authority, acting as principal, required authorisations), margin securities exchange and settlement-system payment mechanics, and Act of Insolvency triggers including filings under the Saudi Bankruptcy Law — which shape settlement and close-out consequences for counterparties.

This node covers the Events of Default machinery in the SAMA-approved Master Agreement for the Sale and Purchase of Securities annexed to the Guidelines on Repurchase Agreements, including notice/service rules (delivery in person, courier, facsimile, registered mail, Electronic Messaging System) and when a Default Notice is deemed effective. It also sets out the close-out mechanics once a default occurs: determination of Default Market Values, Cash Margin, Equivalent Margin Securities, Second Purchase Prices and Cash Equivalent Amounts as at the Early Termination Date, and their replacement by a single Cash Settlement Amount payable by the Undertaking Party to the Exercising Party. It binds both counterparties (Buyer and Seller) to any repo transaction documented under the mandated MRA.

SARIE is a defined term in the Guidelines on Repurchase Agreements, meaning the Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express (or any future instant payments system), and it is the mandated cash settlement channel for repo transactions. Where both counterparties are licensed agents and the transaction is in SAR, cash legs must settle through SARIE (with securities settling via Tadawul, or via SAMA for SAMA-issued securities); otherwise any mutually agreed system may be used. The requirement binds repo market participants transacting in the Saudi repo market.

Tadawul (defined as the Saudi Exchange) is the mandated delivery venue for non-SAMA-issued eligible securities in repo transactions where both counterparties are licensed agents and the currency is SAR, with the cash leg moving through SARIE. SAMA-issued securities instead exchange through SAMA; where a counterparty is a non-licensed agent or the currency is not SAR, counterparties may use any mutually agreed system. Relevant to repo market participants determining permitted settlement infrastructure.

This is the SAMA Guidelines on Repurchase Agreements (2021) together with the standard Master Agreement for the Sale and Purchase of Securities (2020 version) at Appendix A, the Shariah-compliant repo master documentation. It defines the core repo terms (repo/reverse repo, Repo Buyer, Repo Seller, repo market participants, Saudi Repo Market, Tadawul, SARIE, SOCPA) and sets policy requirements on legal documentation, reporting, eligible counterparties and settlement, plus close-out definitions such as Net Value, Deliverable/Receivable Securities and Transaction Costs. It binds all repo market participants transacting in Saudi Arabia, who must use the SAMA-approved MRA with any variations recorded in the Annexes and confirmations.

This node sets out the trigger events (including Act of Insolvency, failure to provide margin, untrue representations, suspension or expulsion from an exchange, and uncured breaches after 30 days' notice) and the designation of an Early Termination Date by the non-Defaulting Party on not more than 20 days' notice, or automatically where Automatic Early Termination is elected in Annex I. It links to the defined terms governing exercise of the unilateral undertakings (Exercise Date, Exercise Notice, Exercising Party, Exercised Transaction) and to equivalence of securities on corporate events. It binds Buyer and Seller under each repo transaction governed by the SAMA-approved MRA.

Annex II is the standard form of Confirmation under the SAMA-approved Master Agreement for the Sale and Purchase of Securities, evidencing each individual repo transaction and incorporating the unilateral undertakings of Seller and Buyer to purchase/sell the Second Purchased Securities at the Second Purchase Price upon satisfaction of the relevant Exercise Condition and delivery of an Exercise Notice. It specifies required transaction terms (Second Purchase Date, Pricing Rate, settlement accounts, additional terms), and the Confirmation together with the Agreement is prima facie evidence of agreed terms, prevailing over the Agreement in case of conflict for that transaction only. Applies to both counterparties documenting repo transactions in Saudi Arabia.

Annex to a SAMA-issued master repurchase-style agreement setting out the exercise mechanics for the parties' undertakings (Seller/Buyer Exercise Conditions tested against Market Value or Default Market Value of the Second Purchased Securities versus the Second Purchase Price), including delivery of an Exercise Notice on an Exercise Date and deemed acceptance if the Undertaking Party does not respond within the stated window. The extract also carries the Events of Default and Early Termination Date provisions, including designation by notice and Automatic Early Termination where elected. It binds the contracting counterparties to the master agreement rather than imposing a free-standing supervisory obligation.

SAMA circular imposing mandatory pre-contract conduct requirements on banks and real estate finance companies before offering residential real estate finance to individuals: affordability/creditworthiness assessment against approved credit policy, a clear explanation of terms and risks by a competent officer, a written finance offer valid for at least fifteen business days containing printed copies of all documents in final form, an explanation by an independent qualified credit advisor (not the officer who dealt with or issued the offer), and a reflection period of at least five business days before contracting. Contracting is prohibited unless all steps are completed and documented in the finance file; full compliance was required by 12/08/2018.

Prescribed acknowledgment form annexed to the real estate finance circular, by which an individual customer accepts the credit risks of variable-rate (variable term cost) real estate finance; it must be included in the finance offer pack in the attached format for variable-cost products. The lender must document the customer's receipt of the form and allow the customer to take the documents away for independent advice, and cannot conclude the contract otherwise. Binds banks and real estate finance companies offering variable-rate products to individuals.
lookup_terms: variable term cost real estate finance

data.summary: SAMA circular requiring financial institutions under its supervision, their subsidiaries, and branches of foreign financial institutions operating in the Kingdom to hold an active and up-to-date Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) issued through a GLEIF-accredited operating unit, building on an earlier LEI circular. It also permits those institutions to sign an agreement with SIMAH, the accredited local operating unit, to issue, update and renew LEIs on behalf of their current and prospective corporate customers. Rationale is risk management, financial stability, market transparency and international (G20/GLEIF) commitments.

Template agreement attached to the LEI circular between SIMAH (as GLEIF-accredited local operating unit) and a SAMA-supervised financial institution, enabling the institution to issue, update and renew Legal Entity Identifiers for its legal-entity customers. It recites the governing framework: the ROC charter, the ROC–GLEIF memorandum of understanding, the GLEIF–SIMAH master agreement, and SAMA instructions. Binds the two contracting parties and shapes how corporate customer identifiers are obtained in practice.
lookup_terms: issuing LEI through a financial institution

data.summary: Governor's decision (transmitted by circular to the Saudi Company for Registration of Finance Lease Contracts, "Sijil") setting the powers, duties and liabilities of the Head of the Contract Registry and registry clerks under the Finance Lease Law and its Implementing Regulation. It covers SAMA no-objection for appointment and SAMA's power to remove for breach, reporting to the company's CEO, responsibility for correct registration of finance lease contracts and supporting data, ten-year retention of records, verification of contracting parties' identity and capacity, Arabic-language documents and certified translation, official seals (including approved electronic means), and grievance routes against refusal to register. Binds the registry company and its registry officers; lessors bear costs where work is performed at their premises.
lookup_terms: Finance Lease Law Implementing Regulation Article 15

data.summary: A SAMA supervisory circular addressed to all banks operating in the Kingdom prohibiting them from dealing or negotiating with non-Saudi representatives of private civil security guarding and cash-transport (cash-in-transit) companies when procuring guarding or cash transport services. Banks must report the employing company to the competent regional police authority for legal action, and must fully comply with the Private Civil Security Guarding Law and the Law on Transport of Cash, Precious Metals and Valuable Documents and their implementing regulations. It binds licensed banks as a procurement/counterparty conduct restriction rather than a prudential rule.

A circular from SAMA's Finance Companies Supervision Department notifying the Governor's decision to form a General Committee of General Managers/CEOs of finance companies, with the attached Terms of Reference for Finance Companies Committees. Issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and Article 98 of its Implementing Regulation (which allows the Governor to form committees to propose measures for developing the finance sector), the ToR set out the committee structure (general committee, executive committee, sub-committees), formation, nomination and removal, meetings and quorum, agendas, minutes and reporting, responsibilities, and SAMA's role and that of its representatives. It binds finance companies participating in the sector-level committee framework.
lookup_terms: Terms of Reference for Finance Companies Committees

data.summary: The Rules Governing BNPL Companies define BNPL activity as financing that lets a Consumer buy goods or services with no term cost borne by the Consumer, and require a SAMA licence (joint stock company form) before conducting it. The Rules cover licensing procedures and minimum operating standards, and expressly operate alongside the Finance Companies Control Law, senior appointment requirements, outsourcing rules, financial-crime instructions, external audit (non-objection for auditor appointment), complaint handling and consumer data confidentiality, and Saudization thresholds. They bind companies licensed by SAMA for BNPL activity; note the distinct defined term "Consumer" (beneficiary of the activity) versus "Customer" in AML/CTF instruments, and the role of "Stores" as sales outlets.

A SAMA explanatory guide (with a disclaimer that it is non-binding guidance) explaining the early repayment amount and the unified method finance providers must use to calculate it for instalment-based finance such as personal finance, vehicle lease finance and real estate finance. It restates the beneficiary's right to early settlement, the permitted compensation to the financier (reinvestment cost capped at the term cost of the following three months on a diminishing-balance basis, plus non-recoverable third-party payments), the diminishing-balance allocation and amortization table requirements, and gives worked examples. It reflects Articles 82 and 84 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law, Articles 9 and 11 of the Finance Lease Law Implementing Regulation, and Article 11 of the Consumer Finance Regulations update, and is directed at banks and finance companies dealing with finance beneficiaries.
lookup_terms: reinvestment cost three months term cost

data.summary: A Banking Supervision circular reaffirming a series of earlier SAMA circulars on disclosure of banking data: institutions must not provide any financial or banking information about their customers or their banking dealings to any party, whether individuals, entities, government bodies, or any other local or foreign party, without first referring to SAMA and obtaining its no-objection. Recipients must cascade it to all departments and branches and confirm compliance within a week. It binds banks, licensed money exchange institutions, and the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH).

A circular from SAMA's Finance Companies Supervision Department transmitting a Ministry of Finance letter and a cable from the National Committee for Narcotics Control announcing the launch of the National Drug Prevention Project (Nebras), and asking supervised entities to coordinate with the Committee's General Secretariat and use the Nebras branding when preparing similar preventive awareness programs. It is an administrative/coordination instruction rather than a prudential or AML obligation, addressed to banks, insurance companies, finance companies and the Saudi Credit Bureau.

A SAMA Currency Department circular (Arabic) implementing Ministry of Interior/Crime Research Center recommendations requiring large companies and commercial establishments to move cash only through licensed cash-transport (cash-in-transit) firms and to use secure bags/containers approved by SAMA, including containers permitting automatic tracking and self-destruction of notes if the planned route is altered. It binds banks and exchange companies operating in the Kingdom, licensed cash-transport companies, and licensed operators of unified cash centres, with SAMA field inspections and penalties for non-compliance.

A SAMA circular (Arabic) on the prudential treatment of non-performing assets, requiring banks to comply with the Basel Committee guidelines on problem assets — notably the harmonised definitions of non-performing exposures and forbearance. It affects asset-quality monitoring and supervisory comparability, internal ratings-based credit risk systems, Pillar 3 asset-quality disclosure, and published asset-quality indicators; addressed to all banks operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: Basel Committee prudential treatment of problem assets

data.summary: A Governor-level SAMA circular (Arabic) directing supervised entities to promptly receive and execute judicial rulings and decisions issued against them without delay or procrastination, and to raise any objection through the competent channels within the prescribed statutory periods rather than deferring compliance. It binds banks, insurance and reinsurance companies and insurance-related free professions, finance companies, exchange businesses, and credit information companies.

A SAMA circular issuing the mandatory standard-form vehicle finance lease (Ijarah) contract for individuals, adopted under the Banking Control Law, the Finance Companies Control Law and the Finance Lease Law and its Implementing Regulation (which empowers SAMA to approve model lease forms protecting the parties' rights). Lessors must use the attached model form by the stated deadline and may not conclude contracts that depart from or amend it; it binds banks and finance companies acting as lessors to individual (retail) lessees.

The early-ownership (early acquisition) provisions within SAMA's mandatory standard vehicle finance lease contract for individuals, referenced in the contract summary sheet alongside early partial repayment, late-payment consequences and transfer-of-title procedures. It governs the lessee's right and the procedure to acquire the leased vehicle before the end of the lease term, and binds lessors (banks and finance companies) that must apply the model form without amendment.

Material issued under the Finance Lease Law (Royal Decree M/48) and its Implementing Regulation: a SAMA circular to the Saudi Finance Lease Contract Registration Company ("Sijil") transmitting the Governor's decision setting the competencies of the Head of the Contract Registry, plus the decision text itself. It governs appointment (subject to SAMA no-objection), the registration duties, liability and record-retention obligations of the registry head and registrars, complaint/grievance routes against refusal to register, and their duty to verify identity, capacity and Arabic-language documentation; it binds the registration company and its registry officials, with knock-on effects for lessors registering leases.
lookup_terms: implementing regulation of finance lease law

data.summary: Node for the Basel Committee guidelines on the prudential treatment of problem assets (d403), covering harmonised definitions and treatment of non-performing exposures and forbearance. SAMA circulated these guidelines to banks operating in the Kingdom, stressing compliance and identifying their use in asset-quality monitoring and supervision, internal ratings-based credit risk management, Pillar 3 asset-quality disclosure, and published asset-quality indicators. It binds banks under SAMA supervision as a supervisory expectation layered on the existing accounting and regulatory framework.

Node for the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH) in its role as the SAMA-licensed credit information company acting as the accredited Local Operating Unit (LOU) for the Legal Entity Identifier in the Kingdom, and as first party to the standard agreement on issuing, updating and renewing an LEI through a financial institution. The agreement lets SAMA-supervised financial institutions register and renew LEIs on behalf of their existing or prospective corporate customers under the LEI regulatory framework (ROC charter, GLEIF master agreement) and SAMA instructions. It binds SIMAH and the signing financial institution.

Concept node for the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF), the international body that accredits Local Operating Units authorised to issue Legal Entity Identifiers. SAMA requires supervised financial institutions, their subsidiaries and branches of foreign financial institutions operating in the Kingdom to obtain and keep current an LEI from a GLEIF-accredited unit, linking the requirement to risk management, financial stability, market transparency, Vision 2030 and G20 commitments. Relevant to any question about which body validates LEI issuers.

Node for the total-loss element of the standard-form vehicle finance lease (Ijarah) contract for individuals annexed to the SAMA circular, which the contract addresses together with partial loss of the leased asset. It governs how lessor and lessee handle destruction or write-off of the vehicle and the resulting effect on the lease obligations, with the contract summary required to point the consumer to those procedures. It binds banks and finance companies acting as lessors, who must use the standard form without amendment.

Node for the partial-loss element of the standard-form vehicle finance lease (Ijarah) contract for individuals issued under the Finance Lease Law and its implementing regulation.
